ideaData.title: Single die-cast structural housing merges motor, gearbox, inverter
ideaData.technicalDescription: Baseline three-housing architecture: die-cast AlSi9Cu3(Fe) (EN AC-46000) motor housing, GJL-250 grey-iron gearbox case, and bolted AlSi10Mg (EN AC-43000) inverter box, joined by ~34 M6/M8 fasteners across two gasketed flanges with two coolant O-ring transitions. Proposal: one HPDC AlSi10MnMg (EN AC-43500, 0.5% Mn, T5/self-hardening) monobloc integrating stator bore, two-stage reduction gear bores and inverter cavity, cast on a 4,400t machine with cast-in coolant galleries (lost-salt-core or drilled cross-galleries). Wall 3.5 mm nominal, 5 mm at bearing bosses; stator bore machined to H7 with 0.02 mm cylindricity in one clamping. Shared walls carry motor and gear reaction loads, deleting redundant flange thickness; single datum removes three-housing stack-up so gear-to-rotor concentricity holds without shims.
ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Deletes 2 flange-machining setups, 2 gasket stations, ~34 fasteners and 2 leak-test transitions. Adds one large HPDC cell + cavity vacuum + one 5-axis machining fixture. Cycle up per part but station count net down; one combined coolant/HV leak test replaces three. Plant capex: 4,400t press.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Deletes two housings, two gasket sets, ~34 fasteners and two joint leak paths; cuts machining setups and inbound logistics from three castings to one.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~€52 housing+fastener+gasket+assembly baseline × ~30% delta × 250,000 ≈ €3.9M direct + machining/logistics/leak-test savings to €9-14M range

ideaData.riskNotes: Monobloc scrap on a large casting is costly (one porous inverter pocket scraps motor+gear bores). Mitigate with cavity-pressure sensors, X-ray sampling and vacuum die casting. Thermal expansion couples inverter heat to gear bore; validate bearing preload over -40/+150°C. NVH: shared walls transmit gear whine to inverter — add cast ribs tuned off 1st mode.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Structural monobloc/integrated die-cast EDU housings are established practice on recent high-volume BEV integrated drive units; the shared-wall load-path and single-datum mechanism is proven without naming a specific programme.
ideaData.materialGrade: HPDC AlSi10MnMg (EN AC-43500) T5; replaces AlSi9Cu3(Fe) EN AC-46000, GJL-250, AlSi10Mg EN AC-43000

ideaData.title: Common carrier platform scales 150/250/350 kW via insert swaps
ideaData.technicalDescription: Baseline: three power classes each get a bespoke housing, bearing plan and gear centre-distance, tripling tooling and validation. Proposal: one HPDC AlSi10MnMg (EN AC-43500) carrier with fixed gear centre-distance and fixed bearing bore pattern across 150/250/350 kW; power scaled inside the fixed envelope by (a) active stack length via lamination spacers on a common M270-35A / M250-35A (0.35 mm, ~2.7 W/kg @1.5T/50Hz) die, (b) rotor magnet grade N38UH→N42UH, and (c) inverter power-module count on a common busbar interface. Gear macro-geometry constant; only face width steps 22/28/34 mm at DIN 3962 quality 6, so the same hobbing/grinding setup and shaft blanks apply. Torque capacity scales with face width and stack length at constant module and centre-distance, keeping the expensive-to-tool load-path geometry invariant.
ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Collapses 3 housing tools to 1 and 3 gear-cut setups to 1 family. Adds spacer/stack-length station on the lamination line. Common machining fixtures across variants raise utilisation. One bearing bore program serves all; inbound part numbers drop sharply.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: One housing tool and one gear-cut family replace three; shared fixtures, shared validation basis and fewer part numbers cut piece cost and NRE.
costSavingPotential.percentage: 18-26% of blended EDU tooling+overhead across the three classes
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~€6-8M tooling NRE avoided (2 of 3 housing+gear tool sets) amortised + ~€25/unit overhead/logistics delta × 400,000 units

ideaData.riskNotes: Highest variant (350 kW) sizes the fixed geometry, so lower variants carry slight over-design mass. Validate bearing L10 across the torque span with common bore/preload. Thermal derate at top variant must be proven in the common jacket; confirm hot-spot margin at 350 kW before freezing centre-distance.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Face-width/stack-length family scaling on a fixed centre-distance is established modular e-drive practice; the constant-load-path mechanism is proven without naming a specific programme.
ideaData.materialGrade: HPDC AlSi10MnMg (EN AC-43500) carrier; M270-35A / M250-35A NGO electrical steel; sintered NdFeB N38UH–N42UH

ideaData.title: Direct-oil rotor-and-stator cooling deletes the water jacket
ideaData.technicalDescription: Baseline EDU uses a cast-in or FSW water/glycol jacket around the stator plus a separate oil circuit for gears/bearings — two fluids, two pumps, an oil-to-water heat exchanger and a coolant fill/leak station. Proposal: single low-viscosity ATF-grade e-fluid (~4-5 cSt @100°C, e.g. GTL Group-III synthetic dedicated e-transmission fluid) sprayed on stator end-windings via a cast oil gallery and fed through a hollow rotor shaft for centrifugal magnet cooling; the same oil lubricates the reduction gears. Delete water-jacket walls, water pump, water-side seals and coolant transitions. Direct-contact oil on the copper (windings insulated to thermal class H, 180°C) removes winding-to-jacket conduction resistance (potting + housing wall), running the same continuous torque ~10-15°C cooler, permitting a shorter magnet stack or a lower magnet grade for equal output.
ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Deletes jacket core/FSW jacket seam, water pump mount, coolant leak-test station and O-ring transitions. Adds a spray-bar/gallery core in the casting and a hollow rotor shaft (gun-drilled or two-piece FSW). One oil fill/leak test replaces oil+coolant. Net station reduction.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Deletes second fluid circuit, water pump, one heat exchanger interface and coolant leak testing; enables magnet grade/stack reduction from lower winding temperature.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~€35 water pump+jacket+HEX interface+leak-test baseline × ~70% delta × 250,000 + magnet-grade saving ~€4/unit

ideaData.riskNotes: Oil in the airgap adds windage/churning loss at high rpm — validate spin loss vs. efficiency target and control oil level. Dielectric compatibility of oil with HV winding insulation over life must be qualified. Cold-start oil viscosity limits torque; validate -40°C. Hollow rotor balancing at high rpm needs added grade.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Direct-oil stator end-winding spray and hollow-shaft rotor cooling are established practice in high-power-density BEV traction motors; the reduced conduction-resistance mechanism is proven without naming a specific programme.
ideaData.materialGrade: Low-viscosity ~4-5 cSt @100°C GTL Group-III e-transmission fluid; Class H (180°C) winding insulation

ideaData.title: Cast-in HV busbar terminals delete inverter-to-motor 3-phase cable
ideaData.technicalDescription: Baseline integrated EDU still routes inverter output to the motor via three shielded/insulated phase cables with ring-lug terminals, two bolted terminal blocks and a shielded connector — copper, crimps, torque stations and an HV isolation test at the joint. Proposal: with motor and inverter sharing one housing, replace the cable with three rigid stamped C11000 (ETP copper, ~2-3 mm thick) busbars, insulation-overmoulded in PPS-GF40 or PA66-GF30, laser-welded directly to the stator hairpin phase leads on one side and to the power-module AC terminals on the other. With fixed relative position inside the monobloc the phase path is a deterministic short rigid link, so flexible shielded cable (needed only to absorb relative motion and EMI over distance) is unnecessary; laser-welded copper-to-copper joints have lower resistance and no crimp-relaxation warranty mode.
ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Deletes 3 phase cables, 6 ring lugs, 2 terminal blocks, shielded connector and 6 torque operations; adds a busbar overmould part and a laser-weld cell (3 welds ×2 ends). Removes one HV joint isolation test point. Net assembly time down.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Removes shielded phase cable, lugs, terminal blocks and crimp/torque labour; lower joint resistance improves efficiency and deletes a crimp-relaxation warranty path.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~€22 cable+lugs+blocks+labour baseline × ~85% delta × 250,000 ≈ €4.7M plus warranty avoidance

ideaData.riskNotes: Rigid busbars must accommodate thermal growth — design expansion loops to avoid stress on hairpin welds. Laser-weld porosity raises phase resistance/hot spot; monitor with in-process weld penetration sensing and DC resistance check. EMI now managed by housing shielding — validate conducted emissions without cable shield.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Laser-welded busbar phase connection between integrated inverter and motor is established practice in current integrated EDUs; the deterministic rigid-link mechanism is proven without naming a specific programme.
ideaData.materialGrade: C11000 ETP copper busbar; PPS-GF40 or PA66-GF30 overmould insulation

Baseline EDU carries a motor rotor-position resolver (or eddy-current sensor) plus separate gearbox/output speed sensors (VR or Hall targets on the diff and intermediate shaft) with their own harness runs and connectors. Proposal: derive output and intermediate speeds algorithmically from the high-resolution rotor-position signal and the fixed, known gear ratios, deleting the discrete gear speed sensors and their targets; retain one wheel-speed reference from ABS for arbitration. ideaData.title: Shared position sensor: one resolver serves motor and gear speed
ideaData.technicalDescription: Baseline EDU carries a motor rotor-position resolver (or eddy-current sensor) plus separate gearbox/output speed sensors (VR or Hall targets on the diff and intermediate shaft) with their own harness runs and connectors. Proposal: derive output and intermediate speeds algorithmically from the high-resolution rotor-position signal and the fixed, known gear ratios, deleting the discrete gear speed sensors and their targets; retain one wheel-speed reference from ABS for arbitration. In a rigid single-speed BEV train with no clutch slip, output speed = rotor speed ÷ ratio exactly, so an independent gear sensor is redundant. The rotor sensor's ~12-14 bit resolution already exceeds gear-sensor accuracy. A software observer flags a fault if ABS-derived and computed speed diverge beyond a slip threshold, meeting ISO 26262 monitoring intent.
ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Deletes 2-3 speed sensors, their machined/pressed target rings, mounting bores, connectors and harness stubs. Adds only software (observer + diagnostic). One fewer sensor calibration step at EOL. Reduces casting complexity by removing sensor mounting bosses.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Removes discrete speed sensors, target rings, connectors and harness stubs plus their EOL calibration and field warranty, replacing them with software.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~€14/unit (2-3 sensors+targets+connectors+labour) × 250,000 ≈ €3.5M plus warranty avoidance

ideaData.riskNotes: Functional-safety: gear speed is used in safety functions (park, regen limits) — the software observer must meet ASIL requirement with ABS cross-check as the diverse channel. Backlash/wind-up introduces transient error; validate against ISO 26262 to justify sensor deletion. Not applicable to multi-speed/clutched EDUs.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Model-based speed estimation from rotor position with ABS/wheel-speed arbitration is established practice in single-speed BEV drive controls; the mechanism is proven without naming a specific programme.

Delete the intermediate spline and one bearing. ideaData.title: Bearing-count reduction via shared shaft between motor and gear
ideaData.technicalDescription: Baseline coaxial/offset EDU supports the rotor on 2 bearings and the gearbox input pinion on a further 2, with a splined coupling between — 4 bearings, one spline, and two bores requiring co-alignment. Proposal: make rotor shaft and reduction-gear input pinion one piece (16MnCr5 / 20MnCr5 case-carburised, or an FSW-joined blank) carried on 3 bearings: one deep-groove ball (e.g. 6208-class) at the non-drive end and a tapered/angular-contact pair (e.g. 7207-class, 25-40° contact) straddling the pinion to react gear separating loads. Delete the intermediate spline and one bearing. Eliminating the spline removes a backlash/NVH source and a fretting-wear warranty path; a straddle-mounted pinion cuts overhung moment, allowing smaller-section bearings for equal L10. Requires the single monobloc datum so pinion and rotor share concentricity.
ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Deletes 1 bearing, 1 machined spline pair and one coupling assembly step; consolidates two bore-machining programs into one shaft. Adds a longer shaft blank (heat-treat and grind length up). One-piece shaft simplifies rotor-to-gear stack-up and balancing.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Removes one bearing, a spline coupling and an assembly/backlash-set step; smaller bearings from reduced overhang and deletes spline fretting warranty.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~€18 bearing+spline+coupling labour baseline − ~€3 longer shaft cost = ~€15 net × 250,000 ≈ €3.75M plus warranty

ideaData.riskNotes: Combined shaft couples rotor imbalance into gear mesh — tighten balance grade and validate NVH order content. Bearing preload across the straddle pair must hold over thermal range; use selective-fit or set-right preload. Depends on single-housing concentricity; verify with combined shaft/housing thermal FEA before deleting the spline compliance.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: One-piece rotor/pinion shafts with a straddle-mounted pinion are established practice in compact coaxial e-axles; the reduced-overhung-moment and deleted-spline mechanism is proven without naming a specific programme.
ideaData.materialGrade: 16MnCr5 / 20MnCr5 case-carburised shaft; angular-contact and deep-groove ball bearings (7207/6208 class)

title: Ferrite-assisted lower-grade magnet rotor at fixed EDU envelope
description: Cuts the most price-volatile EDU material — heavy-rare-earth magnet content — at a fixed envelope, hedging Dy/Tb price and reducing magnet mass. Baseline traction rotor uses sintered NdFeB N42UH/N45UH with ~1.0-1.5% Dy/Tb heavy-rare-earth for 150°C coercivity — the most volatile-cost EDU item. Proposal, at the same housing/stack envelope: switch to a spoke-type (flux-concentrating) IPM lamination that lets a lower-grade, low/zero-HRE magnet (N38UH, a grain-boundary-diffusion Dy-lean grade, or a hybrid NdFeB+ferrite Y30H-2 spoke) reach equal airgap flux by geometry rather than energy product. Spoke geometry concentrates flux from a larger magnet area into a narrow airgap face, dropping remanence requirement; demagnetisation resistance comes from the low permeance coefficient plus direct-oil cooling holding magnet temperature lower. Lamination die changes; stack length and bore unchanged s

ideaData.title: Ferrite-assisted lower-grade magnet rotor at fixed EDU envelope
ideaData.technicalDescription: Baseline traction rotor uses sintered NdFeB N42UH/N45UH with ~1.0-1.5% Dy/Tb heavy-rare-earth for 150°C coercivity — the most volatile-cost EDU item. Proposal, at the same housing/stack envelope: switch to a spoke-type (flux-concentrating) IPM lamination that lets a lower-grade, low/zero-HRE magnet (N38UH, a grain-boundary-diffusion Dy-lean grade, or a hybrid NdFeB+ferrite Y30H-2 spoke) reach equal airgap flux by geometry rather than energy product. Spoke geometry concentrates flux from a larger magnet area into a narrow airgap face, dropping remanence requirement; demagnetisation resistance comes from the low permeance coefficient plus direct-oil cooling holding magnet temperature lower. Lamination die changes; stack length and bore unchanged so housing/gear commonisation is preserved. Laminations in M270-35A / M250-35A NGO steel.
ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Changes rotor lamination die geometry and magnet insertion tooling (spoke slots vs. V-slots); magnet piece cost falls with grade. Rotor bridge stresses rise — may need higher-strength steel (e.g. 35H hi-strength) and slightly slower punch. Balancing/retention (end-plates or sleeve) revalidated. Stator, housing, gears unchanged.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Cuts the most price-volatile EDU material — heavy-rare-earth magnet content — at a fixed envelope, hedging Dy/Tb price and reducing magnet mass.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~€90/unit magnet baseline × ~35% grade/HRE cost reduction × 250,000 ≈ €7.9M; higher if HRE prices spike

ideaData.riskNotes: Spoke rotors have higher mechanical bridge stress at max rpm — validate burst margin, possibly add a retaining sleeve. Cogging/torque-ripple profile changes; retune control and check NVH orders. HRE reduction narrows thermal margin — must be paired with confirmed cooling. Supply-qualify the lower-HRE magnet source for coercivity stability.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Spoke-type flux-concentrating IPM rotors that reduce heavy-rare-earth content are established practice; the geometry-over-energy-product mechanism is proven without naming a specific programme.
ideaData.materialGrade: Spoke magnets N38UH or GBD Dy-lean NdFeB / hybrid ferrite Y30H-2; M270-35A NGO laminations; replaces N42UH/N45UH

title: Pressure-die-cast structural housing doubles as inverter EMC enclosure
description: Removes an entire shield sub-assembly and its fastening/grounding content while merging shield and heatsink functions. Baseline EDU carries a discrete stamped-steel or die-cast inverter lid plus a separate motor housing, each independently qualified for EMC, requiring conductive gaskets, 30-40 M6 fasteners and a machined mating flange. Proposal: cast the inverter cavity walls integrally into the AlSi10MnMg (EN AC-43500) HPDC EDU housing so the power-electronics cavity is a 5-sided Faraday enclosure with only a single flat lid interface. Wall 3.5-4.0 mm to give >60 dB attenuation to 1 GHz; the lid seals via a machined 0.05 mm-flatness land with a single form-in-place conductive gasket bead (Ni/graphite-filled silicone). Cast-in cooling ribs beneath the power-module footprint make the same wall both shield and heatsink, exploiting Al conductivity ~140 W/mK. Deletes the steel shield box, it

ideaData.title: Pressure-die-cast structural housing doubles as inverter EMC enclosure
ideaData.technicalDescription: Baseline EDU carries a discrete stamped-steel or die-cast inverter lid plus a separate motor housing, each independently qualified for EMC, requiring conductive gaskets, 30-40 M6 fasteners and a machined mating flange. Proposal: cast the inverter cavity walls integrally into the AlSi10MnMg (EN AC-43500) HPDC EDU housing so the power-electronics cavity is a 5-sided Faraday enclosure with only a single flat lid interface. Wall 3.5-4.0 mm to give >60 dB attenuation to 1 GHz; the lid seals via a machined 0.05 mm-flatness land with a single form-in-place conductive gasket bead (Ni/graphite-filled silicone). Cast-in cooling ribs beneath the power-module footprint make the same wall both shield and heatsink, exploiting Al conductivity ~140 W/mK. Deletes the steel shield box, its fasteners, and inter-housing shield-continuity ground straps.
ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Adds one machining op for the 0.05 mm lid land and cavity datum; deletes the steel-box stamping die, a spot-weld cell and a fastener station. One cavity added to the existing HPDC tool raises die cost ~8% but removes a full sub-supplier BOM line. Cycle time neutral; scrap risk at thin shield walls managed by vacuum-assist die casting.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Removes an entire shield sub-assembly and its fastening/grounding content while merging shield and heatsink functions.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~€18 saved BOM+labour (steel box €9, 35 fasteners €3.5, gaskets/straps €2.5, assembly €3) × 200,000 = €3.6M, net of ~€0.4M/yr amortised die uplift

ideaData.riskNotes: Porosity in 3.5 mm shield walls can create EMC leakage paths and pressure-tightness failures at the cooling ribs — mitigate with vacuum HPDC and CT sampling per lot. Requires full radiated-emission re-qual (CISPR 25) and lid-gasket compression-set validation over -40/+150°C. Galvanic corrosion at Al-lid interface addressed with chromate-free passivation.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Integrated cast aluminium enclosures serving as both EMC shield and heatsink are established practice in automotive power-electronics packaging; the dual-function-wall mechanism is proven without naming a specific programme.
ideaData.materialGrade: HPDC AlSi10MnMg (EN AC-43500); Ni/graphite-filled silicone form-in-place EMC gasket

title: Common EDU-to-subframe mounting interface across 3 power classes
description: Collapses three subframe/bracket families into one and enables mixed-model vehicle assembly. Baseline EDUs at 150/250/350 kW each use bespoke cast mounting bosses, bushings and torque-roll-restrictor geometry tuned to mass and torque, forcing three subframe cradles and three hydro-mount sets. Proposal: standardise a single 3-point mount pattern (two upper elastomer isolators + one lower torque-roll restrictor) with common bolt PCD, common M12-10.9 fasteners and common cast boss geometry cast into every AlSi10MnMg (EN AC-43500) housing variant. Power-class differences in reaction torque (up to ~4200 Nm peak driveline reaction on the 350 kW) are absorbed by swapping only elastomer durometer (55/65/75 Shore A natural-rubber/hydromount) and the restrictor bushing, not the metal interface. One aluminium subframe cradle and one mount bracket set then serve all three, enabling mixed power class

ideaData.title: Common EDU-to-subframe mounting interface across 3 power classes
ideaData.technicalDescription: Baseline EDUs at 150/250/350 kW each use bespoke cast mounting bosses, bushings and torque-roll-restrictor geometry tuned to mass and torque, forcing three subframe cradles and three hydro-mount sets. Proposal: standardise a single 3-point mount pattern (two upper elastomer isolators + one lower torque-roll restrictor) with common bolt PCD, common M12-10.9 fasteners and common cast boss geometry cast into every AlSi10MnMg (EN AC-43500) housing variant. Power-class differences in reaction torque (up to ~4200 Nm peak driveline reaction on the 350 kW) are absorbed by swapping only elastomer durometer (55/65/75 Shore A natural-rubber/hydromount) and the restrictor bushing, not the metal interface. One aluminium subframe cradle and one mount bracket set then serve all three, enabling mixed power classes down one line without station re-tooling.
ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Consolidates three cast boss patterns to one shared core in the HPDC tool family; deletes two subframe cradle part numbers and two bracket stampings. Vehicle assembly line runs single fixture/nutrunner program across variants. Elastomer variants handled by point-of-fit kanban, no station change.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Collapses three subframe/bracket families into one and enables mixed-model vehicle assembly.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: Tooling avoidance for 2 deleted cradles+brackets (~€1.6M amortised) + ~€12/unit part/logistics saving × ~180,000 combined units = €2.16M/yr recurring plus tooling

ideaData.riskNotes: Common interface must be sized for the 350 kW worst-case load, adding ~0.4 kg of boss mass on lower-power variants. NVH tuning per class relies entirely on durometer/bushing — requires full road-load-data mount-motion and idle-shake validation per variant. Fastener joint-slip and fretting at shared boss validated by torque-to-yield and vibration endurance.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Common mount interface across power variants with durometer-only tuning is established DFMA commonisation practice; the invariant-metal-interface mechanism is proven without naming a specific programme.
ideaData.materialGrade: Cast bosses in AlSi10MnMg (EN AC-43500); 55/65/75 Shore A natural-rubber isolators; M12-10.9 fasteners

title: Fill-for-life gearbox oil shared as inverter/motor coolant
description: Eliminates an entire coolant subsystem and one EOL fill process by unifying to one dielectric fluid. Baseline three-in-one EDUs often run two fluids: a water-glycol loop for inverter and stator jacket plus an ATF-type gear oil (low-viscosity 4-5 cSt e-fluid) for gears and bearings, requiring a chiller-side heat exchanger, two fill ports, two seal regimes and an expansion bottle. Proposal: adopt a single dielectric low-viscosity gear-and-power fluid (GTL Group-III base, ~4 cSt @100°C, dielectric strength >30 kV/mm, e.g. a dedicated e-transmission fluid) circulated by the existing mechanical/electric oil pump to lubricate gears, spray-cool the end-windings (Class H insulation), and flow through a cold-plate under the power module. ideaData.title: Fill-for-life gearbox oil shared as inverter/motor coolant
ideaData.technicalDescription: Baseline three-in-one EDUs often run two fluids: a water-glycol loop for inverter and stator jacket plus an ATF-type gear oil (low-viscosity 4-5 cSt e-fluid) for gears and bearings, requiring a chiller-side heat exchanger, two fill ports, two seal regimes and an expansion bottle. Proposal: adopt a single dielectric low-viscosity gear-and-power fluid (GTL Group-III base, ~4 cSt @100°C, dielectric strength >30 kV/mm, e.g. a dedicated e-transmission fluid) circulated by the existing mechanical/electric oil pump to lubricate gears, spray-cool the end-windings (Class H insulation), and flow through a cold-plate under the power module. Deletes the entire water-glycol circuit: jacket, pump, hoses, expansion tank and the water-side of the exchanger. Oil's dielectric property allows direct contact with live windings and busbars, and its higher usable ΔT (oil to 150°C vs coolant ~65°C) cuts required flow for equal heat rejection.
ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Deletes coolant-jacket core from the casting, the water pump, ~4 coolant hose joints, expansion bottle and one fill/vac-fill station. Adds an oil-side cold-plate under the inverter and slightly upsizes the oil pump. Net EOL fill process simplifies from two fluids to one — one vacuum-fill station removed.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Eliminates an entire coolant subsystem and one EOL fill process by unifying to one dielectric fluid.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~€20/unit removed content (water pump €7, hoses/bottle €5, jacket machining €3, fill-station labour+consumables €5) × 200,000 = €4.0M/yr

ideaData.riskNotes: Oil thermal conductivity is lower than glycol, so power-module junction temps must be validated at peak and fast-charge-analogue duty; may cap continuous power vs dual-fluid. Dielectric fluid ageing, copper compatibility and oxidation over 15-year life require accelerated bench validation. Seal swell with the single fluid checked across all elastomers.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Single-fluid oil-cooled EDUs that share gear oil as motor/inverter coolant are an established emerging practice; the dielectric-direct-contact and higher-ΔT mechanism is proven without naming a specific programme.
ideaData.materialGrade: GTL Group-III dielectric e-fluid, ~4 cSt @100°C, >30 kV/mm; Class H (180°C) winding insulation

title: Press-fit self-clinch inverter busbars delete laser-weld station
description: Deletes a capital-intensive weld cell and enables reworkable, 100%-verified interconnects on a high-value assembly. Baseline inverter-to-motor 3-phase and DC-link joints are laser/ultrasonic-welded C11000 ETP copper busbars needing a weld cell, weld-vision inspection and destructive pull-test sampling. Proposal: replace welds with eye-of-the-needle compliant press-fit pins into busbars stamped from C11000 (or high-conductivity CuSn0.15) and plated 3-5 µm matte Sn over 1-2 µm Ni barrier, pressed into PTH power boards; phase output uses M6 captive self-clinch studs (A2-70 stainless) pressed into the busbar. Controlled plastic deformation into a 100-150 µm interference hole forms a gas-tight cold weld, >200 A continuous at <50 µΩ contact resistance. Deletes the laser-weld cell and inspection loop; a single press with force-vs-displacement signature gives 100% verification.

ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Removes laser-weld cell (high capex), weld-vision inspection and pull-test lab load. Adds a servo-press station with force-displacement SPC. Hole tolerance on busbar and board tightened to ±25 µm — one added CNC/etch control. Rework becomes possible (welds are not reworkable), cutting scrap of high-value assembled inverters.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Deletes a capital-intensive weld cell and enables reworkable, 100%-verified interconnects on a high-value assembly.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~€6/unit process+inspection saving × 200,000 = €1.2M/yr plus ~€1.5M/yr scrap-recovery on reworkable joints and ~€2M weld-cell capex avoidance

ideaData.riskNotes: Compliant-pin current-cycling and thermal-cycling can relax contact force over life; validate contact resistance stability over 1000 thermal cycles and vibration per LV124. ideaData.benchmarkReference: Compliant press-fit power interconnect is established practice in automotive power electronics packaging; no specific programme named.
ideaData.materialGrade: Busbar C11000 ETP copper (or CuSn0.15); plating 3-5 µm Sn over 1-2 µm Ni; self-clinch studs A2-70 stainless; 100-150 µm press-fit interference

Any sub-component defect appears as a distinct order in the combined spectrum, so one station replaces mechanical-gauge and acoustic gates and validates the electrical build. ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Deletes in-line composite gear gauge station(s) and standalone acoustic booth; adds one instrumented spin-test cell (which many lines already have as functional EOL). Reduces station count and floor space; cycle time absorbed into existing EOL functional test. Enables per-unit digital NVH passport for traceability.

costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~€5/unit inspection labour+gauge maintenance saving × 200,000 = €1.0M/yr plus ~€1M/yr warranty reduction from better field-correlated screening

ideaData.riskNotes: System-level test may mask a marginal component that only fails under field thermal/load extremes — mitigate by correlation study establishing order-limit thresholds against known-bad parts and periodic component audit. Test-rig repeatability (GR&R) and background-noise floor must be controlled; requires golden-unit calibration.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: System-level EOL NVH order-tracking plus current-signature testing is established practice in e-drive manufacturing; no specific programme named.

title: Modular power-electronics deck bolts onto common motor-gearbox core
description: Decouples semiconductor upgrades from motor/gearbox tooling, avoiding a full re-industrialisation per silicon generation. Baseline integrated EDUs cast the inverter cavity into the housing, meaning every power-class or silicon change (Si IGBT vs SiC MOSFET, 400V vs 800V) forces a new housing casting and full EDU re-industrialisation. Proposal: define the motor+gearbox as a common mechanical core with a standardised flat machined interface deck carrying the cast-in 3-phase terminals, coolant/oil ports, and a fixed bolt PCD; the inverter becomes a self-contained bolt-on module family sharing that deck. A 400V/Si, an 800V/SiC and a high-power SiC inverter all mount to the identical core. This decouples the fast-moving semiconductor roadmap from the slow-moving, capital-heavy motor/gearbox tooling, so silicon upgrades reuse the same casting, stator winding lines and gear machining. ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Motor/gearbox core casting and machining lines run one high-volume variant regardless of inverter generation, maximising die and line amortisation. Inverter built on a separate flexible cell that can change without touching the mechanical plant. Adds a machined deck and one sealed interface; removes need for new housing tooling per silicon change.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Decouples semiconductor upgrades from motor/gearbox tooling, avoiding a full re-industrialisation per silicon generation.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: Housing die + machining line re-tool per generation ~€6M avoided; over a 3-generation SiC transition and ~200k units/yr the shared core amortises core tooling ~2× longer

ideaData.riskNotes: External deck interface adds a sealing joint and ~2-3 cm of busbar length (small inductance/EMC penalty) versus fully cast-in — validate DC-link ripple and radiated emissions. Interface must be dimensioned for the highest-power/thermal case. Deck sealing over life validated to IP6K9K; thermal interface between inverter cold-plate and deck controlled by TIM spec.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Modular inverter-on-common-drive architecture is established platform practice; no specific programme named.

title: Cast-in mechatronic connector shelf deletes internal LV harness
description: Replaces a hand-routed internal loom with one automated rigid-carrier operation, removing chafe warranty modes. Baseline EDUs route a discrete internal LV harness linking resolver, oil/coolant temp sensors, park-lock actuator and inverter gate-driver, with clipped looms, wall grommets and multiple bulkhead connectors — high labour and a chafe-point warranty source. ideaData.technicalDescription: Baseline EDUs route a discrete internal LV harness linking resolver, oil/coolant temp sensors, park-lock actuator and inverter gate-driver, with clipped looms, wall grommets and multiple bulkhead connectors — high labour and a chafe-point warranty source. Cast channels add minor core complexity to existing HPDC tool. Bulkhead reduced to a single sealed header. Removes several piece-part harness numbers from BOM.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Replaces a hand-routed internal loom with one automated rigid-carrier operation, removing chafe warranty modes.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~€12/unit (harness piece €5, assembly labour €5, warranty allowance €2) × 200,000 = €2.4M/yr net of carrier piece-cost uplift

ideaData.riskNotes: Rigid carrier tolerances must accommodate housing casting variation and thermal expansion mismatch (Al vs PPS) — provide compliant press-fit and slotted retention. Vibration durability of press-fit signal terminals validated per LV124/LV148. Sealing of single bulkhead header to IP6K9K; sensor-signal integrity (resolver) checked for EMC crosstalk on the rigid carrier.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Insert-moulded rigid signal carriers replacing internal looms are established practice in mechatronic modules; no specific programme named.
ideaData.materialGrade: Housing AlSi10MnMg-T7; carrier 40% glass-filled PPS insert-moulded; leadframe C19400 or CuSn0.15 with Sn-plated press-fit terminals

title: Hairpin stator with laser-welded crown replacing round-wire pull-in
timeToImplement: 24-30 months incl. line install and efficiency-map validation
description: Copper mass and direct labour reduction dominate; scrap and floor space secondary. Baseline is a random-wound distributed stator on M270-35A 0.35 mm laminations, needle-wound round Cu magnet wire at ~42% slot fill, with long end-turns and trickle varnish impregnation. Proposal: rectangular flat-wire hairpin winding (2.5×4.0 mm C11000 Cu, grade 220 polyamide-imide base + amide-imide topcoat, ~180-200 µm build) formed on a bending station, inserted, twisted and crown-welded (single-mode fibre laser, ~1 kW, remote scanner, ~0.3 s/joint). Slot fill rises to ~68-73%, raising torque density and cutting active copper mass per Nm; shorter, repeatable end-turns cut Cu length ~10-15%. Higher fill lowers DC resistance so I²R loss falls at equal torque, letting the design shed active length. Automated welding removes the insert/lace labour. Slot fill rises to ~68-73%, raising torque density and cutting active copper mass per Nm; shorter, repeatable end-turns cut Cu length ~10-15%. ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Adds hairpin forming, insertion, twisting and laser-weld cells (~4 stations, laser capex ~€0.6-0.9M) but deletes needle-winder, lacing and trickle-varnish lines. Cycle time drops to ~stator/25-35s. Scrap shifts to weld-joint rework; inline weld-vision inspection required. Net floor space and direct-labour reduction.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Copper mass and direct labour reduction dominate; scrap and floor space secondary.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~€30/motor Cu saving + ~€10/motor labour × 200k; baseline stator ~€260

ideaData.riskNotes: AC/proximity losses rise at high electrical frequency — mitigate with continuous transposition or conductor segmentation and validate efficiency map at 15-20k rpm. Weld porosity risks open circuit; require 100% thermographic or resistance testing. Slot-liner and enamel scuffing on insertion needs tooling radius validation and IEC 60034-18 partial-discharge screening.
ideaData.timeToImplement: 24-30 months incl. line install and efficiency-map validation
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Hairpin (bar-wound) traction stators are widely productionised (GM Chevrolet Bolt EUV/Ultium, VW MEB APP310, Toyota hybrid transaxles), c.2016-2021.
ideaData.materialGrade: Laminations M270-35A 0.35 mm; hairpin 2.5×4.0 mm C11000 copper, grade 220 PAI+AI enamel ~180-200 µm build; fibre-laser crown weld ~1 kW

title: Grain-oriented backiron / non-oriented teeth bi-metal stator lamination
timeToImplement: 28-36 months incl. loss-map and NVH validation
description: Iron mass and copper length reduction from thinner high-permeability yoke. Baseline stator core is single non-oriented steel (M270-35A) uniform through yoke and teeth. Yoke flux is largely circumferential and unidirectional per pole while teeth carry radial flux — a mismatch NO steel serves inefficiently. Proposal: split into a segmented core where the yoke ring uses grain-oriented steel (GOES, e.g. 27ZH100, 0.27 mm) with rolling direction aligned circumferentially, and tooth segments stay NO (M235-35A, 0.35 mm). GOES core loss is ~30-40% lower along the rolling direction. Aligning the GOES easy-axis with dominant yoke flux cuts hysteresis+eddy loss in the backiron, permitting thinner yoke or reduced active length at equal loss budget — trimming iron mass and copper end-turn length. ideaData.title: Grain-oriented backiron / non-oriented teeth bi-metal stator lamination
ideaData.technicalDescription: Baseline stator core is single non-oriented steel (M270-35A) uniform through yoke and teeth. Yoke flux is largely circumferential and unidirectional per pole while teeth carry radial flux — a mismatch NO steel serves inefficiently. Proposal: split into a segmented core where the yoke ring uses grain-oriented steel (GOES, e.g. 27ZH100, 0.27 mm) with rolling direction aligned circumferentially, and tooth segments stay NO (M235-35A, 0.35 mm). GOES core loss is ~30-40% lower along the rolling direction. Aligning the GOES easy-axis with dominant yoke flux cuts hysteresis+eddy loss in the backiron, permitting thinner yoke or reduced active length at equal loss budget — trimming iron mass and copper end-turn length. Executed via segmented-pole joint-lap construction with interlocked tooth-yoke interfaces and backlack bonding.
ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Requires segmented-lamination stamping (two coil feeds/grades) and yoke-ring assembly fixturing; adds a joining/back-ring press station. Progressive-die tooling for segments (~€0.4M). Enables narrower yoke reducing blank OD and improving sheet nesting utilisation, lowering scrap skeleton.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Iron mass and copper length reduction from thinner high-permeability yoke.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~€12-16/motor core+Cu saving × 200k; baseline core ~€150

ideaData.riskNotes: Segment joints add reluctance and localised loss; NVH from segmentation must be validated. GOES is brittle and directional — burr and stress-relief anneal control critical. Validate loss model on dyno across full operating map; risk of flux crowding at tooth-yoke interface needing FEA-driven joint geometry.
dfmaPrinciples: Match material property to load direction
ideaData.timeToImplement: 28-36 months incl. loss-map and NVH validation
ideaData.benchmarkReference: GOES-backiron / NO-teeth bi-material cores are documented in traction-motor R&D; the loss-directionality mechanism is established, not tied to a named programme.
ideaData.materialGrade: Yoke GOES 27ZH100 0.27 mm (rolling direction circumferential); teeth M235-35A 0.35 mm non-oriented

title: Ferrite-assisted synchronous reluctance rotor deleting heavy-rare-earth
timeToImplement: 30-40 months incl. overspeed and demag validation
description: Elimination of heavy-rare-earth NdFeB is the dominant lever; reduces supply-chain price risk. Baseline interior-PM rotor uses sintered NdFeB with Dy/Tb (N42SH/N45UH grades) for high-temp demag resistance — the single largest EDU material cost and price-volatile. Proposal: convert to a ferrite-assisted synchronous reluctance (PM-assisted SynRM) rotor using sintered strontium ferrite blocks (Y30BH, Br ~0.40-0.43 T) inserted into 3-4 multi-barrier flux paths in an M270-35A (0.35 mm) rotor lamination. Reluctance torque from the d/q inductance saliency ratio provides the bulk of output; ferrite adds power factor and field-weakening without heavy-rare-earth. Magnet cost collapses ~90% (ferrite ~€3-5/kg vs NdFeB ~€60-90/kg); ferrite fill lifts PF from ~0.7 to ~0.85. Multi-barrier lamination geometry is the design lever. Best fit for city/urban BEV duty cycles tolerant of ~5-8% lower peak torque

Lamination stamping tool more complex (thin ribs). Balances rotor mechanically; no magnet corrosion coating needed.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Elimination of heavy-rare-earth NdFeB is the dominant lever; reduces supply-chain price risk.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~€55-75/motor magnet cost avoided × 200k; baseline magnet content ~€80-100

ideaData.riskNotes: Thin inter-barrier ribs limit max rpm (centrifugal stress) — validate burst at 1.2× overspeed on 34CrNiMo6 or high-strength lamination steel. Torque ripple and NVH higher than IPM; needs skew/notch optimisation. Ferrite irreversible demag at low temperature — validate cold-crank demag margin at -40°C.
dfmaPrinciples: Exploit geometry (saliency) over material for function
ideaData.timeToImplement: 30-40 months incl. overspeed and demag validation
ideaData.benchmarkReference: PM-assisted SynRM with ferrite is established practice in industrial drives (e.g. ABB SynRM) and traction demonstrators; mechanism proven, not a named vehicle programme.
ideaData.materialGrade: Ferrite Y30BH (Br ~0.40-0.43 T); rotor lamination M270-35A 0.35 mm; 3-4 flux barriers; replaces N42SH/N45UH NdFeB

description: Eliminates a full cooling circuit, casting cores and seal sets; enables copper reduction. Enamel and slot-liner ATF-compatibility and hydrolysis over life require IEC 60034-18 PD plus oil-aging validation. Oil filtration and aeration control critical; validate hotspot at max continuous power and hill-hold. Bearing lube interaction to be verified.

Move cooling to the heat source
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Direct oil end-winding spray cooling sharing the gearbox circuit is established practice in current BEV e-axles across multiple OEM/Tier-1s; no specific programme named.
ideaData.materialGrade: Dielectric e-fluid ~5-8 cSt at 100°C (GTL/PAO ATF); slot liner Nomex 410 aramid or PEN film; oil-resistant PAI enamel

title: Aluminium die-cast rotor cage induction machine as low-cost variant
description: Complete magnet-cost elimination on the secondary-axle variant; drag-loss benefit when disconnected. Baseline dual-motor AWD secondary axle reuses a PM synchronous machine, carrying full NdFeB cost on an axle disconnected/low-duty much of the time. Proposal: for the secondary axle, substitute an induction machine (ACIM) rotor — pressure die-cast aluminium (EN AC-44300 / near-eutectic Al-Si) or die-cast copper (C11000) squirrel cage in an M330-50A (0.5 mm) rotor lamination stack — deleting all magnet content. Torque comes from induced rotor currents, so zero permanent magnets; drag losses are ~nil when de-energised, ideal for a disconnect/coasting axle, unlike a PM machine that spins with back-EMF and iron drag. Die-cast aluminium cage (~€2/kg) replaces ~€80-100 of NdFeB. Slightly lower cruise efficiency is acceptable because the axle serves mainly launch/AWD traction bursts.

title: Segmented bonded stator core replacing single-piece punch stack
description: Steel scrap yield jump plus copper reduction from higher slot fill Baseline stator core is a single annular stack of M250-35A (0.35 mm) non-oriented steel, blanked as full rings with ~38% web scrap and stacked with interlock cleats, giving ~55% slot fill after round-wire insertion. Proposal: convert to individually blanked T-segments (yoke+tooth) nested on the strip, cutting steel scrap from ~38% to ~12% via tessellation. Segments are pre-wound off-tool at open geometry (needle-winder achieves 68-72% fill), then closed into a ring and joined by self-bonding backlack (Voestalpine isovac backlack epoxy-phenolic coating, cured ~180°C under press) instead of welding or interlock, eliminating shorting bridges that raise iron loss. Higher fill lets conductor cross-section drop ~8% at equal I²R. Backlack bond also damps magnetostrictive whine.

title: Hybrid Cu-clad-Al laminated busbar via roll bonding
description: Cuts the dominant copper mass while preserving weldable/platable copper interfaces. Baseline main HV busbar is solid C11000 ETP copper, 2.5mm, stamped and matte-tin plated (2-4µm over 1µm Ni), carrying ~300A continuous in the BDU. Proposal: roll-bonded Cu-clad-Al laminate — EN AW-1050A (min 99.5% Al, ~2.8µΩ·cm) core with C11000 cladding at 17.5% thickness per face, total ~3.2mm to hold equivalent DC ampacity. At DC/low-ripple HV, skin effect is negligible, so copper faces carry the welded/plated contact interface while the Al core carries bulk current. Mill roll-bonding gives a metallurgical Cu/Al bond (>50 N/mm peel) with no internal galvanic crevice. Density falls 8.9→3.6 g/cm³; cost per equivalent-conductance metre drops ~40%. Terminal pads use locally increased clad thickness so ultrasonic/laser welding and bolted M8 lugs behave as today.

ideaData.materialGrade: Core EN AW-1050A-H14; cladding C11000 ETP Cu at ~17.5% t/face; matte Sn 2-4µm over 1µm Ni on pads

description: Eliminates fasteners, clips and manual assembly while fixing creepage tolerances. Baseline HV distribution subassembly uses discrete stamped C11000 busbars (2.0-2.5mm) clipped into a PA66-GF30 carrier then screwed — two parts, tolerance stack on creepage/clearance, manual assembly. Proposal: insert-mould pre-formed C11000 busbars directly into a PA66-GF35 carrier (or PPA-GF such as Zytel HTN/Amodel for >150°C class-H hotspots) so the polymer forms integral 3-4mm dielectric partition walls between phases and self-locates conductors. description: Direct cooling shrinks conductor cross-section and deletes spreader/TIM. title: Two-shot MID moulded HVIL/signal routing replacing discrete low-voltage harness
description: Eliminates the LV sub-harness, connectors and manual routing on the subassembly. Baseline distribution subassembly carries its LV nervous system — HVIL loop, contactor coil feed, pre-charge, temperature sensor wiring — as a discrete sub-harness with connectors, tape and clips routed over the HV housing. Proposal: use LDS (laser direct structuring) MID: mould the housing in an LDS-grade PA (e.g. Vectra/LCP or PA6-GF with LPKF-LDS additive), laser-activate trace paths, then electroless plate Cu (8-12µm) / Ni (3-6µm) / Au (0.05-0.1µm) to form LV signal and coil-drive circuits directly in the plastic. This deletes the discrete LV harness, connectors, clips and routing labour and integrates a defined-impedance HVIL continuity path with no loose wires to chafe. Higher-current contactor-coil traces are sized in plated thickness or served by hybrid press-fit CuSn6 inserts.

ideaData.title: Two-shot MID moulded HVIL/signal routing replacing discrete low-voltage harness
ideaData.technicalDescription: Baseline distribution subassembly carries its LV nervous system — HVIL loop, contactor coil feed, pre-charge, temperature sensor wiring — as a discrete sub-harness with connectors, tape and clips routed over the HV housing. Proposal: use LDS (laser direct structuring) MID: mould the housing in an LDS-grade PA (e.g. Vectra/LCP or PA6-GF with LPKF-LDS additive), laser-activate trace paths, then electroless plate Cu (8-12µm) / Ni (3-6µm) / Au (0.05-0.1µm) to form LV signal and coil-drive circuits directly in the plastic. This deletes the discrete LV harness, connectors, clips and routing labour and integrates a defined-impedance HVIL continuity path with no loose wires to chafe. Higher-current contactor-coil traces are sized in plated thickness or served by hybrid press-fit CuSn6 inserts.
ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Adds LDS laser-structuring and electroless plating line (or outsourced MID housing); deletes LV harness cut/crimp/assembly and clip stations. Higher housing unit cost offset by harness+connector deletion. Capex significant if in-house plating; feasible via MID supplier.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Eliminates the LV sub-harness, connectors and manual routing on the subassembly.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~€6–10/unit LV harness+connectors+labour removed net of MID housing premium × 150k

ideaData.riskNotes: Risk: plated-trace current/thermal limits and adhesion over thermal cycling; HVIL integrity is safety-relevant. Mitigate by limiting MID to true low-current signals, hybrid inserts for coil current, and validation of trace adhesion (tape/thermal shock) plus HVIL continuity fault detection. Confirm creepage from HV nets.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: LDS-MID is established practice for automotive antennas, sensor carriers and LV interconnect integration; mechanism proven, no specific programme named.
ideaData.materialGrade: LDS-capable resin (LCP or PA6-GF with LDS additive); plating Cu 8-12µm / Ni 3-6µm / Au 0.05-0.1µm; insert pins CuSn6

title: Fine-blanked busbar terminals replacing CNC-milled bolt lands
timeToImplement: 10-14 months incl. tool build and PPAP
description: Eliminates chip-forming machining and its scrap on the highest-value copper part of the pack. Baseline pack-side busbar terminations are CNC-milled from C11000 stock to create flat bolt lands with M8 clearance holes at ±0.05mm flatness, generating 30-40% chips. Proposal: fine-blank the terminal from C11000 half-hard (H02) strip on a triple-action fine-blanking press (impinge/counter/blank in one stroke), holding cut-edge burr <0.03mm and hole roundness IT9 without secondary machining. ideaData.title: Fine-blanked busbar terminals replacing CNC-milled bolt lands
ideaData.technicalDescription: Baseline pack-side busbar terminations are CNC-milled from C11000 stock to create flat bolt lands with M8 clearance holes at ±0.05mm flatness, generating 30-40% chips. Proposal: fine-blank the terminal from C11000 half-hard (H02) strip on a triple-action fine-blanking press (impinge/counter/blank in one stroke), holding cut-edge burr <0.03mm and hole roundness IT9 without secondary machining. Fine-blanking's compressive V-ring shear zone yields a full-thickness smooth cut (>90% sheared vs ~30% conventional), giving a Class-A contact land directly; coining the bolt land in the same tool sets flatness to 0.04mm. Contact resistance depends on real asperity contact area, so the burnished face gives a-spots equivalent to milled surfaces — no CR or thermal penalty at 300A continuous. Copper recovery from optimised strip layout rises above 78%.
ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Deletes 2 CNC mill stations and deburr cell; adds one fine-blank press with progressive tool (~€180k). Cycle time drops from ~90 s milled to ~4 s/stroke. Chip handling eliminated; strip scrap baled for higher-value recovery. Tool maintenance interval every 250k strokes.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Eliminates chip-forming machining and its scrap on the highest-value copper part of the pack.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~€9/pack machining+scrap delta × 120,000, plus copper recovery uplift ~78% vs ~62%

ideaData.riskNotes: Fine-blank die wear can raise burr beyond 0.03 mm, risking terminal seating; mitigate with carbide inserts and inline vision burr check. Coined land flatness must be re-validated to connector spec after 250k cycles. Copper strain-hardening from blanking to be annealed if bend radius <1.5t.
ideaData.timeToImplement: 10-14 months incl. tool build and PPAP
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Fine-blanking of copper current-carrying parts is established practice in switchgear and terminal manufacture; no specific OEM programme named.
ideaData.materialGrade: C11000 ETP copper, half-hard temper (H02), ~2.5mm strip

title: Cold-forged copper busbar bends replacing bent-and-annealed strip
description: Removes anneal steps and cuts copper mass via locally optimised section. Baseline 3D-routed busbars are laser-cut from C11000 flat strip then CNC press-brake bent at multiple stations, each 90° bend needing inter-stage stress-relief anneal (~350°C, recrystallisation range for cold-worked Cu) to prevent outer-fibre edge cracking where tensile strain exceeds ~12% on tight radii. Proposal: net-shape cold-forge the busbar including bends and boss features from OF-copper C10200 (99.95% Cu) slug in a 2-hit closed-die transfer press, forming the bend as controlled grain-flow rather than outer-fibre stretch. Forging maintains material continuity around the bend so no annealing is needed and section is preserved (no thinning that raises local I²R). Integral forged bosses replace welded standoffs. ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Replaces laser-cut + multi-station brake + 2 anneal furnaces with a transfer forging press and trim die. Anneal energy and furnace floor space deleted. Adds forging tooling (~€220k/geometry) so best for high-runner busbars only. Cycle ~6 s.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Removes anneal steps and cuts copper mass via locally optimised section.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~€7/pack copper mass saving + ~€5/pack anneal/handling × 100,000

ideaData.riskNotes: Forging tool cost demands volume >60k/yr to amortise. Grain-flow direction must be validated for fatigue under pack vibration; residual stress mapped by hole-drilling. Cross-section reductions require thermal derating sign-off at 95th-percentile duty cycle.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Cold forging of copper conductors and terminals is established practice in electrical hardware; no specific vehicle programme named.
ideaData.materialGrade: OF-copper C10200 (99.95% Cu, oxygen-free) forging slug

title: Reflowed tin-bismuth busbar-to-fuse joint replacing bolted interface
description: Removes fasteners and torque control while stabilising joint resistance to cut warranty. Baseline midi/HRC fuse is bolted between two copper busbar stubs via M8 studs with torque-to-yield fasteners, Belleville washers, torque verification and a plated bolt-land step; the bolted a-spot interface degrades under thermal cycling as creep relaxes preload, raising warranty resistance. Proposal: form the fuse-to-busbar joint as a reflowed lap using Sn42Bi57Ag1 low-temperature paste (liquidus ~140°C) screen-printed on matte-tin-plated C11000 lands and reflowed in a nitrogen convection oven (peak ~170-180°C), giving a gas-tight metallurgical joint with contact resistance <30µΩ and no preload to relax. Low-melt SnBi keeps peak reflow below the fuse-element anneal temperature, protecting the calibrated M-effect element; the continuous solder fillet gives near-full-area contact versus discrete bolt

ideaData.title: Reflowed tin-bismuth busbar-to-fuse joint replacing bolted interface
ideaData.technicalDescription: Baseline midi/HRC fuse is bolted between two copper busbar stubs via M8 studs with torque-to-yield fasteners, Belleville washers, torque verification and a plated bolt-land step; the bolted a-spot interface degrades under thermal cycling as creep relaxes preload, raising warranty resistance. Proposal: form the fuse-to-busbar joint as a reflowed lap using Sn42Bi57Ag1 low-temperature paste (liquidus ~140°C) screen-printed on matte-tin-plated C11000 lands and reflowed in a nitrogen convection oven (peak ~170-180°C), giving a gas-tight metallurgical joint with contact resistance <30µΩ and no preload to relax. ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Deletes stud-weld/bolt-land plating, fastener kitting, torque station and torque-audit. Adds paste printer + short N2 reflow oven (~€150k). Enables panelised assembly of multiple fuse joints per reflow pass, lifting throughput.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Removes fasteners and torque control while stabilising joint resistance to cut warranty.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~€4.50/pack fastener+torque+plating + ~€2/pack warranty accrual × 130,000

ideaData.riskNotes: SnBi is brittle and creep-sensitive; joint must be mechanically supported so it carries no vibration shear (housing takes load). Bi embrittlement with residual Pb forbidden—Pb-free supply chain mandatory. Reflow profile validated against fuse element to avoid pre-ageing. Field-serviceability of fuse changes to module swap.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Low-temperature SnBi reflow is established in electronics assembly; its application to HV fuse joints uses the same established soldering mechanism, no OEM programme named.
ideaData.materialGrade: Solder Sn42Bi57Ag1 paste (liquidus ~140°C); lands C11000 with matte Sn 3-5µm over Ni; N2 reflow atmosphere

title: Self-pierce-riveted Cu-Al busbar-to-terminal joint
description: Eliminates ultrasonic welding capex/consumables and bimetal transition SKU while avoiding intermetallic failure. Baseline aluminium busbar (EN AW-1350 or 6101) joins to copper connector terminals via ultrasonic welding or bolted bimetal transition plates, both costly: USW needs high-power sonotrodes and joint-quality monitoring, bolted transitions add a clad plate SKU. ideaData.title: Self-pierce-riveted Cu-Al busbar-to-terminal joint
ideaData.technicalDescription: Baseline aluminium busbar (EN AW-1350 or 6101) joins to copper connector terminals via ultrasonic welding or bolted bimetal transition plates, both costly: USW needs high-power sonotrodes and joint-quality monitoring, bolted transitions add a clad plate SKU. Proposal: join Al busbar to Cu terminal using a self-pierce rivet (SPR) of C70600 cupronickel with a conductive Sn-based interface compound, set on a servo-electric C-frame at 40–60 kN. Physics: SPR forms a mechanical interlock without melting, avoiding the brittle CuAl2/Cu9Al4 intermetallics that USW and fusion welding generate at the interface and that raise resistance and crack under thermal cycling. The rivet plus interface compound provides parallel conductive paths; galvanic corrosion is managed by the CuNi rivet's near-neutral potential and sealed compound. Real contact area is set by the swaged flare, giving repeatable <50 µΩ.
ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Replaces USW cell (sonotrode consumables, weld monitor) with a servo SPR gun on the assembly line; die/punch changeover per stack thickness. No shielding gas, no weld spatter. Inline force-displacement curve gives 100% joint proof without destructive pull tests.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Eliminates ultrasonic welding capex/consumables and bimetal transition SKU while avoiding intermetallic failure.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~€6/pack USW consumable+monitor delta + ~€3/pack transition-plate deletion × 110,000

ideaData.riskNotes: SPR pierces the top sheet—current path cross-section locally reduced, needs thermal derating check at rivet. Galvanic couple Al/CuNi must pass salt-spray with sealed compound. Rivet flare consistency across Al temper batches validated. Not suited to very thin (<1 mm) busbar without backing.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: SPR of dissimilar metals is established automotive body-join practice; conductive-joint use is an established mechanical-join mechanism, no HV programme named.

description: Removes potting/cure and swaps copper for finned aluminium at larger but cheaper section. Baseline high-current distribution busbar (>400 A) is a flat C11000 bar over-moulded or potted in thermally conductive epoxy to conduct heat into a cooled housing wall, adding potting material, cure time and mass. costSavingPotential.qualitative: Removes potting/cure and swaps copper for finned aluminium at larger but cheaper section.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~€10/pack Cu→Al material + ~€5/pack potting/cure deletion × 90,000

ideaData.riskNotes: Exposed fins require creepage/clearance and finger-guard compliance—fins must sit inside a touch-safe enclosure. Airflow assumption validated against worst-case sealed-pack thermal; if pack is fully sealed, convection benefit drops and section must grow. Al terminal interfaces need CuAl transition management.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Finned aluminium extrusion for conductor cooling is established in power electronics; no vehicle HV busbar programme named.

Proposal: redesign the outer structural housing as two half-shells in PBT-GF30 (30% glass-filled polybutylene terephthalate, CTI 200-250, HDT ~205C), joined by laser-transmission welding at 940-980 nm: one shell natural/transmitting, the mating shell laser-marking-grade carbon-black-absorbing, welded at ~0.3-0.5 J/mm2 with 2-3 bar clamp and integral snap pre-fixation for weld nesting. ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Deletes screw-drive and epoxy dispense/cure for the outer housing; adds a laser-weld station with clamping fixture (~€130k). Two moulded shells replace machined can + lid. Cycle ~8 s weld vs minutes of epoxy cure. Enables poka-yoke internal component nesting.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Removes fasteners and epoxy from the contactor outer housing via welded moulded shells.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~€5/unit fastener+epoxy+cure delta × 140,000

ideaData.riskNotes: Must prove the outer weld is not part of the HV hermetic barrier—FMEA to confirm capsule-only sealing. GF30 laser weld strength validated for coil short-circuit reaction torque and shock/vibration. Colour/additive package tuned for laser absorption without compromising CTI. Serviceability becomes non-openable (whole-unit replace).
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Laser-transmission welding of glass-filled thermoplastic housings is established practice in automotive sensor and actuator enclosures; no specific contactor programme named.
ideaData.materialGrade: PBT-GF30 (30% glass-filled PBT) shells, laser-marking-grade carbon-black absorbing partner; 96% Al2O3 arc chamber (unchanged)

Contact resistance falls with normal force and fresh-metal wipe; over-centre geometry locks force independent of operator torque, removing torque-audit variability. An integral first-make/last-break HVIL pin on the same lever deletes the separate interlock switch and harness. C17200's high yield keeps wedge force stable over 50+ service cycles.
ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Deletes bolted-contact hardware, torque station and separate HVIL micro-switch/harness; adds a cam-lever assembly (moulded lever + BeCu contacts). Assembly becomes tool-free clip/rotate. Fewer piece parts to kit; contact plating (Ag) on BeCu only where it mates.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Consolidates contacts, fasteners and interlock switch into one tool-free lever mechanism.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~€4/unit fastener+torque + ~€3/unit separate-HVIL-switch deletion × 100,000

ideaData.riskNotes: BeCu machining/dust requires controlled process (Be exposure). Over-centre force retention validated over 50 service cycles and thermal soak (creep of BeCu at 125°C). First-make/last-break sequence timing must guarantee HV de-energised before contact part—verified against pre-discharge time. Ag wipe wear budget over service life confirmed.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Cam-actuated wedge/wipe HV connectors are established practice in industrial disconnects and rail power connectors; no specific vehicle MSD programme named.
ideaData.materialGrade: C17200 BeCu (TH04/HT temper) wedge contacts, Ag-over-Ni plating; C11000 ETP-copper receptacle

Cycle time per spine falls versus routing/taping round cable. Scrap on stamped Al is recyclable single-alloy. Plant capex shifts from labour-heavy taping to one automated weld line.

costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~€45/vehicle Cu feeder material + €12 assembly labour; ~55% net saving after Al busbar cost ≈ €30–€50/vehicle × 300k

ideaData.riskNotes: Al terminations creep and form oxide (higher contact resistance, thermal runaway risk at bolted joints); mitigate by welded rather than bolted junctions, Sn/Ag plating at any dissimilar-metal interface, and Belleville-washer preload where bolting is unavoidable. Galvanic corrosion at Al-Cu junctions requires sealed transition ferrules. Requires vibration and thermal-cycle validation per LV/USCAR-2.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Aluminium busbar HV distribution is established practice in EV battery packs; flat busbar body-level distribution is an emerging established DFMA lever, no specific programme named.
ideaData.materialGrade: EN AW-1350-H14 aluminium busbar (2-4 mm), PA6.6 co-extruded insulation carrier; replaces EN 13602 ETP Cu feeders

ideaData.technicalDescription: Baseline routes 12V ground returns as dedicated copper wires from every load to grounding studs welded on the BIW. Replace the discrete ground network with the body as return path, formalised: laser-cleaned, Zn-Ni (12-15 um) plated ground contact islands stamped into BIW panels in CR340LA / HX340LAD hot-dip galvanised steel (Z100-Z140 coating), with sealed bolted interfaces (M6, controlled torque) and characterised return impedance. costSavingPotential.qualitative: Deletes a large share of ground-return copper and multiple stud-weld operations.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~€15/vehicle ground-wire + €5 process, ~70% capture net of plating cost × 300k

ideaData.riskNotes: Corrosion at body ground interfaces raises resistance and EMC noise over life; mitigate with Zn-Ni plating, sealed connectors, and defined contact-island geometry validated by salt-spray (ISO 9227) and 10-year impedance-drift testing. EMC ground-loop behaviour must be re-characterised; requires body-plant plating compatibility.
dfmaPrinciples: Use the structure as a functional conductor
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Chassis-ground return is universal established practice; formalised plated ground islands and floor-pan integrated rails are established DFMA practice, no specific programme named.
ideaData.materialGrade: CR340LA / HX340LAD galvanised steel BIW (Z100-Z140), Zn-Ni plated contact islands

title: Power-line communication collapses signal wires onto DC rails
description: Removes signal conductors and connector cavities from the highest-node-count periphery. Baseline low-bandwidth actuators/sensors (lighting, HVAC flaps, window motors) each carry a dedicated LIN/CAN signal pair plus power - three or four wires per node. Deploy narrowband DC power-line communication (DC-PLC, ISO 21806 / DC-BUS-style modulation) so command data rides on the existing 12V/48V conductor, deleting the dedicated signal pair. Couple a 100-500 kbps carrier onto the power conductor via a series LC coupler (typ. 1-10 uH choke plus DC-blocking capacitor) and receive through a bandpass filter, so the power wire doubles as the data medium; EMI is managed by spread-spectrum modulation and the low bandwidth. Each converted node deletes 1-2 conductors, connector cavities and splice points across the zonal periphery where node count is highest.

ideaData.technicalDescription: Baseline low-bandwidth actuators/sensors (lighting, HVAC flaps, window motors) each carry a dedicated LIN/CAN signal pair plus power - three or four wires per node. Couple a 100-500 kbps carrier onto the power conductor via a series LC coupler (typ. 1-10 uH choke plus DC-blocking capacitor) and receive through a bandpass filter, so the power wire doubles as the data medium; EMI is managed by spread-spectrum modulation and the low bandwidth. Each converted node deletes 1-2 conductors, connector cavities and splice points across the zonal periphery where node count is highest.
ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Deletes signal-pair cut/crimp and the associated connector cavities at every PLC node; adds a coupler IC/passives to node PCBs (cost migrates from harness to silicon). Harness assembly loses splices and reduces circuit count; connector housings shrink. No new plant station—complexity leaves the harness.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Removes signal conductors and connector cavities from the highest-node-count periphery.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~40 PLC-eligible nodes × ~€0.6 conductor+cavity saving net of coupler cost ≈ €15–€22/vehicle × 300k

ideaData.riskNotes: PLC noise immunity on a switched-load power net is the core risk; DC/DC ripple and load transients corrupt the carrier. Mitigate with adaptive equalisation, CRC/retry protocol, and coupler placement away from PWM loads. Requires full EMC (CISPR 25) and functional-safety timing validation; not suitable for hard-real-time safety actuation.
dfmaPrinciples: Merge power and data onto one conductor
Migrate complexity from wiring to silicon
ideaData.benchmarkReference: DC power-line communication is established practice in solar/industrial systems and in automotive LED lighting nodes; broad zonal deployment is emerging practice, no named programme.

ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Collapses 4–6 SMT programmes and test fixtures to 2; single reflow/AOI/ICT setup runs at 2–3× volume improving OEE and yield learning. EOL binding via connector-key detection replaces variant-specific stocking at the station. Aftermarket depot stocks 2 units, not 6.

costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: 5 controllers/vehicle × ~€90 × ~18% blended saving from volume+fixture+SKU × 300k

ideaData.riskNotes: A universal high-current board is over-specified for low-load zones, adding a few € of silicon per low-demand node; net positive only if volume leverage exceeds over-spec cost. Location-key misread must fail safe—requires redundant coding and boot-time plausibility check. Thermal design must cover the worst-case zone. ASIL partitioning revalidated once.
dfmaPrinciples: Configure by coding not by SKU
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Location-agnostic identical-hardware controllers with connector/resistor coding are established modular-electronics practice; specific two-variant zonal deployment not tied to a named programme.

ideaData.title: Injection-moulded 3D circuit carriers replace peripheral micro-harnesses
ideaData.technicalDescription: Baseline short peripheral runs (door switch packs, roof-console clusters, tailgate handles) use tiny discrete harnesses: cut wire, crimp, insert, tape - high labour per metre and many splice/connector failure points. Replace with Molded Interconnect Devices (MID) via Laser Direct Structuring (LDS): an LDS-grade PC/ABS or PA6-GF (LDS additive package, e.g. PA6-GF30 LDS or Xantar LDS) structural bracket is laser-activated then electroless-plated Cu (~8-12 um) / Ni (~4-6 um) / Au (~0.05-0.1 um flash) to form conductor traces directly on the 3D part, integrating switch contacts, LED pads and connector interface into one moulded piece. The mechanical bracket and wiring become one part, eliminating the cut/crimp/tape flow for that sub-branch and collapsing connectors into board-to-board or direct contacts. Best where current is low (<3A) and geometry is fixed.
ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Deletes discrete micro-harness cut/crimp/tape cells for each converted node; adds LDS laser and electroless plating line (or outsourced MID supply). Assembly becomes a single part snap-in versus route-and-clip. Fewer connectors reduces mating stations at final trim.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Removes labour-intensive micro-harness fabrication and connector count on low-current nodes.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~6 convertible nodes × ~€5 harness+connector labour, ~50% net saving after MID part premium × 300k

ideaData.riskNotes: LDS current-carrying capacity and thermal-cycle plating adhesion are the risks; plated traces are thin (limited ampacity) so restricted to signal/low-power. Validate plating adhesion under thermal shock and humidity (IEC 60068), and contact durability at switch pads. Tooling cost is fixed and only amortises at volume—unsuitable for low-runner variants.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: LDS-MID is established practice in antennas, sensors and switch modules; broader peripheral-harness substitution is an emerging DFMA lever, no named vehicle programme.
ideaData.materialGrade: LDS-grade PC/ABS or PA6-GF30, electroless Cu/Ni/Au plating stack

title: Ten Base-T1S multidrop segments replace CAN spokes to zones
description: Collapses star wiring to shared segments and deletes gateway bridging silicon. Baseline mid-tier control networks use multiple CAN/CAN-FD spokes and a gateway, each spoke needing termination and a gateway port. Replace intra-zone connectivity with IEEE 802.3cg 10BASE-T1S multidrop Ethernet: up to ~8 nodes share a single unshielded single-pair (UTP, ~100 ohm) segment on a shared medium with PLCA arbitration, removing per-device stubs and eliminating CAN-to-Ethernet gateway silicon because the segment natively bridges into the 100BASE-T1 backbone. One shared pair with short passive stubs replaces a star of dedicated pairs; PLCA gives collision-free deterministic access without a switch port per node, so switch/gateway port count and backbone-side silicon fall. UTP (no shield) is cheaper and lighter than shielded CAN-FD in high-node zones; segment reach ~25 m at 10 Mbps.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Collapses star wiring to shared segments and deletes gateway bridging silicon.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: gateway/port + shielded-pair reduction ~€18/vehicle × ~90% capture × 300k

ideaData.riskNotes: Shared-medium 10BASE-T1S has bandwidth and node-count limits (~8 nodes, 10 Mbps aggregate); over-loading degrades latency for safety messages. Stub length and mixing-segment topology are constrained—needs SI simulation. EMC of unshielded multidrop under high-current neighbours requires CISPR 25 validation and careful twist/lay control.
dfmaPrinciples: Delete gateway silicon via native bridging
ideaData.benchmarkReference: IEEE 802.3cg 10BASE-T1S multidrop is a released standard entering production for zonal edge networks; established emerging practice, no specific named programme claimed.

ideaData.title: Solid-aluminium single-conductor for large low-flex power runs
ideaData.technicalDescription: Baseline high-current chassis and rear-drive feeders use finely-stranded copper for flexibility even where the route is fixed and only end-flex is needed. On fixed-geometry long runs (floor-tunnel main feeder, sill runs), replace stranded Cu with a single solid or few-strand aluminium conductor in EN AW-8030 (or EN AW-1370), an 8000-series alloy micro-alloyed with Fe/Cu developed for automotive conductors to resist creep and improve elongation vs 1350 while retaining ~61% IACS. The alloy raises creep resistance and terminal-joint reliability that plagued early pure-Al wiring; solid or compacted-few-strand geometry cuts strand-count manufacturing cost and improves fill factor so diameter and insulation volume drop. Only fixed sections use solid conductor; short flexible Cu pigtails (ultrasonic-welded Cu-Al joints, sealed against galvanic corrosion) at each end give connector interface and vibration relief.
ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Adds an Al-Cu transition weld (ultrasonic/friction) at each end plus 8030 draw stock; deletes copper mass on long runs and reduces insulation volume. Cut-to-length of solid conductor is faster than handling fine strand. Terminal crimping replaced by welded transitions at end pigtails.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Copper displacement on large-gauge fixed runs plus faster handling of solid conductor.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~€30/vehicle large-gauge Cu on fixed runs, ~65% net saving after 8030 + transition weld × 300k

ideaData.riskNotes: Al conductor creep and terminal fretting at the transition joint are the failure modes; 8030 alloy plus welded (not crimped) Al-Cu transitions and strain relief mitigate. Solid conductor tolerates limited flex cycles—strict routing to fixed sections only. Validate to USCAR-38 (Al terminals) and full vibration/thermal-cycle regime; galvanic sealing at transitions mandatory.
dfmaPrinciples: Match conductor flexibility to actual route needs
ideaData.benchmarkReference: EN AW-8030 automotive aluminium wiring is established production practice for battery and body feeders; solid-conductor fixed-run application is established DFMA, no named programme.
ideaData.materialGrade: EN AW-8030 (alt. EN AW-1370) aluminium conductor; short Cu pigtails with sealed ultrasonic Cu-Al welds
