ideaData.title: Screwless IDC mass-termination at zone controller headers
ideaData.technicalDescription: Baseline zone controllers receive 60-120 circuits via crimped terminals seated in sealed housings (e.g. TE/Aptiv MCP/MQS), each crimp a discrete process with pull-force and crimp-height verification. Proposal: adopt insulation-displacement contact (IDC) mass-termination for low-current signal/LIN/12V-sense circuits (<8A, 0.35-0.5 mm2 PVC/TPE-I insulation). A single press stroke terminates a full row of 20-40 conductors simultaneously against slotted-beam contacts (typ. phosphor-bronze C51000 or C52100, Sn-plated) that shear insulation and gas-tight cold-weld to the Cu strands. IDC eliminates strip-and-crimp entirely for those circuits and enables ribbon or laid-in discrete wire. The slotted beam maintains normal force via spring-back of the bifurcated tine, giving a gas-tight interface without an intermediate crimped terminal. Retain crimped MCP for >8A power feeds where current density and thermal cycling exceed IDC ratings.
ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Deletes per-circuit strip/crimp/insert stations for signal wires; one IDC press replaces ~40 crimp cycles per header. Cuts harness board cycle time and applicator tooling count. Adds row-alignment fixture and press capex (~€40-70k/line). Reduces crimp-quality scrap and terminal SKU count.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Removes the dominant labour and quality-inspection content of signal-wire termination at zone controller headers.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~120 signal crimps/vehicle × €0.03 avoided labour+scrap × 300k ≈ €1.08M, plus applicator/SKU reduction

ideaData.riskNotes: IDC gas-tight joint sensitive to conductor plating/wire gauge tolerance and micro-fretting under vibration; qualify to LV214/USCAR-2 vibration+thermal-shock. Risk on stranded fine-strand wire spreading in slot — specify compacted or solid conductor and validate contact resistance drift <10mΩ over 1000h. Restrict to sealed dry-zone locations.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: IDC mass-termination is established practice in telecom and appliance connectors and used in some automotive door/roof ribbon interfaces; no specific vehicle programme named.
ideaData.materialGrade: Sn-plated phosphor-bronze (C51000/C52100) IDC slotted-beam contacts; 0.35-0.5 mm2 PVC/TPE-I wire
ideaData.regulatoryContext: USCAR-2/LV214 connector validation; ISO 16750 environmental

title: Local power generation at zones via DC-DC pods deletes heavy 12V feeders
description: Copper feeder mass reduction dominates; secondary weight and packaging benefit. Baseline distributes 12V from a central PDU to each zone over thick copper (6-16mm2) sized to hold end-of-line voltage above ~10.5V under worst-case load, so conductor mass is set by IR-drop, not current-carrying alone. Proposal: run a single higher-voltage 48V trunk (or the HV-derived 48V rail) to each zone and place a compact 48V-to-12V buck pod (GaN/Si synchronous, 300-600W) inside each zone controller enclosure. Physics: for equal power, raising bus voltage 4× cuts current 4× and I2R loss 16×, so the 48V trunk can be ~2.5mm2 versus 10-16mm2 12V feeders — copper mass scales with the square of the voltage ratio for a fixed drop budget. The 12V is regenerated locally with tight regulation, removing the long-feeder voltage-drop penalty and load-dump propagation.

ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Replaces multiple heavy 12V home-run feeders with one thin 48V trunk per zone; slashes copper mass and routing bulk, easing clip/grommet count. Adds a DC-DC pod PCB per zone (integrated, not standalone box). Net reduces harness fill and connector size classes.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Copper feeder mass reduction dominates; secondary weight and packaging benefit.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~4-6 kg feeder copper/vehicle reduced ~2.5 kg × €9/kg + routing labour, netted against DC-DC BOM, × 300k

ideaData.riskNotes: Distributed DC-DC adds EMC sources near zone; qualify conducted/radiated emissions CISPR 25. Thermal management of buck stage in sealed enclosure — validate junction temp over duty cycle. 48V arc/touch requirements per LV148; ensure fusing coordination and fault ride-through so a pod failure degrades gracefully.

Minimise conductor mass via voltage scaling
ideaData.benchmarkReference: 48V distribution with local point-of-load conversion is established power-electronics practice; migrating it into zone controllers is emerging automotive architecture — not naming a specific programme.
ideaData.materialGrade: 48V trunk 2.5mm2 Cu; GaN/Si synchronous buck, 12V regeneration; LV148 48V rail
ideaData.regulatoryContext: LV148 48V, CISPR 25 EMC, ISO 26262 for power-path availability

title: Aluminium-alloy connector shells replace zinc die-cast HV backshells
description: Material substitution and weight; zinc alloy price and density both favour Al. Baseline HV interconnect backshells, shield ferrules and 360° EMC housings are zinc die-cast (ZAMAK 5) or machined brass, chosen for shieldability and die-castability but heavy (density 6.6-8.5 g/cc). Proposal: convert to high-pressure die-cast AlSi9Cu3(Fe) (EN AC-46000) or, for thin-wall shells, AlSi10MnMg, with a conductive chromate-free passivation (or electroless Ni where contact resistance to the braid is critical). Physics: aluminium at 2.7 g/cc gives ~60-68% mass reduction per shell at equal wall; conductivity 61% IACS is ample for shield-current return and EMC bonding. Die-castability of EN AC-46000 supports the same tooling geometry with adjusted gating; wall can stay ~1.5-2.0mm. Retain a plated contact land where the braid clamps to hold bonding resistance <2.5mΩ.

Die-castability of EN AC-46000 supports the same tooling geometry with adjusted gating; wall can stay ~1.5-2.0mm. costSavingPotential.qualitative: Material substitution and weight; zinc alloy price and density both favour Al.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~0.4 kg zinc shells/vehicle at €4.2/kg vs 0.15 kg Al at €3.4/kg; delta ~€1.2/vehicle + freight × 300k

ideaData.riskNotes: Galvanic couple between Al shell and Cu braid/steel fasteners — mitigate with tin/Ni plating at interfaces and sealed joint. Shield attenuation must be re-verified (transfer impedance) to retain EMC margin. Thread strength lower in Al — use steel inserts or thread-forming design. Validate to LV215/USCAR HV connector standards.
dfmaPrinciples: Substitute lighter material at equal process
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Aluminium HPDC for EMC housings is established in power-electronics and inverter casings; applying to HV connector backshells is a direct transfer — not naming a vehicle programme.
ideaData.materialGrade: EN AC-46000 (AlSi9Cu3), AlSi10MnMg thin-wall; electroless Ni at braid clamp
ideaData.regulatoryContext: USCAR/LV215 HV connector, EMC transfer-impedance, RoHS chromate-free passivation

title: Print-in-place ink busbars on structural trim carriers
description: Deletes discrete low-current wiring, clips and connectors by integrating circuit into existing plastic. Baseline low-current lighting/sensor/switch circuits in door cards, headliners and consoles use FFC or discrete wires clipped to trim. Proposal: screen-print (150-200 mesh, 15-25 µm wet) or aerosol-jet a thick-film silver paste (e.g. DuPont 5000-series / Henkel LOCTITE ECI 1010, sintered 120-150°C on PC/ABS or PP-T20) as traces, over-print a UV/thermal dielectric (~15 µm) and encapsulate flexed zones. IME variant: print on 0.1-0.175 mm PC film (Bayfol/Makrofol), thermoform, then insert-mould with PC/ABS. Traces carry ambient-lighting and capacitive-switch loads (<2A) at 25-80 mΩ/sq sheet resistance; the substrate is already present so the circuit adds only ink mass, deleting the wire, its clips and half its connectors.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Deletes discrete low-current wiring, clips and connectors by integrating circuit into existing plastic.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~€5-7 wire+clip+connector content/vehicle displaced net of ink+print op ~€4.5/vehicle × 300k

ideaData.riskNotes: Printed conductors have lower ampacity and mechanical robustness — restrict to low-current, low-flex zones; validate crack propagation over thermal cycling and door slam vibration (ISO 16750). Silver migration/corrosion under humidity — encapsulate and specify anti-migration formulation. Repair strategy differs (replace carrier).
ideaData.benchmarkReference: In-mould electronics and printed circuitry are established practice in overhead consoles and switch panels (TactoTek IMSE-style processing, ~2018 onward); broadening across trim is an emerging lever, no specific vehicle programme named.
ideaData.materialGrade: Thick-film Ag paste (DuPont 5000-series / Henkel ECI 1010), dielectric ~15 µm; substrates PC/ABS or PP-T20; IME film 0.1-0.175 mm PC (Bayfol/Makrofol)
ideaData.regulatoryContext: ISO 16750 environmental, EMC CISPR 25, silver-migration humidity validation

title: Split-and-clamp lay-in connectors delete inline junctions
description: Removes an entire connector pair and its assembly step at each converted inline. Baseline harness architecture uses inline connectors at every branch split so subsegments can be built and joined on separate boards — each inline is two mating halves plus terminals, sealing and assembly. Proposal: replace selected inline splits with lay-in split-body IDC junction blocks: the continuous conductors are laid into a channelled base without cutting, a mating lid presses IDC blades to tap or bridge circuits, and it closes as one CPA-latched block. Physics: because conductors run through uncut, there is no terminal-to-terminal contact pair — only a single gas-tight IDC tap per circuit, halving contact interfaces and eliminating one full connector body per junction. This suits taps (splices) and continuous multidrop segments (Base-T1S, LIN, 12V distribution).

ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Deletes one connector body, its terminals and one mate/CPA operation per converted junction; replaces with a single lid-close press. Reduces terminal SKU count and inline-connector inventory. Enables continuous through-routing, cutting board-transfer joins. Adds lay-in fixture.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Removes an entire connector pair and its assembly step at each converted inline.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~8 inlines/vehicle converted × €0.35 net (body+terminals+op saved) × 300k ≈ €0.84M plus SKU carrying

ideaData.riskNotes: Splice/tap IDC reliability under current and vibration must meet USCAR-2; limit tapped current per contact. Sealing of a split body harder than a barrel connector — validate IPx sealing and thermal cycling. Rework/repair requires block replacement. Not for HV or high-vibration underbody without additional retention.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Lay-in IDC junction/splice blocks are established in building and appliance wiring; automotive adoption for signal/low-power junctions is an emerging lever — not naming a specific programme.
ideaData.materialGrade: CuSn6 IDC blades; PA66-GF30 split body; 0.35-1.0mm2 conductors
ideaData.regulatoryContext: USCAR-2, ISO 16750, IP sealing class per zone

title: Common cross-vehicle harness modules on carry-over connector pinout
annualSaving: €4M-€7M across a 3-platform group at ~600,000 units/yr combined
description: SKU collapse and volume amortisation across lines is the largest structural lever in harness cost. Baseline each vehicle line/variant has unique harness part numbers driven by trim, market and option permutations, exploding SKUs. Proposal: freeze a cross-platform interface standard — fixed zone-controller connector pinouts (e.g. sealed MLK/MQS 1.5 and 0.64 terminal systems, TE/Aptiv), a fixed circuit-colour/gauge dictionary (0.35-2.5 mm² FLRY-B per ISO 6722), and ~6-8 modular building blocks (front-zone, rear-zone, roof, floor spine, door, seat) that snap at standardised sealed inline interfaces (e.g. 40-way IP67). Variants handled by module presence/absence and software feature-flags, not unique routing. One high-volume module amortises applicators, tooling and PPAP across lines, collapsing SKU count by ~10x.

ideaData.title: Common cross-vehicle harness modules on carry-over connector pinout
ideaData.technicalDescription: Baseline each vehicle line/variant has unique harness part numbers driven by trim, market and option permutations, exploding SKUs. Proposal: freeze a cross-platform interface standard — fixed zone-controller connector pinouts (e.g. sealed MLK/MQS 1.5 and 0.64 terminal systems, TE/Aptiv), a fixed circuit-colour/gauge dictionary (0.35-2.5 mm² FLRY-B per ISO 6722), and ~6-8 modular building blocks (front-zone, rear-zone, roof, floor spine, door, seat) that snap at standardised sealed inline interfaces (e.g. 40-way IP67). Variants handled by module presence/absence and software feature-flags, not unique routing. One high-volume module amortises applicators, tooling and PPAP across lines, collapsing SKU count by ~10x.
ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Converts many unique boards to a few high-volume module boards; raises applicator/fixture utilisation and cuts changeover. Reduces PPAP, prototype and validation spend across programmes. Enables dual-sourcing on standardised modules. Requires cross-programme interface governance.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: SKU collapse and volume amortisation across lines is the largest structural lever in harness cost.
costSavingPotential.percentage: 10-16% of total harness spend across platforms
costSavingPotential.annualValue: €4M-€7M across a 3-platform group at ~600,000 units/yr combined
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: SKU reduction ~70%, PPAP/engineering avoidance + 3-5% piece price via volume × combined 600k units

ideaData.riskNotes: Frozen pinout constrains future feature addition — reserve spare pins/gauge headroom up front. Over-specifying common gauge adds slight copper on light variants. Governance risk: programmes deviating erodes commonality — enforce via architecture board. Validate worst-case current on shared circuits.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Modular common-interface harness architecture with zonal controllers is established VA/VE practice at scaled OEMs; stated as established practice, not tied to a named programme.
ideaData.materialGrade: FLRY-B wire 0.35-2.5 mm² per ISO 6722; MLK 1.5 / MQS 0.64 terminal systems (TE/Aptiv); sealed IP67 inline connectors
ideaData.regulatoryContext: Cross-market homologation of common circuits; ISO 26262 interface freeze

title: Aluminium-clad copper (CCA) signal wire for low-current body circuits
description: Conductor material cost and mass reduction on the high-count low-current wire population. Baseline low-current body signal/LIN/lighting circuits use pure-copper (ETP Cu, C11000) 0.35-0.5 mm² per ISO 6722. Ampacity is not the constraint — handling and connectivity are. Proposal: substitute copper-clad aluminium (CCA, 10-15% Cu by volume over an AA-1350 Al core) up-gauged to 0.5-0.75 mm² to recover DC resistance. Al conductivity is 61% IACS, so a modest cross-section increase restores resistance while cutting conductor mass ~45-50% (Al 2.7 vs Cu 8.9 g/cm³). The Cu cladding preserves solderability/crimp behaviour and terminal corrosion resistance, retaining standard crimp terminals; anti-fret dielectric grease recommended at connectors. Reserve pure Cu (or tinned Cu) for high-flex door-hinge and high-current runs.

costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~2 kg low-current Cu/vehicle at €9/kg replaced by CCA ~1.1 kg equiv cost basis; delta ~€3/vehicle × 300k

ideaData.riskNotes: CCA crimp joint fatigue and cold-flow under clamp load — qualify crimp per USCAR-21 with revised specs and confirm resistance stability over thermal cycling. Not for high-vibration or flex-life-critical circuits. Copper-content spec must be controlled to guarantee cladding continuity and terminal corrosion resistance. Handle bend-radius limits.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: CCA is established in coaxial/RF and some automotive low-current applications; broad body-circuit use is a targeted cost lever, stated as established practice, not a named programme.
ideaData.materialGrade: CCA: AA-1350 aluminium core with 10-15%-by-volume ETP copper (C11000) cladding, 0.5-0.75 mm²; insulation FLRY-B per ISO 6722
ideaData.regulatoryContext: USCAR-21 crimp validation, ISO 6722 wire, ISO 16750 environmental

ideaData.title: Rivet-bonded gigacast interface via cast-in steel bushings
ideaData.technicalDescription: Baseline rear gigacastings in AlSi10MnMg-T7 (Aural-2/Castasil) are joined to the surrounding steel/aluminium BIW with self-piercing rivets that demand a minimum 2.5–3.0 mm cast wall at every joint flange, forcing local ribbing and driving casting mass and porosity-driven scrap. Proposal: cast in low-carbon steel (C10E) threaded/plain insert bushings at defined load nodes during the HPDC shot using in-die placement, then join with M8 flow-drill screws or bolts into the bushing rather than SPR into raw casting. This lets the surrounding cast flange drop to 1.8 mm since the bushing carries bearing and pull-out load, and eliminates SPR die wear and the rivet-feed logistics on a station running ~90s cycle. Physics: pull-through failure in T7 AlSi migrates from the ~90 MPa cast wall to the steel bushing shear plane, decoupling joint strength from casting section. Galvanic isolation via zinc-flake bushing coating and sealer.
ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Adds robotic insert-placement to the HPDC cell and a bushing-cleanliness check; deletes one SPR station per side and its rivet magazine. Casting shot weight falls ~4-6% from thinner flanges, cutting melt energy and machining stock. In-die insert risk raises die maintenance slightly.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Removes rivet consumable and SPR tooling wear while lightening the casting.
costSavingPotential.percentage: 7-11% of the rear-underbody joining + casting cost
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~30 SPR joints/side eliminated or converted × €0.11 rivet+wear each + 5 kg casting mass × €2.4/kg saved, × 200k

ideaData.riskNotes: Insert dislodgement/misfill during shot causes scrap of a high-value casting — mitigate with vision-verified nest and pressure-cast-around validation on 300-shot capability run. Galvanic corrosion at steel-Al interface needs cyclic-corrosion (VDA 233-102) sign-off with sealer and coating; validate joint fatigue to 2M cycles.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Cast-in insert practice is established in structural HPDC (e.g. suspension components); application to gigacast joint nodes stated as established die-casting practice, no specific programme claimed.

title: Vacuum-assist-free gigacast via rheocast semi-solid slurry
description: Cuts vacuum-system capex/maintenance and scrap from gas porosity. Baseline structural gigacastings use high-vacuum HPDC of AlSi10MnMg (T7) with die vacuum <50 mbar plus chill vents to hold porosity <1%; vacuum systems, vent maintenance and rejects dominate cost. Proposal: convert mid-size structural castings (shock-tower, rear seat-pan node) to semi-solid rheocasting (SEED or GISS) of A356/AlSi7Mg0.3 at ~40-50% solid fraction. Laminar die fill at low gate velocity (<0.5 m/s vs 30-50 m/s in HPDC) entrains far less air, so vacuum can be reduced or removed and the part is T6-heat-treatable and weldable without blister risk. Thixotropic viscosity suppresses turbulence (low Weber number), giving near-zero gas porosity and finer globular primary-Al for >10% elongation, enabling SPR without cracking.

costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: Scrap from 6% to ~2% on €140 casting + vacuum maintenance ~€0.8M/yr saved, over 150k units

ideaData.riskNotes: Slurry temperature/solid-fraction control is process-sensitive; drift causes cold shuts. Mitigate with closed-loop induction slurry conditioning and thermal imaging per shot. Requires re-qualification of crash performance since alloy/microstructure differs; run full node crush and fatigue matrix.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Semi-solid rheocasting of A356 (SEED process, Rheinfelden/Comptech; GISS) is established practice for structural aluminium chassis components; giga-scale application stated as emerging, no programme named.
ideaData.materialGrade: A356 / AlSi7Mg0.3 rheocast slurry, ~40-50% solid fraction, T6-heat-treatable

description: Collapses a multi-part welded ring into one press-hardened blank. Baseline body-side ring (A-pillar/roof-rail/B-pillar/rocker) is a laser-welded assembly of 22MnB5 hot-stamped outer plus separate cold-stamped 590/780 reinforcements and a soft-zone spacer, joined by ~40 spot welds. Physics: local cooling-rate control below/above the critical 27°C/s quench threshold sets the martensite fraction, so intrusion resistance and controlled fold-down in the rocker/A-pillar transition are engineered into one blank. ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Requires a segmented-temperature hot-stamp die with cartridge heaters/cooling circuits and a larger blank. Deletes 2-3 cold-stamp dies, their presses and the laser-weld cell for reinforcements. Blanking scrap rises on the large ring — offset by nesting and tailor-welded feedstock.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Collapses a multi-part welded ring into one press-hardened blank.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: 3 reinforcement parts × €4.5 + 20 welds × €0.09 + tooling amortisation saved, × 250k

ideaData.riskNotes: Transition-zone fatigue and dimensional distortion from differential cooling need validation; soft-zone width tolerance drives crash mode. Mitigate with die thermal mapping, hardness traverse per batch, and side-impact (FMVSS 214 / Euro NCAP pole) correlation before tooling freeze.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: In-die tailored tempering (partition/soft-zone) of 22MnB5 is established hot-stamping practice; single-ring consolidation stated generically, no invented programme.

title: Adhesive-only structural bonding retires spot welds on aluminium floor
description: Removes the majority of SPR consumables and die wear on floor seams. Baseline aluminium floor (EN AW-5754-H22 / 6014-T4 panels on 6082-T6 extrusions) is joined by self-piercing rivets plus a crash-durable epoxy bead — the SPR carries fixture load until cure. Proposal: move to rivet-minimised full-structural bonding using a two-component crash-toughened epoxy (modified DGEBA with core-shell rubber toughener, e.g. Betamate/SikaPower class), induction pre-gelling at fixturing points to replace the rivets' fixture function, eliminating most SPR on non-peel seams. Lap-shear of the toughened epoxy exceeds ~30 MPa and out-performs a rivet in shear over the bonded area; rivets retained only at peel-critical crash edges. Induction spot-cure ~3 s at anchors gives handling strength so the fixture releases before the ~180°C full oven cure, holding line rate.

ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Adds inline induction pre-gel coils at fixture nests; drastically cuts SPR count and die-change downtime and removes rivet logistics. Requires tighter surface-prep (plasma/laser clean) station. Bonding oven already present. Net stations reduced.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Removes the majority of SPR consumables and die wear on floor seams.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~120 rivets/floor reduced to ~40, saving 80 × €0.12 + die wear, × 180k

ideaData.riskNotes: Adhesive durability under humidity/thermal cycling and crash energy at cold (-40°C) are the key risks — brittle failure must be avoided. Mitigate with cataphoresis-compatible chemistry, wedge-impact test, and cyclic-ageing lap-shear to VDA; retain rivets at peel edges as fail-safe.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Weld-bonding and structural adhesive aluminium floors are established BIW practice (aluminium-intensive premium architectures, ~2010s); rivet-minimisation stated as established practice, no specific programme named.
ideaData.materialGrade: Two-part crash-toughened epoxy (DGEBA + core-shell rubber, Betamate/SikaPower class); panels EN AW-5754-H22 / 6014-T4; extrusions 6082-T6

title: Two gigacasts replace three: cross-car mega-node consolidation
description: Removes two joint interfaces and one die set entirely. Baseline rear underbody uses a left and right rear-rail casting plus a separate cast/stamped rear cross-member, joined by SPR/bolts at the wheelhouse — three castings and their inter-part flanges, datums and joins. Proposal: a single U-shaped rear mega-casting in Castasil-37 (AlSi9MnMoZr, HT-free, ~120 MPa YS, >10% elongation) spanning both rails and the cross-member in one shot on a ~9,000 t locking-force machine, deleting the two inter-casting interfaces. Removing the joint flanges eliminates the ~4 mm double-wall overlaps and SPR bosses, and the HT-free alloy avoids quench distortion that would otherwise blow tolerance on a part this size, so no straightening fixture is needed. Wall thickness topology-optimised 2.0-3.5 mm to hold torsional stiffness at the shock-tower nodes.

costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~60 joints deleted × €0.11 + 2 fixtures + 1 die amortisation + handling, × 200k

ideaData.riskNotes: Single-part scrap value is very high; a rejected shot loses one whole underbody. Mitigate with real-time process monitoring, X-ray CT sampling, and repair-weld procedure qualification. Repairability in service worsens — provide sectioning/replacement-node repair kit for insurers.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: HT-free Castasil-37 gigacasting and rear-underbody consolidation are established EV practice (Rheinfelden Castasil-37, single-piece rear underbody, ~2020 onward); the specific 3-to-1 layout stated generically without naming a programme.
ideaData.materialGrade: Castasil-37 (AlSi9MnMoZr), HT-free, ~120 MPa YS, >10% elongation, wall 2.0-3.5 mm

title: Remote-laser-welding replaces resistance spot on roof-frame assembly
description: Faster joining, lighter flanges, no electrode consumables. Baseline roof-frame-to-bodyside and cross-bow assembly uses ~120 resistance spot welds needing ~16 mm flanges for electrode access plus shunt spacing, driving flange width and electrode-cap change downtime. Proposal: convert accessible seams to remote laser welding (scanner-on-robot, 4-6 kW single-mode fibre, ~1070 nm, ~600 mm working distance) using stitch/wobble welds, shrinking flanges from 16 mm to ~10 mm and replacing each spot with a shorter, stronger stitch. Fusion-stitch shear strength per mm exceeds a spot nugget, non-contact processing removes two-sided access and electrode wear, and scanner throughput (~50 m/min beam-on) collapses cycle time versus reposition-per-spot. Flange reduction saves sheet mass across the full roof perimeter; joint gap held <0.15 mm for zinc-coated steel.

ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Adds laser scanner cells and Class-1 enclosure; deletes multiple spot guns, transformer cabling and cap-changers. Requires tighter gap control (<0.15 mm) so clamping/fixturing upgraded. Cycle time per joint drops sharply, freeing line capacity.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Faster joining, lighter flanges, no electrode consumables.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: Cycle-time capacity gain + electrode-cap savings €0.6M/yr + ~1.5 kg flange steel/car × €0.9, × 220k

ideaData.riskNotes: Laser welding is gap-sensitive; poor fit-up causes undercut/humping. Mitigate with seam-tracking, adaptive power, and pre-weld gap gauging. Zinc-coated steel outgassing needs a controlled gap or wobble strategy; validate weld strength and fatigue and corrosion at cut edges.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Remote laser welding of BIW roof/bodyside seams is established high-volume practice (widely deployed since the 2000s on volume steel bodies); flange-narrowing benefit stated generically, no programme named.

title: Cast-node aluminium extrusion sub-frame ring replaces stamped front-end
description: Consolidates 8 stampings into a lighter bolt-on repairable module. Baseline front-end carrier / bumper-to-shock-tower load path is an assembly of ~8 cold-stamped 340LA/DP600 steel brackets and rails spot-welded into a subframe, carrying cooling module, crash box and fender datums. Proposal: an aluminium ring built from EN AW-6082-T6 extruded profiles (closed multi-void sections) MIG/CMT-welded to two AlSi7Mg0.3 permanent-mould cast corner nodes, forming a bolt-on front module. Physics: closed extruded sections give far higher section modulus per kg than open stampings so wall can be tuned to buckling load; cast nodes resolve the multi-axis loads at the shock-tower/rail junction that would otherwise need overlapping stamped gussets. Bolt-on integration decouples the front module for parallel sub-assembly and damage repair.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Consolidates 8 stampings into a lighter bolt-on repairable module.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: 8 stampings × €3.8 + weld line labour + ~3 kg mass × €2.4 + repair-warranty benefit, × 160k

ideaData.riskNotes: Aluminium crash tuning and weld HAZ softening in 6082-T6 (drops to ~T4 near welds) must be managed via node placement away from crush zones and post-weld artificial ageing. Validate frontal crash (offset/full/MPDB) and pedestrian loads; corrosion isolation at steel bolts.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Extrusion-plus-cast-node aluminium front structures are established premium practice; front-module bolt-on stated generically without a named programme.

title: Steel-shot-peened gigacast surface deletes CDC corrosion overspec
description: Removes masking labour, one robot, and reduces casting wall mass Baseline AlSi10MnMg(Fe) rear-floor gigacasts are e-coated (CDC) with the full BIW dip, adding masking of cast-in threaded inserts and a dedicated seal-bead robot at the cast-to-steel galvanic interface. Proposal: apply controlled shot-peening (Almen 0.20–0.30A, S110 cast-steel shot) to the as-cast Al surface to close the porous skin (removing the 80–150µm oxide-rich casting rind that traps CDC), then use a thin-film silane conversion (3-glycidoxypropyltrimethoxysilane) in place of masked e-coat on the casting only. Peening also imparts −80 to −140 MPa compressive residual stress at fatigue-critical fillet radii, offsetting the 30-40% fatigue debit of as-cast porosity so nominal wall can drop 0.5mm on non-crash ribs. The steel BIW keeps CDC; only the casting is decoupled from the masking/seal burden.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Removes masking labour, one robot, and reduces casting wall mass
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~€14/casting masking+seal removed + ~€4/casting wall mass saved × 120k = €2.16M; upper bound adds oven throughput credit

ideaData.riskNotes: Silane durability must pass 6-week CASS/240h neutral salt spray and 10-cycle SAE J2334; galvanic couple at SPR/steel joints needs sealed-fastener validation. Mitigate with local wax-injection at mixed-metal nodes and DoE on peen intensity vs. fillet fatigue on constant-amplitude coupons.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Shot-peening for Al fatigue enhancement and silane conversion coatings are established aerospace/automotive practice; not tied to a named BIW programme.

title: Cast-in extruded conduit deletes downstream wiring/coolant brackets
description: Eliminates bracket parts and their fastening/logistics Baseline rear underbody gigacast (AlSi10MnMg) carries 12-18 separately fastened clips/brackets for HV cable, coolant lines and body harness, each an SPR or FDS plus a stamped clip. Proposal: over-cast pre-bent EN AW-6060-T4 thin-wall extruded tubes (channel sections) directly into the casting by placing them in the die as inserts, so the routing channels and snap features become part of the single shot. The 6060 tube (liquidus ~655°C) survives the AlSi10MnMg fill (pour ~680°C, contact <2s) with a metallurgical/mechanical lock via a thin interfacial eutectic; the tube stays hollow via ceramic-fibre core plugging. Eliminates the entire bracket BOM and their fastening operations at assembly.

ideaData.technicalDescription: Baseline rear underbody gigacast (AlSi10MnMg) carries 12-18 separately fastened clips/brackets for HV cable, coolant lines and body harness, each an SPR or FDS plus a stamped clip. Proposal: over-cast pre-bent EN AW-6060-T4 thin-wall extruded tubes (channel sections) directly into the casting by placing them in the die as inserts, so the routing channels and snap features become part of the single shot. The 6060 tube (liquidus ~655°C) survives the AlSi10MnMg fill (pour ~680°C, contact <2s) with a metallurgical/mechanical lock via a thin interfacial eutectic; the tube stays hollow via ceramic-fibre core plugging. Eliminates the entire bracket BOM and their fastening operations at assembly.
ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Adds one die-insert loading robot to the cast cell (cycle +6-8s). Deletes 12-18 clip-fasten stations across trim/chassis marriage. Requires insert-positioning nest in die; no new press.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Eliminates bracket parts and their fastening/logistics
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: 15 brackets × (€0.9 part + €0.35 fasten labour) = €18.75/veh × 120k = €2.25M

ideaData.riskNotes: Risk of insert flotation/collapse during fill and interfacial gap causing loosening; validate with CT porosity scan at interface and pull-out testing to 3× clip load. Thermal-fill simulation (Magmasoft) required to freeze insert position. Mitigate with mechanical knurling on tube OD for lock.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Over-casting of inserts (cast-in bushings/tubes) is established casting practice; not attributed to a specific vehicle programme.

title: Hot-stamped ring-frame joined by resistance element welding, not SPR
description: Shifts joints from consumable SPR to near-free resistance spots on existing guns Baseline mixed-material body-side ring (22MnB5 hot-stamped inner + 6xxx Al outer/reinforcements) is joined with self-piercing rivets: ~180 SPR/vehicle at €0.06 element plus tool-wear and a 60kN C-frame gun that limits reach into the closed ring section. Proposal: substitute Resistance Element Welding (REW) at ~40% of those joints where a steel-to-steel spot is impossible — a pre-set auxiliary steel element (DP600 element, cold-driven into the Al sheet) is then resistance spot-welded to the 22MnB5 with standard weld guns already on the line. This reuses existing spot-weld capacity (marginal cost of a spot ~€0.008 vs SPR ~€0.06+), removes the second SPR robot, and gives a repairable, inspectable nugget on the crash ring.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Shifts joints from consumable SPR to near-free resistance spots on existing guns
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: 70 joints × (€0.06−€0.015 element+spot) = €3.15/veh + robot depreciation avoided; ×150k ≈ €1.3M+

ideaData.riskNotes: Element-to-Al interface corrosion and the Al-side hole quality govern durability; needs galvanic sealing and cross-tension/peel validation per hot-stamp crash cases. Weld schedule for element-to-22MnB5 must avoid martensite HAZ softening—validate hardness traverse and 3-point ring crush.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: REW is an established Fraunhofer/industry multi-material joining method; not tied to a named production programme here.

title: Modular gigacast with bolt-on crash horns preserves repairability
description: Avoids scrapping full casting on low-speed hits; improves insurance rating Baseline monolithic front gigacast (AlSi10MnMg-T7) integrates the crash-load path so a low-speed (RCAR 15 km/h) hit condemns the whole casting, driving insurer repair ratings and warranty exposure up. Proposal: split at the front-rail interface and bolt on a replaceable EN AW-6082-T6 extruded crash-horn cassette with engineered crush initiators (bead pitch 45 mm, wall 2.5 mm) via a 4-bolt M10 (10.9) shear-plane flange cast into the T7 node. The permanent casting sees only elastic loads below the sacrificial-zone threshold; the cassette absorbs impact and is unbolted for repair. This lowers RCAR/Thatcham rating (insurance-driven residual value) and removes structural repair welding from dealer networks.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Avoids scrapping full casting on low-speed hits; improves insurance rating
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: Repair-event avoidance ~€350/incident × ~5% fleet low-speed hit rate × 120k = €2.1M + insurance-tier residual credit

ideaData.riskNotes: Bolted interface must not shift the crash pulse or FMVSS 208 timing; validate full-frontal + ODB with the joint modelled as failing in the correct sequence. Bolt preload relaxation and NVH boom at the flange need fatigue and modal validation.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Bolt-on aluminium crash boxes/crash horns are established practice on premium front ends (aluminium bumper-beam-plus-crash-box modules, longstanding); the gigacast-modularisation is the novel combination, no programme named.
ideaData.materialGrade: Casting AlSi10MnMg-T7; crash-horn cassette EN AW-6082-T6 extrusion, wall 2.5 mm; M10 class-10.9 bolts

title: Non-heat-treat gigacast alloy deletes solution/aging furnace pass
description: Removes the entire heat-treat energy and straightening burden Baseline structural gigacasts in AlSi10MnMg are cast then T7 heat-treated: solution ~480°C, quench, artificial age ~180°C — an 8-10h furnace cycle that also causes blister/distortion requiring a straightening/coining fixture. Proposal: switch to a self-hardening (as-cast/natural-age) high-ductility alloy such as Rheinfelden Castasil-37 (AlSi9MnMoZr) or Silafont-derived non-HT variants that reach ~120-150 MPa YS and >10% elongation as-cast without solution treatment, adequate for non-crash floor/underbody castings. Eliminating the furnace removes the dominant energy cost and the distortion-driven straightening op; casting properties are set in the die by controlled solidification (die-thermal management, local squeeze).

ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Deletes solution+aging furnace line and quench tank plus straightening fixture — a major capex and floor-space reduction. Adds tighter die-thermal control. Cycle time governed by casting only, improving throughput.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Removes the entire heat-treat energy and straightening burden
costSavingPotential.percentage: 12-20% of casting conversion cost on eligible parts
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~€22-35/casting HT energy+straighten removed × ~1.2 eligible castings/veh × 120k ≈ €3.2M+; capex avoidance separate

ideaData.riskNotes: As-cast alloys give lower YS than T7, so crash-critical zones must stay on heat-treatable grade — application limited to sub-crash castings. Validate elongation/fracture at cold temp (−40°C) and porosity fatigue; confirm SPR/FDS joinability at lower matrix strength.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Castasil-37 / non-heat-treat structural die-cast alloys are established Rheinfelden/foundry practice; not tied to a named vehicle here.

title: Adhesive-free gigacast-to-sill lock via cast-in dovetail geometry
description: Eliminates structural adhesive and its cure/gauging at a primary joint Baseline sill-to-underbody-casting joint uses structural epoxy (crash-durable, ~€9/vehicle bead) plus SPR, requiring an adhesive robot, oven-cure dwell and bond-gap control. Proposal: exploit the design freedom of HPDC to cast a dovetail/tongue interlock feature directly into the AlSi10MnMg casting that mates with the EN AW-6082-T6 extruded sill's internal chamber; assembly is a slide-and-lock followed by two clinch/SPR to fix axial position. The mechanical interlock reacts the shear and peel that the adhesive previously carried, so bond-line is deleted on the primary interface. Casting draft and extrusion die tolerance (±0.15mm) are co-designed so the interlock is press-fit with a controlled interference.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Eliminates structural adhesive and its cure/gauging at a primary joint
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: €9 adhesive + €3.5 cure/gauge robot allocation = €12.5/veh × 120k = €1.5M

ideaData.riskNotes: Interlock must carry side-pole/IIHS small-overlap shear without unlocking; validate with quasi-static and dynamic joint coupons and full crash. Tolerance stack of interference fit vs. thermal expansion (Al-Al matched, low risk) needs GD&T control. Corrosion in the crevice needs sealed drainage.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Mechanical interlock joints replacing adhesive are established in extrusion spaceframe practice; the cast-in dovetail combination is novel, not a named programme.

title: In-die-quenched hot-stamped floor tunnel deletes weld-on reinforcement pair
description: Three parts to one; deletes reinforcement welding and dies Baseline centre-tunnel assembly is a cold-formed HC340LA tunnel plus two spot-welded 22MnB5 tunnel reinforcements to meet side-pole intrusion and tunnel-brace load, totalling 3 parts and ~30 spot welds. Proposal: form the tunnel as a single deep-draw hot-stamped 22MnB5 part with in-die tailored quenching — fast-cooled die zones (>27°C/s) give full 1500MPa martensite along the intrusion path, while heated die inserts (~450°C zones) leave soft ~600MPa ferritic-bainitic zones at the flange transitions for weld and energy management. The graded microstructure replaces the reinforcement stack with strategic strength, removing 2 parts and their welding entirely.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Three parts to one; deletes reinforcement welding and dies
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: 2 parts × €5.5 + 30 welds × €0.02 + handling €2 = ~€13.6/veh × 150k ≈ €2.04M; upper bound adds tooling amortisation credit

ideaData.riskNotes: Soft-zone boundary placement is critical — a mis-located transition can create a stress riser under side-pole; validate with hardness mapping and dynamic pole intrusion. Deep-draw of 22MnB5 risks thinning at tunnel radius; simulate formability (blank-holder force) and check min wall.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: In-die tailored tempering of 22MnB5 is established hot-stamp practice (e.g., B-pillar soft zones); tunnel application stated as mechanism, not a named programme.

title: Tailor-welded blank shock-tower reinforcement replaces reinforcement stack
description: Eliminates a multi-part sub-stack and its welding cell, cutting piece and conversion cost. Baseline front strut-tower is a nest of 3-4 discrete stamped CR4 / HC340LA parts (0.8-2.0 mm) spot-welded with ~28 welds to carry the ~12 kN vertical strut reaction and lateral cornering moment. Proposal: consolidate to a single laser-welded tailored blank in HC340LA transitioning to HC500LA at the bearing-seat, welded before draw so the 2.0 mm thick zone sits only under the strut-bolt boss while the wheelhouse skirt runs 0.8 mm. One deep-draw die replaces three transfer dies. Strut-tower fatigue is a local hot-spot at the bolt circle, so tailoring gauge to the stress field removes mass and part-count carried purely to bolt a reinforcement onto a thin panel. Weld line placed 25 mm from the max-principal-stress ring per FE, off the fatigue-critical zone.

ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Deletes 2 transfer stampings and ~28 spot welds; adds one laser-blank-weld station upstream and one larger draw die. Net -1 assembly cell, cycle time drops ~9s/BIW. Tooling capex for the single deep-draw die partly offset by scrapped small dies. Scrap improves via optimised blank nesting.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Eliminates a multi-part sub-stack and its welding cell, cutting piece and conversion cost.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~€3.10/BIW piece+weld saving × 2 sides × 200k, plus avoided cell labour/overhead ~€0.6M/yr

ideaData.riskNotes: Weld-line formability in the draw is the key risk: HC340LA/HC500LA laser seam can neck if the line crosses the punch radius. Mitigate by CAE forming sim with weld-softening zone modelled and locating the seam on the flat skirt. Strut-tower fatigue re-validated to full corner-load block plus pothole abuse.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Tailor-welded-blank strut towers and load-bearing panels are established practice in high-volume steel BIW; mechanism proven, no specific programme claimed.
ideaData.materialGrade: Laser-welded tailored blank: HC340LA (0.8-1.2 mm) transitioning to HC500LA (2.0 mm) at bearing-seat, micro-alloyed HSLA per EN 10268

description: Converts high-count fastening labour and corrosion warranty into a low-cost metered dispense. Baseline underfloor heat-shield and tunnel-insulation carriers attach via ~40 CD-welded M6 weld studs into the floor pan, each needing a pierced/located boss, a stud-weld station and a torqued nut. costSavingPotential.qualitative: Converts high-count fastening labour and corrosion warranty into a low-cost metered dispense.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~€0.11/stud installed × 40 × 200k = €0.88M piece+labour, plus corrosion warranty avoidance ~€0.3M/yr

ideaData.riskNotes: Risk is long-term bond durability under salt-spray and gravel impact plus repairability in service. Mitigate with cataplasma-aged lap-shear validation, retained locating clips for fail-safe, and a documented service-replacement adhesive kit. Confirm ED-oven cure window matches line temperature profile.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Structural/semi-structural bonding of underbody heat shields is established practice; mechanism proven, no specific programme claimed.
ideaData.materialGrade: Single-component heat-cure toughened epoxy, ~30 MPa lap shear (Betamate/Terokal class), 180°C ED-oven cure; shields aluminised-steel with mica insulation

title: Roll-formed constant-section rear rail replaces stamped two-shell rail
description: Removes draw tooling and weld count while down-gauging via higher-strength grade. Baseline rear longitudinal rail is a two-shell stamped closed box (inner+outer HC420LA per EN 10268, 1.5mm, ~24 flange RSW nuggets) that is largely constant-section over its straight run behind the rear seat. Proposal: roll-form the straight segment as a closed HCT980X/DP1180 (CR1180Y700T, GI50/50 coated) tube with an online HF-welded seam, flying-cut, then end-form only the kick-up node for stamping/casting mate. Constant-section crush/bending members need no draw dies; roll-forming gives thickness uniformity within ±0.03mm and no draw-thinning, so gauge drops 1.5→1.3mm at equal section modulus because DP1180 (Rm≥1180MPa) carries the axial crush the HC420LA (Rm~470MPa) needed extra thickness for. Straight-run flange welds are eliminated as the section is inherently closed.

Proposal: roll-form the straight segment as a closed HCT980X/DP1180 (CR1180Y700T, GI50/50 coated) tube with an online HF-welded seam, flying-cut, then end-form only the kick-up node for stamping/casting mate. ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Replaces two stamping dies + inner/outer weld cell for the straight run with one roll-forming line and a cut-off. Deletes ~18 spot welds/rail. Adds end-forming press for the node interface. Scrap drops sharply (coil-to-part vs blanked draw). Capex: roll-form line offset over volume.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Removes draw tooling and weld count while down-gauging via higher-strength grade.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~€4.20/rail piece+weld+material saving × 2 × 200k = €1.68M, plus scrap/tooling amortisation benefit

ideaData.riskNotes: Crash tuning is the risk: constant-section tubes crush more stably but the kick-up node transition must trigger controlled folding, not global buckling. Mitigate with dynamic axial-crush correlation and engineered crush beads at the node. HF weld-seam toughness validated at -40°C impact.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Roll-formed AHSS closed-section body rails and door beams are established practice in high-volume BIW; mechanism proven, no specific programme named.
ideaData.materialGrade: DP1180 (HCT1180X / CR1180Y700T-DP, GI50/50 coated) roll-formed tube; baseline HC420LA per EN 10268

title: Warm-formed 7xxx extruded sill replaces hot-stamped steel sill assembly
description: Consolidates a hot-stamped multi-part stack into one extrusion, cutting weight-driven and conversion cost. Baseline rocker/sill is a hot-stamped 22MnB5 (AlSi-coated, ~1.6mm, Rm~1500MPa after press-hardening) outer + inner + reinforcements, austenitised ~900°C and quenched in-die, joined by ~30 welds to meet FMVSS 214 / side-pole intrusion. Proposal: a single warm-formed EN AW-7003 or 7075 multi-cavity extruded sill (T5/T6, wall 2.5-3.5mm) with internal crush ribs. A closed multi-void extrusion carries side-impact bending as stabilised cell walls, matching the steel stack's intrusion energy at ~40% mass as ONE part, deleting the weld stack. Warm forming at ~150-200°C permits the door-cut bend/end-form without T6 cracking; subsequent artificial aging (~120°C/24h) restores strength. A ~30MN extrusion die is a fraction of a press-hardening line's capital.

A closed multi-void extrusion carries side-impact bending as stabilised cell walls, matching the steel stack's intrusion energy at ~40% mass as ONE part, deleting the weld stack. Warm forming at ~150-200°C permits the door-cut bend/end-form without T6 cracking; subsequent artificial aging (~120°C/24h) restores strength. ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Eliminates the press-hardening furnace loading for the sill parts and ~30 welds; replaces with extrusion press, cut-off, warm end-form, and an aging oven. Joins to steel BIW via SPR/flow-drill screws at the flanges. Removes several stamping dies. Aging oven is shared batch capex.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Consolidates a hot-stamped multi-part stack into one extrusion, cutting weight-driven and conversion cost.
costSavingPotential.percentage: 12-18% of the sill subassembly (net of Al premium)
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: Weld/part deletion + press-hardening energy saving ~€9/side offset by ~€4 Al premium, net ~€5/side × 2 × 150k = €1.5M

ideaData.riskNotes: Steel-to-aluminium galvanic corrosion at the body interface and SPR joinability are the risks; mitigate with e-coat + adhesive isolation and validated SPR die/rivet combos. 7075 stress-corrosion cracking mitigated by T73 temper where durability dominates over peak strength. Full side-pole and IIHS re-validation.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Aluminium multi-void extruded sills are established practice on aluminium-intensive BIW (e.g. premium EV battery-frame rockers); mechanism proven, no specific programme named.
ideaData.materialGrade: EN AW-7003 or EN AW-7075 (T6) warm-formed multi-void extrusion; baseline 22MnB5 (AlSi-coated) press-hardened steel

title: Common front-structure carry-over module across two wheelbases
description: Avoids a duplicate front-structure tooling set and weld cell by absorbing wheelbase in the floor. Baseline: two variants (SWB, LWB) each carry a fully unique front-end structure (rails, shock towers, dash-panel lower, front cross-member) with separate tooling, the wheelbase delta absorbed forward of the dash. Proposal: freeze the entire structure ahead of the A-pillar as a common module and take the wheelbase delta in the floor centre via a lengthened flat CR340LA (1.0-1.2mm) floor extension. Crash pulse, rail geometry and shock-tower loads are set by front-mass and front-overhang, which are shared; the wheelbase change is a straight floor-length variable a constant-section 590DP tunnel/rocker run absorbs with no new draw tooling — only a longer, simpler flat-field die. This commonises ~11 stampings and one full weld cell across both programmes.

Floor extension is a simple constant-section add. Massive tooling capex avoidance; higher line utilisation. One added floor-length variant fixture.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Avoids a duplicate front-structure tooling set and weld cell by absorbing wheelbase in the floor.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~11 dies × ~€0.5M avoided + one weld cell ~€2M, amortised over programme life; plus utilisation/overhead

ideaData.riskNotes: Risk is over-constraining future variant packaging (motor/engine bay) and crash-tuning both mass variants to one rail. Mitigate by validating the crash pulse at the heavier variant's GVW (worst case) and reserving shock-tower boss flexibility. Requires early cross-programme governance lock.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Front-structure carry-over ahead of the A-pillar across wheelbase variants is established modular-platform practice; mechanism proven, no specific programme named.

title: Self-piercing rivet + adhesive replaces flow-drill screws on rear floor node
description: Faster, cheaper joining consumable with fewer joints where two-sided access allows. Baseline rear-floor-to-rail node in a mixed steel/aluminium region uses flow-drill screws (FDS, e.g. EJOT/Arnold M5-M6 coated), needing a high-thrust spindle, ~2-3s form-tap dwell and one-sided access, at ~24 joints/node. Proposal: where two-sided access exists, convert to self-piercing rivets (semi-tubular boron-steel, 5.3mm, ~1500MPa, ZnNi/Almac coated) with a 1K crash-durable epoxy bead (weld-bond equivalent). SPR sets in ~1s with no chip, no thread-forming heat and no pre-drilled hole; the adhesive carries continuous shear so rivet count drops ~20%. FDS is retained only at truly single-sided closed sections. Saving: cycle time (SPR ~1s vs FDS ~2.5s), consumable cost (rivet < coated FDS screw), and elimination of thread-strip warranty.

ideaData.benchmarkReference: Patchwork/tailor-welded hot-stamping is established press-hardening practice (patchwork blanks in B-pillar production); no specific programme claimed.

title: Structural sandwich (steel-polymer-steel) dash panel deletes damping mastic
description: Trades applied bitumen mass and its labour for a thinner integrated laminate, cutting both weight and multiple bonding stations. Baseline dash/firewall panel is a 0.8mm CR3 (DC03, EN 10130) mild-steel stamping carrying 3-5 bituminous/asphaltic melt-sheet damping pads (each 1.5-2.5kg) to control 200-800Hz booming, plus spray deadener. Proposal: replace the flat central field with a laminated steel-viscoelastic-steel sandwich — two 0.35mm DC03/DC04 skins bonded to a ~40-65µm constrained-layer acrylic/polyester viscoelastic core (loss factor η≥0.15 at 20°C). The constrained layer dissipates bending energy in shear, giving equivalent loss factor at ~1.0mm total, deleting all applied pads. Formability suits shallow-draw firewall geometry; the joining perimeter uses a solid-steel picture-frame flange for RSW since laminate edges cannot be resistance-welded directly.

title: Hydroformed single-tube rear rail replaces stamped shell + reinforcements
description: Consolidates a welded two-shell plus internal bulkheads into one closed section, removing tooling, weld line and parts. Baseline rear longitudinal rail is a two-shell HCT590X (590DP, ~1.5mm) stamping closed by spot welds plus 2-3 internal 780DP bulkheads to stabilise the section against buckling under rear-impact and trailer-tongue loads. Proposal: a single hydroformed closed tube in 440-590 grade tubular steel (e.g. S460MC / CR440Y grade, ~1.3mm) with variable perimeter, formed in one op with no longitudinal weld flange. The naturally closed section gives ~30-40% higher torsional/buckling stiffness per unit mass than an open two-shell, letting internal bulkheads be deleted or halved and wall gauge cut ~0.2mm. Circumferential crush-initiator beads are formed directly into the tube to tune axial collapse for RCAR/rear-impact energy management.

ideaData.benchmarkReference: Tubular hydroforming of rails and cross-members is established practice (widely used for engine cradles and roof rails); no specific programme named.

title: Weld-bonding replaces added spot welds on floor-pan seams
description: Substitutes continuous cheap adhesive shear for expensive discrete welds and deletes a sealer pass, cutting cycle time and consumables. Baseline floor-pan-to-longitudinal and floor-to-tunnel seams use dense RSW pitch (25-35mm) on HCT590X (590DP)/CR340LA to meet stiffness and NVH sealing, plus a separate PVC seam-sealer bead. Proposal: weld-bonding — a continuous 1K heat-cure epoxy structural adhesive bead (e.g. ~0.2-0.3mm bond line, lap-shear ≥20MPa) in the flange with spot-weld pitch relaxed to 45-60mm. The adhesive carries continuous shear so far fewer welds reach the same joint stiffness and fatigue life; the continuous bond line also seals the seam, letting the separate PVC pass be deleted or reduced. Adhesive co-cures in the existing e-coat oven (~180°C, no added oven). Floor-group spot-weld count typically drops 25-40%.

costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: welds saved ~120/vehicle × ~€0.03 + PVC reduction + tip-life gain ≈ €5/vehicle × 200k; baseline joining ~€45/vehicle

ideaData.benchmarkReference: Weld-bonding (adhesive + reduced spot pitch) is long-established BIW practice for stiffness, NVH and fatigue; no specific programme named.

title: Progressive-die tailor-rolled floor cross-member replaces welded doubler stack
description: Replaces a three-piece welded assembly with one variable-gauge stamping, cutting parts, welds and mid-span mass. Baseline seat-mount floor cross-member is a uniform 1.5mm HCT590X (590DP) U-channel with two spot-welded local doublers (1.2mm 780DP/CR700Y) at seat-anchorage and tunnel-junction points to meet FMVSS 207/210 seat-pull and side-load. Proposal: a tailor-rolled blank (TRB) in HCT590X whose thickness varies continuously along the rolling direction from ~0.9mm in low-load spans to ~1.9mm at anchorage zones, stamped as one part. Continuous thickness placement replaces the discrete doublers, deleting their blanks, welds and fixtures and removing spot-weld softening at the highest-stress bolt line. TRB places mass exactly on the bending-moment envelope, cutting mid-span mass while raising section capacity at the anchorage with no added parts.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Replaces a three-piece welded assembly with one variable-gauge stamping, cutting parts, welds and mid-span mass.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: doublers+welds+mass ~€5–7/vehicle net of TRB premium × 180k; baseline cross-member ~€38/vehicle

ideaData.riskNotes: TRB coil carries a €/kg premium and needs a qualified flexible-rolling supplier; springback varies along the transition zones requiring die compensation. Validate seat-pull and 20g anchorage tests; confirm formability at thickness-transition ramps (avoid necking). Mitigate with generous ramp length ≥50 mm.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Tailor-rolled blanks for cross-members and rails are established practice (Mubea flexible-rolling technology); no specific vehicle programme named.
ideaData.materialGrade: Tailor-rolled HCT590X (590DP), ~0.9-1.9mm continuous profile; baseline 1.5mm 590DP + 1.2mm 780DP doublers

ideaData.technicalDescription: Baseline front-end module carrier (cooling-module/headlamp/bumper-beam support) is a 5-8 piece HC340LA/CR4 (DC04) stamped-steel weldment, spot-welded and bolted. Proposal: a single injection-moulded long-glass-fibre polypropylene carrier (LGF-PP, ~40wt% glass, e.g. Celstran/Sabic STAMAX grade) with an over-moulded U-shaped HSLA insert (0.8mm HC340LA) only in the bumper-beam crash-load path — a plastic-metal hybrid frame. The polymer forms the complex low-load lattice in one shot with integrated fastener bosses, cable clips and airflow ducting, deleting the entire steel weldment except the local crash insert. Bending stiffness comes from the closed hybrid box where the steel insert works in tension/compression, while the polymer handles packaging geometry at near-zero incremental cost per feature.
ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Deletes 5–8 stampings, their dies, and ~40 spot/MIG welds; deletes a subassembly weld cell. Adds one large injection-moulding tool + insert-loading. Integrates ~10 clip/bracket parts into the moulding. Weight down 3–5 kg. Big plant footprint reduction.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Replaces a multi-piece steel weldment and dozens of clips with one moulded hybrid part, collapsing part count and a weld cell.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~€12–18/vehicle (parts consolidation + weld cell + integrated clips) × 200k; baseline steel carrier ~€65/vehicle

ideaData.riskNotes: LFT-PP creep and thermal expansion mismatch with steel insert — design floating attachment and validate at −40/+90°C. Insert bond via mechanical interlock (windows/holes), not adhesion. Low-speed crash and pedestrian-protection load paths must be re-homologated; validate insert pull-out and fatigue at bumper-beam interface.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Plastic-metal hybrid front-end carriers are long-established practice (technology pioneered for front-end modules and widely produced); no specific current programme named.
ideaData.materialGrade: LGF-PP ~40wt% glass (e.g. STAMAX-type long-glass PP) + over-moulded 0.8mm HC340LA insert; baseline HC340LA/DC04 steel

Consumable rivet cost per joint exceeds a spot weld, so target only problem welds, not wholesale replacement. Fatigue-validate rivet-bonded joint.

title: Rollformed door ring-frame replaces stamped inner + reinforcements
description: Eliminates multiple reinforcement dies and cuts joining operations while trimming door mass ~1.8 kg. Baseline door-in-white is a deep-drawn DC04 (EN 10152, ~0.7 mm) inner plus 4-6 spot-welded reinforcements (B-pillar tie, hinge-face doubler, latch-face doubler, beltline beam), ~34 welds, 5 dies. Proposal: replace the load path with a variable-thickness roll-formed ring frame in HSLA HX340LAD or DP600 (EN 10346, Z100 GI), roll-formed on one line into a closed hat 1.2-2.0 mm (in-line thickness step via tailor-rolled coil), then MIG-brazed with CuSi3 filler at four corner nodes. The stamped inner becomes a non-structural DX54D shell (0.65 mm) laser-welded to the ring. Roll-forming carries bending in a continuous section with zero draw-thinning, so section modulus/kg beats a shell thinning ~25% at corners; hinge/latch loads react into cast-tolerance ring nodes, not local doublers.

Spot-weld count drops from ~34 to ~12 plus laser stitch. Cycle time neutral; scrap falls as blank utilisation on roll strip exceeds 80% vs ~55% deep-draw.

costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~€6 material+process delta/door + amortised tooling avoidance (~€2.5M over 4 die sets / programme life) × 250k doors

Corner braze nodes are fatigue-critical; require slam-durability (100k cycles) and salt-spray on brazed joint. Mitigate with node gussets and e-coat penetration checks.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Roll-formed structural door and body ring frames are established practice among body-in-white tier-1 suppliers (e.g. Shape Corp, Gestamp roll-formed sections); no specific vehicle programme named.
ideaData.materialGrade: Ring: HX340LAD or DP600 per EN 10346, Z100 GI, 1.2-2.0 mm tailor-rolled; Inner shell: DX54D 0.65 mm; braze filler CuSi3

title: Common bolt-on hinge cassette across all four side doors
description: Collapses hinge SKU count and integrates the check strap, cutting piece price and inventory. Baseline: front and rear doors carry unique upper/lower hinges (typ. 4 distinct GJL-250 or stamped SPFH590 hinge halves), each with door-side and body-side leaves, unique gooseg to package the check strap. Proposal: standardise on a single symmetric hinge cassette — a zinc-alloy (ZAMAK 5) or GD-AlSi9Cu3 die-cast body-side bracket plus a common pressed DP600 door leaf with integrated detent check-link, packaged identically at all four positions via a shared bolt pattern (3× M8 door-side, 2× M10 body-side). Handing achieved by mirroring one part number, not new tooling. Physics/economics: check-strap integration removes a separately-mounted stamped bracket + fastener set; commonisation collapses 8 hinge SKUs to 2 castings + 2 leaves, quadrupling volume per cavity and cutting piece price via die amo

ideaData.manufacturingImpact: One die-cast tool set (2 cavities) replaces up to 4; check-strap sub-assembly station deleted from door line and merged into hinge. Assembly poka-yoke improves — same cassette torqued at every corner. Body-side pierce pattern standardised, simplifying framing fixtures.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Collapses hinge SKU count and integrates the check strap, cutting piece price and inventory.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~€3.5–4.5 saved per corner × 4 corners × 300k, net of retooling

ideaData.riskNotes: Door sag/set at full open with integrated check must meet slam and abuse (150 N tug) durability; integrated detent adds a wear surface — validate detent force retention over 100k cycles. Rear-door geometry (shorter, higher belt) must accept common check travel; mitigate with two detent-spring calibrations sharing the body.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Hinge/check-link integration and cross-door commonisation are established VA/VE practice; no specific programme claimed.

title: Composite tailgate module with in-moulded latch/hinge bosses
description: Consolidates ~7 metal parts to 2 shells with in-moulded load points and can delete paint on mould-in-colour trims. Baseline steel tailgate is inner + outer stamped DC04 panels, hem-flanged and adhesive-bonded, with welded GJS-450-10 hinge brackets and a bolted latch reinforcement (~7 metal parts). Proposal: two-shell tailgate with outer in low-density Class-A SMC and inner in 40% long-glass polypropylene (LFT-PP, e.g. Celstran/SABIC-class, MFI ~40 g/10min) compression-moulded with hinge and striker load bosses over-moulded onto in-tool DP780 (EN 10346, Z100) metal inserts ~1.5 mm. Shells joined with a 2K PU structural adhesive (e.g. Sika/Betamate-class, ~5 mm bead); composite needs no e-coat. Glass-PP inner carries slam/torsion at ~1.1 g/cc vs 7.85 for steel; the DP780 inserts take concentrated bolt bearing loads so the polymer never sees bearing stress. Consolidation deletes hem-flangin

ideaData.benchmarkReference: Composite/glass-reinforced-thermoplastic liftgates are established mass-production practice (multiple tier-1 closure suppliers, e.g. Magna, Plastic Omnium, mid-2010s onward); no specific programme named.
ideaData.materialGrade: Inner: 40% long-glass PP (LFT-PP); Outer: low-density Class-A SMC; load inserts DP780 per EN 10346 Z100, ~1.5 mm; 2K PU structural adhesive

title: Cinching e-latch deletes secondary latch, striker and seal margin
description: Enables downgauged seals, deletes lock-knob linkage and reduces closing-effort warranty claims, offsetting e-latch premium. Baseline mechanical rotary latch requires a two-stage pawl (safety + primary), a heavy-gauge striker, and door seals compressed by manual slam energy — driving high closing-effort seal loads and a robust check. Proposal: adopt an electric cinching (soft-close) e-latch that draws the door from secondary to primary electrically. This lets seal cross-section and compression set-line be reduced (lower slam energy needed), and permits deleting the mechanical child-lock and manual-effort-driven over-travel margin. Latch body moves to a single-stage rotor + motorised cinch, striker to a lighter stamped SPFH590 loop. Economics: at Assembly level the win is not the latch alone — it is the reduced EPDM seal mass/section, relaxed hinge check duty, and deletion of the interior

Pinch-protection and current-limit on cinch require software validation. Quiescent draw must not violate battery-drain budget. Mitigate with capacitor-backed single-cinch and mechanical redundant release.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Cinching e-latches are established production technology across premium closures; no specific programme claimed.

title: Single-piece hydroformed hood inner replaces stamped inner + rings
description: Removes two reinforcement dies and a weld cell while integrating pedestrian-impact crush structure into one part. Baseline hood is a stamped DC04 outer plus a stamped inner with separate welded latch- and hinge-reinforcement rings, hem-bonded; pedestrian-crush geometry is stamped waffle beads limited by draw depth. Proposal: sheet-hydroform the inner in AA6016-T4 (or DX56D steel where cost-driven) into a deep egg-crate pattern, 0.9-1.1 mm nominal wall, with integral hinge and latch bosses, deleting the two welded rings. Hydroforming holds material against a single die under ~200-400 bar fluid pressure, achieving deeper controlled crush cells and thinner walls without the matched-die draw-thinning fracture limit, so pedestrian head-impact energy (GTR9 / Euro NCAP HIC1000) is tuned in one part with local boss reinforcement replacing bolted-on rings. Outer bonded with 1K epoxy hem adhesive.

ideaData.benchmarkReference: Sheet hydroforming of aluminium closure inners is established practice in low-to-mid-volume premium body shops (e.g. hydroformed aluminium closures at Audi/Jaguar-tier plants); no specific programme named.
ideaData.materialGrade: AA6016-T4 aluminium (or DX56D steel), 0.9-1.1 mm nominal wall; 1K epoxy hem adhesive

title: Flow-drill-screw + adhesive joining replaces spot welds on mixed-material closures
description: Lowers per-joint consumable and equipment cost with single-side access, and reduces fastener count via load-sharing adhesive. Baseline mixed steel/aluminium closures cannot be resistance spot welded across the dissimilar interface, forcing self-piercing rivets (SPR), each a consumable (~EUR 0.02-0.04) plus a heavy C-frame gun and per-rivet cycle. Proposal: convert inner-to-ring and bracket joints to flow-drill screws (FDS, e.g. EJOT FDS M5x18) combined with a 1K crash-durable epoxy bead (e.g. Betamate/SikaPower-class, ~5 mm), where the adhesive carries shear/peel and the FDS provides fixation and clamp during ~180 C e-coat cure. FDS forms its own threaded boss by frictional heating at ~5000 rpm, no pre-hole, single-side access (ideal for closed roll-formed/hydroformed sections), and the adhesive distributes load over area so fewer, cheaper fixation points are needed than discrete SPR/spo

Adhesive station added (or shared with existing hem-bond dispenser). Fastener logistics simplify to bulk screws vs handed rivet cassettes.

ideaData.materialGrade: FDS M5 (e.g. EJOT) into DP600/AA6xxx stack; 1K crash-durable epoxy structural adhesive

Cast-in bosses take hinge and latch bolts directly, eliminating reinforcement plates and their tolerance stack. Class-A outer stays AA6016-T4, bonded with 2K PU and isolated (e-coat primer + sealer) against galvanic corrosion.

Cycle ~75-90 s/casting vs multi-station stamp+weld. Plant capex shifts from press shop to foundry cell; scrap remelted in-cell.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Collapses a multi-piece weldment into one casting, removing weld labour, fixtures and reinforcement parts
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~€14/door inner labour+weld+reinforcement saving × delta, plus tooling amortisation avoided; baseline ~€62 assembled inner × ~22% × 200k units

Side-intrusion FMVSS 214 / ECE R95 deflection must be validated on cast wall; casting porosity at hinge pads needs X-ray CT sampling. Slam-durability 100k cycles on cast bosses.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Magnesium one-shot HPDC door inners have been demonstrated in production and by multiple tier-1 casters (e.g. earlier Mg inners on premium models, 2000s); no specific current programme claimed.
ideaData.materialGrade: AM60B magnesium HPDC, 2.0-2.5 mm wall / 4 mm pads; outer AA6016-T4; 2K PU adhesive with galvanic-isolation primer

title: Shared tailgate/liftgate carrier across notch and estate body styles
description: One carrier + mechanism part-number set replaces two, cutting tooling and validation spend and raising purchased-part volume leverage Baseline runs two distinct tailgate assemblies per platform: a saloon bootlid and an estate/SUV liftgate, each with unique inner, hinge set, gas-strut mounts and wiring carrier — roughly 40+ unique part numbers. Introduce a common structural carrier: one GJS-450-10 or die-cast AlSi10MnMg hinge-and-strut node plus a common PP-LGF30 injection-moulded inner backbone that both body styles bolt to, with only the outer skin and glass aperture body-specific. The carrier standardises hinge axis geometry, strut gas-force mounting angle and latch striker position so the same e-latch, hinge cassette and strut part numbers serve both. Commonisation targets the load-carrying and mechanism interfaces, which are style-independent, while leaving the visible skin free.

title: Rotary damped hinge deletes gas struts on hood assembly
description: Eliminates gas struts and their brackets/fasteners plus the strut leak-test and charging operations Baseline hood uses two four-bar or single-pivot steel hinges plus two gas-pressurised struts (or a torsion-rod prop + manual stay). Replace with a pair of integrated constant-torque rotary hinges: a stamped/formed hinge body housing a rotary friction-and-spring cartridge (spiral torsion spring in oil-tempered valve-spring steel per EN 10270-2 VDSiCr, plus a viscous silicone rotary damper) sized so the hood self-balances through the arc and holds at any angle. This deletes both gas struts, their body/hood brackets (4 brackets, 4 ball studs, ~8 fasteners) and the prop rod. Rotary spring torque is profiled to counter the hood weight moment across the opening angle and the damper controls closing rate, with no pressurised nitrogen cylinder to leak or lose force in cold. Applies equally to BEV

ideaData.materialGrade: Spiral torsion spring in oil-tempered VDSiCr per EN 10270-2; silicone viscous rotary damper; formed steel hinge body

title: In-line laser-brazed roof-to-body-side closure joint replaces welded drip channel
description: Removes the ditch molding, clips and PVC channel seal at the aperture while improving seam water integrity Baseline roof ditch joint at the closure aperture uses a spot-welded flange plus an applied trim strip or PVC-sealed channel to hide the weld and manage water. Replace with a laser-brazed lap joint using CuSi3 (silicon-bronze) filler wire, ~1.6 mm, between the HX340LAD roof and body-side aperture (both GI Z100 per EN 10346), producing a smooth wetted seam needing no trim strip; the brazed fillet is Class-A after clear-coat. Brazing at ~1000 C wets both zinc-coated sheets without melting the base steel, giving a continuous water-tight seam superior to intermittent spot welds and removing the ditch moulding and its clips from the aperture region. It also cuts sealant length around the aperture and stiffens the roof rail for door-seal load.

ideaData.benchmarkReference: Laser brazing of roof-to-body-side seams with CuSi3 is established mass-production practice (widely used by Volkswagen Group including Golf and Audi models since the early 2000s); mechanism named, no new programme claimed.
ideaData.materialGrade: CuSi3 silicon-bronze filler ~1.6 mm; roof/body-side HX340LAD, GI Z100 per EN 10346

title: Integrated door-seal-on-panel two-shot moulding deletes applied weatherstrip
description: Removes the applied weatherstrip and its labour-intensive fitting, cutting water-leak rework Baseline door aperture seal is a separate EPDM extruded-and-corner-moulded weatherstrip with a metal carrier or clip-on retention lip, hand-fitted around the flange (~2-3 min/door labour, plus corner-vulcanised joints). Replace on plastic/composite tailgate and frameless door modules by co-moulding a TPV sealing bulb (Santoprene-class, Shore ~55-65A) directly onto the PP-based closure panel or carrier in a two-shot / overmould tool, so the seal is a captive feature with no clips, carrier or applied step. The TPV chemically/mechanically bonds to the PP substrate during the second shot, giving a leak path with zero assembly variation versus a clipped extrusion. Compression set of the TPV bulb is tuned to seal-closing load; corners are moulded, not spliced.

costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~€8-12 EPDM strip + ~€3-4 fitting labour saved per closure × 200k, net of added second-shot cycle cost

ideaData.riskNotes: TPV compression set and long-term sealing load over 10 yr / thermal cycling must be validated vs EPDM benchmark. Two-shot bond integrity (peel) needs adhesion testing. Repairability worse — damaged seal means panel replacement; scope to service-replaceable zones only.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Two-shot TPV seals moulded onto plastic closure panels are established practice in sunroof frames and encapsulated tailgate/fixed glass modules (e.g. Webasto, Saint-Gobain Sekurit encapsulation); mechanism named, no specific programme claimed.
ideaData.materialGrade: TPV sealing bulb (Santoprene-class, Shore ~55-65A) over PP-based substrate; two-shot / overmould tooling

ideaData.benchmarkReference: Domain-controller consolidation of low-duty closure actuators over LIN is established E/E-architecture practice (body-domain controllers integrating latch/cinch drivers, 2010s onward); mechanism named, no specific programme claimed.

title: Snap-fit datumed door trim-and-carrier cassette eliminates screwed fixings
description: Tool-free snap-fit install and integrated carrier remove fasteners, sub-parts and the torque-verify station Baseline door trim panel and wet/dry barrier attach via 8-14 self-tapping screws plus fir-tree clips, hand-driven at trim line (~90-120 s/door) with torque verification. Replace with a single injection-moulded PP + 20% talc (PP-T20, MFR ~10-13 g/10min) carrier integrating vapour barrier, speaker baffle, wire routing and armrest substrate, retained to moulded-in door-inner catches by 6 self-aligning cantilever snap-fits (30° lead-in chamfer, 0.6-0.8 mm interference, audible detent) plus 2 M5 service screws at the high-load armrest zone. Snap beam deflection tuned to insertion force <60 N with retention >250 N via ~5° asymmetric hook return angle, giving tool-free single-motion install while meeting BSR pull-off and 0.5 mm gap/flush class.

title: Bolt-on subframe with self-piercing rivet crush spacers vs full weld
description: Eliminates distortion-driven machining and reduces weld consumables/energy Baseline front subframe is a 4-piece welded box in HC340LA/S355MC with ~2.8 m MAG weld across 6 fixturing stations; weld distortion forces a downstream coining/reaming of the 4 body-mount bores (H8 to body). Proposal: replace 2 shear-loaded internal weld seams with self-piercing rivets (Böllhoff/Henrob C-type, 5.3 mm dia, boron-steel ~1500 MPa, zinc-flake coated) joining the stamped shells, and press-fit hardened DC04 (case-hardened ~600 HV) crush tubes into the mount bores as datum, so bore tolerance is set by the tube not weld position. Removes weld thermal distortion at datum, deletes coining, cuts weld length ~40%. SPR joints carry in-plane shear/peel elastically without HAZ softening of the S355 near the mount; the pressed tube fixes bore concentricity mechanically.

costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~€5.50/unit machining+rework delete + €3/unit weld consumable/energy delete − €2.50/unit rivet+adhesive cost ≈ €6/unit × 200k
