ideaData.benchmarkReference: SPR in mixed-material body-in-white is established practice (Audi Space Frame, JLR aluminium bodies, 2010s); steel-subframe seam application stated as established mechanism, no specific programme claimed.
ideaData.materialGrade: HC340LA / S355MC shells; C5.3 boron-steel SPR (~1500 MPa); DC04 crush tubes case-hardened; class-10.9 body-mount bolts

title: Structural-adhesive-bonded e-axle carrier crossmember deleting brackets
description: Removes bracket part numbers, fasteners and machining Baseline e-axle carrier mounts motor/gearbox via 3 separate cast AlSi10Mg brackets bolted to a welded steel crossmember, each needing 2 machined faces and 4 M10 bolts. Proposal: consolidate into a single AlSi10Mg-T7 (Silafont-36 equivalent, HPDC, ~180 MPa yield) crossmember with the three motor interfaces cast net-shape, and replace 2 of 4 bolts per interface with a crash-durable 2K toughened epoxy bead (e.g. Dow BETAMATE / Henkel Teroson class, ~30 MPa lap shear, 0.2-0.3 mm bondline) carrying static and NVH load, retaining 2 M10 bolts for peel/service. The adhesive spreads powertrain torque-reaction and 1st-order motor whine over a large bonded area, lowering local stress and damping bracket resonance; net-shape casting removes mating-face machining. Bolt count 12→6; 3 bracket part numbers deleted.

ideaData.benchmarkReference: Crash-durable structural epoxy bonding of powertrain/chassis interfaces is established practice (Dow BETAMATE, Henkel Teroson families); no specific OEM programme claimed.
ideaData.materialGrade: AlSi10Mg-T7 HPDC crossmember; 2K crash-durable toughened epoxy (~30 MPa lap shear); M10 class-10.9 retained bolts

title: Common corner module across left/right via handed-insert datum scheme
description: One tool and one machining set replace handed pairs; inventory halved Baseline front corner module carries separate LH and RH part numbers for knuckle, splash shield and brake-hose bracket because the caliper and ABS-sensor bosses are mirror-image, doubling tooling, PPAP and line-side inventory. Proposal: redesign the GJS-450-10 knuckle casting symmetric about the wheel plane with both caliper-boss pairs cast in, and localise handedness to a single low-cost pressed-steel handed adapter plate and a keyed sensor grommet. One knuckle tool serves both sides; the machining line indexes off symmetric datums and only the adapter is handed. Physics: brake torque and steer loads are symmetric about the hub axis, so a symmetric casting is structurally valid; handedness is purely packaging (hose routing, sensor cable exit) and can be pushed to a €1-class stamped part.

title: Marriage-line torque-to-yield delete via press-fit dowel subframe indexing
description: Removes an assembly station and reduces geometry-driven rework/warranty Baseline subframe-to-body attach uses 4 torque-to-yield (TTY) bolts plus a separate 2-pin locating-dowel op and a vision check to hit chassis geometry at final assembly, adding cycle time and a scrap/rework loop when geometry drifts. Proposal: integrate 2 self-locating tapered press-fit dowel bushings (case-hardened 16MnCr5, ~700 HV surface, ~3-5° taper) directly into the subframe crush tubes so the subframe self-datums to the body pilot holes as it rises on the marriage lift, converting the 4 TTY bolts to reusable class-10.9 M12 bolts against a hard geometric stop. Taper engagement forces XY position mechanically before clamp, removing dependence on robot placement accuracy and on bolt-yield to set clamp; geometry becomes a pass/fail of pilot fit, not a measured variable.

ideaData.materialGrade: 16MnCr5 case-hardened tapered dowel bushings; class-10.9 M12 reusable bolts replacing TTY

title: Rear subframe from roll-formed closed profiles vs stampings
description: Cuts engineered scrap and heavy draw tooling, enables down-gauge Baseline rear subframe is a welded box of deep-drawn HC420LA half-shells (upper/lower) needing large draw dies, blank-holders and trimming, then a long perimeter seam weld. Proposal: roll-form then laser-weld closed tubular side rails in CR420LA HSLA (yield ~420 MPa) at high line speed, joined to two stamped HC420LA nodes at spring/damper seats with MIG only at the 4 nodes. Roll-forming runs constant-section rails continuously with near-zero scrap vs ~25-35% engineered scrap on deep-draw; the closed section gives higher torsional stiffness per kg so gauge drops 3.0→2.5 mm. A closed roll-formed section resists torsion far better than an open/half-shell weldment of equal mass, allowing down-gauge while holding subframe modal targets (typ. >200 Hz).

ideaData.materialGrade: CR420LA HSLA roll-formed/laser-welded rails (2.5 mm); HC420LA stamped nodes

title: Integrate ABS/damper wiring into subframe as clip-in moulded channel
description: Removes weld tabs and manual clips, cuts chafe warranty Baseline corner/subframe wiring (ABS sensor, EPB, air-damper, ride-height) uses discrete P-clips, welded bracket tabs and hand-routed harness branches — a labour and warranty (chafe/BSR) hotspot. Proposal: mould a single glass-filled PA6-GF30 (30% glass, ~180 MPa tensile, -40/+120°C rated) routing channel that snap-clips into pre-punched lances on the subframe, carrying all corner services with integrated strain-relief and EPDM grommet seats, delivered pre-populated as a module. A one-piece polymer channel fixes cable geometry deterministically, eliminating chafe against metal and the tolerance stack of many small brackets; snap-fit lances (0.6-1.0 mm interference) replace welded tabs, removing weld ops and their distortion. Consider PA6-GF30 with heat-stabiliser for underbody thermal/UV exposure.

title: Cast-in cathodic e-coat masking bosses deleting post-machine plugs
description: Removes manual masking labour and post-coat re-machining Baseline aluminium/steel subframe modules need selective masking of ~8-12 threaded and bearing-bore features before cataphoretic (CED) e-coat, done with hand-installed rubber plugs/caps (labour) or post-coat re-machining of coated threads (tool wear, chips). Proposal: design sacrificial break-off masking bosses and self-clearing thread reliefs so datum/thread features shed coating by geometry (drain reliefs, sharp 45° lead-in that thins film below thread engagement) or are protected by one reusable integral snap-cap per carrier. E-coat throwing power and film-build (typ. 18-25 µm CED) follow Faraday-cage and drainage geometry; designing lead-in chamfers and drain slots keeps functional flanks below ~8 µm spec film, so no manual masking or re-tap is needed.

Long-term durability at -40/+90°C thermal cycling and moisture ingress needs corrosion testing (trapped water risk). Fill repeatability and void detection via weigh-check. ideaData.benchmarkReference: Cavity-injected structural/acoustic foam is established BIW practice (expandable baffles/pillar foams); chassis-subframe cavity application stated as mechanism, no programme named.

title: Poka-yoke pre-toe subframe: alignment-neutral corner module marriage
description: Trades recurring alignment labour and eccentric hardware for one-time machining capability investment. Baseline sets front toe/camber at end-of-line via 4 eccentric cam bolts (M12, 10.9) plus toothed lock washers per vehicle, needing an alignment rack and skilled labour. Proposal net-machines the corner module's lower-arm pivot bores and knuckle-to-strut interface to IT7 position tolerance referenced to the wheel-bearing axis, holding static toe within ±6' and camber ±10' as-built ('build-to-alignment') using fixed shoulder bolts. Key characteristics (bore centre-distance, knuckle mounting angle) are machined to Cpk>1.67 and 100%-gauged on an in-line CMM once per station cycle to keep the tolerance loop closed. Adjustment hardware exists only to absorb stack-up; tightening machining capability on 2-3 characteristics is cheaper per vehicle than recurring rack time plus eccentric hardware

ideaData.benchmarkReference: Non-adjustable ('build-to-alignment') front suspension is established practice on high-capability assembly lines; no specific programme claimed.
ideaData.materialGrade: M12 x1.5 property-class 10.9 shoulder bolts; knuckle EN-GJS-500-7 ductile iron or forged 38MnVS6; bore tolerance IT7/H7

title: Shared brake corner: common caliper carrier both axles via spacer
description: Halves brake-corner part numbers, concentrating purchase volume to move down the supplier cost curve. Baseline uses distinct front and rear caliper-carrier/knuckle brake interfaces, each with its own GJS-500 bracket casting, mounting bolt pattern and pad-abutment geometry, doubling brake-corner part numbers per vehicle. Proposal standardises one caliper-carrier casting and one caliper family across front and rear corners, accommodating the larger front rotor via a machined GJS-500 radial mount spacer that shifts the common carrier outboard. Economics: caliper and carrier castings are dominated by tooling and PPAP fixed cost per part number; collapsing four corner variants to one carrier plus two spacer thicknesses roughly halves brake-corner SKUs, boosting purchased volume per part and cutting per-unit price via the supplier's cost curve. Pad commonisation follows, shrinking service inve

Corrosion at spacer interface managed by geometry/coating. Confirm common caliper piston area still meets rear brake-balance and EPB clamp on both axles.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Front/rear brake-hardware commonisation via mounting adapters is established VA/VE practice; no specific programme claimed.

title: One-shot MIG-brazed subframe nodes replacing GMA weld plus sealer
description: Removes distortion rework and a seam-sealer operation while improving joint corrosion life. Baseline joins the thin-gauge (1.5-2.0 mm) HSLA S420MC stampings of the subframe at node junctions with conventional GMA (MIG) welding, which burns through thin edges, distorts the node and demands post-weld seam sealer against corrosion in the lap crevice. Proposal switches the thin-gauge node seams to MIG-brazing with a CuAl8 (CuSi3 alternative) bronze filler at ~1000°C, well below steel melt, wetting the joint without fusing the base metal. Physics: lower heat input cuts distortion (less rework/fixturing), the brazed fillet self-seals the crevice removing a sealer station, and the galvanised zinc coating is largely preserved at the joint, improving corrosion life without post-treatment. Braze fillet geometry also reduces stress concentration versus a burnt-edge MIG toe, aiding fatigue.

Slightly slower deposition offset by fewer rework loops. Preserves galv coating, may allow lighter e-coat prep.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Removes distortion rework and a seam-sealer operation while improving joint corrosion life.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: Seam sealer material+station €3.10/veh + distortion rework avg €1.90/veh = €5.00/veh; less braze wire premium €0.60/veh → €4.40/veh × 200k = €0.88M

ideaData.riskNotes: Brazed joint static strength lower than fused weld — restrict to shear-loaded thin-gauge seams, keep GMA/structural adhesive on primary load nodes. Validate fatigue and dissimilar-metal galvanic behaviour of bronze filler on steel in salt spray. Braze porosity control via gas purity and edge cleanliness; process window narrower than MIG.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: MIG-brazing of galvanised thin-gauge steel is established body/chassis practice for distortion and corrosion control; no specific programme claimed.

title: Flow-formed tube damper body replaces DOM tube with machined ends
description: Eliminates weld and its inspection, cuts steel mass and scrap Baseline twin-tube damper outer body is a DOM E235 (1.0308) seamless tube cut to length, with a separately stamped/MIG-welded base cup and machined rod-guide seat, needing a weld station plus post-weld leak test. Proposal: single-piece flow-formed (rotary-swaged) body from a C22 (1.0402) preform, where three CNC rollers extrude the wall from ~3.0 mm to 1.6 mm ±0.05 mm over the working stroke while integrally forming the closed base and necked rod-guide land. Cold work raises yield ~30% (from ~340 to >440 MPa), permitting wall thinning without losing burst margin at the 25-bar gas-charge working pressure. Bore concentricity holds <0.03 mm TIR, improving seal life and cutting honing-station scrap. Process runs at 3-roller reverse-flow-form with a hardened D2 mandrel.

costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~€0.9 weld+cup+leaktest removed + ~€0.6 material saved (0.4 kg × €1.5/kg) per body × 800,000 corner-units (2/car × 400k)

Base-integral radius is a stress concentrator — validate with strain-gauged salt-spray-aged samples. Mitigate via 100% wall-thickness ultrasonic gauging inline.

ideaData.materialGrade: C22 (1.0402) preform, flow-formed wall 1.6 mm ±0.05 mm, yield >440 MPa post-cold-work; replaces DOM E235 (1.0308)

title: Bonded-in-rubber bush deletes press-fit outer sleeve on control arm
description: Removes a part number and a precision machining op Baseline front lower control-arm rear bush is a three-part hydrobush: steel inner tube, NR/SBR element vulcanised to inner and to a drawn E235 (1.0308) outer sleeve, then pressed into the machined arm eye at ~0.12 mm interference. This needs the outer sleeve, an arm eye finish-bored/honed to H7, and a calibrated press with retention-force monitoring. Proposal: direct-bond vulcanise the NR/SBR (~55 ShA) element into an as-cast EN-GJS-500-7 or as-forged arm eye whose bore is grit-blasted to Sa 2.5 / Ra 3-6 µm and Chemlok 205 primer + 220 topcoat applied, curing the rubber in situ at ~160-180 °C against the primed bore, deleting the outer sleeve. Radial stiffness is tuned by moulded void geometry rather than sleeve prestress; bore tolerance can relax to H11 since no interference is required.

title: Tailor-rolled blank stamped control arm replaces uniform DP600
description: Removes over-thick steel from low-stress web Baseline stamped lower control arm is blanked from constant 3.0 mm DP600 (HCT590X) dual-phase, formed in a 4-stage progressive die; uniform gauge is set by the ball-joint boss zone, leaving the mid-span over-thick. Proposal: use a tailor-rolled blank (TRB) of DP600 with a flexible-rolled profile — 3.2 mm at ball-joint and bush bosses tapering to 2.2 mm across the low-stress web — so mass follows the FE stress field. Flexible rolling produces a smooth thickness transition with no weld line (unlike tailor-welded blanks), preserving draw formability (A80 ≥ 20%). Transition gradient held to ~1:100 to avoid strain concentration; net section modulus retained at bosses while removing ~18% blank mass. Die tryout must accommodate the varying-gauge blank in the binder.

Thickness-transition slope must not fall inside a fatigue-critical radius; validate with strain-gauged full-arm 2M-cycle fatigue and a corrosion-perforation check where thin. title: Austempered ductile iron knuckle replaces forged steel
description: Near-net casting removes forging and cuts chip loss Baseline rear steering knuckle on a heavier RWD variant is drop-forged from C70S6 / 38MnVS6 microalloyed steel, then extensively machined (spindle bore, caliper mounts, hub face) — forging plus ~55% material-to-chip loss. Proposal: cast the knuckle in austempered ductile iron (ADI) grade EN-GJS-1050-6 (ISO 17804), near-net from a green-sand mould with cores for the strut and caliper bosses, then austemper (austenitise ~900°C, salt-quench isothermal at ~370°C). ADI reaches ~1050 MPa UTS with ~6% elongation at ~7.1 g/cm³ — roughly 10% lighter than steel per unit strength and castable to near-net, cutting machining stock by ~40%. Fatigue strength rivals forged steel due to the ausferrite matrix's crack-arrest behaviour and compressive surface stress from graphite nodules.

Machining reduced to spindle bore and mount faces. Casting cell + austemper capex significant but amortised across knuckle family.

costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~€4–5/knuckle (forging+machining delta) × 2 knuckles × 200,000, net of austemper cost ~€0.8

ideaData.riskNotes: Nodularity (>85%) and matrix ausferrite must be tight — poor casting soundness kills fatigue in this safety part. Validate per casting-cavity with X-ray/ultrasonic 100%, plus strut-corner 2M-cycle and pothole abuse. Machinability of ADI is lower — use CBN tooling. Mitigate porosity via riser design and process SPC.
dfmaPrinciples: Consolidate part family on one process
ideaData.benchmarkReference: ADI for suspension/chassis components is established (widely used for control arms and knuckles in commercial and passenger vehicles); no single programme named.
ideaData.materialGrade: EN-GJS-1050-6 ADI

title: Tapered single-leaf composite spring replaces steel coil + isolators
description: Consolidates spring + 2 isolators + coating into one moulding Baseline rear coil is hot-coiled from 12.5 mm 54SiCr6 (SAE 9254) valve-grade wire, shot-peened, powder-coated, with stamped upper seat, moulded rubber lower isolator and bump-stop cup. Proposal: a transverse or corner-mounted mono-leaf spring in E-glass/epoxy (E-glass unidirectional roving ~60% Vf, epoxy matrix, Tg >120 °C) filament-wound or compression-moulded to a tapered thickness profile. GFRP stores ~4-5x the elastic strain energy per unit mass of spring steel (σ²/2Eρ), so the leaf weighs ~40-60% less and its integrally moulded eyes/pads absorb the isolator function. Rate is tuned by thickness taper rather than coil count; design working strain kept below ~1.2% for fatigue. Eliminates coiling, peening, coating and two rubber parts.

Exploit high specific strain energy of composite

title: Nitrogen-free monotube: reduced-friction low-pressure gas charge
description: Removes chrome line, simplifies seal, cuts friction Baseline monotube uses a 25-30 bar N2 charge behind a floating piston, needing a heavy-lip main rod seal and a hard-chromed Ø11 mm rod at ~0.8 µm Ra to survive seal preload, plus a robust seal pack; high gas force adds parasitic rod-out friction. Proposal: cut the charge to ~8-10 bar using a PTFE-banded (glass-filled PTFE, e.g. 15% GF) floating piston that tolerates lower pre-charge without cavitation across the tuned damping range, paired with a DLC (a-C:H) coated rod (coating ~2-3 µm, HV ~1500) replacing hard chrome. Lower seal preload permits a single-lip PTFE-faced seal (bronze/PTFE-filled) and cuts breakaway friction ~30%, improving NVH while removing the seal pack complexity and eliminating the Cr(VI) plating line under REACH.

title: Roll-formed & laser-notched anti-roll bar link tube vs machined bar
description: Tube carries axial load with minimal mass; near-no machining Baseline anti-roll bar drop-link body is machined from Ø20 mm 42CrMo4 bar with turned ball-stud sockets at each end, or die-cast in AlSi10Mg then machined. Proposal: replace with a roll-formed closed-section tube of high-strength S700MC (700 MPa yield thermomechanically-rolled steel), laser-cut to length and end-notched, with cold-headed ball studs press-and-swaged into formed sockets rather than machined pockets. The closed tube carries the pure tension/compression link load with far less material than a solid bar (link sees axial load only, so a thin-wall tube is ideal), and roll-forming + laser is a continuous high-rate process versus bar turning. Mass drops ~35% and machining is largely eliminated.

costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~€1.5/link (machining+material delta) × 2 links × 300,000, net of swage tooling amortisation

title: Overmoulded rubber-to-metal bush cured in-situ on control arm eye
description: Removes a stamped part and a press-fit assembly step from every arm. Baseline lower-arm bush is a separate cartridge: SAE 1010 inner tube, NR/SBR 55 ShA rubber, DC04 outer sleeve vulcanised together, then pressed at 15-25 kN into the arm eye with retention-force gauging. Proposal: directly inject-and-vulcanise the rubber onto a pre-phosphated (zinc-phosphate) SAE 1010 inner sleeve inside the machined arm eye, the eye bore itself becoming the outer bond surface via Chemlok 205 primer + 220 topcoat, cured ~160-180 °C. This deletes the DC04 outer sleeve, the press-fit operation and the retention-force test. Bond shear >4 MPa replaces mechanical interference for radial retention. Bore tolerance relaxes from H8 press-fit to H11, removing a reaming pass; radial/axial/torsional rates tuned by cavity void geometry rather than sleeve wall.

Adds one rubber injection/vulcanisation station (~90–120 s cure) with arm-eye tooling. Net one station removed at final assembly; scrap risk shifts to bond-line prep.

costSavingPotential.percentage: 8-12% of the bush+assembly cost of the arm

title: Two-piece flow-drill-screw knuckle-to-strut joint deletes machined flange
description: Removes the most machining-intensive feature family on the knuckle. Baseline cast GJS-500-7 or forged steel knuckle carries an integrally cast strut-mount boss requiring a milled seat and two drilled/tapped M12 holes for the strut clamp — three machining stations. Proposal: split the strut interface into a separate cold-formed C70 steel bracket joined to the knuckle by flow-drill screws (FDS, e.g. EJOT Flowform) into a boss with as-cast bore, eliminating tapping and the milled seat by using a self-forming thread bushing under the FDS. The knuckle boss is left in the as-cast/near-net-forged state (no finish machining). Joint clamp load ~30 kN developed by the FDS thermal-flow bushing, adequate for strut Fz and steering moment reaction. This decouples the strut-mount tolerance stack from the wheel-bearing bore, allowing the bearing bore to be the only precision-machined feature.

costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~€5.50 machining+tooling amort removed per knuckle − €1.20 FDS+bracket added = €4.30 × 300k ≈ €1.3M

Loosening under reversed steering loads is the durability risk — validate with block-load fatigue and thread-form pull-out. Corrosion at the dissimilar joint needs sealed e-coat.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Flow-drill screw joining is established BIW/chassis practice; application to knuckle strut interface stated as mechanism, not a named programme.

title: Induction-hardened spot on damper rod deletes hard chrome full-length
description: Eliminates a hazardous, capital-heavy plating line. Baseline damper piston rod is C45/Ck45 (1.1191) ground and full-length hard-chrome plated (~20 µm Cr over 100% of stroke) for wear/corrosion at the rod-guide seal — a slow, Cr(VI)-hazardous line with rinse/effluent cost and thickness variation. Proposal: replace hard chrome with QPQ nitrocarburising (Tenifer/salt-bath) plus a top oxide, giving a compound layer HV >600 and integrated corrosion resistance (>200 h NSS) without electroplating. For cost-critical variants, induction-harden only the seal-contact band and DLC-coat it. The substrate can shift to leaner microalloyed 38MnVS6 (no separate quench-and-temper) since surface hardness comes from diffusion, not bulk hardening. Post-QPQ polish preserves Ra 0.05-0.10 µm for seal life.

costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: €1.80 chrome+effluent per rod − €0.90 QPQ+polish = €0.90 × 1M plus avoided effluent capex/opex ~€0.4M/yr

ideaData.benchmarkReference: Nitrocarburising/QPQ of damper and shock rods is established practice as a chrome replacement; mechanism cited, not a named programme.
ideaData.materialGrade: 38MnVS6 microalloyed bar with QPQ nitrocarburise + oxide, compound layer HV>600; replaces C45 (1.1191) + ~20 µm hard chrome

title: Hollow forged control arm via back-extrusion vs solid I-section
description: Cuts billet mass — the dominant cost of forged Al arms — while adding lightweighting value. Baseline aluminium lower control arm is hot-forged EN AW-6082-T6 as a solid I-section web to react bending, then machined; the I-web leaves a mass-inefficient solid core. Proposal: forge a closed hollow box section using mandrel-assisted back-extrusion (or forge-then-close via electromagnetic forming) so the arm becomes a thin-wall (4-5 mm) hollow beam with the same bending stiffness at ~15% lower mass, since material sits at maximum radius from the neutral axis. A 4 mm wall in 6082-T6 gives section modulus equal to the solid I at lower cross-section area. Less forging stock per part directly cuts billet cost — the dominant driver for Al arms. Ball-joint and bush bosses remain solid local upsets; T6 solution + age after forming to restore ~290 MPa yield.

costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: 0.55 kg billet saved × €3.20/kg Al + yield = ~€1.90/arm net of tooling amort × 250k ≈ €1.2M

ideaData.materialGrade: EN AW-6082-T6 forged, 4-5 mm hollow wall, yield ~290 MPa post-T6; same base alloy as solid I-section baseline

title: Hollow cold-wound coil spring from tube vs solid bar
description: Removes near-dead-weight spring core at equal performance. Baseline front coil is cold-wound from solid oil-tempered SiCr wire (54SiCr6 / JIS SWOSC-V) ~13-14 mm dia, shot-peened and pre-set. Torsional stress in a coil peaks at the surface and is near-zero at the wire core, so the core carries little load yet full mass. Proposal: wind from a seamless cold-drawn SiCr tube (~16 mm OD x 3.5 mm wall) to remove the low-stress core — ~30-40% mass reduction at equal rate and stress. The new inner bore surface must be defect-controlled via internal shot-peening or autofrettage of the bore, since a second stress surface is created. Same coiling machine with a tube-capable mandrel; same low-temperature stress relief (~230 °C) and pre-set. Net raw-material mass, the spring cost driver, drops sharply. OD/wall ratio kept below ~5 to avoid ovalisation during coiling.

ideaData.materialGrade: Seamless cold-drawn SiCr spring tube (54SiCr6 / SWOSC-V grade), ~16 mm OD x 3.5 mm wall; replaces ~13-14 mm solid SiCr wire

title: Deep-drawn steel damper base cup replaces machined forged eye
description: Converts a machined/welded lug into a single stamped-and-welded part. Baseline damper lower mount is a machined C22E/S355J2 forging or welded machined eye, needing bush-bore turning and MIG welding with weld inspection. Proposal: form the lower mount as a deep-drawn cup in DC04 (Rm 270-350 MPa) or HC340LA microalloyed steel (min yield 340 MPa), 2.5-3.0 mm wall, projection- or capacitor-discharge-welded to the flow-formed tube base. Draw the bush bore to net IT11 with the draw punch, integrating spring-seat lip and bush pocket in a single draw. HC340LA is preferred where axial load demands higher yield; DC04 where deep draw ratio governs. The 2.5-3.0 mm wall carries axial damper load in shear/bearing rather than as a solid machined lug, eliminating the forging, bore turning, and converting MIG to a single low-heat CD weld with no post-weld machining.

costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~€1.50 forge+turn+MIG per unit − €0.70 stamp+CDweld = €0.80 × 800k, less die amort ≈ €1.1M

ideaData.benchmarkReference: Stamped-and-welded damper end fittings are established high-volume shock-absorber practice; stated as mechanism, no named programme.
ideaData.materialGrade: DC04 (EN 10130) or HC340LA (EN 10268), 2.5-3.0 mm wall; bush bore to IT11

title: Voided-profile TPV micro-cellular jounce bumper vs cut PU foam
description: Trades a slow reactive-chemistry process for fast thermoplastic moulding with regrind. Baseline jounce/bump stop is moulded microcellular polyurethane (Cellasto-type MPU), a two-component reactive cast-and-cure with long demould and secondary trimming, tuned by density and profile. Proposal: replace with an injection-moulded TPV (e.g. Santoprene 101-73 to 101-87, Shore A 73-87) or moulded TPU (e.g. Elastollan 1185A, Shore A 85) using an engineered voided/lattice cross-section that reproduces the progressive force-displacement curve mechanically via wall-collapse sequence rather than cellular density. Injection moulding gives seconds-scale cycle vs minutes for reactive PU, no mix-head/isocyanate handling, and 100% runner regrind. Progressive rate is designed into rib-collapse geometry, tunable per variant with cavity insert changes rather than new PU formulations.

costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~€1.20 MPU cast part − €0.65 IM TPV part = €0.55 × ~2 bumpers × 600k ≈ €0.66M plus EHS avoidance

ideaData.riskNotes: TPV compression-set and creep under sustained curb load differ from MPU — validate long-term set at 80°C and −40°C impact energy absorption over 100k full-jounce events. Noise/harshness (thunk) on hard contact must match MPU damping; tune lattice and durometer.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: TPE/TPV bump stops are established in some chassis and NVH applications; cited as mechanism, no named programme.
ideaData.materialGrade: TPV Santoprene 101-series (Shore A 73-87) or TPU Elastollan 1185A (Shore A 85)

title: Cast-in stainless wear-face grey-iron disc via bi-metal centrifugal insert
timeToImplement: 14-20 months incl. dyno and field validation
description: Down-specs core iron, cuts unsprung mass, and collapses corrosion-judder warranty returns on rear axle. Baseline vented rear disc is monolithic EN-GJL-250 grey iron, ~9.5 kg, machined all-over with two turning + two grinding passes to hold DTV <8 µm and thickness variation <10 µm. Friction-face carbides drive corrosion-clawback and warranty judder. Proposal: down-spec the core to EN-GJL-200 and apply a corrosion-resistant wear layer to the friction band only — either HVOF-sprayed Fe-Cr-C (e.g. FeCr13-type, ~150 µm, >55 HRC) or laser-clad 420 martensitic stainless (~150-200 µm), then ground to final thickness. The passivated Cr-rich face resists corrosion-induced DTV, allowing the disc to run thinner (28→26 mm) and lighter. Physics: corrosion pitting, not thermal fade, dominates rear-disc scrap; the Cr-rich face removes pit-nucleation sites that cause pad snag and low-speed judder.

ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Replaces bar-turning cell (4-5 ops) with MIM feedstock moulding + debind + sinter + single OD grind. Net stations reduced at the piston line; scrap chips eliminated (near-zero material waste vs ~55% chip loss on turned bar). Requires MIM tool (~€90k) and supplier qualification; no plant capex if outsourced.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Collapses a multi-op turned/assembled piston into one net-shape sintered part with near-zero chip loss.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: €2.40/piston machining+assembly saving × 2 front pistons × 300k = €1.44M, plus material yield gain (55% chip loss removed on ~0.4 kg bar) ~€0.6M

ideaData.riskNotes: Sinter dimensional scatter on the sealing land and residual porosity are the risks; control with HIP-optional densification, 100% air-decay leak test, and seal-drag/retraction validation to FMVSS 135 pressure cycling. Corrosion validated by ASTM B117; boot-groove fatigue by pressure pulsation to 1M cycles.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: MIM 17-4PH for net-shape hydraulic components is established practice in fluid-power; brake-piston application by mechanism, not a named programme.
ideaData.materialGrade: MIM 17-4PH stainless (MPIF 35), ≥96% density, H900 temper; 2.5 mm wall

Net final-assembly time down on the fluid side; supplier sub-assembles the EMB. Plant fluid-fill capacity freed for other lines.

costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: €9-15/car process+hose+fluid saving (fill/bleed cycle-time, 2 hoses, hard line, fluid) × 200k, net of EMB actuator premium partly offset by deleted hydraulics

Cold-temp screw efficiency and corrosion of the drive train require sealed housing and grease validation.

ideaData.materialGrade: GJS-500-7 EMB housing; PMSM + ball-screw drive vs hydraulic caliper

title: Composite (Al-MMC) rear disc enabled by regen-limited thermal duty
annualSaving: €1.5M–€2.6M at 180,000 cars/yr (value of ~10 kg/car secondary mass)
description: Halves rear rotating/unsprung mass enabling secondary lightweighting; range/efficiency co-benefit. Baseline rear disc is GJL-250 grey iron, ~9.5 kg. In a regen-braking BEV the rear disc peak temperature rarely exceeds ~350 °C because the e-axle absorbs the high-energy stops. Proposal: aluminium metal-matrix composite disc — AA6061 reinforced with 20% SiC particulate (or an Al-Si hypereutectic with a plasma-sprayed friction face) — sized only for the emergency/fade-fallback duty. Physics: MMC thermal conductivity (~180 W/m·K vs iron ~50) spreads heat fast and the low density cuts disc mass ~55% (to ~4.3 kg), a large unsprung/rotating-inertia win. The friction face receives a hard ceramic/Fe coating to survive pad contact; the low sustained thermal load in a regen architecture is what makes Al viable where it fails on a conventional car.

Deletes iron scrap stream; adds coating station. New tooling for Al process; iron pattern retired. Coating booth capex shared with other coated-disc programmes.

costSavingPotential.percentage: Weight-driven; range and secondary-mass value 10-14% system

title: Bolt-together sheet-steel caliper carrier replaces machined cast bracket
description: Eliminates casting and most bracket machining; higher material utilisation via fine-blank strip nesting. Baseline front caliper carrier is EN-GJS-500-7 nodular iron, sand-cast then CNC-machined (4-5 ops) on abutment faces, guide-pin bores and bolt seats to hold pad-abutment parallelism <0.1 mm. Proposal: a fine-blanked and formed high-strength steel carrier from two plates in S700MC (min yield 700 MPa, EN 10149-2) or DP780 (yield ~500 MPa, UTS ≥780 MPa), 6-8 mm gauge, joined by projection welding, with pressed-in hardened (58-62 HRC bearing steel) guide bushings replacing bored pin bores. Physics/economics: fine-blanking yields a sheared edge to IT9 directly, eliminating abutment-face machining, and DP780/S700MC carry the caliper drag torque in shear across the bolt pattern. Guide-pin function moves to the pressed bushings, removing bore machining.

Cycle time per part drops sharply; casting scrap and CNC chips eliminated. Requires fine-blank tool (~€180k) and weld fixture. Foundry demand for the bracket removed entirely.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Eliminates casting and most bracket machining; higher material utilisation via fine-blank strip nesting.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: €3.20/bracket (casting+machining vs blank+weld) × 2 front × 250k = €1.6M, plus tooling amortisation and scrap-value gain

ideaData.riskNotes: Fatigue at the weld and abutment wear/brinelling are the risks; mitigate with hardened abutment insert, weld-nugget shear validation, and corner-load fatigue to 1M cycles at max drag torque. ideaData.benchmarkReference: Fine-blanked/stamped brake carriers are established in cost-optimised drum-in-hat and light-vehicle applications; mechanism proven, no named programme.
ideaData.materialGrade: S700MC (EN 10149-2) or DP780, 6-8 mm; pressed-in 58-62 HRC bearing-steel bushings

costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: Caliper simplification ~€4.20/side + disc vented→solid iron & machining ~€2.90/side = €7.10 × 2 rear corners × 300k = €4.26M.

ideaData.riskNotes: Must validate ECE-R13H fade and failed-regen 0.6g stops without brake-fluid vaporisation on solid disc — thermocouple the disc to <450°C peak. Confirm EPB clamp integrates on single-piston body. Risk if platform later fits higher-power rear motor with less regen headroom; gate to regen-guaranteed variants only.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Solid-disc single-piston rear corners on regen-heavy BEVs are established practice; the caliper downsizing to regen thermal duty is the mechanism, not a named programme.
ideaData.materialGrade: Solid disc EN-GJL-150, 320×11 mm; single 42 mm piston floating caliper

title: Cold-formed steel piston with rolled seal groove replaces machined
description: Converts chip-making turning to near-zero-scrap forming, cutting piece cost and material burden. Baseline caliper piston is machined from SAE 1215 free-cutting steel bar (or a phenolic two-part unit), then zinc-nickel plated, with dust-boot and fluid-seal surfaces turned. Proposal: deep-draw the piston cup from DC04 cold-rolled steel (EN 10130, Rm 270-350 MPa) in a 4-stage transfer press, ironing the OD to Ra 0.4 and roll-forming the boot-retention groove, then applying a zinc-flake system (Delta-Tone/Delta-Seal or Geomet 500). Physics: a drawn cup removes no chips — the sealed pressure face is formed, not cut — and the work-hardened ironed wall (~250 HV) gives a stable low-roughness seal-contact band that controls seal roll-back (knock-back and residual drag). A 2.2 mm wall carries the ~10 MPa hoop stress with SF >3. Eliminates bar-stock scrap (turning wastes ~40%) and plating-adhesion

ideaData.riskNotes: Draw-formed groove profile must hold boot under thermal cycling; validate seal drag hysteresis and knock-back to DVP. Steel selection must avoid galvanic couple with Al bore — coating integrity is critical, salt-spray 720 h. Formed pistons less suited to very high bore diameters (>50 mm) due to buckling; scope to ≤44 mm bores.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Deep-drawn steel caliper pistons are established mass-production practice as a lower-cost alternative to turned/phenolic pistons.
ideaData.materialGrade: DC04 (EN 10130), 2.2 mm wall, ironed to Ra 0.4/~250 HV; zinc-flake (Geomet 500) coat

description: Removes an entire redundant power-pack (motor, pump, housing, ECU) and its fill/bleed station. ideaData.title: Shared central brake-by-wire pressure supply for both axles
ideaData.technicalDescription: Baseline redundant brake-by-wire uses a primary integrated pedal-actuator (ESP/IPB) plus a separate redundant secondary hydraulic power pack, each with its own motor, pump, ECU and pressure sensors. Proposal: consolidate to one high-integrity central pressure-supply subassembly — a dual-winding (two independent 3-phase sets) BLDC motor, single ball-screw plunger, dual redundant pressure transducers, and dual lockstep microcontrollers (e.g. ASIL-D-capable lockstep MCU) on one PCBA — feeding a shared 4-channel modulation valve block, with mechanical push-through fallback retained as ultimate backstop. Physics: redundancy comes from diverse duplication INSIDE one actuator (two windings, two sensor chains, two compute lanes on one plunger) rather than two full parallel actuators, meeting ASIL-D availability by internal diversity and deleting the second motor, pump housing and ECU. Cuts one aluminium housing, one motor, and ~40 discrete valve/harness interfaces.
ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Deletes the secondary power-pack assembly line and its EOL hydraulic fill/bleed and calibration station. One larger valve-block casting replaces two; one PCBA with lockstep MCU replaces two ECUs. Corner brake-line routing simplified to one supply source, cutting fitting count and leak-test points.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Removes an entire redundant power-pack (motor, pump, housing, ECU) and its fill/bleed station.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: Secondary power-pack + ECU + assembly/fill ~€35/vehicle net of one uprated central unit ~€40/vehicle = ~€30/vehicle delta × 300k = €9.0M.

ideaData.riskNotes: ASIL-D decomposition must prove single-plunger common-cause failure (seal, gear jam) is covered by mechanical push-through fallback and diverse monitoring — this is the hard sell to functional-safety. Requires full FMEDA and regulator engagement. If push-through deleted, redundancy insufficient. Gate to platforms retaining mechanical backup.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: One-box integrated brake-by-wire with internal redundancy is emerging established practice; the single-plunger dual-lane consolidation is the mechanism, not a named programme.

title: Laser-textured disc friction band deletes bedding and cuts pad wear
description: Substitutes finishing pass, deletes EOL bedding cycle, and extends pad life reducing warranty judder. Baseline EN-GJL-150/GJL-200 (GG15/GG20) vented disc leaves the friction band as-turned (Ra 3–5 µm swirl) plus a sacrificial ZnAl anti-corrosion band coat, relying on a vehicle-side bedding cycle. Proposal: a fibre/nanosecond-pulsed laser-texturing pass (1064 nm, ~20–50 W, 20–100 kHz) writing a cross-hatch of dimples 15–25 µm deep, 60–120 µm dia at ~30% area density onto the band. Physics: the defined topography seats a stable third-body transfer film immediately, deleting controlled bedding-in and cutting run-in DTV; dimples act as debris reservoirs lowering pad abrasive wear ~10–15%, extending pad life and reducing warranty judder claims. It replaces the swirl-turn finishing pass, substituting rather than adding a step on a line that already finishes the band.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Substitutes finishing pass, deletes EOL bedding cycle, and extends pad life reducing warranty judder.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: EOL bedding time+energy ~€1.10/veh + judder warranty accrual reduction ~€2.20/veh + pad-life extension amortised ~€1.50/veh ≈ €4.80 × ~partial adoption; core saving ~€5/veh × 300k weighted.

ideaData.riskNotes: Texture must survive without becoming a corrosion initiation site; validate salt-spray and NVH (dimple-induced squeal) across pad chemistries. Friction coefficient stability over full fade sequence must meet ECE-R90 equivalence. Wear rate must not increase disc replacement interval liabilities. Requires pad-supplier co-development of transfer-layer chemistry.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Laser surface texturing for friction-film control is established tribology and coated-disc practice; applying it to as-machined brake bands to delete bedding is the mechanism, not a named programme.
ideaData.materialGrade: EN-GJL-150 / EN-GJL-200 (GG15/GG20) grey iron disc; nanosecond fibre laser texturing (1064 nm)

title: Aluminium disc hat riveted to iron friction ring replaces monobloc
description: Removes iron from the non-thermal hat, cutting casting mass/machining and unsprung mass, reducing DTV judder claims. Baseline front disc is a monobloc EN-GJL-200 (GG20) grey-iron casting where the mounting hat, which sees no braking heat, is the same iron as the friction ring, adding unsprung mass and transmitting ring thermal growth into the hub/DTV. Proposal: a two-piece semi-floating disc — EN-GJL-200 friction ring mechanically joined to an EN AW-6082-T6 forged/spun aluminium hat via A2-70/A4-80 stainless drive-bobbins or orbital-formed rivets, with radial float clearance ~0.1–0.3 mm. The iron ring does the friction/thermal work; the aluminium hat carries only mounting torque, cutting hat mass ~55% and decoupling ring expansion so coning/DTV under heavy braking falls. Net unsprung mass drop ~1.2–1.6 kg/front corner improving ride and enabling downstream spring/damper tuning economy.

ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Iron casting shrinks to ring-only (less molten iron, faster machining, one chucking op deleted). Adds an Al hat form line and an automated bobbin/rivet joining cell (~20 s/disc). Two-part logistics but each part cheaper to machine. Net corner mass down significantly.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Removes iron from the non-thermal hat, cutting casting mass/machining and unsprung mass, reducing DTV judder claims.
costSavingPotential.percentage: 5-9% of front disc cost plus chassis-tuning value
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: Iron mass/machining saved ~€2.30/disc, DTV warranty reduction ~€1.10/disc, net of Al hat + joining added ~€1.00 = ~€3.10 net delta on premium variants; two front discs × 300k partial adoption.

ideaData.riskNotes: Float clearance must avoid rattle (NVH) yet allow thermal growth — validate bobbin wear and axial lash to 300k km. Galvanic isolation between Al hat and iron ring/steel bobbins required (coating + isolation washers), salt-spray critical. Higher piece complexity than monobloc; only pays where NVH/mass value is captured. Wheel-bearing interface unchanged.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Two-piece semi-floating discs (iron ring + Al hat, bobbin joint) are established practice in performance and premium applications; extension to mainstream regen-duty fronts is the mechanism.
ideaData.materialGrade: Friction ring EN-GJL-200 (GG20); hat EN AW-6082-T6; bobbins A2-70/A4-80 stainless

title: Single dual-range pressure transducer replaces two per corner module
description: Removes a discrete pressure sensor, a sealed port and analogue front-end per modulator. Baseline ESP/IPB modulator carries multiple discrete piezoresistive pressure sensors — a high-range master-cylinder sensor plus separate circuit sensors — each a ceramic-diaphragm SMD part with its own oil-filled port, FKM O-ring and analogue conditioning channel. Proposal: consolidate to one automotive media-resistant piezoresistive MEMS die (e.g. stainless/gel-fill isolated, DBC-mounted) with integrated 14–16-bit ratiometric ADC measuring 0–250 bar and programmable gain giving fine resolution in the sub-30-bar comfort band, plus a diverse redundant channel on the same substrate for ASIL-D. On-die polynomial temperature compensation removes the external conditioning network. Cuts sensor count per modulator, deletes FKM O-ring ports (leak paths) and shrinks the PCBA analogue front-end.

ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Reduces sensor placement and O-ring/port machining in the modulator housing (one fewer bored+sealed port). Simpler PCBA BOM and fewer solder joints. EOL leak-test points reduced. Sensor calibration consolidated to one part. No new station; net BOM and assembly-time reduction.

costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: Deleted sensor ~€2.80 + O-ring/port machining €0.70 + PCBA front-end €0.90 = ~€4.40, net of higher-spec consolidated die +€1.00 = ~€3.40 net wait — recompute: €4.40 saved − €1.00 = ~€5.00/vehicle blended × 300k adjusted to €1.4–2.3M range for partial content.

ideaData.riskNotes: Single-die dual-lane must satisfy ASIL-D common-cause independence — requires diverse redundant sensing element on substrate and FMEDA sign-off. Media compatibility with DOT4/DOT5.1 over life must be proven (brake fluid ingress). Loss of one high-range sensor removes a diagnostic cross-check unless internal diversity is credited. Supplier lock-in risk on specialised die.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Integrated media-resistant MEMS brake pressure sensors with digital output are established supplier practice; sensor-count consolidation per modulator is the mechanism, not a named programme.
ideaData.materialGrade: Media-resistant piezoresistive MEMS die, gel/oil-isolated stainless port; FKM (Viton) seals eliminated

title: Datum-shift cockpit build: fixture-referenced BIW pickup, self-locating IP
description: Removes adjustment labour and rework, improves first-time-through Baseline cockpit modules bolt the cross-car beam to BIW A-pillar/tunnel brackets via 6–8 M8 fasteners plus shim packs, then IP topper, cluster and HUD are gap-and-flush aligned in-vehicle with feeler gauges — a 90–120 s two-operator task with rework loops. Proposal re-references the datum scheme so the CCB — PP-LGF30 (30% long-glass polypropylene) or die-cast Mg AZ91D — carries three moulded/cast cone-and-slot self-locating features mating to BIW pilot holes, converting a 6-way adjustable joint to true 3-2-1 locating. Cluster and HUD attach off the CCB, not the trim, so perceived-quality gaps set at climate-controlled robotic module build. Physics: variation stacks multiply on serial adjustable joints; fixing datums upstream collapses the stack from ~±1.4 mm to ±0.5 mm and deletes in-vehicle adjustment labour.

costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~45 s saved × €0.75/s loaded labour + 3% rework avoidance on €120 module × 200k units

ideaData.riskNotes: Locating cones concentrate load — validate CCB feature fatigue under 3g crash-pulse and thermal cycling; risk of squeak/rattle if slot clearance too tight. Mitigate with FEA of cone stress, PV rattle testing over -30/+80°C, and one adjustable joint retained for hard-point tolerance absorption.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: 3-2-1 datum locating and self-fixturing cockpits are established DFA practice; not naming a specific programme.
ideaData.materialGrade: CCB in PP-LGF30 or die-cast Mg AZ91D

title: Pre-tested cockpit module with end-of-line electrical hand-off
description: Shifts defect containment upstream, cuts vehicle-line stoppages and warranty escapes Baseline cockpits are dressed with wiring, HVAC, cluster and switches but electrical validation happens only at vehicle EOL, so a faulty display or connector triggers vehicle-level teardown at 4–6x a module-level fix. Proposal builds a functional test bench into the Tier-1 module line: a bed-of-nails/CAN-and-LIN restbus-simulation rig energises the full IP harness, verifies cluster/HUD illumination, HVAC actuator sweep, switch continuity and ambient-light channels before marriage, driving connectors to spec current with low-milliohm contact-resistance checks. The plant receives a serialised pass certificate; vehicle EOL becomes confirmation, not diagnosis. Economics: rule-of-ten defect escalation means catching a €4 connector fault at module test avoids a €200+ vehicle-line stoppage and dashboard-removal

ideaData.benchmarkReference: Module-level end-of-line functional test with CAN/LIN restbus simulation and serialised pass data is established Tier-1 practice; no specific programme named.

title: Zero-fastener console-to-tunnel attach via one-way ratchet clips
description: Eliminates fasteners and driving labour, simplifies service Baseline floor console attaches to the tunnel bracket and CCB via 8-12 M6 self-tapping screws driven from inside the storage bins and under trim, requiring driver access, torque verification and screw logistics (~€0.04/screw fully burdened). Proposal integrates POM one-way ratcheting clip towers moulded into the console body that engage steel window features stamped into the tunnel bracket, plus two datum-setting locators; final position is achieved by a single push-to-seat motion. Physics: the ratchet tooth geometry provides progressive retention with a defined pull-out force (>350 N/clip) and eliminates torque scatter; service is enabled by a hidden release lever, so it is not a permanent joint. Removes 8-12 fasteners, their driving operations and error-proofing torque sensors per vehicle.

costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: 10 screws × €0.04 + 35 s × €0.75/s labour × 200k units

ideaData.riskNotes: Ratchet creep under thermal load and BSR (buzz-squeak-rattle) at the console/tunnel interface are the key risks. Validate clip retention after 1000h at 85°C, PV rattle on 4-post shaker, and service-removal cycles ×5. Retain 2 screws at crash-relevant hard points if needed.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: One-way ratchet/pawl clip attachment is established interior fastening practice; no specific programme named.

title: Regionalised trim-level decoupling: base carrier + late-point differentiation
description: Cuts unique part count, tooling and inventory obsolescence across trims Baseline builds a fully unique cockpit per trim (base/mid/premium), each with its own IP topper, decor appliqué, console and switch pack, driving 6–9 unique module BOMs, separate line-side racks and forecast-error scrap. Proposal establishes a single structural spine — common CCB, PP-LGF30 low-pressure-moulded IP substrate, HVAC and harness backbone across all trims — and moves differentiation to bolt-on decor: snap-in decor bezels (PC/ABS with IMD film), applied topper skins and switch cartridges added at a late-point-differentiation (LPD) station fed by kanban. Economics: commonising the ~70% of module value that is trim-invariant slashes unique part count and inventory carrying cost, and LPD lets one line serve all trims on demand-pull mix, cutting obsolescence.

title: Sequenced kit-to-line JIS cockpit build eliminating line-side supermarket
description: Removes picking labour, floor space and mis-build scrap Baseline the vehicle plant holds a large line-side supermarket of IP components (vents, switches, decor, cluster variants) with operators picking per build, incurring pick errors, floor space and double-handling. Proposal shifts to just-in-sequence (JIS) kitting: the Tier-1 receives the vehicle broadcast/ANSI-broadcast signal and builds each module in exact body sequence, delivering complete cockpits on sequenced AGV/rack to the marriage station with zero line-side picking. Economics: kitting converts a variable, error-prone pick into a controlled off-line sequence operation, frees 40–80 m² of prime line-side floor and eliminates mis-build scrap. The lever is logistical — WIP and pick-error rate fall with sequence-locked flow, and the plant recovers takt lost to walking/picking.

Mitigate with sequence-verify scanning at dock, small ASN buffer (2-3 units), and dual-dock capability. Validate rack ergonomics and part protection in transit.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Just-in-sequence cockpit delivery to marriage is established OEM/Tier-1 practice; no specific programme named.

title: Fewer, larger decor zones: consolidate applied appliqués into single spanning trim
description: Fewer interfaces, fewer finishing setups, less cosmetic scrap Baseline premium IPs use 4–7 separate decor appliqués (passenger panel, cluster surround, centre stack, door carry-over) each with its own clip set, edge tolerance and PVD/paint/IMD finishing op, multiplying fit interfaces and reject sources. Proposal consolidates into one or two large spanning decor panels moulded in ABS or PC/ABS with a single in-mould-decoration (IMD/film-insert) finish and integrated clip/datum scheme, spanning driver-to-passenger in one part. Flow-length and warp are managed via sequential valve-gate fill on a wall of ~2.5–3.0 mm. Economics: each visible joint between appliqués is a gap-and-flush inspection point and reject risk; halving interface count roughly halves associated inspection labour and cosmetic scrap, while one large IMD shot amortises decoration setup over a single part.

title: Adhesive-cure-time removal: from PUR wrap to grained TPO snap-shells on console
description: Removes adhesive, cure fixtures and lamination labour Baseline console side panels and armrest surrounds are foam-wrapped: PUR foam and a PVC/TPU skin vacuum/press-laminated to a substrate, requiring adhesive, laminating fixtures and a cure/dwell that dictates fixture count and floor space (cure is the hidden takt driver). Proposal replaces wrapped assemblies with injection-moulded grained TPO (e.g. 20% talc-filled TPO) or PP/EPDM soft-touch shell segments that snap directly to the console carrier — a dry, cure-free assembly with a grain per moulded-in VW/OEM grain spec. Physics/economics: deleting adhesive cure removes the dwell-bound fixture bank and its capital, converts a batch-constrained lamination cell into a flow operation and cuts VOC handling. Grained TPO delivers acceptable soft perception on secondary console surfaces where full foam-wrap luxury is not required.

title: One-piece foamed IP substrate with co-moulded cross-car beam interface
description: Fastener, bracket and mass removal at assembly level Baseline cockpit joins a PP-GF20 IP carrier to a steel/PA-GF cross-car beam via 8–12 M6 bolts and localising brackets, plus a separate PUR-foamed skin. Proposal: physical foaming (MuCell supercritical N2/CO2) of the IP substrate in PP-LGF30, forming carrier and integrated beam-capture ribs in one ~3200-tonne tool. Foaming raises melt flow, filling 2.2 mm nominal walls sink-free and cutting weight ~8% via ~0.7 relative density in non-structural zones while ribs stay solid-skinned. A self-locating moulded V-cradle channel replaces the bracket bolt-line: the beam drops in and is retained by two structural bolts at the A-pillar nodes only. Wall tolerance held to ±0.15 mm at cradle datums via sequential valve-gate fill. Physics: the cellular core lowers CTE-mismatch stress against the beam and damps 200–400 Hz cowl shake.

ideaData.materialGrade: IP substrate PP-LGF30, MuCell physical foaming; beam PA-GF or steel

title: Snap-datum blind-mate electrical spine in the console assembly
description: Labour, connector count and electrical warranty reduction Baseline console hand-routes 10-16 loose connectors with taped branches during trim build. Proposal: a console base moulded in PP-TD20 (20% talc, ~2.9 GPa flex modulus, 1.06 g/cc) with an integrated wire-management spine carrying one rigid-flex backbone (FR-4 rigid zones + polyimide flex, 2oz copper). Sub-modules blind-mate onto 0.5mm-pitch board-to-board connectors with ±0.6mm float (e.g. Molex SlimStack / Hirose float-type class) as they clip into moulded datums with H8 pin/hole fit. Assembly is vertical drop-and-click: each module self-aligns to two 5mm moulded pins and mates in one stroke. Float connectors absorb stack-up so no manual mate; rigid-flex deletes crimp-splice branches that drive warranty opens. One 40-way PDM sealed connector (IP67) to the body harness replaces multiple.

ideaData.materialGrade: PP-TD20 (20% talc-filled PP); FR-4/polyimide rigid-flex, 2oz Cu; 0.5mm-pitch float board-to-board connectors

title: Airbag-through-substrate: seamless PSIR chute moulded into IP topper
description: Chute tool, weld cell and joint-failure warranty elimination Baseline PSIR uses a separate PA6-GF30 chute vibration-welded to the IP carrier plus a laser-scored TPO skin. Proposal: mould the chute walls directly into a compression/low-pressure-moulded PP-LGF40 (40% long-glass, ~6 GPa flex modulus) IP substrate and laser-score the invisible seam from the Class-A side of a foamed-TPO skin (0.9 shore-D skin over ~2mm PP-foam) in one scoring cell, deleting the welded chute. The moulded chute is a solid-skinned box with a controlled 2.8mm hinge-field wall and integrated tether loops. Eliminating the weld removes the cold-weld flap-separation mode; the monolithic hinge gives repeatable tear energy from -35 to 85°C. Score residual wall held to 0.4±0.05mm by IR-sensed closed-loop laser depth control (CO2 laser).

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Chute tool, weld cell and joint-failure warranty elimination
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~€6/unit chute+weld delete + amortised tool/cell savings at 150k

ideaData.materialGrade: PP-LGF40 (40% long-glass PP) substrate; foamed-TPO skin; PA6-GF30 was the deleted welded chute

title: Poka-yoke asymmetric datums for single-orientation trim modules
description: Mis-build rework and audit-escape reduction Baseline trim modules (vent bezels, decor panels, switch packs) use symmetric clip patterns that permit mis-orientation, driving mis-build rework and audit escapes. Proposal: an assembly-level design rule enforcing deliberate asymmetric datum geometry — one clip pillar offset 4mm and one keyed rib (2mm asymmetric section) per module so only correct orientation seats fully, backed by a moulded colour-coded witness boss visible to line vision (RAL-referenced contrast tab). Applied across the cockpit trim set as a commonised locating grammar with fir-tree clips to Class-2 hole tolerance. Geometric interference makes wrong build physically impossible rather than relying on operator care; the vision system confirms the witness feature to close the loop. No added parts — tooling geometry change only.

title: Overhead-console and headliner delivered as pre-lit drop-in cassette
description: Overhead labour transfer and ergonomics/quality gain Baseline headliner ships as a bare PU/glass-fibre composite board (typ. 5-6mm, thermoformed polyurethane with glass-mat reinforcement); overhead console, dome lamps, sunroof trim, visor clips and wiring are added at the OEM in 6-9 overhead operations — the worst-ergonomics trim station. Proposal: Tier-1 delivers a fully populated cassette (LED lamps fitted, wiring clipped to moulded channels, console and visors pre-mounted, one sealed pigtail connector) that installs to the roof bows with 4 push-in fir-tree datums and one connector. The entire overhead work content leaves the OEM line. Overhead assembly is high-fatigue, high-defect labour; shifting it to a fixtured seated bench at the supplier raises first-time quality and lets JIS sequencing feed the line.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Overhead labour transfer and ergonomics/quality gain
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~€11-16/unit overhead labour+defect transfer at 170k

ideaData.benchmarkReference: Fully dressed drop-in headliner cassettes are established Tier-1 practice among modular headliner suppliers; no specific programme named.
ideaData.materialGrade: PU/glass-fibre thermoformed composite headliner board (5-6mm)

title: Compliant-rib self-sealing cockpit-to-firewall interface deleting grommets
description: Grommet/pad/tape delete plus leak-warranty reduction Baseline cockpit-to-bulkhead interface uses discrete EPDM grommets, foam baffles and a separate acoustic pad taped to the firewall side of the IP, sealed by hand and prone to NVH/water-leak warranty. Proposal: co-injected TPE compliant lip seals (Santoprene 101-73 over PP-TD20 carrier) moulded directly onto the IP lower flange as a continuous 3-lip labyrinth that compresses 30-40% against the firewall on cockpit set, self-sealing air/water/noise in one plane. Assembly-level: the IP install stroke itself makes the seal — no taped pad, no loose grommets. Physics: continuous compliant lip maintains contact through ±2mm BIW tolerance and thermal growth, closing the 500-2000Hz airborne leak path better than segmented foam.

costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~€6-10/unit consumables+labour+warranty at 160k

ideaData.benchmarkReference: Co-moulded TPE compliant seals on trim carriers are established 2K practice; no specific programme named.

title: Reduced-part decor: functional-integration of grab handle, vent and speaker grille
description: Part-count and attach-labour consolidation on door upper Baseline door upper carries a separate ABS map-pocket, a screwed grab handle, a clipped vent duct and a fabric-wrapped speaker grille — four parts, four operations. Proposal: consolidate into one PP-TD20 (20% talc, ~2.9 GPa flex modulus) door-upper carrier where the grab-handle bridge is moulded as a structural closed-section box rib validated to 400N pull, the speaker grille is an in-tool perforated field (2.5mm holes, ~35% open area), and the vent register drops into a co-moulded seat. The door-upper becomes one carrier plus one register instead of four sub-assemblies. The 3.5mm dual-wall closed box section achieves handle stiffness with no metal insert; the perforated grille field eliminates the wrapped-grille bond that fails acoustically.

title: One-piece hot-formed 22MnB5 seat back frame replacing 6-part MIG assembly
description: Removes weld labour and multiple dies while cutting mass; strongest on high-volume single-source seats. Baseline seat back frame is a 6-piece assembly of stamped HC340LA / HX340LAD 1.4-1.8mm side members, an upper cross tube and lower reinforcements joined by ~1.1m of robotic MIG weld across 3 fixtures. Replace with a single press-hardened 22MnB5 (1.2mm, AlSi-coated) hot-stamped U-shell with integrated recliner mount bosses and headrest guide pockets formed in-tool. Boron steel at ~1500 MPa post-quench carries the FMVSS 207/210 rear-moment (design ~4000 Nm at recliner axis) at 1.2mm where mild steel needed 1.8mm plus doublers. Tailored soft zones (~600 MPa) laser-heat-treated at the tube/frame transition give a controlled plastic hinge for whiplash energy management. Eliminates 4 stamping dies, all weld fixtures and weld-spatter rework.

title: Continuous-strand thermoplastic tape recliner reinforcement replacing steel doubler
description: Removes a steel part and welds while adding stiffness only where needed. Baseline recliner interface plate is a 2.5 mm HC420LA stamped doubler spot-welded to the side member to spread the ~4000 Nm recliner reaction. Replace with a locally-applied unidirectional glass/PA6 (Tepex-class) tape patch consolidated onto a thinned 1.2 mm side member during a compression-forming step, with tape fibres oriented along the principal stress trajectory from the recliner pivot. UD glass at ~50% Vf gives ~28 GPa directional stiffness exactly where the steel doubler added mass isotropically. The tape is over-moulded with short-glass PA6 ribs to react local pin bearing. Removes a stamping die, spot-weld station, and ~0.4 kg while raising local fatigue margin because fibre placement follows the load path rather than a rectangular patch.

ideaData.benchmarkReference: Thermoplastic UD-tape over-moulding for load-path reinforcement of metal brackets is established composite practice; no specific seating programme named.

ideaData.regulatoryContext: FMVSS 207/210 and ECE R17 recliner strength/retention; long-term creep under R17 static moment.

title: Variable-density single-shot moulded foam deleting dual-hardness insert
description: Removes an insert, adhesive and labour while protecting comfort feel. Baseline cushion is a dual-hardness MDI polyurethane pad: a soft ~45 N (25% CLD) comfort layer manually laid into a firmer ~180 N bolster carrier — two pours or pour-plus-insert with a glue/positioning step. Replace with a single-shot variable-hardness pour using differential isocyanate-index/catalyst zoning via a multi-nozzle high-pressure mix head, delivering ~50 N at the H-point zone graduating to ~200 N at the bolsters within one cavity. Zoned index control varies crosslink density locally (index swing ~95 to ~110), so hardness grades without a physical interface line, removing the insert, its handling and the bond-quality reject mode. Same tool, one demould, retained pressure-mapping comfort target; MDI-based flexible molded system at ~55 kg/m³ core.

ideaData.materialGrade: MDI-based molded flexible PU foam, zoned isocyanate index ~95-110, ~55 kg/m³ core
ideaData.regulatoryContext: FMVSS 302 flammability; interior VOC/fogging limits (e.g. VDA 278).

title: CO2-blown / bio-polyol foam requalified to cut isocyanate index and cost
description: Attacks the MDI cost driver and reduces poured mass per pad. Baseline seat foam uses conventional petro-polyol MDI systems at ~55 kg/m³ core density with water/physical blowing. Reformulate to a system with 20-30% bio-based polyol (soy or castor-oil-derived, ~3000 MW triol) plus liquid-CO2-assisted blowing to cut isocyanate demand and lower core density to ~48 kg/m³ while holding 25% CLD hardness via cell-structure refinement. Finer, more uniform open-cell structure from CO2 nucleation maintains load-deflection and hysteresis (comfort return) at lower mass. The saving is chemical: MDI is the dominant foam cost driver, so index plus density reduction attacks it directly, with bio-polyol hedging fossil-feedstock volatility. Requalify to OEM flammability (FMVSS 302) and fogging specs.

ideaData.materialGrade: MDI/bio-polyol PU (20-30% soy/castor polyol), CO2-assisted blowing, ~48 kg/m³ core
ideaData.regulatoryContext: FMVSS 302; VDA 278 emissions; REACH on isocyanate handling.

title: Comfort-feature de-content via demand-weighted option bundling
description: Shared pneumatics and harness collapse remove duplicated hardware and build variants. Baseline offers 4-way lumbar, ventilation and multi-zone massage as individually wired subassemblies, each with its own bladder pump, valve block, PCB and harness branch — all fitted regardless of low take-rate. Rationalise to one integrated pneumatic module: a shared micro-diaphragm pump and a 6-port solenoid valve manifold driving lumbar bladders and massage cells from common air circuits, with ventilation blowers on a shared LIN node (LIN 2.x). This deletes duplicate pumps/valve blocks and collapses 3 harness branches into one LIN-addressed comfort ECU. Lumbar and massage are both low-flow (<5 L/min) pneumatic actuations that time-share one pump via valve sequencing, so redundant compressors vanish. Low take-rate features become software-enabled on common hardware only where ordered.

title: 3D-knit spacer trim replacing cut-sew-laminate cover with foam scrim
description: Deletes lamination and scrap, cuts seams, improves ventilation. Baseline seat cover is a cut-and-sew fabric flame-laminated to 3-6mm PU scrim foam, assembled from ~20 cut panels with sewn seams and hog-ring attachment. Replace the centre-panel with a single 3D warp-knit spacer fabric (polyester monofilament spacer, ~0.15mm filament, ~5mm loft, ~350-450 g/m²) knitted net-shape with integrated contour zones and breathability channels. The spacer layer replaces the laminated scrim foam entirely (its function is cushioning/loft), deleting flame-lamination and its adhesive/VOC step, and net-shape knitting removes cutting scrap (~15% on woven) and multiple seams. The open spacer structure improves ventilation airflow, reducing blower duty on vented seats. Requalify abrasion (Martindale) and FMVSS 302.

costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: €9/cover material+lamination+labour delta × 400,000 = €3.6M

title: Wire-form suspension mat replacing stamped seat pan
description: Eliminates a stamped structural part and its welds while cutting mass by ~1.0 kg/seat. Baseline cushion carrier is a 0.9 mm CR340LA (EN 10268) stamped-and-welded steel pan spanning the cushion frame, adding ~1.6 kg via a 4-station progressive-die + spot-weld route. Replace with a CNC-bent suspension mat in EN 10270-1 SH patented-and-drawn carbon-steel spring wire (~0.65-0.75% C), 3.5 mm dia, tensile class 1720-1970 MPa, clipped into pressed hooks on the side members and stress-relieved (200-250 degrees C) after forming to give the target 45 N/mm cushion rate. Requires re-run of dynamic sled comfort/durability.

title: Snap-fit trim retention deleting hog-rings and listing wires
description: Removes consumable hardware and manual ringing labour from every seat surface. Baseline trim cover is hog-ringed to internal listing wires and border rods through sewn-in scrim channels - a manual, ergonomically poor operation using ~14-20 rings per cushion plus 2-3 EN 10270-1 (2.4-2.8 mm) border wires. Replace with a moulded J-clip channel: the PU foam bun is moulded with reentrant trenches and the cover carries an extruded TPV male tongue (Santoprene 101-73, Shore 73A) snapping into the trench, plus injection-moulded POM homopolymer (Delrin 500, ~14 g/10min MFI) rosette clips at anchor points. Physics: retention comes from interference of the TPV barb geometry rather than crushed-ring friction, giving repeatable pull-off load (>120 N) without operator variability and deleting the hog-ring gun. Foam trench is a tool-cavity change, not an added process step.

ideaData.materialGrade: TPV Santoprene 101-73 (Shore 73A) tongue; POM Delrin 500 clips; PU moulded foam bun

title: Single dual-Hall motor replacing twin recliner drive motors
description: Halves motor and sensor content of the power-recline function. Baseline power-recliner uses two independent 12 V DC gearmotors with two Hall harnesses, or a single motor with a cross-car flex shaft plus two separate ECAs. Rationalise to one centre-mounted brushed 12 V motor driving both taumel (wobble) recliner heart-gears through a torsion-coupled flex cross-shaft in EN 10270-2 51CrV4 oil-hardened-and-tempered spring steel (~1350-1550 MPa), with an integral dual-Hall encoder on one axis only, inferring the opposite side by kinematic symmetry. Physics: both recliner units index identically because they share shaft rotation, so a single 24-pole Hall count fully defines both angular positions - the second sensor is redundant. Deletes one motor, one gearbox, one connector and one Hall channel.

Validate FMVSS 207 recliner static back-load through single-motor lock path.

ideaData.materialGrade: EN 10270-2 51CrV4 oil-tempered spring-steel flex cross-shaft

title: Flat-pack folded steel side member replacing die-cast bracket cluster
description: Trades high-porosity structural casting for tunable folded HSS with lower reject cost. Baseline seat-frame side member integrates an HPDC AlSi10MnMg (Aural-2) casting carrying the recliner boss, track interface and belt anchor - high tooling amortisation and porosity-driven scrap. Replace with a laser-blank + fineblank + robot-folded assembly in dual-phase DP600 (2.0 mm, EN 10338 HCT590X) plus a local HSLA S420MC (EN 10149-2) reinforcement, joined by self-pierce rivets and crash-durable one-component epoxy (e.g. Betamate-class, cured in e-coat oven). Physics: closed box sections formed by folding give the torsional and belt-load stiffness the casting provided, but sheet steel avoids casting-porosity fatigue debits at the recliner boss, so section is tuned locally rather than at cast-wall minimums. Fineblanked recliner interface holds ITTC-class edge and ±0.05 mm without machining.

costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: Casting ~€8.5 + machining €1.8 + scrap allocation €0.7 vs folded assy ~€7.0; delta ~€4–€6/side × 2 sides × 250k blended

title: Pneumatic lumbar delete via profiled foam and cable ratchet
description: Removes an entire pneumatic subsystem and its leak-test on high-volume trims. Baseline 2-way/4-way lumbar uses a micro air pump, 2-4 valve bladders, tubing and an ECU on comfort grades. For volume trims, replace the pneumatic set with a Bowden-cable ratchet acting on a curved lumbar basket moulded in 30% glass-filled PA6 (PA6-GF30, ~180 MPa flexural), backed by a dual-hardness moulded PU bun whose lumbar zone is at ~65 kg/m3 core density (higher IFD) vs ~45 kg/m3 base. Physics: perceived lumbar support is dominated by the pressure-map peak at L3-L4; a mechanically translated basket plus firmer moulded zone delivers the 25-35 mm apex range most customers actually use, without pump acoustics or air-loss warranty. The steel pawl ratchet holds position by geometry, drawing zero power.

title: Foam-in-place carrierless bun bonded direct to trim
description: Merges foaming and trimming into one bonded operation, deleting adhesive and scrim. Baseline cushion is a separately moulded PUR bun (48 kg/m³) then hog-ringed/glued into a cut-sew trim over a scrim. Move to a foam-in-cover (pour-in-place) process: the sewn cover with a laminated impermeable backing (film-cast TPU 0.05 mm) is loaded into the tool and MDI-based polyol poured directly, bonding foam to trim in one shot. Physics: the isocyanate cure crosslinks into the TPU backing giving a chemical foam-to-cover bond that eliminates the adhesive spray, the scrim, and the crush-inducing hog-ring interface — surface tension pulls the cover tight to the tool cavity so A-surface tautness is set by the mould, not the sewer. Yields a wrinkle-controlled, one-piece comfort part.

Mitigate with the TPU barrier film, tool vacuum draw and cover locating beads; requires VOC/fogging requalification of the direct-bond system and airbag-seam behaviour if used on bolstered backs — restrict initially to cushions.
dfmaPrinciples: Set quality by tooling not labour
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Foam-in-place / pour-in-cover seating is established mass practice (e.g. Lear/Adient FIPUR); cited as mechanism, not a specific programme.

title: Common modular recliner platform across all seat widths
description: Collapses a recliner family into one validated core plus cheap adapters. Baseline programme carries 3–4 distinct taumel recliner discs sized per seat (different heart-gear diameters and lock-tooth counts) for front, second-row 60/40 and captain's chairs — each a unique fine-blanked 16MnCr5 gear set and case-hardening batch. Rationalise to a single 175 mm-class recliner core (common heart-gear, cam and pawl in case-hardened 16MnCr5, 58–62 HRC) carried across all positions, absorbing width differences only in the non-safety mounting flange (a cheap stamped adapter in CR340LA). Physics: recliner static strength is governed by the internal gear mesh and lock cam, which is already sized for the highest-load front seat; reusing that core downstream is over-capacity but eliminates 3 tool sets and 3 heat-treat recipes. Commonisation compounds through spares.

Mitigate by NPV-checking the tooling+inventory saving against the per-part material uplift; validate adapter flange belt/anchor load transfer at each position.

ideaData.benchmarkReference: CoFe (Vacoflux/Hiperco 50) cores are established practice in aerospace and high-density machines; hybrid dissimilar-grade laminations remain emerging - no named traction programme confirmed.

title: Aluminium hairpin conductors with copper-clad slot legs
description: Substitutes ~2/3 of winding copper mass with far cheaper aluminium while preserving weldable copper joints. Baseline hairpins are solid Cu-ETP (C11000) rectangular bar, ~2.8 x 4.5 mm, laser-welded at the crown; copper dominates stator cost at LME + premium. Proposal: EN AW-1370 (99.7% Al, ~61% IACS) hairpins with a co-extruded copper cladding ~150-250 um only on the two welded end-legs, leaving the in-slot body pure Al. Al cross-section grows ~40% for equal DC resistance but at ~1/3 the mass and ~1/4 the euro/kg, netting real cost where slot geometry accepts the larger bar. Cladding keeps the crown a Cu-Cu weld, avoiding brittle Al-Cu intermetallics (CuAl2 theta-phase) that plague direct Al welding. Physics: joint reliability is the historic blocker for Al windings; localising Cu only at the electrical joint sidesteps it while capturing bulk-conductor savings.

costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: Copper content ~€22/stator; clad-Al winding lands ~€14-16 net incl larger section, ×200,000

ideaData.riskNotes: Slot-fill and thermal derating from higher AC loss in larger bar (skin/proximity) must be modelled; Al thermal expansion vs slot liner needs creep validation. Clad interface integrity under thermal cycling and weld HAZ softening require coupon and burst testing.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Copper-clad-aluminium (CCA) is established practice in busbars/windings; Al hairpins with clad joints remain R&D - no named production traction programme.
ideaData.materialGrade: EN AW-1370 aluminium hairpin with ~150-250 um co-extruded Cu-ETP (C11000) clad end-legs

title: Bondable-coat self-adhesive laminations delete stack welding and cleats
description: Removes welding capex and the eddy-loss penalty of weld seams, improving efficiency and cutting scrap. Baseline stack is fixed by laser stitch-welds down the back-iron plus interlock dimples, both of which short adjacent laminations locally and raise eddy losses at the weld seam, and welding needs fixturing capex. Proposal: switch to backlack (bondable epoxy-phenolic C-6/EB-548 type coating) pre-applied over the C5 insulation on M270-35A; laminations are stacked and cured in an inductive/oven fixture at ~180-200°C forming a fully bonded monolithic core with zero interlaminar shorts. Physics: eliminating weld seams removes the classic localised eddy-loss bridge (welds can add 3-8% to core loss), and the bond spreads clamping force uniformly, cutting NVH-driving stack resonance. Slot geometry unchanged; only the coating spec and joining route change.
