costSavingPotential.percentage: 3-6% of core cost plus efficiency gain
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: Weld/cleat process cost ~€1.20/core + 4% core-loss reduction valued via warranty/efficiency, ×200,000

ideaData.riskNotes: Bond shear strength at 180°C hotspot and over 15-year thermal ageing must be validated; delamination under vibration is the failure mode. Mitigate with lap-shear + resonance dwell testing and adhesion QC per lot. Ensure coating stack-factor loss (~1-2%) is accounted in magnetic sizing.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Backlack bonded cores are established production practice (electrical steel suppliers offer bondable coatings); widely used in traction and industrial motors.

title: Grade-graded stack: thin-gauge teeth zone, thick-gauge yoke zone
description: Buys expensive thin-gauge steel only for the teeth that need it, using cheaper thicker steel for the yoke. Baseline uses a single grade/gauge (e.g. 0.27 mm M250-27A) across the whole stack to satisfy the highest-frequency tooth loss, over-specifying the yoke where flux frequency content is the same but the classical eddy penalty is less leveraged and mechanical stiffness matters more. Proposal: axially graded stack — the electromagnetically active teeth use 0.20 mm NO270-20 for low high-order harmonic loss, while a proportion of yoke-region laminations use cheaper 0.35 mm M330-35A. Because eddy loss scales with gauge², concentrating the expensive thin gauge only where dB/dt harmonics are severe captures most of the loss benefit at a fraction of the thin-gauge premium (thin gauge carries a large €/kg surcharge and lower punching throughput).

costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: Thin-gauge premium ~€0.60/kg × ~40% of core mass avoided (yoke fraction) × ~14 kg core × 200,000

ideaData.riskNotes: Interface between gauge zones must not create a flux discontinuity or NVH mode; magnetic FEA of the transition needed. Validate that yoke-region loss with thicker gauge stays within thermal budget at max-speed field-weakening. Stack-factor mixing affects sizing.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Multi-gauge/graded electrical steel stacks are an emerging established-practice lever; no specific OEM programme named.

title: Encapsulant potting replaces trickle varnish and slot-liner layers
description: Collapses three insulation consumables and two process steps into one potting shot and improves cooling. Baseline insulation: NMN (Nomex 410 / Mylar / Nomex) slot liner + phase paper + trickle/dip epoxy varnish, a multi-consumable long-cure route with a poor slot thermal path. Proposal: delete varnish and phase paper by vacuum potting the wound stator in an alumina-filled epoxy (1.5-3 W/mK, e.g. Al2O3-filled anhydride- or amine-cured system) that provides turn-to-turn, phase-to-phase and slot-to-ground insulation plus rigid encapsulation in one shot. Retain a single thin PEN film slot liner (~0.15-0.25 mm, class 200) only for the ground wall. Physics: filled potting raises winding-to-lamination thermal conductance ~3-5x, allowing higher current density or a shorter stack, while collapsing three insulation consumables and two process steps into one vacuum-fill operation.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Collapses three insulation consumables and two process steps into one potting shot and improves cooling.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: Insulation consumables+varnish process ~€9/stator, ~25% net saving after resin cost ×200,000

ideaData.riskNotes: CTE mismatch between filled epoxy and copper/steel can crack under thermal cycling; partial-discharge inception voltage must be validated for HV (800V) systems. Mitigate with toughened resin and PDIV testing; ensure full void-free fill via vacuum process and CT sampling.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Thermally-conductive potting of stators is established practice in aerospace/high-power-density motors; adoption in cost-driven traction is emerging - no named programme claimed.
ideaData.materialGrade: Alumina-filled epoxy potting (1.5-3 W/mK); PEN film ground-wall liner (~0.15-0.25 mm, class 200)

title: Open-slot stator with insert-molded preformed coils
description: Maximises slot-fill to cut copper and replaces the complex hairpin insert/weld chain with drop-in coils. Baseline distributed hairpin winding uses semi-closed slots needing insertion, twisting and laser welding of many hairpins, with scrap and slot-fill limits. Proposal: redesign to fully open (parallel-wall) slots and drop in pre-wound, pre-insulated concentrated coils made off-line as rigid insert-moulded modules, then bridge each slot opening with a soft-magnetic-composite wedge (Fe-powder SMC, e.g. Somaloy 700-class, ~0.5-1.5 T at working flux). Physics: open slots enable near-perfect slot-fill (>65% vs ~45-50%) and eliminate in-slot insertion; the SMC wedge restores a near-closed magnetic opening to suppress cogging and slot-harmonic loss. Copper mass drops for equal resistance and winding is fully automated on flat tooling.

costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: Copper reduction (~10%) + hairpin process cost (~€6/stator) eliminated, ×200,000

ideaData.benchmarkReference: Open-slot machines with magnetic wedges and preformed coils are established in industrial/large machines; traction adoption is emerging - no named OEM programme.
ideaData.materialGrade: Fe-powder SMC slot wedge (Somaloy 700-class); pre-insulated concentrated coils (round Cu / class-200 film)

title: Nested-blank slot geometry punching to cut electrical-steel scrap
description: Turns the punched-out bore scrap into usable rotor laminations and tightens web, lifting strip utilisation. Baseline stator laminations are blanked from strip with the bore centre disc and inter-part web punched to scrap, typically yielding only ~55-62% utilisation. Proposal: adopt a nesting progressive/notching die where the stator-bore slug is not scrapped but sized (matched OD/ID) to serve as the rotor lamination blank, plus tighter part-to-part web via rotary/interlock notching rather than full-perimeter blanking. Applies to NO grades such as M270-35A / M235-35A (0.35 mm, EN 10303) where price/kg is high and every yield point is direct margin. Physics: electrical steel is ~40-50% of core cost; pairing stator and rotor from one strip pass converts former scrap into a second usable part. Requires airgap-compatible OD/ID pairing and interlock-tab placement outside flux paths.

ideaData.benchmarkReference: Rotor-from-stator-slug nesting and rotary notching are established high-volume lamination practices; stated as mechanism, no named programme.
ideaData.materialGrade: NO electrical steel M270-35A / M235-35A (0.35 mm, EN 10303) - no new grade, a blanking-yield lever

title: Shingled overlapping-lap joint replaces butt-jointed lamination stack corners
description: Downgrades electrical-steel grade one full loss class while holding efficiency, on the single largest-mass stator material. Baseline segmented stator cores butt-abut laminations at each segment interface, creating an air-gap discontinuity that spikes local reluctance and forces higher-grade steel (M270-35A, 2.7 W/kg at 1.5 T/50 Hz, 0.35 mm) to hold flux. Proposal: punch each 0.35 mm M330-35A lamination with a stepped half-lap tongue so successive laminations overlap the joint in a shingled brick-bond pattern, offsetting the magnetic seam through stack thickness. Overlap geometry (2-3 mm step land, min 0.5 mm tongue web) recovers ~60-70% of the reluctance lost at a hard butt joint, letting the 3.3 W/kg grade match the effective permeability of a 2.7 W/kg butt-jointed core. Half-lap punched on the existing progressive die by adding one forming station; no coil-side change. Effective joint

Stacking fixture indexes alternate laminations 180° for brick-bond; adds ~0.3 s/stack cycle. Scrap unchanged. Deletes the pressure needed for tight butt tolerance grinding at segment ends.

costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~18 kg core × €0.55/kg grade delta (M270→M330) × 250,000 = €2.5M; plus grind-station labour saving

ideaData.riskNotes: Overlap tongue must not exceed lamination gauge or it fouls stacking flatness — control coining depth to <25 µm. Validate core loss on Epstein plus assembled no-load loss test; confirm NVH (12th/24th order) unchanged since joint modulates radial force. Fatigue of thinned tongue verified over thermal cycling -40/+150°C.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Mitred step-lap and overlapped joints are established practice in transformer core construction; application to segmented traction stators is the transfer, no specific programme named.
ideaData.materialGrade: M330-35A NO electrical steel (0.35 mm) replacing M270-35A; both EN 10106 grades

title: Semi-processed non-annealed steel stress-relieved by winding-cure cycle
description: Buys cheaper input steel and extends die life while improving assembled magnetic quality. Baseline uses fully-processed NO steel (e.g. M270-35A) delivered final-annealed with insulation coating, priced at a premium for guaranteed core loss. Proposal: source semi-processed grade (fully-finished cold-rolled, un-annealed, ~2.4% Si, C1 organic coat) which is ~€0.20-0.35/kg cheaper, and recover its magnetic properties by exploiting the decarburising/stress-relief anneal that the assembled stator already needs — or by running a dedicated 780°C strand anneal after punching but before winding. Punching a not-yet-annealed strip also improves die life because the metal is softer, cutting burr and edge-hardening that itself degrades core loss. The final anneal relieves punch-induced residual stress in the tooth tips (the highest-flux, most stress-sensitive zone), often yielding lower assembled loss

ideaData.title: Semi-processed non-annealed steel stress-relieved by winding-cure cycle
ideaData.technicalDescription: Baseline uses fully-processed NO steel (e.g. M270-35A) delivered final-annealed with insulation coating, priced at a premium for guaranteed core loss. Proposal: source semi-processed grade (fully-finished cold-rolled, un-annealed, ~2.4% Si, C1 organic coat) which is ~€0.20-0.35/kg cheaper, and recover its magnetic properties by exploiting the decarburising/stress-relief anneal that the assembled stator already needs — or by running a dedicated 780°C strand anneal after punching but before winding. Punching a not-yet-annealed strip also improves die life because the metal is softer, cutting burr and edge-hardening that itself degrades core loss. The final anneal relieves punch-induced residual stress in the tooth tips (the highest-flux, most stress-sensitive zone), often yielding lower assembled loss than punching hard fully-processed stock.
ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Adds a continuous/batch anneal furnace (~€1.2M capex) or outsources annealing. Die life up 20-40% from softer stock, cutting tooling regrind. Handling of uncoated edges post-anneal requires oxidation control. Net stations neutral if bondable/varnish coat applied post-anneal.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Buys cheaper input steel and extends die life while improving assembled magnetic quality.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: 18 kg × €0.28/kg × 250,000 = €1.26M material; plus ~€0.4M die-life saving, net of anneal energy/opex

ideaData.riskNotes: Anneal atmosphere and cooling rate must hit target grain size (~150 µm) or core loss overshoots — requires closed-loop furnace control and per-lot Epstein check. Risk of stack distortion if annealed loose; mitigate by fixture-anneal. Coating must survive winding insertion.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Semi-processed lamination steel with post-punch stress-relief anneal is long-established in industrial and appliance motor manufacture; transfer to traction stators is the lever.

title: Aluminium-conductor concentrated tooth-wound coils on cheap grade back-iron
description: Halves conductor mass and swaps copper for aluminium plus a cheaper steel grade on a full sub-assembly. Baseline distributed hairpin stators use copper conductors and demand low-loss steel because distributed windings spread flux and tolerate no reluctance penalty. Proposal for lower-power (e-axle secondary / range-extender) variants: single-tooth concentrated needle-wound coils in EN AW-1350 (99.5% Al, IACS ~61%) round wire on segmented teeth. Concentrated winding shortens end-turns ~30-40% versus distributed, and the shorter path plus larger conductor cross-section (sized to equal DC resistance at 1.6× copper area) offsets aluminium's higher resistivity while cutting conductor mass ~50% and cost ~65%. Segmented teeth allow near-100% slot fill by winding before assembly. The bulk yoke can move to lower-cost M400-50A because concentrated winding's short flux paths keep yoke loss low.

ideaData.title: Aluminium-conductor concentrated tooth-wound coils on cheap grade back-iron
ideaData.technicalDescription: Baseline distributed hairpin stators use copper conductors and demand low-loss steel because distributed windings spread flux and tolerate no reluctance penalty. Proposal for lower-power (e-axle secondary / range-extender) variants: single-tooth concentrated needle-wound coils in EN AW-1350 (99.5% Al, IACS ~61%) round wire on segmented teeth. Concentrated winding shortens end-turns ~30-40% versus distributed, and the shorter path plus larger conductor cross-section (sized to equal DC resistance at 1.6× copper area) offsets aluminium's higher resistivity while cutting conductor mass ~50% and cost ~65%. Segmented teeth allow near-100% slot fill by winding before assembly. The bulk yoke can move to lower-cost M400-50A because concentrated winding's short flux paths keep yoke loss low.
ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Replaces hairpin bending/laser-weld cell with needle/flyer winders per segment — parallel, scalable, lower capex than hairpin line. Deletes ~40 laser welds/stator and their inline CT. Al termination requires crimped/ultrasonic-welded Cu bimetal transition tabs to avoid galvanic joint.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Halves conductor mass and swaps copper for aluminium plus a cheaper steel grade on a full sub-assembly.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: Cu ~6 kg @ €9/kg → Al ~3 kg @ €2.8/kg saves ~€45/motor conductor; + steel grade delta + weld-line capex avoided × 200,000

ideaData.riskNotes: Al-Cu terminal interface is the durability risk — galvanic corrosion and creep; mitigate with cold-welded/ultrasonic bimetal ferrules and sealed potting. Concentrated winding raises torque ripple/harmonics — restrict to NVH-tolerant secondary drives. Validate thermal derate: Al conductor runs hotter per amp.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Aluminium concentrated-wound stators are established in appliance and some 48V/auxiliary automotive motors; Cu-Al bimetal terminations are proven practice.

title: Corona-resistant thin enamel replaces slot liner on 800V stators
description: Removes a discrete insulation part and its insertion station while unlocking slot-fill for stack shortening. Baseline 800V hairpin stators carry a Nomex/PEN slot liner (0.20-0.25 mm) plus standard PAI-topcoat magnet-wire enamel to survive partial-discharge (PD) from fast SiC dv/dt. Proposal: delete the discrete slot liner and upgrade the wire film to a corona-resistant grade — nano-alumina/nano-silica-filled polyamide-imide over polyesterimide (Type II/III corona-resistant enamel) at ~0.14 mm build with PDIV raised above the worst-case 800V surge. The filled enamel erodes ~10-30× slower under PD than unfilled, so the liner's PD-barrier function migrates into the wire coating itself. Removing the ~0.22 mm liner frees slot area, raising slot fill 6-9% for equal copper or allowing a shorter stack for equal torque.

ideaData.riskNotes: Must qualify PDIV margin at max coolant temp and altitude (reduced dielectric strength) per IEC 60034-18-41; PD test 100% at EOL. Ground-wall creepage at slot exit now relies on end-winding potting — validate. Enamel abrasion during hairpin insertion must not breach film.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Corona-resistant nano-filled magnet wire is established for inverter-fed and 800V traction motors; slot-liner deletion via wire-film-only insulation is the design move.

title: Litz-substitute transposed-strand hairpin to cut AC copper loss
description: Converts recovered AC-loss efficiency into a steel-grade downgrade and/or shorter stack. Baseline high-speed (>16k rpm) hairpin stators suffer heavy skin/proximity AC loss in solid rectangular conductors, forcing designers to fatten the stack or upgrade steel to hold efficiency. Proposal: replace the solid rectangular hairpin with a two- or three-strand transposed hairpin — thin flat strands stacked and mechanically transposed (rolled/twisted) at the end-turn so each strand samples both slot-bottom and slot-top positions. Splitting the conductor below the skin depth at the fundamental-plus-harmonic frequency cuts AC/DC resistance ratio from ~1.8 to ~1.2 at top speed, recovering copper loss without more copper. That efficiency headroom permits downgrading from M250-35A to M330-35A steel and/or shortening the stack, converting an efficiency gain into a material-cost saving.

No new machine line, extends existing cell. Strand insulation adds minor wire cost.

costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: Steel grade delta ~€0.30/kg × 18 kg + ~5% stack-shorten copper/steel ≈ €9/stator × 220,000, less strand-wire uplift

ideaData.riskNotes: Weld integrity across multi-strand bundle is the key risk — incomplete fusion raises resistance and hot spots; mitigate with green-laser copper welding and 100% CT. Inter-strand short from insulation damage negates benefit — validate hi-pot per pin. Transposition geometry must fit end-winding envelope.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Strand transposition to suppress AC loss (Roebel/Litz principle) is established in large machines and turbo-generators; miniaturised transposed hairpins are the traction transfer.

Baseline stacks are interlock-cleated or laser-welded along the OD, which shorts laminations locally, adds an eddy-current bridge and a welding station. ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Deletes OD laser-weld station and its fume/CT equipment; deletes standalone bond-press oven. Adds one inline edge-bead applicator (~€120k). Light fixture holds stack through winding until the impregnation bake sets the bond. Net stations reduced by ~two.

costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: Weld cell + bond-oven capex/opex ~€8-10/stator amortised + full-face vs edge-only bondcoat delta ~€1.5/stator × 250,000

ideaData.riskNotes: Green (uncured) stack must survive winding-insertion handling forces — validate fixture retention and green-strength shear. Edge-only bond must resist stack-end fretting under electromagnetic vibration; verify OD shear after 300h vibration + thermal. Impregnation bake profile must guarantee full epoxy cure — DSC per lot.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Backlack/bondable-coat stacks and co-cure with impregnation are established practice; edge-only application co-cured in the existing varnish bake is the cost move, no specific programme named.
ideaData.materialGrade: B-stage phenolic/epoxy backlack (Backlack-type) on 0.30-0.35 mm NO electrical steel (e.g. M330-35A)

title: Common lamination blank with variable stack length across power tiers
description: Collapses multiple lamination dies to one and consolidates press volume across the power family. Baseline motor families punch a unique lamination profile (unique progressive die, ~€1.5-3M each) for each power variant, differing in OD/slot to hit torque. Proposal: fix ONE M330-35A lamination cross-section (same OD, ID, slot geometry) across the whole power ladder and vary only stack length and winding turns to set torque/power. Torque scales linearly with active length, so a 150 kW and 220 kW motor share the identical blank and identical progressive die, differing only in how many laminations are stacked. This collapses N dies to one, slashes tooling amortisation and die-maintenance spares, and lets one high-utilisation press feed the whole family — driving down per-part press overhead through volume.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Collapses multiple lamination dies to one and consolidates press volume across the power family.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~4 dies × €2M avoided over 5-yr life = €1.6M/yr + press-overhead reduction from higher OEE across ~600k combined units/yr

ideaData.riskNotes: Fixed cross-section is a compromise — the shared slot may be sub-optimal at the ladder extremes, costing ~1-2 pts efficiency at the endpoints; validate each variant still meets its efficiency and thermal targets. Housing/coolant-jacket family must be co-designed for length variation. NVH re-check per length.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Scaling torque by active stack length on a common lamination is established electric-machine family-platform practice; the lever is disciplined cross-tier die commonisation.

title: Structural PP-LGF30 bumper beam co-moulded with EPP absorber
description: Removes steel beam, its e-coat, and a full assembly operation; ~2.8 kg mass out. Baseline front bumper stacks a roll-formed DP600 steel beam (1.6 mm), a separately bead-fused EPP absorber at 30 g/L, and 4 M8 crush-can bolts. Proposal: replace the beam with a compression/flow-moulded long-glass PP (PP-LGF30, 30 wt% glass, ~9 GPa flexural modulus, ~180 MPa flexural strength) I-section and co-mould the EPP absorber into the beam front channel in one in-mould step — insert a pre-fused EPP bead block (~60 g/L in crush zone) into the tool and overmould keying ribs. The LGF beam meets FMVSS Part 581 4 mph and RCAR/IIHS low-speed by tuning rib pitch (~12 mm) and wall (3.2 mm) rather than gauge, deleting the steel-to-EPP clip/bond op. title: Radar-transparent fascia zone by local resin/paint control
description: Eliminates a part number, its fasteners, and reduces paint masking labour. Baseline front fascia hides a 77 GHz corner/mid radar behind a separately moulded radar window sized to n×λ/2 (~1.9 mm per half-wave layer in PC, εr≈2.9) plus a metallic-look film laser-ablated or masked to control attenuation — adding a part, fasteners and a mask op. Proposal: mould the aperture as an integral thickness-controlled boss in the main PP-TD15 fascia, local wall stepped to n×λ/2 for the fascia dielectric (εr≈2.3, ~2.4-2.5 mm per half-wave), and delete the metallic film in that zone via a robotic paint-shadow mask leaving a base-coat-only, non-metallic-flake window colour-matched with a mica-/aluminium-free tint. Physics: two-way attenuation must stay <1 dB; controlling only local thickness and pigment (no aluminium flake, no conductive primer) keeps the window transparent without a discrete part.

costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: Emblem+fasteners+mask op ≈ €7/veh; delta ≈ €7 × 200k = €1.4M

ideaData.riskNotes: Metallic colour match between flake and non-flake window is the key aesthetic risk; attenuation drift with paint film thickness variation. Mitigate with in-line paint-thickness gauging, transmission-loss AOI, and a colour-harmony sign-off under multi-angle lighting. Re-run radar EMC.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Integral radar-transparent fascia zones with pigment/thickness control are established OEM practice; no specific programme named.
ideaData.materialGrade: PP-TD15 (15% talc-filled PP, εr≈2.3) fascia; mica-free/aluminium-flake-free colour-matched basecoat over the radar zone

description: Massive piece-count and assembly-labour reduction plus rattle-warranty elimination. Baseline active grille shutter subassembly uses a glass-filled PA66-GF30 frame, separate POM vanes on steel or POM pivot pins, PA linkage bar, and an electric actuator — typically 20+ discrete pivot/pin interfaces assembled by hand. ideaData.title: Grille shutter flap-and-frame single-material film-hinge design
ideaData.technicalDescription: Baseline active grille shutter subassembly uses a glass-filled PA66-GF30 frame, separate POM vanes on steel or POM pivot pins, PA linkage bar, and an electric actuator — typically 20+ discrete pivot/pin interfaces assembled by hand. Proposal: mould the vane array and its pivot compliance as living film hinges in a single POM (Delrin acetal homopolymer, fatigue-rated for >1M flex cycles) shutter cassette, replacing individual pins with integral 0.35 mm film-hinge webs and consolidating the frame, vanes, and linkage retention into two mouldings that snap together. Physics: POM's high fatigue endurance and low creep let a thin film hinge survive thermal cycling and vibration; deleting metal pins removes the biggest assembly-labour and squeak/rattle source. Actuator torque falls because pin friction is replaced by low-hysteresis elastic hinge return.
ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Reduces AGS piece count from ~30 to ~4. Deletes pin-press and vane-insertion stations; adds a two-plate POM tool with film-hinge gating. Lower actuator torque may allow a smaller motor. Assembly cycle roughly halved.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Massive piece-count and assembly-labour reduction plus rattle-warranty elimination.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: Baseline AGS ≈ €42/veh, ~€14/veh in mechanism+labour; delta ≈ €13 × 200k = €2.6M

ideaData.riskNotes: Film-hinge fatigue at −30 °C and creep under continuous open load are the risks; POM notch sensitivity at the hinge root. Mitigate with radiused hinge geometry, DMA/fatigue rig to 1M cycles across temperature, and airflow-sealing validation for the closed state. Confirm no cold-crack.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: POM living-hinge consolidation is established plastics-design practice; AGS-specific application not tied to a named programme.

title: Ultrasonic park sensors flush-mount behind unbroken fascia
description: Deletes bezels, seals, holes, and sensor-face painting; improves appearance and reduces ingress warranty. Baseline rear bumper carries 4-6 ultrasonic park sensors, each needing a Ø18 mm through-hole, a moulded/painted bezel, a rubber decoupling ring, per-hole paint-edge sealing and colour-matched face painting on a flow-rack. Proposal: mount the transducers on the fascia B-side against a locally thinned membrane (PP-TD20 wall reduced from ~3.0 mm to ~1.0 mm over the transducer footprint) so the sensor radiates through the intact painted skin — a true blind/flush install. Physics: at 48-58 kHz the acoustic wavelength (~6 mm in the polymer) lets a thin same-material membrane, coupled via a silicone gel pad (Shore 00 ~30), transmit adequately if wall thickness and damping are tuned. Deleting the hole removes all bezels, seals and face painting and closes a corrosion/water-ingress path.

costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: Bezels+seals+face-paint+drill ≈ €12/veh over 5 sensors; delta ≈ €12 × 200k = €2.4M

Mitigate with membrane-thickness DoE, gel-pad selection, and full parking-aid homologation across temperature and paint colours. Verify no resonance with road noise.

ideaData.materialGrade: PP-TD20 (20% talc PP) fascia with ~1.0 mm local membrane; Shore 00 ~30 silicone gel coupling pad

title: Fascia-to-fender datum self-locating via moulded snap gauges
description: Removes shims/adjusters and slashes gap-and-flush labour and rework. Baseline fascia is aligned to fenders and headlamps at final trim using adjustable brackets, shims and a fitter judging gap-and-flush by eye — driving labour, rework and warranty complaints. Proposal: integrate compliant self-datuming snap features (moulded 4-way and 2-way locators in PP-TD20) into the fascia end-caps that mate to hard reference points on the fender rail and lamp housing, converting a hand-adjusted joint into a net-build snap engagement. Physics: locating the fascia off the same hard datums as the lamp (not a chain of adjustable brackets) collapses the tolerance stack; compliant fingers absorb thermal expansion (PP CTE ~90 µm/m·K over a 600 mm span ≈ 3 mm swing at -30 to +80°C) while a rigid primary locator sets the visible gap to a ~3.5±0.5 mm target. Deletes shims, adjusters and most fitter time.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Removes shims/adjusters and slashes gap-and-flush labour and rework.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: Adjusters+labour+rework ≈ €8/veh; delta ≈ €8 × 200k = €1.6M

ideaData.benchmarkReference: Net-build self-locating trim datums are established DFA practice; no specific programme named.
ideaData.materialGrade: PP-TD20 (20% talc-filled PP, CTE ~90 µm/m·K) for the moulded locators/end-caps

title: Consolidate front-end sensing into one heated bracket carrier
description: Part-count and harness reduction plus fewer calibration and sealing operations. Baseline: forward radar, front camera bracket, and AGS controller each mount to separate PA66-GF35 brackets bolted at different points on the bumper/front-end carrier, each with its own connector and, for the camera, a discrete resistive heater film and harness. Proposal: mould a single PA66-GF35 sensor-carrier cross-plate that positions radar, camera, and AGS actuator on one datum-referenced part, with an integrated conductive PTC heater trace (over-moulded PPS carrier) serving both camera window and radar face de-icing, and a single sealed connector interface. Physics: co-locating sensors on one moulded datum removes alignment shims and cross-tolerance between brackets (critical for radar boresight <0.3°); one shared PTC heater with self-limiting resistance replaces two heater circuits and their controllers

costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: 3 brackets+fasteners+2 heaters+harness ≈ €22/veh, delta ≈ €10/veh × 200k = €2.0M

ideaData.riskNotes: Radar boresight stability on a larger single moulding under thermal load and PTC EMC near radar are the risks. Mitigate with glass-flow FEA for warp control, boresight validation over −40/+85 °C, and EMC screening of the heater trace routing away from the radar aperture.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Integrated front-end sensor carriers with shared heating are established ADAS-packaging practice; no specific programme named.

title: Two-shot fascia grille surround delete brightwork insert
description: Eliminates electroplating supply chain and an assembly step; removes plating adhesion warranty. Baseline upper fascia/grille surround is a painted PC/ABS carrier into which a separately moulded, PVD- or chrome-plated bright bezel is clipped or hot-staked — requiring a plating supply chain, its environmental burden and a stake/assembly station. Proposal: produce the surround as a single two-shot (2K) moulding — structural PC/ABS first shot, then a second shot of pre-coloured high-gloss UV-stabilised PMMA (or metallic-effect ASA) delivering the decorative bright ring without electroplating or PVD. Physics: 2K melt-interface bonding gives a fastener-free, gap-free bright-to-body transition; a high-flow PMMA capstock (e.g. Plexiglas-type moulding grade) provides Class-A gloss and weathering without a metal layer, and mono-decorative moulding removes the plating adhesion/tolerance failure mod

ideaData.benchmarkReference: 2K decorative brightwork replacing plating is established interior/exterior trim practice; no specific programme named.
ideaData.materialGrade: PC/ABS first shot (e.g. Bayblend-type); UV-stabilised PMMA (Plexiglas-type) or metallic-effect ASA second shot

title: Living-hinge in-mould folded lower fascia energy chin
description: Eliminates a tool, a weld station and the foam air-dam while cutting inbound freight. Baseline lower fascia/chin is a separate PP-TD20 injection moulding heat-staked to the main fascia via 14 posts, plus a foam air-dam splitter — 3 mouldings, 2 tools, 1 assembly station. Proposal: mould the chin as an integral flap on the main PP-TD20 fascia joined by a co-moulded ~0.8 mm PP living hinge, then fold-and-latch into a moulded snap channel on the closeout. PP homopolymer's high flex-fatigue endurance (>10^6 cycles at low strain when the hinge neutral axis is centred) lets one tool make a part that ships flat for freight density and folds line-side. Deletes one ~800-tonne press, one hot-plate welder and the foam air-dam. Hinge thinned via a 4 mm shut-off land held to ±0.05 mm; use unfilled/low-talc PP at the hinge for ductility since 20% talc embrittles the fold.

ideaData.materialGrade: PP-TD20 fascia body with a local unfilled/low-talc PP homopolymer living-hinge zone (~0.8 mm)

title: Grille shutter driven off HVAC vacuum, delete electric actuator
description: Trades a mechatronic bus node for a low-cost diaphragm and valve, cutting BOM and warranty exposure. Baseline active grille shutter uses a 12 V brushed/BLDC actuator (2-4 W, LIN bus, gear train, position feedback) driving a rack that opens/closes PA6-GF30 vanes — ~€9-13 actuator plus a harness node. Proposal: on ICE/MHEV platforms retaining a vacuum reservoir, drive the shutter with a single-diaphragm pneumatic actuator and a 2-port thermal/solenoid valve, spring-return to fail-open. A ~80-100 mm effective-area diaphragm delivers >40 N stroke at 300 mbar depression — ample against vane torque and aero load — with no gearbox, encoder or LIN node. Vanes stay PA6-GF30 with the existing film-hinge frame. Removes a bus address and its DTC burden; position sensed binary via 2 reed switches rather than continuous.

Mitigate with fluorosilicone diaphragm rated −40/+120°C, hydrophobic vent, and fail-open spring so a leak cannot cause engine overheat. Aero/CD certification unchanged as end positions identical.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Vacuum diaphragm actuation of underhood flaps is long-established practice (turbo wastegates, EGR valves); no specific grille-shutter programme named.
ideaData.materialGrade: PA6-GF30 (30% glass-filled nylon 6) vanes retained; no material change on the actuation lever

title: Shared substrate for radar bracket and shutter frame
description: One structural moulding does two jobs, shortening tolerance chain and cutting tooling. Baseline front end carries two separate structural mouldings behind the fascia: a PA6-GF30 radar bracket (3-point kinematic mount, ±0.3° aim tolerance) and the active grille shutter frame, each with its own tool and carrier attachment set. Proposal: mould them as a single PA6-GF35 (higher stiffness for aim retention, ~11 GPa flexural) 'sensing frame' where the radar's three datum bosses are cored directly into the shutter frame's top rail. Because both parts already reference the same fascia datum, integration removes a stack-up interface — radar aim variation improves (fewer tolerance links) while deleting one tool, one part number and 4 fasteners. Shutter vane bearings and radar bosses share one shot, guaranteeing coplanarity to ±0.15 mm; box-section ribbing on the top rail preserves aim under therma

title: Fascia colour-matched via bulk-dyed clearcoat film, delete basecoat
description: Removes two wet paint layers and their energy/VOC burden from the fascia. Baseline body-colour fascia runs the full liquid line: adhesion promoter, waterborne basecoat, 2K clearcoat plus flash/bake — 3 wet layers, ~€14–20/part with high VOC and oven-energy burden. Proposal: mould the fascia in PP-TD20 (20% talc-filled polypropylene, MFR ~12 g/10min, ~1.05 g/cm³) and apply a pre-manufactured 2-layer film — pigmented cast base plus aliphatic-polyurethane UV clearcoat — via in-mould-film (IMD/IMG) or thermoform-then-bond. Film is cast to the OEM colour master (ΔE<0.8 to adjacent e-coat/painted metal), setting match by incoming film QC not two spray booths. Total film 120–180 µm gives Class-A DOI (>80) and 5-year Florida weathering. Removes the fascia from the wet line, freeing booth capacity and cutting solvent-capture load.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Removes two wet paint layers and their energy/VOC burden from the fascia.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~€12/veh paint-cost delta × 160k = €1.92M plus booth energy/VOC and capacity value

Mitigate by limiting minimum radius to ≥3 mm, pre-heat forming, and 10-cycle Florida/thermal-shock + stone-chip validation. Colour harmony vs painted metal panels needs a controlled film-to-paint master; risk if body colour palette is wide.
dfmaPrinciples: Move colour control upstream to material
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Paint-replacement/appliqué films for exterior panels are established practice; PVDF-based weatherable films (e.g. Kynar-type fluoropolymer topcoats) are a widely-reported route — no specific fascia programme named.
ideaData.materialGrade: PP-TD20 substrate; cast paint film = pigmented PMMA/PVDF base + aliphatic-PU UV clearcoat, 120–180 µm

title: Snap-in fascia grille consolidating four clip families to one
description: Collapses four retention systems into one geometry, cutting parts, a station and mispicks. Baseline fascia carries the grille, fog bezels, tow-eye cover and lower trim each retained by a different clip/fastener family — typically 4 distinct clip part numbers, some metal doghouse clips, some screws — driving line complexity and mispick warranty. Proposal: redesign all four fascia-attached trims to share ONE moulded-in PA66 arrowhead snap geometry mating to a common cored slot on the fascia. A single clip spec (retention >90 N pull-off, insertion <40 N) covers every interface; metal clips and screws are deleted. Because the fascia slots are all cored in the same shot to the same tolerance, the trims become truly interchangeable at line-side and error-proofing is by geometry, not by picking the right clip.

ideaData.benchmarkReference: Clip-family rationalisation to a single arrowhead snap is established DFMA practice; no specific programme named.
ideaData.materialGrade: PA66 (snap features), PP-TD20 (fascia)

title: EPP bumper absorber overmoulded with PA6-GF beam ribs
description: Monolithic beam+absorber deletes the bolted interface, foam clip-in and a part number. Baseline bumper system stacks a separate steel or PP-LGF crash beam bolted to crush cans, with an EPP energy absorber block clipped in front — 2 major parts, bolted interface, foam that must be assembled and can dislodge. Proposal: use a moulded EPP absorber (60–90 g/L density-graded) as an insert placed into an injection tool and overmoulded with a PA6-GF40 rib grid that forms the structural beam directly on the foam. The GF-rib skin carries the RCAR/low-speed bending load while the graded EPP tunes the pedestrian lower-leg pulse; the chemical/mechanical key between EPP cells and the GF melt eliminates the bolted interface and the clip attachment. One tool produces beam+absorber as a monolithic module referenced to the crush-can bosses.

title: Camera/lidar mounted on fascia-integrated die-cast Al thermal pad
description: One casting replaces multiple brackets, a heater and the washer manifold, shortening aim tolerance and harness. Baseline forward ADAS camera and fascia lidar mount on separate stamped-steel brackets (DC04, ~1.2 mm) with add-on PTC heater pads, ad-hoc convection cooling and discrete washer nozzles/clips. Proposal: a single AlSi10Mg high-pressure die-cast bracket (as-cast T5, k≈150 W/m·K, wall 2.5–3 mm) bonded behind the fascia acts as (a) the kinematic 3-point sensor datum (machined pads, ±0.1 mm), (b) a conduction heat-spreader wicking sensor waste heat and giving de-ice thermal mass, and (c) an integrated washer manifold with cast/cored 3–4 mm internal channels feeding both sensors. The alloy's conductivity replaces the discrete heater on low-power sensors and the cast channels delete the moulded PA washer plumbing and clips.

title: IMSE in-mould electronics rear lamp — delete PCB, connectors, screws
description: Eliminates rigid PCB, connector, fasteners and one sub-assembly step by fusing electronics into the moulded part. Baseline rear lamp routes LEDs on a rigid FR4 PCB (or FR4+FPC stack) fixed with 6–8 M3 screws into a PC/ASA housing, wired via a discrete connector and harness pigtail. Proposal: in-mould electronics (IMSE) — screen-print silver conductive ink (e.g. DuPont 5064H, ~10 µm dry) onto 0.5 mm optical PC film (e.g. Makrofol), SMT-mount side-fire 0402/0603 LEDs plus driver passives with conductive adhesive, thermoform to the lamp 3D contour, then back-injection-mould PC-ABS behind it in one shot. The film becomes functional layer and diffuser substrate. Traces and LEDs are encapsulated by the melt front, killing solder-joint vibration fatigue and deleting the FR4 laminate (~€0.9/dm² vs PC film ~€0.15/dm²). Trace pitch 300 µm carries ~300 mA in printed silver.

title: Silicone (LSR) primary optic replaces PMMA + air-gap lens
description: Recovered optical efficiency reduces LED count; index coupling removes a lens and its alignment. Baseline projector/DRL uses an injection-moulded PMMA primary lens (e.g. Plexiglas 8N, n≈1.49, Tg~105 °C, softens ~80 °C service) held in a bezel with a defined air gap to the LED, plus a PC outer lens — two air interfaces and ~4% Fresnel loss per surface. Proposal: mould the primary optic in optical LSR (e.g. Dow MS-1002 or Sylgard optical-grade, n≈1.41, transmission >92% at 3 mm, Shore A ~60) over-moulded as a dome directly onto the LED phosphor, index-coupling optic to emitter. Index matching removes one air interface (recovers ~4% flux, permitting one fewer LED per string at equal lumens); LSR withstands 200 °C continuous vs PMMA's ~80 °C, so the optic sits closer to the die and shrinks optical track length ~15%.

title: Graphite thermal-interface pad replaces cast Al heat-sink fins
description: Replaces a machined aluminium casting with a die-cut laminate and offloads convection to the existing housing. Baseline high-power LED module dumps ~15 W into a die-cast AlSi9Cu3 finned heat-sink (~180 g), machined for flatness and coupled to the MCPCB via a gap filler. Proposal: bond a compressed/pyrolytic graphite spreader sheet (e.g. Panasonic PGS or NeoGraf eGraf, in-plane k≈400–1500 W/m·K, ~25–100 µm) laminated to a 1.0 mm 6082-T4 aluminium backplate, spreading heat laterally into the existing PC/ASA housing wall which becomes the radiator. Graphite's anisotropic in-plane conductivity moves heat sideways 4–8× faster than aluminium at a fraction of the mass, so bulk fin volume is unnecessary — the housing surface does the convection. Removes ~120 g and the machined-flat interface; a thin thermal adhesive replaces the gap filler.

title: Linear (non-switching) LED driver on 48 V lamp rail
description: Deletes inductor, catch diode and EMC filter by exploiting a low input-to-Vf headroom on 48 V. Baseline DRL/tail driver is a buck switching constant-current regulator (inductor, Schottky catch diode, MOSFET, controller IC, CISPR-25 EMC filter) sized for 12 V input with 9–16 V transient tolerance. Proposal: on vehicles with a 48 V or stabilised DC-DC lamp rail, replace the switcher with a linear active-current-sink IC (e.g. TI TPS9261x-class or an integrated linear string regulator) driving a longer series string so the summed LED Vf sits just below rail. With a 13-LED string at ~42 V total Vf on a tight 48 V rail, linear dropout is only ~6 V (~13% loss) so efficiency is acceptable, and the inductor, catch diode and EMC filter delete entirely — linear operation produces no switching harmonics, drastically cutting CISPR-25 compliance cost.

ideaData.benchmarkReference: Linear LED drivers on stabilised/higher-voltage rails are established practice; 48 V zonal lamp supply enables it — no specific OEM programme named.

title: Metal-core PCB deleted via direct LED-on-housing DBC route
description: Removes the MCPCB and a thermal interface, enabling a cheaper LED bin at equal beam performance. Baseline high-beam LED sits on an aluminium MCPCB (1.0 mm Al + 100 µm dielectric, k≈3–8 W/m·K, + 70 µm Cu) screwed/bonded to the heat-sink through a TIM — a 6-layer path (die–solder–Cu–dielectric–Al–TIM–sink). Proposal: mount the bare LED die/CSP onto a thin ceramic DBC tile (direct-bonded copper on Al2O3, k≈24 W/m·K, or AlN, k≈170 W/m·K) soldered directly (SAC305) to a machined boss on the AlSi10Mg die-cast housing, deleting the MCPCB and TIM. Each interface adds ~0.5–2 K/W; collapsing 6 layers to 3 roughly halves junction-to-housing Rth, letting the LED be driven harder or a cheaper lower-lumen bin used at equal output. AlN DBC far exceeds the MCPCB dielectric.

title: Outer lens hard-coat swap: flame-coat to plasma-CVD SiOx
description: Replaces a slow wet multi-step coat with a fast dry in-line plasma coat, cutting scrap and solvent capex. Baseline PC outer lens gets abrasion/UV protection via a wet flow-coat acrylic primer + acrylic-siloxane hard-coat (multi-step dip, flash, ~1 h thermal cure at 120 °C) — high WIP, solvent VOC handling, and 3–6% cosmetic reject for runs/dust. Proposal: replace with in-line atmospheric-pressure plasma-CVD of a graded SiOx/organosilicon hard-coat (HMDSO/O2 precursor) deposited directly on the moulded PC lens as a ~3–5 µm plasma-polymerised layer. Plasma cross-linking builds a dense SiOx network meeting ECE R7 Taber abrasion and UV/weathering requirements without a liquid primer, and the dry line cures in seconds not an hour — collapsing cycle time and eliminating solvent-capture capex and dip-tank consumable churn.

title: Vibration-weld lens seal replaces hot-melt butyl bead + clips
description: Removes butyl consumable and clips, and attacks condensation warranty via a hermetic parent-material weld. Baseline headlamp seals the PC outer lens to the PC/ASA housing with a heated butyl hot-melt bead in a groove plus 8–12 spring clips and a lens-press fixture; the butyl reservoir, applicator heater and clip inventory carry cost, and moisture-ingress condensation is a top-3 lamp warranty claim. Proposal: replace with linear or orbital vibration welding (weld frequency ~200–240 Hz, amplitude ~0.7–1.4 mm) of like-to-like PC lens to PC housing flange, no adhesive, producing a homogeneous fused joint. Frictional heating melts a thin PC layer at the flange that re-solidifies as parent material — a hermetic weld stronger than a butyl bond, eliminating the condensation moisture path. title: Phosphor-on-die white LED replaces remote-phosphor primary optic
description: Deletes phosphor plate, holder and a diffuser; reduces emitter count and QA rework. Baseline low-beam uses blue InGaN LEDs (~450 nm) with a separately moulded remote-phosphor plate (Ce:YAG in silicone, ~0.4 mm) held at an air gap in a PMMA collimator, plus a discrete diffuser. Change to chip-scale-package (CSP) white LEDs with Ce:YAG phosphor deposited conformally on-die by spray-coating and silicone overmould, wafer-tested and colour-binned. Deletes the phosphor plate, its holder, the ±0.15 mm air-gap tolerance stack that drives colour-over-angle, and one diffuser stage. On-die phosphor sits at the emission plane, minimising étendue so the downstream reflector/lens shrinks for equal lux at 25 m. CSP flip-chip has no wire bonds or ceramic submount, cutting junction-to-board Rth from ~6 K/W to ~2.5 K/W, permitting higher drive current and fewer emitters for the same 1350 lm.

title: Snap-fit LED module replacing screw-and-gasket serviceable mount
description: Removes fasteners, gasket, torque station and grease dispensing. Baseline LED sub-module is fastened to the ADC12 (A383) die-cast Al heat-sink with 3 × M3×6 self-tapping (Delta-PT/Plastite-class) screws through a 0.5 mm die-cut silicone gasket (VMQ, 50 Shore A), torqued to 0.6 Nm with in-line torque verification. Replace with a snap-fit: the 1.6 mm aluminium-core MCPCB is captured by two moulded PA66-GF30 spring latches on the housing that clamp the board against a pre-applied thermally conductive acrylic PSA (3M 8815-class, 0.2 mm, ~3 W/mK) doubling as gasket and thermal interface. The PSA replaces gap-filler grease and the compression gasket; latches replace all fasteners. Thermal contact pressure comes from latch preload (8–12 N) not screw torque, giving repeatable 0.2 mm bond-line and eliminating torque-driven MCPCB warp that raises Rth.

title: Aluminium IMS core downgauged to 0.8 mm on thermal-via FR4
description: Swaps specialty IMS for commodity FR4 on low-power channels; enables double-sided densification. Baseline rear-lamp LED board is a 1.6 mm aluminium IMS (5052-class base, 75 µm dielectric) — costly base metal, single-sided routing only. For low-power signals (<0.5 W/LED) replace with a standard 0.8 mm FR4 (Tg ≥150 °C, IPC-4101/126, 2×35 µm Cu) using dense thermal-via arrays: 0.3 mm plated (25 µm Cu barrel) vias at ~1 mm pitch under each LED thermal pad, tied to a bottom Cu pour that contacts the housing via a 0.5–1 mm gap pad (~3 W/mK). This achieves ~8–12 K/W junction-to-housing for sub-watt emitters — adequate below the ~2 W/cm² flux where IMS becomes necessary. FR4 permits double-sided placement (driver on back), shrinking board area, and uses commodity fab rather than specialty IMS lines, cutting bare-board cost 40–60%.

title: Housing pressure-vent membrane replaces labyrinth breather boss
description: Removes tool slide, foam filter and an assembly step; reduces condensation warranty. Baseline sealed headlamp manages condensation with a moulded labyrinth breather (tortuous multi-rib channel needing tool slides) plus a foam filter, sized to equalise pressure over thermal cycling while blocking water/dust. Replace with an oleophobic ePTFE vent membrane (Gore PolyVent / Donaldson-class, IP69K, ~10–15 mm active area, water-entry pressure >7 kPa) laser- or ultrasonic-welded over a simple straight-through moulded port in the PP/ASA housing. The membrane passes water vapour and equalises pressure but blocks liquid, deleting the labyrinth geometry, its tool slides, the foam filter and its assembly step. The straight port removes a mould action, shortening cycle and cutting tool maintenance; membrane airflow (>200 ml/min at 70 mbar) improves demisting versus the restrictive labyrinth.

ideaData.title: Housing pressure-vent membrane replaces labyrinth breather boss
ideaData.technicalDescription: Baseline sealed headlamp manages condensation with a moulded labyrinth breather (tortuous multi-rib channel needing tool slides) plus a foam filter, sized to equalise pressure over thermal cycling while blocking water/dust. Replace with an oleophobic ePTFE vent membrane (Gore PolyVent / Donaldson-class, IP69K, ~10–15 mm active area, water-entry pressure >7 kPa) laser- or ultrasonic-welded over a simple straight-through moulded port in the PP/ASA housing. The membrane passes water vapour and equalises pressure but blocks liquid, deleting the labyrinth geometry, its tool slides, the foam filter and its assembly step. The straight port removes a mould action, shortening cycle and cutting tool maintenance; membrane airflow (>200 ml/min at 70 mbar) improves demisting versus the restrictive labyrinth.
ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Deletes labyrinth slide from housing tool (major tool simplification, shorter cycle). Removes foam-filter insertion station. Adds one membrane weld/apply station (fast, automated). Net wash roughly neutral on stations but strong tool-cost and cycle-time gain.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Removes tool slide, foam filter and an assembly step; reduces condensation warranty.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: Membrane €0.30 vs foam+labyrinth assembly €0.55 + €0.25 cycle-time saving + tool-slide amortisation €0.15 = €0.65 net × 300,000 × 2 ≈ €0.9M; condensation warranty avoidance adds upside

ideaData.riskNotes: Membrane must survive high-pressure wash (IP69K) and not clog with road film/wax — validate airflow retention after mud/salt soak. Adhesive/weld seal integrity checked by helium leak and thermal-shock cycling. Anti-fog demisting time re-validated per OEM condensation spec.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: ePTFE pressure-equalisation vents are established, widely-used practice in automotive lighting and electronics enclosures; no specific programme named.
ideaData.materialGrade: Oleophobic ePTFE vent membrane (Gore PolyVent / Donaldson-class), IP69K, WEP >7 kPa; no board material lever

title: Copper-clad bond wires downgauged via silver-alloy replacement
description: Removes gold content from high-count emitters via supplier package spec. Baseline high-power LED emitters in the low-beam module use 25 µm gold (Au, 4N) ball-bond wires at the die interconnect — a legacy standard whose cost tracks the gold price. Specify LED packages using palladium-coated copper (PCC) or silver-alloy (Ag-Pd, ~2–4% Pd) bond wires: 25 µm PCC has ~40% lower electrical resistivity (~1.7 vs ~2.4 µΩ·cm) and comparable ampacity to Au, at a fraction of the per-length cost. This is a supplier-package specification lever, not a board change: mandating PCC or Ag-alloy-bonded emitters at sourcing drops emitter unit price with no change to footprint, reflow profile or photometrics. Lower wire resistance marginally cuts I²R bond self-heating, slightly aiding lumen maintenance. Applies across high-count matrix modules where wire-bond content dominates BOM.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Removes gold content from high-count emitters via supplier package spec.

Confirm no photometric or Vf drift. Sole-source risk if only one emitter vendor offers the spec — dual-source before commit.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: PCC and silver-alloy bond wires are established mainstream practice in LED and IC packaging (broad industry migration off gold since the 2010s); no specific programme named.
ideaData.materialGrade: 25 µm palladium-coated copper (PCC) or Ag-Pd (~2–4% Pd) bond wire, replacing 25 µm 4N Au — supplier package spec

title: Driver EMI filter simplified by spread-spectrum switching IC
description: Shrinks EMI filter BOM by exploiting dither headroom. Baseline LED driver is a fixed-frequency 2.2 MHz buck whose conducted/radiated EMI (CISPR 25) is tamed with a heavy front end: two common-mode chokes, an X-cap, two Y-caps, a ferrite bead and a shielded inductor — bulky, over-margined parts. Replace the controller with a driver IC using dithered/spread-spectrum frequency modulation (±10% triangular, ~10–15 kHz modulation, e.g. TI LM53635/LMR33630-class or Infineon TLD5-class parts), which smears switching harmonics across a band, dropping peak/QP EMI 8–15 dBµV. That headroom shrinks the filter to one common-mode choke and a single Y-cap and permits an unshielded standard inductor. Physics: EMI limits are peak/QP measured in a fixed 9 kHz/120 kHz RBW, so spreading the same energy over more frequency bins lowers the measured peak without lowering total energy.

ideaData.benchmarkReference: Spread-spectrum switching regulators for EMI reduction are established practice across automotive power electronics (offered in mainstream TI, Infineon, ADI buck families); no specific programme named.

title: Chemically strengthened aluminosilicate thin windscreen outer ply
description: Mass reduction supports range/CO2 credits; glass material volume down offsets CS premium at high volume. Baseline windscreen is 2.1 mm soda-lime float outer + 0.76 mm PVB + 2.1 mm inner. Replace the 2.1 mm outer with a 1.1 mm ion-exchanged aluminosilicate (Corning Gorilla / AGC Dragontrail class) chemically strengthened in a KNO3 molten-salt bath (~420 °C) to ~700 MPa surface compressive stress with ~40 µm depth-of-layer. The high DoL suppresses stone-chip crack propagation despite the thinner ply, so it survives field impact where a downgauged soda-lime ply would not. Net glass mass drops ~2.6 kg/vehicle. The asymmetric build (thin CS outer + standard soda-lime inner) laminates on existing autoclave lines with a modified de-airing ring for the stiffness mismatch. Interlayer stays 0.76 mm acoustic (tri-layer) PVB. Gravity-sag bending runs at reduced peak temperature to avoid stress relax

ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Adds an ion-exchange salt-bath station (or bought-in CS glass) before lamination; deletes no stations. Gravity-bend furnace profile retuned per ply. Autoclave cycle unchanged. Deairing tooling revised for mixed-modulus stack; expect scrap uptick first 3 months during bend-match tuning.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Mass reduction supports range/CO2 credits; glass material volume down offsets CS premium at high volume.
costSavingPotential.percentage: 8-12% of windscreen weight, net 3-6% cost at scale
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: 2.6 kg saved × €4-6/kg fleet CO2/lightweighting credit value + glass volume delta, less CS ply premium ~€8/screen × 120k

ideaData.riskNotes: Asymmetric ply stiffness raises optical distortion (roller wave, edge lensing) risk — mitigate with matched gravity-sag bend and RhoMap distortion gating. Long-term edge-impact durability differs from monolithic; validate FMVSS 205 / ECE R43 impact and gravel-blast. Alkali migration into PVB controlled by primer.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Ford GT (2017) used a Corning Gorilla Glass hybrid laminated windshield — a genuine, widely-reported chemically-strengthened auto-glazing example; applied here as a downgauge lever.
ideaData.materialGrade: 1.1 mm ion-exchanged aluminosilicate outer (Corning Gorilla / AGC Dragontrail class), ~700 MPa CS / ~40 µm DoL; 0.76 mm acoustic PVB; soda-lime inner
ideaData.regulatoryContext: Must meet FMVSS 205, ANSI Z26.1, ECE R43 for laminated windscreens including impact and abrasion.

title: Modular seal corner injection replacing full-frame extrusion moulding
description: Tooling amortisation collapses; enables low-volume glass variants economically. Baseline fixed side/quarter-glass seal uses full-perimeter RIM injection overmoulding (PVC or TPE) requiring a large closed-frame tool and long shot. Change to straight co-extruded EPDM (or TPV, e.g. Santoprene-class) run sections joined only at the four corners by localised injection-moulded corner nodes (TPV ~85 Shore A) in a compact 4-cavity corner tool. Straight runs are cut-to-length from continuous extrusion (near-zero per-profile tooling), and only the geometrically complex corners carry mould cost. This decouples seal length from tool size, so glass variants sharing corner geometry reuse one corner tool across the range. The corner interface is joined by molten-TPV welding onto the extrudate ends within the node cavity, giving a monolithic sealed loop without adhesive.

ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Deletes large full-frame RIM tool (~€180-350k) and replaces with small corner-node tool (~€40-70k). Adds extrusion cut + corner-injection cell; cycle time per corner node ~25-40 s parallelised. Lower melt volume cuts energy/shot; scrap from purge minimal versus large RIM shots.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Tooling amortisation collapses; enables low-volume glass variants economically.
costSavingPotential.percentage: 20-35% of seal tooling cost per variant
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: Tool delta ~€200k × 5 variants amortised + melt/energy saving ~€0.6/part × 400k parts

ideaData.riskNotes: Corner weld line is the water-tightness weak point — validate with pressurised leak, thermal-cycle and UV-aged peel adhesion at the extrudate/node interface. Dimensional stack of cut runs must hold ±0.5 mm to seat glass; mitigate with fixtured cut and datum-located corner cell.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Corner-moulding of extruded weatherstrip (injection-moulded corners on cut runs) is long-established tier-1 door/glass sealing practice; applied here to fixed-glass encapsulation.
ideaData.materialGrade: Sulphur-cured EPDM (60–70 Shore A) straight runs; injection-moulded TPV corner nodes ~85 Shore A (Santoprene-class)
ideaData.regulatoryContext: Water intrusion / wind-noise sealing to internal OEM specs; no direct type approval.

title: Bio-based EPDM with recycled-EPDM core in co-extruded seal
description: Recyclate cheaper than virgin EPDM and diverts scrap from disposal. Baseline body weatherstrip is 100% virgin EPDM with carbon-black (N550/N660-class) reinforcement and sulphur cure. Change to a co-extruded dual-durometer profile where the non-visible, non-sealing carrier/backbone uses a devulcanised recycled-EPDM compound (cryogenically ground production offcuts + post-industrial regrind) at ~30–40% loading, while the outer sealing lip and Class-A visible skin remain virgin EPDM (or bio-attributed EPDM from bio-naphtha ethylene, ISCC+ mass-balance). The recycled core carries only geometry and clip retention, so reduced elongation-at-break (~150–250%) is acceptable there. Sulphur cure retained; recyclate size-classified <0.4 mm to avoid lip surface defects and back-fed only to the core extruder head in the co-extrusion crosshead.

ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Adds a second extruder feed and crosshead for the recyclate core (many lines already have dual/triple extruders). Requires regrind classification and drying station. No cure oven change. Slight line-speed reduction during recyclate dispersion tuning; scrap self-consumes, cutting waste disposal cost.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Recyclate cheaper than virgin EPDM and diverts scrap from disposal.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: Core ~35% of profile mass × €0.8-1.2/kg saved vs virgin × ~2 kg seal/car × 150k, plus avoided scrap disposal

ideaData.riskNotes: Recyclate raises compression-set and lowers tear in the core — must confirm clip retention force and long-term set (ISO 815) at 70/100°C. Odour/VOC from devulcanisate needs cabin-air compliance testing. Keep recyclate strictly out of sealing lip to protect wind-noise/water function.
dfmaPrinciples: Use lower-grade material where duty allows
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Devulcanised EPDM regrind in non-visible seal cores is established practice among tier-1 sealing suppliers' sustainability lines (Cooper Standard, Hutchinson); no specific programme named.
ideaData.materialGrade: Virgin EPDM (60–70 Shore A) lip/skin, optional ISCC+ bio-attributed EPDM; devulcanised recycled-EPDM core (<0.4 mm regrind, ~30–40% loading); sulphur cure; N550/N660 carbon black
ideaData.regulatoryContext: Cabin VOC/odour (VDA 270/278) and ELV recyclate content targets.

title: Encapsulation-integrated antenna and rain sensor bracket in glass frame
description: Deletes bonded brackets, adhesive, and two assembly operations; fewer part numbers. Baseline windscreen carries separately bonded brackets for the rain/light sensor, camera mount and a discrete header-clipped antenna module. Change the PA66-GF30 (or TPE) injection encapsulation frame to integrate: (a) a moulded-in datum boss and snap features for the rain/light-sensor gel pad, and (b) an in-mould-assembled stamped antenna/ground conductor insert (0.3–0.5 mm CuZn37/C260 brass or tin-plated CuSn) positioned in the frit-hidden frame zone. The encapsulation shot captures the metal insert and forms the sensor interface in one tool cycle, deleting two downstream bond operations and their adhesive/cure time. Frame wall in the insert region is thickened to 3.2 mm for encapsulation and dielectric spacing; snap tolerances held ±0.2 mm to the glass datum for sensor optical alignment.

ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Adds insert-loading robot + preheat to encapsulation cell; deletes two adhesive bond/cure stations and their fixtures downstream. Slightly longer encapsulation cycle (~+6-10 s for insert load). Reduced adhesive consumption and cure oven load; fewer error-proofing checks in assembly.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Deletes bonded brackets, adhesive, and two assembly operations; fewer part numbers.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: 2 deleted ops × €0.9/car labour+adhesive + 2 fewer part numbers logistics × 100k units

ideaData.riskNotes: Insert encapsulation risks flash over conductor pads and read-through sink on Class-A frame — mitigate with sequenced valve gating and insert masking. Antenna performance shift from PA66-GF30 dielectric must be tuned. Sensor optical alignment now depends on moulded datum; validate with camera calibration yield study.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: In-mould insert integration into glass encapsulation (function-integrated windscreen modules) is established tier-1 glass-module practice; no specific programme named.
ideaData.materialGrade: PA66-GF30 encapsulation frame; 0.3–0.5 mm CuZn37 (C260) brass or tin-plated CuSn stamped antenna/ground insert
ideaData.regulatoryContext: ADAS camera field-of-view and calibration standards; antenna EMC to vehicle spec.

title: Cold-bent single-curvature panoramic glass replacing hot-bent laminate
description: Avoids bend furnace/mould capex and cuts distortion scrap. Baseline panoramic roof glass is gravity-sag/press bent to compound curvature, needing a dedicated bending mould, long furnace dwell, and optical-distortion scrap. For roofs with gentle single-axis curvature, change to cold-bending: flat laminate of 2.1 mm + 0.76 mm PVB + 2.1 mm soda-lime (heat-strengthened, not fully tempered, to allow the sustained bend stress) is elastically deformed onto the body flange during bonding and held by a high-modulus one-part PUR bead (e.g. Sika SikaTack, E >7 MPa). Requires R > ~5 m so surface tensile stress stays <25 MPa (well below heat-strengthened threshold). Acoustic or stiff-PVB (e.g. Saflex DG) interlayer limits shear creep; retained stress managed via bead geometry and cure fixture dwell.

ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Deletes glass bending furnace/mould for this part (major capex avoidance) — glass runs on flat lamination line. Adds a cold-bend fixture at the body bonding station holding curvature during PU cure. Lower glass scrap (no bend distortion reject). Increased bonding-station dwell and fixture count.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Avoids bend furnace/mould capex and cuts distortion scrap.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: Bend mould+furnace amortisation ~€8-12/part + scrap reduction ~€4/part × 70k, plus ~€300k mould capex avoided

ideaData.riskNotes: Retained elastic stress + PVB creep risks delamination or spontaneous fracture over life — cap surface stress, validate with FEA + long-term thermal-cycle and hail impact. Adhesive bond becomes structural/safety-critical; specify HM PU with proven creep and validate bond durability to VDA/OEM crash-retention. Limited to shallow curvature only.
dfmaPrinciples: Use assembly force to create geometry
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Cold-bent laminated glass is established practice in architectural facades and has been adopted on automotive panoramic roofs (early 2020s); mechanism proven, no specific programme claimed.
ideaData.materialGrade: Soda-lime float, heat-strengthened, 2.1/0.76(PVB)/2.1 mm; stiff/acoustic PVB (e.g. Saflex DG); high-modulus 1K PUR structural adhesive
ideaData.regulatoryContext: ECE R43 roof glazing, roof-crush/retention per FMVSS 216; structural bond durability.

title: Water-clear TPV encapsulation deleting painted frit on backlite edge
description: Cuts ceramic paste, screen-print time and firing energy on the frit band. Baseline tempered backlite hides the bond line and blocks UV with a ceramic frit band screen-printed and fired at ~600°C, plus a separate PVC/TPE encapsulation. Change to a wide-lip injection/co-extruded TPV encapsulation (Santoprene-type, Shore A 65–80, EPDM-PP dynamically vulcanised) whose opaque black lip provides the UV shadow and cosmetic edge hide, cutting fired frit band width by ~60% (retained only as a thin adhesion-priming stripe) or eliminating it where the lip fully overlaps the PUR bond. TPV compounded with HALS UV stabiliser plus ≥2% carbon black (N550/N660) for opacity and weathering; lip section ~1.5–2.5 mm defines the visible edge. Polymer lip absorbs UV protecting the PU bond and removes screen-print + firing value from the wider band.

ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Reduces or deletes ceramic frit screen-print + tempering-furnace fire-on step width; encapsulation tool lip widened. Fewer screen changes and less ceramic paste. Requires encapsulation lip dimensional control to guarantee UV overlap over the bead. Net station reduction on glass pre-process.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Cuts ceramic paste, screen-print time and firing energy on the frit band.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: Reduced ceramic paste + screen throughput gain ~€3-5/backlite × 130k, net of wider encapsulation lip material

ideaData.riskNotes: Any bond-line gap between TPV lip and PU bead exposes adhesive to UV — mitigate with guaranteed overlap dimension and edge-seal geometry; validate with QUV/Florida exposure and lap-shear retention. Frit also aids adhesion; keep priming stripe or apply silane primer to bare glass. Confirm backlite defrost busbar clearance.
dfmaPrinciples: Let one feature serve multiple functions
Remove printed/fired features where polymer substitutes
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Encapsulation lip as UV/cosmetic edge is established practice on modular backlites; frit reduction under a wide encapsulation lip is a known lever, no specific programme claimed.
ideaData.materialGrade: TPV (EPDM/PP dynamically vulcanised, e.g. Santoprene), Shore A 65–80, HALS + ≥2% carbon black (N550/N660)
ideaData.regulatoryContext: ECE R43 backlite, adhesive UV durability to OEM bond spec.

title: Glass-run channel flock replaced by low-friction TPV slip-coat co-extrusion
description: Removes flock consumables, VOC abatement and a full sub-line. Baseline door glass-run channel uses EPDM/TPV carrier with a separately applied flock (adhesive + electrostatically deposited polyamide fibre) on the sliding lips to give low glass-drop friction and quiet run. The flock line requires a solvent-based adhesive, flocking chamber, curing oven, and generates VOC and adhesive cost. Change to an in-line co-extruded ultra-low-friction slip-coat: a thin (~0.15-0.3 mm) surface layer of siloxane-modified or UHMW-PE-filled TPV extruded simultaneously onto the lip contact zones, delivering coefficient of friction ~0.15-0.25 against glass without fibre. Eliminates the entire flocking sub-line and its consumables. Slip-coat compound bonds by co-extrusion melt fusion, so no adhesion primer.

The flock line requires a solvent-based adhesive, flocking chamber, curing oven, and generates VOC and adhesive cost. Change to an in-line co-extruded ultra-low-friction slip-coat: a thin (~0.15-0.3 mm) surface layer of siloxane-modified or UHMW-PE-filled TPV extruded simultaneously onto the lip contact zones, delivering coefficient of friction ~0.15-0.25 against glass without fibre. ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Deletes flock adhesive spray, flock chamber, and flock cure oven (significant line/floor space and VOC abatement). Adds a small third co-extruder + slip-coat crosshead layer. Net cycle unchanged. Removes solvent handling and flock-fibre inventory; cuts VOC permit load.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Removes flock consumables, VOC abatement and a full sub-line.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: Flock adhesive+fibre+energy ~€0.4-0.6/run × 4 runs × 150k, plus sub-line labour/VOC abatement avoided

ideaData.riskNotes: Slip-coat must match flock on friction, squeak/rattle (stick-slip) and abrasion over 30k+ cycles — validate with glass drop-cycle rig, cold-temperature CoF, and Ziegler/BSR testing. Acoustic 'felt' quietness of flock is hard to match; tune slip-coat surface texture. Verify no glass surface marring long term.
dfmaPrinciples: Replace secondary coating with integral extruded layer
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Low-friction slip-coat co-extrusions as flock alternatives are established supplier practice (siliconised/UHMW-PE surface layers on glass runs); no specific programme claimed.

ideaData.regulatoryContext: Cabin VOC (VDA 278), BSR/NVH internal specs; no type approval.

title: Two-mode PUR encapsulation gate switch cutting cavity fill time
description: Throughput gain on a capacity-constrained encapsulation cell plus scrap reduction Baseline windscreen/quarter-glass PUR-RIM encapsulation runs a single centre-gate RIM head into an aluminium tool, forming an ~8–12 mm profile of ~1.1 g/cm³ two-component MDI-polyol PUR (e.g. Bayflex/Baydur). Long flow paths force 45–55°C mould temp and 90–120 s cure to avoid short-shots at the far corner, needing 3–5% overfill flash. Proposal: convert to a sequential dual-gate RIM manifold with servo needle valves, filling from two diagonal corners so max flow length halves. Shorter flow lets isocyanate index (~105) and tin catalyst (DBTDL, ~0.02–0.05 phr) be re-tuned for faster gel, dropping cure to 60–75 s and overfill to 1–2%. Physics: fill pressure scales with flow-length squared, so halving path quarters pressure and shear heat, permitting a cooler tool and less demould scrap.

title: Frameless door glass edge-strengthened by laser cut plus etch
description: Grinding elimination, furnace energy, and slight glass downgauge Baseline frameless side glass (3.85–4.0 mm soda-lime, thermally toughened) is CNC seamed/ground on all edges, leaving microcracks that are the fracture origins, so glass is over-toughened (surface compression ~110 MPa, longer furnace time) to hit the 3 J impact and self-weight spec. Proposal: replace mechanical grinding with picosecond laser filament cutting (Bessel-beam perforation + cleave) followed by a short buffered-HF etch (dilute HF/NH4F, ~1–3 min) that blunts crack tips to <1 µm radius. A defect-free edge raises inert strength, so target surface compression can fall to ~90 MPa, cutting furnace dwell/energy and allowing a ~0.2 mm downgauge to 3.7 mm. Physics: edge strength follows Griffith flaw depth; the polished laser edge removes the grinding-flaw population that drives failure.

title: Structural-adhesive-ready ceramic frit deletes primer wipe step
description: Deletes primer material, station and VOC handling at direct-glaze Baseline bonded windscreens/backlites carry a black ceramic frit band, then require a two-step activator-plus-PUR-primer wipe on the frit before the high-modulus PUR bead (e.g. Sika Betaseal/SikaTack). The primer exists because standard frit surface energy and residual organics give marginal aged adhesion. Proposal: switch to a UV-blocking, adhesion-active ceramic enamel (silane/organofunctional-modified lead-free glass frit, co-fired during bending at ~640°C) presenting a hydroxyl-rich, high-surface-energy face engineered for direct silane-terminated PUR bonding. Physics: fired-in coupling chemistry forms siloxane bonds to the PUR silane package directly, so the wet primer wipe and its 5–10 min flash-off become unnecessary while cataplasma/humidity-aged lap-shear stays above spec (cohesive failure retained).

title: Recycled-content post-industrial cullet loop for tempered backlites
description: Melt-energy and raw-batch reduction plus reject-glass value recovery Baseline tempered backlites and side glass are melted from batch dominated by virgin sand/soda-ash/limestone with ~10–20% mixed external cullet. Melting soda-lime consumes ~4.2 GJ/tonne, dominated by endothermic batch reactions; each +10% cullet cuts specific melt energy ~2.5% by skipping carbonate decomposition. Proposal: establish a closed colour- and composition-matched post-industrial cullet loop — automotive edge-trim, CNC offcuts and reject tempered glass crushed, ceramic/frit-contamination sorted by optical + LIBS/XRF, and returned to the same float furnace at 40–50% cullet for the specific low-iron/green-tint composition (Fe2O3 held to the tint spec). Physics: matched cullet holds redox ratio and iron content in-spec so solar/optical (Tvis, TTS) targets hold while decarbonation energy and CO2 fall sharply.

title: Foam-core weatherstrip via microcellular chemical foaming downgauge
description: EPDM mass reduction per metre at equal sealing force Baseline dense-EPDM body weatherstrip lip/bulb sections run solid or sponge-foamed with conventional ADC/azodicarbonamide blowing at ~30-40% void, giving a bulb of set wall thickness for the required 30-50 N/100 mm closing force. Proposal: co-extrude the bulb wall in microcellular EPDM using a controlled endothermic-plus-nucleator chemical foaming system (sodium bicarbonate/citric masterbatch with a nucleating filler) tuned to 45-55% uniform closed-cell void with cell size <100 µm. Finer, higher void lowers effective wall modulus so the same compression-deflection curve is met at ~15% less polymer mass and thinner wall. Physics: compression force scales with wall stiffness (E·t); replacing solid rubber with fine closed-cell foam drops effective E faster than it drops sealing integrity, so target CLD is held at lower material weight.

title: Metal carrier deletion via extruded engineered-polymer spine in seal
description: Metal carrier and its supply chain deleted; mass and corrosion risk removed Baseline door-aperture weatherstrip clip-on channel uses a continuous roll-formed steel or knitted-wire carrier co-extruded inside EPDM to give retention grip force on the flange (typ. 40-70 N/100 mm pull-off). The steel adds mass, corrosion risk, and forces a stamping/roll-form supply chain. Proposal: replace the metal carrier with a co-extruded high-modulus glass-fibre-reinforced polypropylene spine (PP-GF30, ~7 GPa flex modulus) profiled with integral barbed flange-gripping ribs, extruded simultaneously with the EPDM bulb. Physics: retention comes from elastic clamp force of the ribbed spine on the flange; a GF30 spine section can be dimensioned to match the flange clamp stiffness of thin steel while cutting density from 7.8 to ~1.15 g/cm³, and eliminating galvanic corrosion at the flange.

title: Backlite silver busbar replaced by copper-foil laminated bonded tab
description: Silver mass reduction on busbars, largest precious-metal driver on the part Baseline heated backlites screen-print silver-frit busbars and connection pads (fired ~620°C) feeding the printed heating grid; the wide busbars carry the largest silver mass, and silver at commodity price dominates conductor cost. Proposal: keep the thin fired silver heating lines but replace heavy silver busbars/solder pads with pre-tinned copper foil ribbon (35–70 µm, C11000 ETP copper) laminated to grid ends using isotropic Ag-filled epoxy conductive adhesive or ACF film, or ultrasonic-bonded, avoiding lead solder. Physics: copper resistivity (1.7 µΩ·cm) beats printed fired silver (~3–6 µΩ·cm effective), so thin copper carries busbar current with far less precious metal; fired silver is reserved only for the fine grid where print resolution is needed.

title: Nonwoven cotton-shoddy absorber with graded airflow-resistivity loft
description: Deletes PU chemistry, scrim adhesive and a press station while using low-cost recyclate. Baseline hood/engine-bay absorber is a two-density moulded PU foam pad (~60 g/L skin over 25 g/L core, ~28 mm) with a PET scrim facing, cut and heat-formed separately. Replace with a single-shot thermobonded nonwoven of recycled cotton-shoddy + 15% low-melt bico-PET fibre (sheath ~110°C co-PET / PET core, ~4 dtex), needle-punched then hot-air through-bonded to create a graded airflow-resistivity gradient: dense 1200–1800 Ns/m³ skin at the noise-source face grading to lofted 400–600 Ns/m³ at the panel side. Physics: peak absorption (α>0.9) shifts with the AFR·thickness product, so loft grading tunes 500–4000 Hz without a discrete facing layer. The bico melt-web fuses the skin during the same oven pass, deleting the adhesive scrim; low-melt fibre gives formability so one tool covers 3 contour variants.

title: Semi-active particle-damper cartridge replacing three tuned-mass dampers
description: One robust broadband device replaces three tuned devices and their variant complexity. Baseline subframe/steering-column NVH fix is 3 discrete tuned-mass dampers (TMD): each a cast-zinc or steel seismic mass on a vulcanised natural-rubber spring tuned to a single resonance (~180/240/320 Hz).
