Seal integrity/leak-down (shot egress) over life is critical; ultrasonic weld and helium-leak test. Rattle/tonal risk at low amplitude — confirm subjective NVH.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Particle/granular damping is established in aerospace and machine tools; automotive subframe use is an emerging but proven mechanism — no specific programme named.

title: Injection-moulded microperforated PC barrier-absorber for e-motor cover

title: Feedforward road-noise cancellation replaces bulk floor barrier mat
description: Trades passive low-frequency mass for near-free active cancellation on speaker-equipped trims. Baseline structure-borne road-noise control uses a heavy mass-spring floor barrier (EVA/EPDM heavy-layer ~5 kg/m² over PU decoupler) across the floor pan. Trade this against a feedforward Active Road Noise Control (ARNC) subassembly: 6–8 accelerometers on suspension knuckles/subframe feeding an FxLMS DSP that drives the existing premium audio speakers with anti-noise below ~500 Hz — exactly the band where passive barrier mass is least efficient (mass law needs doubling mass per 6 dB). Physics: at low frequency, active cancellation delivers 3–8 dB with zero added mass, letting the passive heavy-layer downgauge from 5 to ~2.5 kg/m² while the 500 Hz–4 kHz range stays with a thinner fibrous absorber. Reuses amplifier DSP headroom and cabin mics already fitted for hands-free.

title: 3D-knitted spacer-fabric absorber replacing moulded fibre + scrim
description: Roll-good conformable absorber at ~40% areal mass deletes the moulding tool entirely. Baseline pillar/headliner-edge absorber is moulded PET fibre felt (~800 g/m², ~15 mm) with a thermobonded scrim facing and a die-cut outline. Replace with a warp-knitted 3D spacer fabric (two PET face layers joined by PET monofilament spacer yarns, ~0.10–0.20 mm monofil, 8–12 mm gauge) whose open architecture gives a tuned uniform AFR set by yarn denier and stitch density. Physics: the monofilament pile creates a controlled tortuous air path (AFR ~600–1500 Ns/m³) and the two knit faces act as porous resistive skins, giving broadband absorption at ~40% the areal mass of moulded felt for equal α across 1–5 kHz. Produced to net width on a double-needle-bar Raschel machine and simply cut — no heated compression mould; highly conformable, drapes into pillar cavities without a moulding tool.

title: Integrated foam-in-place decoupler around wiring in dash insulator
description: Closes dominant dash leak paths cheaply, avoiding a costly heavy-layer upgrade, and deletes grommet SKUs. Baseline dash insulator is a moulded EVA heavy-layer (ISO 15xx-grade, 4–6 kg/m²) over a 15–20 mm PU ether-foam decoupler (0.03 g/cm³) with hand-cut relief slots and add-on foam grommets at the steering column, HVAC and harness pass-throughs — the leak paths that cap real dash insertion loss. Replace discrete grommets with a robot-dispensed 2K polyurethane foam-in-place bead (MDI/polyol, ~50–120 g/L free-rise, 25–40 s tack) shot into a moulded 8–12 mm channel that seals continuously around penetrations after harness routing. Physics: dash IL is set by the weakest leak, not panel average; a continuous compliant FIP seal (Shore 00 30–45) closes flanking paths, adding 3–6 dB effective IL for a few grams — cheaper than upgrading the heavy-layer.

title: Active-control trade: 6-mic ANC replaces heavy-layer only above 300 Hz split
description: Swaps a heavy passive barrier for a mostly-reused electronic system, cutting mass and a moulding cell. Baseline front-floor NVH is a full mass-spring package: EVA heavy-layer (~6 kg/m²) plus 15–20 mm PU decoupler tuned for 100–500 Hz road boom. Proposal is a frequency-split hybrid: retain a thin light decoupling felt (~400 g/m² 100% PET needle-punch) for structure-borne >300 Hz, delete the heavy-layer, and offload 60–300 Hz boom to a 6-microphone feedforward road-noise ANC running on the premium-audio DSP with door/headliner speakers plus two tri-axial accelerometers on the front subframe. title: Foamed-in-place poroelastic decoupler with integrated barrier skin
description: Part-count and assembly-clip elimination via one graded-density shot. Baseline wheelhouse-to-rocker absorber is a moulded fibre absorber clipped to a separate PP barrier tray (talc-filled PP, ~2.5 mm) with a foam gasket. Proposal: a single reaction-injection over-moulded part — self-forming integral-skin PU-RIM (MDI/polyol) shot in one closed mould so a dense outer skin (~1.1 g/cm³) is the reflective barrier and the foamed core (~0.25 g/cm³ open-cell) is the poroelastic spring. Physics: integral-skin RIM naturally grades density from a sealed low-permeability skin to open-cell core, delivering mass-spring behaviour in one shot without lamination or a tray. The skin seals against water/mud, deleting the PP tray and gasket. Tooling is a single RIM cavity with variable venting to control skin thickness (0.8–1.5 mm) and core rise; demould at 60–120 s.

title: Melt-blown micro-fibre absorber replaces needled felt + scrim
description: Equal absorption at ~35% lower media mass, plus deleted scrim. Baseline engine-bay top-cover absorber is needle-punched PET felt (~1400 g/m²) with a bonded nonwoven scrim facing on a moulded rigid backing. Proposal: a self-supporting bicomponent melt-blown PET/coPET web at 800–1000 g/m² where fine melt-blown fibres (1–3 µm) deliver the airflow resistivity of heavier needled felt at lower mass, since absorption scales with fibre surface area not bulk mass. The low-melt coPET sheath (softening ~110–130 °C) in-tool thermobonds a self-skinned facing, deleting the separate scrim. Physics: micro-fibre diameter raises tortuosity and viscous loss per unit mass, so a lighter web reaches α>0.8 at 1–2 kHz. Backing rigidity comes from higher local die-compaction (0.6–1.0 mm skin zones) rather than a discrete moulded tray in low-load zones; press at 180–210 °C.

title: Airflow-resistive porous film facing replaces perforated + fleece
description: Collapses a two-layer facing into one tunable resistive membrane and deletes perforation. Baseline headliner/pillar absorber subassembly uses a fibrous absorber behind a decorative layer, protected by a perforated PP film plus a nonwoven fleece to set surface impedance and stop fibre migration. Proposal: replace the perforated-film + fleece pair with a single monolithic micro-porous cast PU/TPU film (10–30 µm pores, calibrated to ~400–800 Ns/m³ flow resistance) laminated directly to the absorber. The physics: a precisely resistive facing forms the acoustic boundary that maximises absorption at the target band, doing the job of perforation-plus-fleece in one membrane while also acting as a fibre-containment and cleanability skin. Flow resistance is set by pore density/size during film casting rather than by a mechanical perforation tool, giving tighter tuning and no perforation debris.

ideaData.technicalDescription: Baseline headliner/pillar absorber subassembly uses a fibrous absorber behind a decorative layer, protected by a perforated PP film plus a nonwoven fleece to set surface impedance and stop fibre migration. Proposal: replace the perforated-film + fleece pair with a single monolithic micro-porous cast PU/TPU film (10–30 µm pores, calibrated to ~400–800 Ns/m³ flow resistance) laminated directly to the absorber. The physics: a precisely resistive facing forms the acoustic boundary that maximises absorption at the target band, doing the job of perforation-plus-fleece in one membrane while also acting as a fibre-containment and cleanability skin. Flow resistance is set by pore density/size during film casting rather than by a mechanical perforation tool, giving tighter tuning and no perforation debris.
ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Deletes the perforation station (needle/laser) and one fleece lamination pass. One flame/adhesive lamination of resistive film retained. Reduces inbound rolls from two to one. No press capex; net removes perforation tooling and its maintenance.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Collapses a two-layer facing into one tunable resistive membrane and deletes perforation.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~€1.80/veh (fleece + perforation labour) removed − ~€0.70/veh film premium = €1.10 net × 200k ≈ €0.22M direct; balance from deleted perforation tooling and reduced logistics

ideaData.riskNotes: Micro-porous film can clog with dust/soiling, drifting flow resistance; validate cleanability and long-term α retention. Fogging/VOC of TPU and flame lamination emissions to be certified. Mitigate with oleophobic surface treatment and FMVSS 302 re-test.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Resistive micro-porous facing films are established in premium interior acoustics; no specific programme named.

Cycle time per gear drops from ~90 s machining to ~15 s press + shared furnace. Chip handling and coolant scope reduced. Tooling: carbide compaction die set, moderate capex amortised over volume.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Eliminates hobbing and grinding on low-torque gears with drastic material-utilisation gain.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: Baseline machined gear ~€6.20 each; PM route ~€4.10; delta €2.10 × ~3 gears/unit × 250k = €1.575M

ideaData.riskNotes: PM flank RCF and NVH must be validated: run 10^7 cycle pitting tests and single-flank transmission-error measurement vs wrought baseline. Risk of sub-surface porosity initiating spalling if densification depth <0.25 mm; enforce eddy-current density check 100%. Restrict to the sub-200 Nm stage only; keep wrought steel on the high-torque final gear.
dfmaPrinciples: Locate material only where stress demands it
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Surface-densified sinter-hardened PM gears are established practice among PM specialists (e.g. GKN Powder Metallurgy, Miba, Stackpole densified PM gear technology); no specific vehicle programme claimed.
ideaData.materialGrade: Sinter-hardened FLN2-4405 (Fe-2Ni-Cu-0.5Mo, MPIF Std 35), core 7.1 g/cc, flank surface-densified >7.6 g/cc to 0.3 mm; replaces wrought 20MnCr5 case-carburised 58–62 HRC

title: Grease-for-life sealed bearings deleting shared oil sump on e-axle idler
description: Deletes a lube gallery and simplifies fill while cutting churning drag. Baseline reducer splash-lubricates all shaft bearings from a common gear-oil sump (75W-90 GL-5, ~1.4 L). The idler/intermediate-shaft supports see modest load (P<C0/8) and low PV. Replace the open deep-groove ball bearings (6xxx series) on the lightly loaded idler shaft with sealed grease-for-life units (2RS, PFPE or lithium-complex EP grease rated to 150 °C, e.g. filled ~30% cavity) and add a steel slinger to shield them from sump churn. This drops sump level ~15–20 mm, cutting fill ~0.25 L and, more importantly, reducing windage/churning drag on the fast idler at high rpm (drag falls with the square of immersed pitch-line velocity), improving efficiency. Sealed bearings arrive pre-greased, deleting line oil-path drilling and a housing lube gallery. Confirm grease compatibility with 75W-90 splash and 150 °C peak.

ideaData.materialGrade: Sealed 2RS deep-groove ball bearings (52100 bearing steel) with PFPE or lithium-complex EP grease rated 150 °C; sump oil 75W-90 GL-5

title: Asymmetric-tooth gear profile to shrink face width on drive flank
description: Shrinks gear face width and axial train length via drive-flank-optimised geometry. Baseline final-reduction helical pair uses a symmetric 20° pressure-angle involute sized for the dominant drive direction but carrying full face width on both flanks. Since a traction reducer transmits >90% of energy on the drive flank, adopt an asymmetric tooth: 28° pressure angle on the drive flank, 20° on the coast flank. The higher drive-side angle increases the radius of relative curvature at contact, cutting Hertzian contact stress ~10–14% for the same load. That headroom is spent shrinking face width ~8–12% (or module), reducing blank mass and, critically, axial train length — shortening shafts, the housing casting and one bearing span. Housing casting shortens axially, trimming aluminium mass and machining envelope. No new stations; net capex is a cutter set.

costSavingPotential.percentage: 10-15% on the final gear pair mass + housing length
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: Gear mass/machining saving ~€3.50 + housing Al & machining ~€2.80/unit = ~€6.30 × 250k = €1.575M

Manufacturing: tool wear differs per flank; enforce SPC on both profiles. NVH transmission error must be re-optimised via micro-geometry. Not suitable where coast torque approaches drive torque (e.g. heavy regen calibrations).
dfmaPrinciples: Match geometry to actual load spectrum, not symmetric worst case
Reduce axial package to shrink adjacent parts
Reuse existing process with tooling change
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Asymmetric involute gearing is established practice in aerospace and motorsport transmissions; mechanism proven, no high-volume automotive programme claimed.
ideaData.materialGrade: 20MnCr5 case-carburised 58–62 HRC (unchanged); asymmetric involute 28° drive / 20° coast flank cut with custom-profile hob or skiving cutter

title: High-pressure die-cast housing with cast-in bearing bores via local squeeze
description: Near-net cast-in bores and thinner walls cut Al mass, machining and scrap. Baseline reducer housing is HPDC AlSi9Cu3(Fe) then fully machined bearing bores that require oversized bosses to remove porosity-laden skin before reaching sound metal. Introduce localised squeeze/forge-assist (local pressurisation of the die at the bearing-boss regions during solidification) so the bore zones solidify pore-free, allowing bore bosses to be cast much closer to net (leaving ~0.6 mm machining stock instead of ~2.0 mm) and reducing the safety wall added purely to guarantee soundness. Sound cast-in bores also permit direct bearing seating with a single fine-bore pass rather than rough+finish. Squeeze zones raise local density/strength, letting nominal wall thickness drop from ~4.0 to ~3.2 mm away from the bosses.

Requires CT/X-ray validation of bore-zone porosity to <1% and dimensional capability on cast-near-net bores. Thinner walls need modal/NVH and drop-test re-validation. Mitigate with process-window DOE and 100% inline density gauging during ramp.
dfmaPrinciples: Cast closer to net shape in critical zones
Remove material added solely for process safety
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Local squeeze / semi-solid-assisted HPDC for pore-free critical zones is established foundry practice; no specific programme claimed.
ideaData.materialGrade: AlSi9Cu3(Fe) HPDC with local squeeze; option AlSi10MnMg for structural zones

title: Superfinished (isotropic) gear flanks enabling lower-viscosity fill
description: Superfinish enables low-viscosity fill, cutting drag, break-in time and micropitting warranty. Baseline hard-finished gears (case-carburised 18CrNiMo7-6) run a ground/honed flank at Ra 0.4-0.6 um and require 75W-90 GL-5 for adequate lambda ratio at the mesh. Apply chemically-accelerated vibratory isotropic superfinishing (REM ISF-type, oxalate/phosphate conversion + ceramic media) to bring flank Ra below 0.10 um (target Rz < 0.8 um) with a plateaued bearing-area (Rk) profile. The smoother asperity spectrum raises lambda, so full-film separation holds at lower viscosity — permitting a switch to 75W-85 or an ATF-grade fluid (~ISO VG 22-32, e.g. a Dexron-type 5.5-6.5 cSt at 100C). Lower viscosity cuts churning and hydrodynamic drag (Petroff-scaling), while the polished flank cuts micropitting and near-eliminates green-run scuffing and reduces cold-crank drag.

title: Modular shared centre-distance across 3 reduction ratios
description: Collapses housing tooling and fixtures from three variants to one via fixed centre distance. Baseline reducer family uses three ratios (8.5/9.5/10.5:1), each with its own centre distance, HPDC housing (AlSi10MnMg), shafts and bearing bores — three unique tool sets. Re-architect to a single fixed centre distance (e.g. 118 mm) by achieving ratio spread through normal module (e.g. 1.75/2.0/2.25 mm) and tooth-count changes only, holding the same shaft axes and bore positions within IT6. With centre distance fixed, one housing casting die and machining fixture, one shaft blank family and common bearing bore positions (e.g. 72/80 mm) serve all three ratios; only the gear-cut hob/skive tooling differs. This collapses casting dies from three to one, slashes machining-fixture and gauging variety and MRO spares complexity across plants.

dfmaPrinciples: Fix interfaces, vary only what must vary
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Common centre-distance modular gearbox families are established platform-engineering practice; no specific programme claimed.
ideaData.materialGrade: HPDC housing AlSi10MnMg (or AlSi9Cu3(Fe)); gears 18CrNiMo7-6 at common centre distance ~118 mm, modules 1.75/2.0/2.25 mm

title: Split-torque two-path reduction to halve gear face width
description: Load-sharing halves per-mesh stress, shrinking every gear despite an added path. Baseline single-mesh final reduction carries all traction torque through one 18CrNiMo7-6 gear pair, forcing wide face and large module to meet ISO 6336 root-bending and contact stress at peak torque. Replace with a split-torque (dual-path) layout: the pinion drives two identical idler paths recombining on the output gear, so each mesh carries ~50% of load. This lets face width and module drop ~35-40% per gear (e.g. face 42 to 26 mm, module 2.5 to 1.75 mm), each gear/shaft smaller and lighter, since tooth size scales sub-linearly with load. Load balancing uses a torsionally compliant quill/spline mount on one path or matched-lead grinding to ISO 1328 Q5, avoiding costly precision splitting.

costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: Net gear+shaft mass/machining saving ~€7.5/unit less added idler+bearing ~€1.5 = ~€6.0 × 250k = €1.5M

Validate with strain-gauged torque split across temperature and manufacturing tolerance; use compliant path or lead-matching to hold split within ±5%. NVH gains an extra mesh order to tune. Mitigate with tolerance stack analysis and rig durability at worst-case split.

Trade one added part for many smaller ones
Use compliance instead of precision for balancing

ideaData.materialGrade: 18CrNiMo7-6 case-carburised gears; matched-lead ground to ISO 1328 Q5; compliant quill shaft in 42CrMo4

title: Cast-in ferrous bearing liners deleting standalone bearing cups
description: Removes discrete bearing cups, press fitting, and associated bore finishing tolerance stack. Baseline BEV single-speed reduction housing is HPDC AlSi9Cu3(Fe) with pressed-in SAE 52100 (100Cr6) bearing cups in machined bores, requiring interference-fit press stations and thermal-growth compensation. Proposal: insert-cast thin-wall (2.5-3 mm) 16MnCr5 or 100Cr6 liner sleeves during high-pressure die casting; aluminium shrinks onto the sleeve OD as it solidifies, creating the fit (differential CTE ~23 vs 12 um/m·K gives ~0.09 mm shrink grip over an 80 mm bore). The ferrous liner carries the raceway Hertzian load and confines aluminium fretting while deleting the discrete cup, its press station and hot-soak bore-ovalisation risk. Sleeve OD is knurled/roughened for mechanical keying; raceway is finish-ground in-situ post-cast to hold C4/P4 running clearance.

ideaData.materialGrade: Housing HPDC AlSi9Cu3(Fe); insert liner 16MnCr5 or 100Cr6 (SAE 52100), 2.5-3 mm wall, in-situ ground to P4

title: Dry-sump splash-lubrication delete via oil-mist channels in housing
description: Halves lubricant fill and cuts parasitic loss, improving range which offsets battery cost at pack level. Baseline low-torque e-axle idler/reduction stage runs a shared oil bath (~1.1 L 75W-90 GL-5) sized to immerse the final-drive gear, driving churning losses (~250-400 W at 12k rpm) and a large sump. Proposal: minimum-quantity oil-mist scheme — a scoop off the fastest gear flings oil into cast-in labyrinth galleries (as-cast 4-6 mm channels in the AlSi9Cu3(Fe) housing) that route metered flow to the two loaded meshes and upper bearings, cutting fill to ~0.4 L of a lower-viscosity ATF (~ISO VG 32) and running the sump below the pitch line. Removing full immersion removes windage/churning torque scaling with immersion depth and the square of rim velocity, while galleries guarantee EHL film at the contact. Housing gains cast channels only; no active pump added.

description: Removes joining operations, cuts machining scrap, and reduces buy-to-fly material by near-net forming. Baseline intermediate reduction stage uses a separate 20MnCr5 gear pressed/splined and shrink-fitted onto a machined 42CrMo4 shaft, requiring spline broaching, interference heating, and runout correction after assembly. Proposal is a single powder-forged (PM densified to >7.7 g/cm³ surface) integral gear-shaft from FLN2-4405-type pre-alloyed powder, net-forged with the gear and journal features in one blank, then case-carburised and hard-turned/ground only on the journals and flanks. Eliminating the joint removes the spline interface (a torsional compliance and micro-fretting source) and the assembly runout stack, while forge densification restores rolling-contact fatigue capacity of the flank to near wrought. title: Tapered-roller to angular-contact ball bearing swap on e-axle output
description: Eliminates selective-shim preload loop and reduces friction torque, adding efficiency credit. Baseline BEV reduction output shaft carries a matched pair of tapered roller bearings (e.g. 30208-class, 100Cr6) requiring selective-shim preload at assembly to react helical thrust, adding a measure-and-select station and spinning-torque check. For torque classes where dynamic axial load is bounded (single-speed EDUs, helix ~22°), use a back-to-back (DB) angular-contact ball bearing pair (100Cr6, 25-40° contact angle, e.g. 7208-class) with factory-set wave-spring preload, or a matched-duplex ACBB cartridge ground to a defined offset. ACBBs run lower friction torque (rolling vs sliding roller-flange contact), improving efficiency, and the duplex/wave preload deletes the selective-shim loop. Lower radial capacity is offset by up-sizing ball complement/bore within the existing envelope.

ideaData.materialGrade: 100Cr6 (SAE 52100) angular-contact ball bearings, 25-40° contact angle, DB/duplex 7208-class with wave-spring preload; ceramic hybrid balls (Si3N4) optional

title: Nitrided 31CrMoV9 gears replacing carburised-and-ground with grind delete
description: Removes finish grinding and distortion scrap for load-appropriate stages. Baseline reduction gears are case-carburised 18CrNiMo7-6 quenched, incurring heat-treat distortion that mandates post-hardening profile grinding (~0.3-0.5 mm stock) to recover lead/profile to ISO 1328 Q6. Proposal: gas-nitride 31CrMoV9 (or 41CrAlMo7) at ~510C for 40-60 h, forming a hard compound (white) layer plus diffusion zone (surface ~700-900 HV) at low temperature with negligible dimensional change, allowing hard-hobbing/skiving before nitride and deleting the finish-grind for moderate-load stages. Nitride case depth is shallow (~0.3-0.4 mm) so it suits lower Hertzian pressures; the low-temperature process avoids martensitic quench distortion, so soft-machined geometry is retained. One high-cost grinding operation is removed with reduced distortion scrap.

ideaData.materialGrade: 31CrMoV9 (or 41CrAlMo7) gas-nitrided at ~510C, case ~0.3-0.4 mm, surface 700-900 HV — replacing carburised 18CrNiMo7-6

title: In-line laser gear-flank inspection deleting end-of-line coordinate metrology
description: Cuts metrology labour, CMM capex, and scrap via earlier tool-drift detection. Baseline reduction gears are 100%-sampled on offline tactile gear-measuring CMMs (lead, profile, pitch, runout per ISO 1328) at ~90-180 s/gear, forming a throughput/labour bottleneck needing a climate-controlled (20±1C) metrology room and trained operators. Proposal integrates in-line structured-light/blue-laser-line optical gear scanning at the machine exit, capturing full-flank point clouds in ~8-15 s and computing ISO 1328 profile/lead/pitch deviations in software, escalating only out-of-tolerance parts to the CMM. This is a subassembly-line quality-cost lever, not a gear redesign: it converts sampling to 100% fast inspection, catching hob/skive tool-wear drift earlier and cutting scrap and CMM fleet size. Correlation to tactile CMM is established via gauge R&R (target GRR < 10%).

title: Front-end accessory drive deletion via 48V electrified ancillaries
description: Removes belt, tensioner, idlers and large HPDC bracket; kills belt-related field warranty. Baseline P0 mild-hybrid front-end accessory drive (FEAD) uses a poly-V belt (6PK1200 EPDM), tensioner, idler, mechanical A/C compressor and belt-driven coolant/vacuum pumps mounted on a die-cast AlSi9Cu3 accessory bracket with ~14 fasteners. Proposal: delete the entire belt path by moving to a 48V P2 architecture where the ISG handles start/regen and A/C compressor, water pump and vacuum/brake-vac pump become 48V electric units on a shared plastic-media rail. This removes the belt, tensioner (~35 N·m spring), two idler bearings and the large accessory bracket, replacing them with three sealed BLDC modules driven by the existing 48V DC-DC. Physics: decoupling ancillaries from crank speed lets the A/C compressor run at optimal 2500 rpm regardless of engine idle, cutting parasitic drag ~1.2 kW at idle

HPDC bracket tool retired, replaced by low-cost stamping die.

Embossed-and-welded channels hold 20+ bar clutch-apply pressure with zero gasket creep, eliminating cross-leak drift that forces wider clutch-fill calibration margin. title: Combine close-coupled catalyst and underfloor GPF into single canned module
description: Eliminates a full underfloor canned assembly, flex pipe and clamps; trims PGM. Baseline gasoline-hybrid aftertreatment uses a close-coupled TWC (400 cpsi cordierite, 4.66×3.0 in, ~90 g/ft3 PGM ~ Pd/Rh) in a stamped 1.4509 (441) ferritic-stainless clamshell, plus a separate underfloor coated-cordierite GPF in its own can with an interconnecting flex-decoupler pipe and two V-band clamps. Proposal: package a coated four-way GPF (TWC-on-filter, ~300 cpsi/8 mil wall coated cordierite) directly close-coupled in a single insulated 1.4509 can, deleting the underfloor unit, flex pipe, both V-bands and one O2-sensor boss. Hybrid engines run cold-start-heavy with low exhaust mass flow, so a close-coupled coated GPF lights off faster (>250C in <20 s) and the shorter thermal path lets PGM loading drop ~10% for equivalent EU7 conversion.

description: Deletes a cast bracket, its machining and interface fasteners; potential mass-damper deletion. title: Replace turbo oil-feed/return hard lines with integrated block galleries
description: Removes braided line, return pipe, coolant hoses and multiple leak-prone joints. Baseline turbocharged hybrid uses a braided-PTFE oil-feed line with two M10 banjo bolts plus a formed 1.4301 steel oil-return pipe on an O-ring flange, and a separate coolant feed/return pair — six leak-paths. Proposal: in the AlSi7Mg0.3-T6 (or AlSi9Cu3 ladder-frame) block casting, cast integral oil-feed (Ø4-5mm) and coolant (Ø8-10mm) galleries terminating at one machined turbo-mount face (flatness ≤0.05mm, Ra ≤1.6µm), so the turbo bolts direct with two FKM-elastomer-carrier seals on steel carriers, deleting feed line, return pipe and hoses. Physics: hybrid hot-soak after engine-off coke external banjo joints; a short cast gallery cuts thermal length and dead volume. Face seals rated 150°C oil / 120°C coolant; drill-and-plug cores kept above 3mm wall for casting integrity.

title: Common exhaust manifold-turbine housing across ICE and hybrid variants
description: Deletes one casting SKU, its tooling and duplicate PPAP; raises combined lot size. Proposal: commonise on a single 1.4849-family housing sized to hybrid duty, using variant-specific wastegate spring/actuator calibration and a bolt-on Inconel 625 or 1.4849 flow-restrictor sleeve rather than a distinct casting. title: P2 hybrid coolant pump + oil pump onto single BLDC e-drive
description: Eliminates a full motor+inverter BOM by exploiting non-coincident hydraulic duty cycles. Baseline P2 ancillary set carries a standalone 12V PMSM wet-rotor coolant pump (~50W) plus a separate mechanical or e-actuated transmission oil pump, each with own housing, controller PCB, connector and ports. Proposal: consolidate onto one dual-shaft 48V BLDC module — an N42SH NdFeB (Dy-enhanced, 150°C-capable) ring-magnet rotor on a common EN AW-6082-T6 spindle driving a POM-GF25 gerotor (oil, 6 bar) at one end and a PPS-GF40 centrifugal impeller (coolant, 1.8 bar) at the other, sharing one sensored FOC inverter in a die-cast AlSi10Mg housing with cast-in dual volutes. Physics: oil peaks at launch/shift, coolant at sustained load — non-coincident, so one ~250W motor sized to the duty-cycle envelope covers both rather than summing rated powers.

Circumferential laser welds cut weld length ~60% and remove post-weld leak rework. Fewer parts to buffer; lower stamping tool amortisation across variants.

Mat canning stress must be re-set for the tighter bore to keep gap-bulk-density in the substrate hold window (avoid substrate crush or ring-off).

ideaData.materialGrade: Seamless shell 1.4512 (409) stabilised ferritic stainless, 1.5→1.2mm; deleted clamshell 1.4509 (441); circumferential laser welds

title: Hybrid P2 clutch actuation — electro-hydraulic to direct electro-mechanical ballramp
description: Deletes the wet holding circuit and its parasitic pump load, plus valve-body machining. Baseline P2 disconnect clutch is closed electro-hydraulically: an accumulator, solenoid valve block, piston and the transmission pump feeding line pressure — a wet circuit needing continuous parasitic flow to hold clamp. Proposal: replace with a self-locking electro-mechanical ball-ramp actuator driven by a 48V BLDC through a planetary reducer, converting motor torque to axial clamp via three 100Cr6 (AISI 52100, 60-62 HRC) balls on 20MnCr5 case-hardened ramps (case 0.6-0.9mm, 58-62 HRC), held by a sub-6° self-locking lead angle at zero current. Physics: the clutch spends the cycle either fully open (EV) or fully closed (parallel) — static states where hydraulic holding wastes pump power; the ramp self-holds with no current, cutting parasitic loss and deleting the accumulator/valve/piston circuit.

Semi-solid feeding at ~0.58 solid fraction eliminates turbulent fill, cutting gas porosity below 1% by area on the flame-deck and permitting T5 instead of T6 on selected variants, deleting the solution-treat furnace pass. Wall stock for CNC of the deck drops from 2.5 mm to 1.2 mm because dimensional scatter tightens.
ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Deletes sand-core making + core-gas scrubbing station for jacket; adds salt-core injection + wash-out cell. Squeeze-cast press capex ~€2M but cycle drops to ~3 min. Reduced deck machining stock cuts one roughing pass and swarf. Scrap 8%→<2%.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Yield recovery plus deleted heat-treat and machining passes on a high-value casting
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: Baseline bare head ~€95; ~€11 saving (scrap recovery €5, HT delete €3, machining €3) × 200,000

ideaData.riskNotes: Flame-deck fatigue under thermal cycling and 180 bar peak firing pressure must be re-validated (thermo-mechanical fatigue rig, 2000 cycles) — semi-solid grain refinement generally improves this. Salt-core dimensional repeatability on port cross-section affects swirl; CFD + flow-bench sign-off required. Water-jacket cleanliness after salt wash-out is a corrosion risk; mitigate with DI-water rinse + dry.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Salt-core (lost-core) and semi-solid rheocasting of Al heads are established production practice; not attributing to a specific named programme.

title: Turbine housing NiResist D5S to SiMo51 ferritic ductile iron
description: Eliminates the dominant nickel cost driver of the casting Baseline single-scroll turbine housing is austenitic Ni-Resist D-5S (~35% Ni, ~1050°C capability), sand-cast for a petrol application at 950-980°C exhaust, carrying ~1.8kg nickel per housing at volatile LME pricing. Proposal: down-substitute to SiMo51 (GJS-SiMo ferritic ductile iron, ~4.2% Si, ~1% Mo) where peak skin temperature is capped ≤930°C, verified by transient thermocouple mapping. SiMo51 forms a stable, adherent Si-rich oxide scale resisting scale growth and cracking; its ferritic matrix avoids the phase change driving Ni-Resist cost, and Ni drops from ~35% to <0.3%. Where duty cycle peaks 930-980°C, use higher-Mo SiMo1000 (Mo raised toward ~2%) or shift wastegate calibration to cap pre-turbine temperature by 20-30°C, keeping within the ferritic window.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Eliminates the dominant nickel cost driver of the casting
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~1.8 kg Ni × ~€16/kg saved ≈ €13-18/housing net of Mo add × 300,000

ideaData.materialGrade: Target SiMo51 (GJS-SiMo, ~4.2% Si, ~1% Mo) or SiMo1000 (higher Mo ~2%); deleted Ni-Resist D-5S (~35% Ni)

title: Exhaust manifold — cast SiMo to fabricated 1.4509 tube weldment
description: Mass and machining reduction plus faster catalyst light-off cutting cold-start emissions margin Baseline log-style manifold is a SiMo51 (GJS-SiMo4-6, ~4% Si / 0.6% Mo ferritic ductile iron) casting ~4.8 kg, machined at four flange faces. Proposal: fabricated air-gap-insulated manifold using 1.4509 (X2CrTiNb18, 441, Nb+Ti stabilised 18%Cr ferritic). Inner runners hydroformed/bent from 1.5 mm 1.4509 sheet, TIG or laser welded to a 1.2 mm stamped 1.4509 outer shell, with a 6-8 mm laser-cut 1.4509 head flange. Mass drops to ~2.3 kg; the air gap retains exhaust enthalpy, improving catalyst light-off 8-15 s from cold. Ferritic 441 avoids austenitic Ni and has a lower CTE (~11 vs ~19 ppm/K), cutting flange thermal-fatigue distortion; oxidation-stable to ~950°C. Bend-tuned runners allow late acoustic/scavenging changes without new pattern tooling.

ideaData.materialGrade: 1.4509 (441, X2CrTiNb18) 1.5 mm runner / 1.2 mm shell; replaces SiMo51 (GJS-SiMo4-6) casting

title: Catalyst substrate — 600/4 to 900/2.5 thin-wall + reduced PGM
description: Higher GSA lets equal conversion be met at lower precious-metal loading — the true cost lever Baseline TWC uses 600 cpsi / 4.0 mil (102 µm) wall cordierite (2MgO·2Al2O3·5SiO2) at ~4.5 g/L PGM (Pd-heavy, typ. Pd:Rh ~10-20:1). Proposal: step to 900 cpsi / 2.5 mil (63.5 µm) ultra-thin-wall cordierite (or equivalent thin-wall extrudate). Higher cell density with thinner walls raises geometric surface area ~20% and open frontal area, improving mass-transfer-limited conversion per unit washcoat and enabling 8-15% PGM thrift at equal tailpipe conversion. Lower thermal mass improves light-off several seconds. Pd/Rh dominate cost; a 10% cut at ~€25-30/g Pd dwarfs the substrate delta. Backpressure rises ~5-8%, partly offset by thinner walls — verify against turbine match and canning with 3100-3600 g/m² intumescent mat.

costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~4.5 g/L × ~1.2 L × €25/g ≈ €135 PGM; 10% cut ≈ €13.5 net of substrate add × 400,000

ideaData.materialGrade: 900/2.5 (63.5 µm wall) cordierite substrate; Pd/Rh PGM washcoat reduced ~8-15%

title: Injector nozzle — EDM spray holes to laser percussion drilling
description: Cycle-time and consumable reduction plus fewer flow-trim classes and lower scrap Baseline GDI nozzle tip/plate has 5-7 orifices (~120-180 µm) micro-EDM'd in hardened martensitic stainless (440-type, ~1.4112/AISI 440B, ~58-60 HRC) — slow, electrode-wear-limited, with a diffuse recast edge scattering spray-cone tolerance to ±8-10 µm. Proposal: femtosecond/ultrashort-pulse (~300 fs-10 ps, ~1030 nm) laser percussion drilling, optionally with a controlled inward taper (k-factor ~1.5) to stabilise discharge coefficient. USP gives near-zero recast, <1 µm heat-affected zone and sub-±3 µm diameter control, tightening flow distribution so injectors bin into fewer flow classes — fewer ECU trim codes and less out-of-window scrap. No electrode dressing raises throughput and eliminates dielectric-fluid consumables and filtration.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Cycle-time and consumable reduction plus fewer flow-trim classes and lower scrap
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~€2.2/nozzle drilling saving (consumables + cycle + scrap) × 1,000,000

Recast-free edge can alter coking behaviour; validate deposit tests. Laser process window control critical to avoid barrelling.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Ultrashort-pulse laser drilling of injector orifices is established high-precision practice replacing EDM among fuel-system tier-1s; not naming a specific programme.
ideaData.materialGrade: Nozzle in martensitic stainless (440-type, ~1.4112) ~58-60 HRC; process change to USP laser (no new material)

title: Cylinder block bores — gray-iron liners to plasma-sprayed coating
description: Removes iron liners and a foundry sub-process while cutting distortion-driven rework and friction Baseline AlSi9Cu3(Fe) HPDC block uses cast-in gray-iron (GJL-250) liners (~0.5-0.7 kg for 4 cyl), adding mass, an Al/iron thermal interface that worsens bore distortion, and an insert-handling step. Proposal: delete liners and thermally spray an iron layer onto the machined Al bore — atmospheric plasma spray or rotating single-wire/twin-wire arc of low-carbon iron feedstock (~0.13% C wire), ~0.15-0.30 mm as-sprayed, then rough+finish hone to a ~0.10-0.15 mm functional layer with 3-6% engineered porosity for oil retention. The homogeneous Al wall improves heat transfer, cuts distortion (lower blow-by/oil consumption) and removes ~0.6 kg iron/block. Requires activation (e.g. high-pressure water-jet or mechanical roughening) of the bore for adhesion prior to spray.

Adds bore activation (mechanical/high-pressure water-jet roughening), a spray booth with overspray extraction, and a two-stage hone. Net capex significant but mass, iron cost and a foundry sub-process are removed; reduced distortion cuts machining rework.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Removes iron liners and a foundry sub-process while cutting distortion-driven rework and friction
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~0.6 kg iron + liner handling + rework ≈ €12-15/block net of spray consumable × 300,000

ideaData.riskNotes: Coating adhesion and cohesion under peak firing pressure and thermal cycling is the core risk — bond-strength (ASTM C633), thermal-shock, and 500 h WOT endurance with oil-consumption and blow-by tracking required. Bore-surface activation repeatability is critical to avoid delamination. Field repairability differs from liners; document reman path.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Thermally sprayed iron bore coatings replacing cast-iron liners are established production practice on multiple performance and volume engines; not naming a specific programme.
ideaData.materialGrade: Sprayed low-carbon iron (~0.13% C) coating on AlSi9Cu3(Fe) HPDC bore; replaces GJL-250 liners

title: Intake manifold — vibration-welded PA6-GF35 with in-mould integration
description: Part-count and fastener consolidation plus deletion of a machined aluminium flange and gasket Baseline air intake manifold on many builds is a 3-shell PA6-GF30 vibration-welded assembly with separately bolted-on aluminium throttle-body flange, EGR takeoff, MAP boss and mounting brackets. Proposal: consolidate to a 2-shell PA6-GF35 (35% glass, higher creep/burst margin for boosted 2.5 bar abs) vibration weld, with the throttle-body sealing face, EGR interface, sensor bosses and mounting eyes all moulded net-shape into the shells — eliminating the aluminium flange, its gasket, and up to 8 fasteners. A lost-core (fusible metal or soluble core) technique forms complex internal runner geometry in a single shell where needed, reducing weld-plane count from two to one on the tuned-length runners. Glass step-up from GF30 to GF35 restores the burst-pressure and creep margin lost by deleting metal

Injection tools grow more complex (integrated bosses, lost-core cell) — higher tool capex, but assembly line stations and torque operations are deleted; leak-test unchanged.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Part-count and fastener consolidation plus deletion of a machined aluminium flange and gasket
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: Al flange + gasket + 8 fasteners + one weld station ≈ €7-10/unit × 350,000

ideaData.riskNotes: Burst pressure (≥3x boost), thermal creep at ~120°C under-hood, and weld-seam fatigue under pulsation are the key risks — hydro-burst, hot-creep, and pulsation-fatigue (10^7 cycles) validation. Integrated plastic sensor/throttle faces need flatness/sealing verification vs the deleted machined Al face. Chemical resistance to blow-by/EGR condensate confirmed for PA6-GF35.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Glass-filled PA intake manifolds with vibration welding and integrated interfaces are established mass practice; lost-core variants likewise. Not naming a specific programme.

title: Crankcase main-bearing ladder — bimetal insert-cast steel bulkhead beam
description: Deletes cross-bolt hardware and a full machining operation while stabilising bore geometry to cut honing rework. Baseline AlSi9Cu3(Fe) HPDC crankcase carries main-bearing loads through Al bulkheads alone, needing cross-bolts and 8-9 mm wall to limit bore distortion and cap walk at ~130 bar peak firing. Proposal: insert-cast a single ferrous ladder-frame beam — GJL-250 gray iron or a sintered/MIM ferritic-steel preform — into the crankcase during HPDC so main-bearing saddles run in a stiff low-CTE (~11-13 ppm/K) iron path within an Al structure. The CTE mismatch pre-tensions caps on heat-up, eliminating 5-6 M12 cross-bolts, cutting bulkhead wall ~2 mm and reducing bore ovality so honing stock drops from ~120 to ~70 µm. Consolidates ladder + separate caps + cross-bolts into one insert; requires clean, pre-heated inserts and controlled die fill to avoid cold shuts at the Al/iron interface.

Net one station added, three deleted downstream. Honing cycle shortens ~15%. Requires insert fixturing tooling (~€180k) but reuses existing die base.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Deletes cross-bolt hardware and a full machining operation while stabilising bore geometry to cut honing rework.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~€10.30/engine saved (6 bolts + line-bore op + 30% honing time + 0.4 kg Al) × 300,000; delta €10.30 vs baseline crankcase machined cost ~€82

Casting porosity around insert needs X-ray CT gating.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Insert-cast ferrous bearing beams/bedplates in Al crankcases are long-established practice; not naming a specific programme.
ideaData.materialGrade: Insert beam GJL-250 (or sintered ferritic-steel preform) in AlSi9Cu3(Fe) HPDC crankcase

title: Cast-in exhaust port thermal isolation via ceramic sleeve insert in head
description: Faster light-off allows PGM thrift and downsized coolant pump; secondary warranty benefit from reduced cold-start emissions drift. Baseline aluminium cylinder head (AlSi7Mg0.3 or AlSi10Mg) has bare aluminium exhaust ports, so a large fraction of exhaust enthalpy is lost to the coolant, forcing an oversized coolant pump and delaying catalyst light-off (>25 s cold). Proposal: insert-cast a thin cordierite/mullite ceramic port liner (1.5-2 mm wall, thermal conductivity ~3 W/mK vs ~150 for Al) into the exhaust runners during low-pressure casting. The liner reflects heat into the gas path, cutting port heat rejection ~30% and raising turbine-inlet temperature — enabling either a smaller coolant circuit or PGM reduction on the catalyst via faster light-off. Physics: an insulating boundary layer at the port wall reduces the convective sink without touching combustion-chamber cooling.

Validate 1,000 thermal-shock cycles and gas-tightness leak test. Risk of liner fragment ingestion — retention geometry critical.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Insulated/ceramic-lined exhaust ports are established heat-management practice; no specific programme named.

title: Turbo compressor wheel — machined-from-billet to net-shape MIM
description: Eliminates 60%+ material buy-to-fly loss and multi-axis machine hours on the highest-cost turbo rotating part. Baseline compressor wheel is 5-axis flank-milled from EN AW-2618A or C355 (AlSi5Cu1Mg) billet, generating 60-70% swarf; high-temp e-turbo duty sometimes uses investment-cast Ti-6Al-4V. Proposal: metal-injection-mould the wheel near-net from 17-4PH (1.4542) or a gas-atomised aluminium feedstock, leaving only bore and back-face finish grind. MIM holds ±0.05 mm on 0.3 mm trailing edges and reaches >95% theoretical density after catalytic debind and sinter (~1350°C for 17-4PH), with H900 age to ~1070 MPa giving fatigue capacity for small-frame turbos <180,000 rpm. Blade aero tolerance is set by trailing-edge thickness and tip contour, both formed in the tool cavity, so multi-axis milling is eliminated except the bore. Sinter shrinkage (~15-18% linear) must be compensated in the tool

ideaData.materialGrade: MIM 17-4PH (1.4542, H900) or MIM aluminium feedstock; replaces EN AW-2618A / C355 billet milling

title: Catalyst substrate — ceramic monolith to metallic foil in close-couple position
description: Lower thermal mass cuts PGM loading; deletes intumescent mat and shrinks substrate volume. Baseline close-coupled cat uses an extruded cordierite monolith (900/2.5, ~1.8 mm outer wall to can) with an intumescent mat and bulky can. Proposal: switch the close-couple brick to a wound/brazed FeCrAl foil substrate (e.g. 1.4767 / Aluchrom-type, ~0.03-0.05 mm foil, aluminide-forming Al ~5-6%) at 1000+ cpsi, vacuum-brazed with Ni-based filler and pre-oxidised to grow the protective alumina scale. Foil wall is ~15% of ceramic, giving lower thermal mass for faster light-off, ~40% lower backpressure at equal frontal area, and enough mechanical robustness to simplify the mat or braze the matrix directly into the housing. Thin high-conductivity metal heats and flows more freely, improving PGM utilisation and allowing ~20% substrate-volume reduction at equal conversion.

ideaData.title: Catalyst substrate — ceramic monolith to metallic foil in close-couple position
ideaData.technicalDescription: Baseline close-coupled cat uses an extruded cordierite monolith (900/2.5, ~1.8 mm outer wall to can) with an intumescent mat and bulky can. Proposal: switch the close-couple brick to a wound/brazed FeCrAl foil substrate (e.g. 1.4767 / Aluchrom-type, ~0.03-0.05 mm foil, aluminide-forming Al ~5-6%) at 1000+ cpsi, vacuum-brazed with Ni-based filler and pre-oxidised to grow the protective alumina scale. Foil wall is ~15% of ceramic, giving lower thermal mass for faster light-off, ~40% lower backpressure at equal frontal area, and enough mechanical robustness to simplify the mat or braze the matrix directly into the housing. Thin high-conductivity metal heats and flows more freely, improving PGM utilisation and allowing ~20% substrate-volume reduction at equal conversion.
ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Moves canning from mat-wrap/stuffing to a brazed foil-in-housing assembly with vacuum braze furnace. Deletes intumescent mat and mat-density control station. Adds foil winding + brazing line. Washcoat adhesion process changes to metallic-surface pre-treatment. Canning capex partly offset by mat-line deletion.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Lower thermal mass cuts PGM loading; deletes intumescent mat and shrinks substrate volume.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~€10/vehicle net (PGM save €12 + mat delete €3 − foil premium €5) × 250,000

ideaData.riskNotes: Foil telescoping and washcoat spallation under thermal cycling, plus high-temp oxidation limit (~1,100°C) in close-couple position; mitigate with pre-oxidised alumina-scale foil and structured herringbone winding to lock layers. Validate 300h aged conversion and vibration durability. Higher raw foil cost partly offsets PGM/volume gains — net depends on PGM price.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Wound/brazed FeCrAl metallic substrates are established production technology for close-coupled catalysts; not naming a specific programme.
ideaData.materialGrade: FeCrAl foil (1.4767/Aluchrom-type, 0.03-0.05 mm, ~5-6% Al) substrate; replaces 900/2.5 cordierite

title: Injector body — free-machining bar to cold-formed then hard-turned blank
description: Halves swarf and turning hours on a high-volume precision part while improving bore fatigue. Baseline GDI injector body is machined from 1.4542 (17-4PH) or 100Cr6 bar with deep gun-drilling of the fuel bore and multiple turning ops — high swarf, long cycle. Proposal: cold-extrude the body to near-net external form and pre-form the central bore in a multi-station former from 16MnCr5 (case-hardening) or a formable martensitic grade, leaving only ID hone and seat grind after heat treat (carburise/quench 16MnCr5 to ~60 HRC case, or harden-temper the martensitic). Cold forming develops favourable grain flow around the high-pressure sac (350+ bar GDI; 2000+ bar for DI rails), raising hoop-fatigue life while removing ~50% of turning stock. Formed flow lines follow the bore contour, lifting the fatigue limit versus interrupted machined lines; requires phosphate/soap or polymer lube and controlle

ideaData.benchmarkReference: Cold-forming of injector and common-rail components is established practice among fuel-system tier-1s; not naming a specific programme.
ideaData.materialGrade: Cold-formed 16MnCr5 (case-hardened) or formable martensitic grade; replaces 1.4542/100Cr6 bar machining

title: Cylinder head cam-carrier — separate bolted part to cast-in integrated frame
description: Removes an entire casting, its fasteners, sealing and sub-assembly labour on every engine. Many DOHC Al heads use a separate cam-carrier/ladder (AlSi10Mg die-cast) bolted to the deck with 10-14 M6 bolts plus a machined mating face and RTV sealant bead to control cam-bore alignment. Proposal: where deck stiffness allows, cast the cam bores directly into the head as a monolithic upper structure and line-bore the cam tunnel in one setup — deleting the carrier, its bolts, sealing face and sealant robot, and pairing with end-loaded/built (assembled) camshafts. Single-setup line-boring of the integrated tunnel achieves ≤0.02 mm total cam-bore concentricity, matching an assembled carrier, provided the casting locates the bearing beam stiffly. Consolidates two AlSi castings into one; verify no-machining access for the built camshaft assembly path.

ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Deletes the cam-carrier casting, its machining line, 10-14 bolt holes+bolts, sealant application and a sub-assembly station. Adds a line-boring op on the head (or extends existing tunnel bore). Net one casting and one sub-assembly deleted; head fixture revised. Reduces WIP and one supplier PPAP.

Head casting complexity rises (more cores) risking porosity at the cam beam; mitigate with simulation-guided gating and CT sampling. Line-bore cycle adds time.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Integrated cam-bore heads run with built/assembled camshafts are established practice; not naming a specific programme.

title: Turbine housing to bearing-housing — machined joint to integral cast waste-gate seat
description: Removes a discrete high-alloy seat ring and its press-fit and machining on every turbo. Baseline turbine housing (SiMo51 / GJS-SiMo4-6 ductile iron) uses a separately machined, pressed-in wastegate valve seat ring plus a bushing bore for the wastegate arm, needing precision machining and a press-fit station. Proposal: cast the wastegate seat contour net-shape into the SiMo51 housing using a chill/hardening insert core to refine the local matrix, finishing with a single form-milling pass and deleting the pressed seat ring; integrally cast the arm-bushing boss and press a self-lubricating sintered bronze bush as the only insert. SiMo51 at the seat sees ~850°C; the ferritic matrix with localised pearlite refinement (via the chill) gives adequate seat-erosion resistance for the duty if seating pressure is moderated, removing the discrete high-alloy seat ring.

costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~€9/housing saved (seat ring €3.5 + press station €2 + machining delta €3.5) × 200,000

ideaData.materialGrade: SiMo51 (GJS-SiMo4-6) housing with chill-refined cast seat; sintered bronze arm bush only insert

title: GaN totem-pole PFC replaces Si-IGBT bridgeless boost in OBC
description: Fewer power semiconductors, smaller magnetics and capacitor bank, lighter heatsink offset higher per-device GaN cost as GaN pricing falls below $1.5/A. Baseline 11kW OBC: diode bridge + 650V/40A field-stop Si-IGBT boost PFC at 65kHz, LLC stage, BN-filled heatsink, 470µF/450V DC-link electrolytic (e.g. Nichicon/EPCOS 105°C long-life). Replace front end with 650V/50mΩ E-mode GaN HEMT (GaN Systems GS-065-060 class or Infineon CoolGaN IGT65R) in a totem-pole bridgeless PFC at 140–300kHz. Zero reverse-recovery deletes bridge-diode conduction loss (~1.4pt), lifting peak efficiency ~95.5%→~98%. Higher frequency shrinks the boost inductor from a 40mm PQ (3C95/3F36) ferrite to ~26mm and halves DC-link to ~220µF, and reduced loss cuts heatsink mass ~35%, enabling a denser potted assembly.

GaN requires tighter gate-loop PCB layout (4-layer with buried power planes) and Kelvin-source routing; adds AOI inspection for solder voiding on thermal pads. Net PCB area down ~18%.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Fewer power semiconductors, smaller magnetics and capacitor bank, lighter heatsink offset higher per-device GaN cost as GaN pricing falls below $1.5/A.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~€25/unit net saving (magnetics -€9, capacitor -€6, heatsink -€5, bridge delete -€5) × 150,000 units

Short-circuit withstand of GaN is <1µs vs IGBT ~5µs, so desat protection must be redesigned. AEC-Q101 qualification and long-term dynamic Rds(on) drift validation required over 15-yr life.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: GaN totem-pole PFC in onboard chargers is established practice among Tier-1 OBC suppliers; mechanism proven, no specific programme claimed.

title: Single-stage LLC-integrated OBC merges PFC and isolation magnetics
description: Eliminates hand-wound magnetics labour and one core set; shifts to scalable PCB fabrication. Baseline OBC keeps the PFC boost choke and LLC resonant transformer as two discrete magnetics, each with its own ETD/PQ ferrite core (3C95/3F36), bobbin, and litz winding plus inter-stage DC-link. Replace with a matrix-transformer integrated-magnetics design combining PFC choke and LLC transformer onto a shared low-profile planar core stack in Ferroxcube 3F46 material (optimised 300–500kHz), windings etched into a 6-layer 2oz (70µm) copper PCB with 2kV reinforced primary/secondary insulation. Interleaved primary/secondary layers cancel proximity-effect AC resistance; shared flux paths cut core volume ~30%. Deletes one magnetic component, its potting, its manual winding station, and hand-wound litz/bobbin/tape.

Thermal hotspot at core centre demands thermal-via array and validated to 105°C coolant-adjacent operation. Insulation coordination (reinforced isolation per IEC 62368) across PCB layers requires creepage/clearance validation and partial-discharge testing.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Planar integrated magnetics in resonant converters is established power-electronics practice; no specific vehicle programme claimed.
ideaData.materialGrade: Ferroxcube 3F46 planar ferrite; 6-layer 2oz (70µm) FR4 PCB, 2kV reinforced insulation

title: Aluminium charge cable conductor with crimped Cu-clad terminals
description: Copper-to-aluminium substitution on the heaviest conductors captures both metal-price and mass savings. Baseline AC/DC charge inlet-to-battery cabling uses tinned Cu Class 5 stranded conductor (35mm² and 70mm² for HV DC legs). Replace with EN AW-8030 (or 1370) aluminium conductor in H14/H16 temper, sized one gauge up (50mm²/95mm²) to match copper's ~61% IACS. Al at ~2.7 g/cm³ vs Cu 8.9 g/cm³ gives ~48% conductor mass cut and a large per-kg material delta at LME spreads. Aluminium creep/oxide joint-resistance rise is defeated with friction-welded or ultrasonic-welded Cu-clad transition ferrules at both ends so the crimp/bolt interface sees only copper; DIN 72623-class HV crimps. Up-sized cross-section fits existing conduit for the DC legs where bend radius allows.

Connection resistance drift over 15-yr thermal cycling must stay within HV interlock thresholds; periodic resistance monitoring via BMS recommended.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Aluminium HV cabling with welded Cu transitions is established practice among EV harness Tier-1s; no specific programme claimed.
ideaData.materialGrade: EN AW-8030 / EN AW-1370 aluminium conductor, H14/H16 temper; Cu-clad ultrasonic/friction-welded transition ferrules

title: Coolant-loop sharing deletes standalone OBC/DC-DC cold plate
description: Consolidating two cold plates and their plumbing removes castings, fittings, and a leak-test operation. Baseline HV power-electronics packaging gives the OBC and DC-DC each a dedicated cast aluminium (AlSi9Cu3) cold plate with its own inlet/outlet ports, O-rings and jumper hose, teed off the battery loop. Replace both with a single shared serpentine cold plate, CAB furnace-brazed from AA3003 core clad in AA4045 braze alloy (~7.5% Si), onto which both OBC and DC-DC power modules mount directly via sintered-Ag (75–150µm) or gap-pad interfaces, flow arranged in series with the higher-loss OBC upstream. Deletes one casting, one quick-connect set, two O-ring joints, one hose, and a leak-down test point. Direct module-on-plate mounting removes a TIM layer, cutting junction-to-coolant resistance and relaxing device deratings.

title: SiC-monolithic DC-DC synchronous rectification deletes output diodes
description: Efficiency gain shrinks heatsinks and magnetics, offsetting SR-MOSFET and gate-drive addition. Baseline 3kW HV-to-12V DC-DC uses a phase-shift full-bridge with a Schottky-diode output bank on the LV secondary; at 200A the ~0.5V drop dissipates ~100W, forcing a large secondary heatsink. Replace the diode bank with synchronous rectification using low-Rds(on) LV MOSFETs (Infineon OptiMOS or ON NVMFS-class 40V, 1.0mΩ split-gate trench) with adaptive/self-driven gating. Conduction loss falls to ~40W, cutting secondary heatsink mass ~50% and lifting efficiency ~93%→~96%. Primary switches consolidate to a 750V/60mΩ SiC MOSFET bridge (Wolfspeed C3M / onsemi EliteSiC), enabling 250kHz operation and a smaller 3F36-core transformer. Net: deletes the diode bank, shrinks two heatsinks and the transformer core.

title: PPS-GF40 charge inlet housing replaces PA6-GF + Al shield
description: Higher-temp polymer eliminates the aluminium thermal shield and associated fasteners/gasket, netting saving despite PPS resin premium. Baseline CCS combo charge inlet uses a PA6-GF30 moulded housing with a separate die-cast aluminium DC-pin thermal/EMI shield and metallic bracket, screwed with a foam gasket. Replace with a single-shot linear PPS-GF40 moulding (Celanese Fortron 1140-class) integrating the pin-carrier, mounting bosses and DC-pin coolant-passage bosses in one part. PPS continuous-use ~220°C (vs PA6-GF ~120°C) directly withstands DC fast-charge pin heating, deleting the aluminium shield; where EMI shielding remains, selective electroless Ni/Cu plating on the moulded surface replaces the casting. PPS near-zero moisture uptake holds pin-alignment features to ±0.05mm without humidity conditioning.

title: Bidirectional V2L/V2G firmware unlocks OBC hardware already fitted
description: Reuses latent hardware capability to delete a whole separate inverter module, converting a feature into near-pure firmware value. Baseline OBC uses a totem-pole PFC and LLC/CLLC-capable topology whose power stage is physically bidirectional but ships with unidirectional firmware; V2L is instead a bolt-on inverter module with its own enclosure, contactors and AC outlet harness. Delete the standalone inverter and enable reverse flow in the OBC via control firmware plus a low-cost hardware delta: a bidirectional current-sense shunt (e.g. 0.5mΩ Kelvin shunt), an anti-islanding grid-sync sensing circuit meeting IEEE 1547/VDE-AR-N 4105, and an AC-routing relay. Because the CLLC and totem-pole stages already reverse power, incremental BOM is <€8 while deleting a €60-class inverter subassembly — a subassembly-level function absorption.

ideaData.title: Bidirectional V2L/V2G firmware unlocks OBC hardware already fitted
ideaData.technicalDescription: Baseline OBC uses a totem-pole PFC and LLC/CLLC-capable topology whose power stage is physically bidirectional but ships with unidirectional firmware; V2L is instead a bolt-on inverter module with its own enclosure, contactors and AC outlet harness. Delete the standalone inverter and enable reverse flow in the OBC via control firmware plus a low-cost hardware delta: a bidirectional current-sense shunt (e.g. 0.5mΩ Kelvin shunt), an anti-islanding grid-sync sensing circuit meeting IEEE 1547/VDE-AR-N 4105, and an AC-routing relay. Because the CLLC and totem-pole stages already reverse power, incremental BOM is <€8 while deleting a €60-class inverter subassembly — a subassembly-level function absorption.
ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Deletes an entire bolt-on inverter subassembly (enclosure, PCB, contactors, outlet harness) from vehicle build — removes an assembly station and a supplier interface. Adds three small components to the OBC PCB and one firmware load. Net plant assembly time reduced.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Reuses latent hardware capability to delete a whole separate inverter module, converting a feature into near-pure firmware value.
costSavingPotential.percentage: Deletes a €55–€70 subassembly at <€8 added cost
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~€52/vehicle net (inverter module -€60, added components/firmware +€8) × 150,000

ideaData.riskNotes: Anti-islanding and grid-code compliance (IEEE 1547 / EN 50549 / regional) is the gating risk — requires certified grid-tie protection and reconnection logic. Reverse-mode thermal duty cycle stresses OBC magnetics; validate continuous discharge at rated V2L power over ambient range. Warranty exposure shifts to OBC — accelerated life test in bidirectional mode required.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Bidirectional CLLC OBCs delivering V2L are established — Hyundai/Kia E-GMP platform (2021) ships an integrated V2L discharge function; mechanism proven.

title: Planar-matrix transformer replaces wound litz-wire OBC isolation stage
description: Eliminates skilled winding labour and per-unit magnetics trimming, the OBC's highest-touch subassembly. Baseline 11kW OBC isolation transformer is hand-wound litz (630×0.071mm) on a PQ50/50 3C95 ferrite core, needing manual bobbin winding, tape insulation, varnish impregnation and per-unit LCR trimming — high labour and copper-loss scatter. Replace with a planar matrix transformer, windings etched into the multilayer power PCB (4oz/140µm copper, 6-layer FR4, 2kV reinforced primary/secondary insulation) interleaved with E32 planar cores in Ferroxcube 3F46 for low loss at 300–500kHz LLC operation. Splitting into 2–3 paralleled matrix elements halves leakage inductance and equalises current sharing without trimming. Windings become a PCB-fab output — zero winding labour, ±3% repeatable turns ratio, 40% lower window height for a flatter package.

Adds core-clip press-fit and gap-shim station. Reflow-compatible; scrap shifts from winding rework to PCB yield, which is statistically tighter.

costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~€14/unit magnetics labour+scatter baseline × ~€8 delta × 200k + core material saving

ideaData.riskNotes: Planar windings run hotter per unit area — thermal validation of PCB dielectric at 130°C hotspot and 2 kV isolation partial-discharge testing (IEC 61851) required. Interlayer creepage/clearance must pass CTI-600 substrate. Mitigate with thermal vias to cold plate and potting over core window.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Planar matrix transformers are established practice in telecom/server rectifiers and are appearing in EV OBCs; not tied to a named programme.
ideaData.materialGrade: Ferroxcube 3F46 E32 planar ferrite; 6-layer 4oz (140µm) FR4 PCB, 2kV reinforced insulation; replaces 3C95 PQ50/50 + litz

title: Charge-port DC contactor deleted via OBC-side pyrofuse and MOSFET disconnect
description: Removes wear-prone electromechanical contactors and their driver electronics from the charge branch. Baseline DC charge path uses two 500A sealed gas-filled HV DC contactors (~€22 each, ~180g each) in the inlet subassembly for isolation and fault interruption, with dedicated coil drivers. Replace the isolation function with a solid-state disconnect: back-to-back 1200V SiC MOSFETs (Wolfspeed C3M 20mΩ die, paralleled) for controlled soft-connect and µs fault cutoff, backed by a single non-resettable pyrotechnic squib fuse (150kA interrupt, e.g. Autoliv/Bosch-class pyrofuse) for the catastrophic short-circuit case solid-state cannot clear thermally. Removes contactor arcing wear, contact-bounce inrush and coil drivers. Precharge resistor and relay are deleted because the SiC stage ramps gate voltage to control inrush di/dt.

ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Deletes 2 contactors, precharge resistor + relay, and 2 coil drivers from the port subassembly harness. Adds a SiC half-bridge module onto existing HV PCB (reflow) plus one pyrofuse press-in. Net part count down ~6; harness routing simplified, one fewer leak-tested sealed component.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Removes wear-prone electromechanical contactors and their driver electronics from the charge branch.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~€52 contactor+precharge+driver baseline − ~€28 SiC+pyrofuse = ~€24 × 150k

ideaData.riskNotes: SiC body-diode reverse conduction and thermal runaway under sustained fault must be bounded — pyrofuse sizing and gate-driver desat protection are the key validations (ISO 6469-3, UL 2251). Squib is single-use: field-replacement logistics and cost per event must be modelled.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Pyrofuse + solid-state HV disconnect is established practice in EV main HV junction boxes; extension to the DC charge branch is the novel move.
ideaData.materialGrade: Wolfspeed C3M 1200V 20mΩ SiC MOSFET (back-to-back); 150kA pyrotechnic squib fuse; deletes 500A gas-filled DC contactors

title: Ferrofluid-free — dry thermal pad replaces gap filler in DC-DC potting
description: Converts a wet, cure-bound dispense process to a dry drop-in, plus enables SiC die downsizing. Baseline DC-DC power stage rejects heat to the cold plate through a dispensed 2-part silicone gap filler (~3 W/mK, ~1.5mm bond line, e.g. Dow TC-3040/Henkel Bergquist GF class) needing a meter/mix dispense robot, cure dwell and per-batch viscosity control, with destructive rework. Replace with a die-cut pre-formed compressible graphite/ceramic-loaded silicone pad (~6 W/mK, 2.0mm, ~30% compression set, e.g. Bergquist Gap Pad TGP class) placed by pick-and-place on FET drain pads and magnetics footprints. The higher-conductivity path roughly doubles heat spreading, allowing ~10% smaller SiC die area at recovered Tj margin — a second-order semiconductor BOM saving. Dry op with instant line verification versus wet-dispense cure lag.

ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Deletes 2-part metering/mix dispenser, static mixer consumable stream, and 30-min cure oven from the DC-DC line — frees floor space and removes a capex-heavy dispense cell. Adds one pick-place feeder for die-cut pads. Cycle time drops (no cure wait); scrap becomes recoverable (pad peels off for rework).

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Converts a wet, cure-bound dispense process to a dry drop-in, plus enables SiC die downsizing.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~€4/unit dispense+cure+scatter − ~€2 pad delta + SiC die saving, × 200k

Higher pad unit price offset by process savings; verify at target volume.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Die-cut high-conductivity thermal interface pads are established practice in power electronics; application to DC-DC gap-fill is the lever.
ideaData.materialGrade: Bergquist Gap Pad TGP-class 6 W/mK graphite/ceramic-loaded silicone pad, 2.0mm; replaces Dow TC-3040 / Bergquist GF-class 3 W/mK dispensed gap filler

title: Charge inlet + DC-DC + OBC share one 3-in-1 cast HV busbar frame
description: Collapses many bolted busbar interfaces into one welded molded backbone shared across three units. Baseline connects charge inlet, OBC output and DC-DC I/O with discrete stamped C11000 (ETP, 99.9% Cu) busbars, each PA-sleeved and torqued at 6-8 M6 joints (5-6 Nm) with anti-vibration washers — many bolted interfaces, each a fretting/warranty and torque-verification risk. Replace with a single overmoulded HV busbar frame: 2.0-3.0 mm laser-cut C11000 (or EN AW-1050 Cu-clad-Al for ~40% mass save) conductors insert-moulded in PA66-GF35, UL94 V-0, CTI PLC0 (>=600 V), forming one rigid backbone locating all three subassemblies. Contacts reduce to laser-welded lap joints (>=3 mm weld) except serviceable interfaces. Moulding fixes creepage/clearance to IEC 60664-1 geometrically, deleting loose insulators and per-joint torque logging.

Molding tool is new capex but consolidates SKU count; assembly becomes drop-and-weld, lowering cycle time and rework.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Collapses many bolted busbar interfaces into one welded molded backbone shared across three units.

ideaData.riskNotes: Laser-welded Cu joints need weld-quality monitoring (resistance/pull test); overmold must survive HV thermal cycling without delamination causing tracking. Cu-clad-Al variant needs bimetallic corrosion sealing. Validate to LV123 HV coupling and ISO 6469 clearance.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Insert-moulded HV busbar modules are established practice in EV power-distribution units (PDUs); the 3-way charging-subassembly consolidation is the novelty. No specific programme named.
ideaData.materialGrade: C11000 ETP copper (2.0-3.0 mm) or EN AW-1050 Cu-clad-Al; overmould PA66-GF35, UL94 V-0, CTI >=600 V

title: Thermistor NTC deletion via SiC on-die temperature sensing in OBC/DC-DC
description: Deletes discrete temp-sense circuits and unlocks power headroom for silicon downsizing. Baseline power stages monitor junction proximity with discrete board-mounted 10 kO NTC thermistors (B57' series-class, plus divider, RC filter and dedicated ADC channel) near each FET cluster — they read PCB temperature with lag, forcing conservative derating. Modern 1200 V SiC MOSFET modules (e.g. Wolfspeed/onsemi/ROHM 1200 V trench SiC) and their gate drivers expose an on-die temperature-sense diode or a digital thermal readout (SPI/dedicated pin). Wiring this into the OBC controller deletes 4-8 NTC circuits and gives true, fast Tj. Reduced sensing lag lets the algorithm run nearer SOA, recovering ~5% continuous rating from the same die, or downsizing to a lower current-rating SiC die/module for equal output.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Deletes discrete temp-sense circuits and unlocks power headroom for silicon downsizing.
costSavingPotential.percentage: 3-6% of control-board BOM plus power-stage headroom
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~€3–5/unit NTC circuits + derating-driven silicon saving × 200k

ideaData.riskNotes: On-die sense accuracy and calibration drift must be characterised; loss of a discrete redundant sensor requires functional-safety analysis (ISO 26262) for thermal-protection ASIL path — may need a single retained backup NTC. Firmware derating map must be re-tuned and re-validated over life.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: On-die/gate-driver temperature sensing in 1200 V SiC power stages is established practice; applying it to eliminate charging-stage NTCs is the lever. No specific programme named.
ideaData.materialGrade: 1200 V trench SiC MOSFET modules with integrated Tj sense diode; deletes 10 kO NTC (B25/85 ~3435 K)

title: AC charge cable gauge reduction via active thermal-derating firmware
description: Cuts internal AC cable copper by a third by exploiting statistical duty cycle rather than worst-case sizing. Baseline single-phase 32 A AC inlet-to-OBC internal cable is sized to worst-case continuous thermal limit — 6 mm2 Class 5 stranded C11000 Cu with XLPE insulation rated 125 °C — to hold 32 A indefinitely at 45 °C ambient below 90 °C conductor temp. Replace with 4 mm2 Cu plus an inline I2R/thermal RC model in the charge controller using the inlet thermistor mandated by IEC 62196/61851 (Type 2), dynamically limiting current only in the rare high-ambient/high-current corner. Because real sessions almost never hold simultaneous worst-case ambient and full current for the thermal time-constant (minutes), 4 mm2 is thermally safe >99% of sessions, trading brief edge-case derating for ~33% copper cross-section reduction (6->4 mm2).

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Cuts internal AC cable copper by a third by exploiting statistical duty cycle rather than worst-case sizing.
costSavingPotential.percentage: 25-33% of internal AC cable copper cost
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~2 m × copper mass delta @ ~€8/kg Cu × 250k plus terminal/clip savings

ideaData.riskNotes: Conductor thermal model must be validated against connector standards (IEC 61851 mandates inlet temp monitoring already) — the derating logic becomes safety-relevant and must be robust to sensor fault (fail to lower current). Customer-perception of occasional derating must be managed. Bounded thermal-abuse testing required.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Temperature-based charging-current derating is established practice mandated by IEC 61851; using it to justify conductor downsizing is the cost lever. No specific programme named.
ideaData.materialGrade: Downsize 6 mm2 -> 4 mm2 Class 5 C11000 Cu, XLPE (125 °C rated); inlet NTC per IEC 61851

title: OBC/DC-DC housing to thixomolded AM50 Mg replacing HPDC AlSi
description: Thin-wall near-net Mg cuts mass and machining while preserving shielding and coolant sealing. Baseline OBC/DC-DC housing is HPDC EN AC-43500 AlSi10MnMg (~1.2 kg) with machined sealing/mounting faces, providing EMI shielding and a cold-plate interface. Replace with thixomoulded AM50A magnesium (semi-solid injection ~580-620 °C) yielding near-net thin walls (1.0 mm feasible vs ~2.0 mm min for Al HPDC) with tight dimensional repeatability and near-zero gas porosity, so sealing/connector faces need far less machining stock. Mg density 1.77 vs 2.68 g/cm3 cuts housing mass ~30%. Lower process temp and low porosity improve leak-tightness (target <5x10^-6 mbar·L/s He) for the coolant channel and cut machining passes. EMI shielding retained via grounded seams and conductive gasket at the split line.

Requires Mg-capable molding + chip-handling safety (Mg fines). Fewer machining passes cut cycle time; scrap/chips are recyclable and higher value.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Thin-wall near-net Mg cuts mass and machining while preserving shielding and coolant sealing.
costSavingPotential.percentage: 8-13% of housing subassembly cost + weight credit
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~€6/unit machining reduction + weight-attributed value − Mg alloy premium, × 200k

ideaData.riskNotes: Mg galvanic corrosion at dissimilar-metal fasteners and coolant contact demands isolation coatings/inserts and validated e-coat; flammability handling of Mg swarf needs plant controls. Creep at sustained temp and cooling-channel compatibility validated per thermal-cycle spec. Higher alloy €/kg partly offsets mass saving.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Thixomoulded AM50/AM60 Mg is established practice for thin-wall EMI-critical electronics housings; the power-electronics housing application is the lever. No specific programme named.
ideaData.materialGrade: Thixomoulded AM50A Mg (1.0 mm walls) replacing HPDC EN AC-43500 AlSi10MnMg (2.0 mm)

title: Radome-integrated heater trace replacing discrete PTC de-icer
description: Removes a bonded sub-assembly and a connector interface, cutting parts and a warranty-prone adhesive joint. Baseline forward radar (77 GHz) uses a moulded PC/ASA radome with a separately bonded polyimide-film PTC heater (Kapton + etched Cu, ~5 W) plus its own connector, harness pigtail and PSA layer — three parts, two joins. Proposal: two-shot mould the radome in low-Dk PBT-GF (e.g. 20-30% glass, er ~3.1, tand <0.004 at 77 GHz) and insert-mould an LDS heater grid onto the inner face, then MID-plate Cu (~8-12 µm)/Ni/Au. Trace pitch tuned so the heater sits at a lambda/2 node (~1.95 mm in medium) to keep insertion loss <0.3 dB one-way. Deletes foil, PSA and pigtail; heater return uses the same LDS pads carrying bracket ground. A sub-skin-depth Cu grid on a resonant plane is near-RF-transparent, so heating and RF share one wall.

Removes PSA cure dwell (~90 s). Scrap risk shifts from bond voids to plating adhesion, controlled by tape-peel SPC. Net one-fixture reduction on radar line.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Removes a bonded sub-assembly and a connector interface, cutting parts and a warranty-prone adhesive joint.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~€3.0–4.5 saved/unit (foil €1.2 + PSA €0.3 + pigtail/crimp €0.9 + 2 stations amortised €0.8) × 400k

Mitigation: full anechoic pattern correlation and thermal-imaging ice-melt test to OEM winter spec; DoE on trace pitch vs insertion loss; salt-fog + thermal-shock (−40/+85 °C, 1000 cyc) on plated MID adhesion.
dfmaPrinciples: Design for a single process cell
ideaData.benchmarkReference: LDS/MID heater integration is established practice in antenna and heated-optics packaging. No specific programme named.
ideaData.materialGrade: Radome PBT-GF (er ~3.1, tand <0.004 @77 GHz); LDS grid MID-plated Cu 8-12 µm / Ni / Au flash

title: Ultrasonic sensor shared harness backbone via daisy-chain LIN
description: Collapses copper home-runs and per-sensor connectors into one bus, shrinking ECU header. Baseline park-assist uses 8-12 ultrasonic sensors, each with a discrete 3-wire home-run (0.35 mm2 Cu) to the ECU via a sealed bumper harness and a large header. Proposal: convert to a 2-wire daisy-chained DSI3 (or LIN) bus overmoulded into a single bumper-carrier harness where each transducer taps the backbone via an IDC (insulation-displacement) T-splice rather than a discrete sealed connector. DSI3 supports addressed/PDCM sensors, collapsing home-runs to one loop; ECU header shrinks from ~30 to ~6 pins. Bus conductor 0.5 mm2 Cu with sealed IDC splices (IP6K9K). Digital addressing removes the one-wire-per-position need, and IDC splicing eliminates per-sensor connector housings and their seals.
