ECU connector tooling downsized. Cuts bumper build cycle time and reduces mis-mate rework at fascia marriage.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Collapses copper home-runs and per-sensor connectors into one bus, shrinking ECU header.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~€4–6/vehicle (copper reduction €1.5 + 8–10 connectors €2.5 + ECU header €0.8) × 600k

ideaData.riskNotes: Risk: bus fault (single open) can lose multiple sensors — availability/ASIL concern for park brake-assist. Mitigation: dual-loop or ring topology with end-of-line addressing verification; IDC crimp validated to USCAR-21 for corrosion and vibration in bumper wet zone; EMC re-test of shared bus.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: DSI3/LIN daisy-chained ultrasonic bus is established supplier practice. No specific programme named.
ideaData.materialGrade: DSI3/LIN 2-wire bus, 0.5 mm2 Cu; sealed IDC T-splices (replaces per-sensor 3x0.35 mm2 home-runs)

title: Camera housing die-cast AlSi10 replaced by CFRP-hybrid PPA
description: Eliminates casting and precision machining for a moulded near-net optical datum. Baseline front windscreen camera bracket/housing is HPDC EN AC-43500 AlSi10MnMg, machined at the lens-barrel datum and windscreen-bond flange for ±0.05 mm optical boresight — Al used mainly as a low-CTE (~21 ppm/K), high-modulus reference. Proposal: mould the housing in 30% chopped-CF-reinforced PPA (PA6T/6I, CTE ~8-12 ppm/K, flexural modulus ~22 GPa), close to glass/steel, combined with a moulded-in 3-point kinematic mount that decouples thermal strain over -40/+95 °C. Machining at the bond flange is deleted by a moulded self-locating datum boss. Boresight stability depends on differential CTE across the mount triangle, not absolute stiffness, so kinematic decoupling substitutes for aluminium's low CTE.

ideaData.title: Camera housing die-cast AlSi10 replaced by CFRP-hybrid PPA
ideaData.technicalDescription: Baseline front windscreen camera bracket/housing is HPDC EN AC-43500 AlSi10MnMg, machined at the lens-barrel datum and windscreen-bond flange for ±0.05 mm optical boresight — Al used mainly as a low-CTE (~21 ppm/K), high-modulus reference. Proposal: mould the housing in 30% chopped-CF-reinforced PPA (PA6T/6I, CTE ~8-12 ppm/K, flexural modulus ~22 GPa), close to glass/steel, combined with a moulded-in 3-point kinematic mount that decouples thermal strain over -40/+95 °C. Machining at the bond flange is deleted by a moulded self-locating datum boss. Boresight stability depends on differential CTE across the mount triangle, not absolute stiffness, so kinematic decoupling substitutes for aluminium's low CTE.
ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Deletes HPDC casting, trim and 2 CNC datum-machining ops; replaces with one injection tool + minimal reaming of the lens bore. Removes deburr/wash. Adds moisture-conditioning step for PPA dimensional set. Net removal of a machining cell from the camera line.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Eliminates casting and precision machining for a moulded near-net optical datum.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~€4–6/unit (delete casting+machining €5 net of resin premium €1) × 500k

ideaData.riskNotes: Risk: PPA moisture uptake shifts datums and long-term boresight drift affects lane-keep accuracy (ASIL-B). Mitigation: DSC/DMA characterisation, conditioned-part dimensional SPC, on-vehicle boresight drift test over humidity+thermal cycling; retain in-service self-calibration bound check.
dfmaPrinciples: Kinematic mount to decouple thermal strain
ideaData.benchmarkReference: CF-reinforced PPA for dimensionally stable optical brackets is established practice. No specific programme named.
ideaData.materialGrade: 30% chopped-CF PPA (PA6T/6I), CTE ~8-12 ppm/K, flex modulus ~22 GPa, replacing HPDC EN AC-43500 AlSi10MnMg

title: Common bracket family for radar/camera via modular datum plate
description: Collapses four bracket tools and PNs into one plate family plus small clips. Baseline: each ADAS sensor (front radar, corner radar ×2, front camera) has a bespoke stamped-steel or die-cast bracket with unique body-in-white interface, driving 4 part numbers, 4 tools and 4 EOL alignment routines. Proposal: a single stamped HC340LA (or CR3-grade) high-strength steel 'datum plate' family with a common 3-slot kinematic interface to BIW and sensor-specific adapter clip-ins moulded in PA66-GF30. The steel plate carries all crash/vibration load; only the small clip changes per sensor. Commonisation across sensor set and across vehicle variants amortises one progressive die instead of four. Physics/economics: separating the load-bearing datum (invariant) from the sensor-specific geometry (variant) removes tooling duplication and standardises the alignment jig.

Mitigation: modal + crash sim on the shared plate at each sensor mass; EMC ground-path validation; PPAP each clip variant; ensure clip retention under 15 g vibration and thermal cycling.

ideaData.materialGrade: HC340LA HSLA steel plate; PA66-GF30 adapter clips

title: Sensor-cleaning: telescopic nozzle deleted via fascia-integrated fluidic
description: Removes a per-sensor mechatronic actuator in favour of a moulded static nozzle. Baseline camera/LIDAR cleaning uses a pop-up telescopic washer nozzle with a small DC motor or pressure-actuated piston, check valve, seal and dedicated hose branch — a mechatronic sub-assembly per sensor. Proposal: replace with a static fluidic-oscillator nozzle (no moving parts), moulded directly into the fascia/sensor bezel in glass-filled PBT or PA, fed by a demand-pulsed pump at ~2.5-4 bar. The Coanda-switching cavity creates a fanned sweeping spray from a fixed ~0.8-1.2 mm orifice, covering the lens at lower flow (~150-250 mL/min). Deletes the motor, actuator seal, telescoping barrel and its cavity. Bistable internal jet attachment produces oscillating spray without mechanical parts, so coverage comes from fluid dynamics, not actuation.

title: Corner-radar PCB substrate downgrade to hybrid RF/FR-4 stackup
description: Confines costly PTFE laminate to the antenna region, reverting the rest to FR-4. Baseline 77 GHz corner/short-range radar uses a full high-frequency laminate (Rogers RO3003-class, er 3.0, tand ~0.001 @10 GHz) across the entire multilayer PCB — expensive PTFE-ceramic used even on DC/digital layers. Proposal: hybrid stackup — a thin RO3003-class cap (~127 µm) only for the antenna array and feed network, bonded (fusion or 2929 bondply) to an FR-4/mid-Dk core (e.g. Isola 370HR, er ~4.0, Tg 180 °C) for power, digital and mounting layers. RF-critical patch array + feed keeps low-loss laminate; ~60-70% of board area reverts to FR-4. At 77 GHz only the top layers see field concentration; buried digital layers tolerate FR-4 loss, so PTFE laminate on all layers is waste.

costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~€3–4.5/board laminate delta (60–70% area × ~€5/board exotic premium) × 800k

Mitigation: TDR/insertion-loss coupon control, IPC-6012 Class 3 thermal-cycle + IST testing, EM-sim the layer transition, restrict FR-4 to below the RF reference plane.
dfmaPrinciples: Use costly material only where physics requires
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Hybrid RF/FR-4 (mixed-dielectric) stackups for mmWave radar are established PCB practice. No specific programme named.
ideaData.materialGrade: RO3003-class cap (127 µm, er 3.0) over Isola 370HR FR-4 core (er ~4.0, Tg 180 °C); bondply 2929

title: Radar EOL alignment deleted via moulded self-aligning boss
description: Removes a capital EOL alignment rig and mechanical adjustment hardware. Baseline front radar requires a mechanical EOL boresight rig with a corner reflector and 2-3 adjustment screws to set azimuth/elevation, plus a per-vehicle alignment record — capital rig, floor space and cycle time. Proposal: replace mechanical adjustment with a poka-yoke kinematic mount: three moulded conical bosses on the radar mating matching V-grooves on the common bracket (Kelvin/Maxwell coupling), fixing pose deterministically to ±0.1°, combined with software auto-alignment that learns residual offset from stationary road targets (guardrails, signs) in the first drive cycle. Adjustment screws, shims and the mechanical rig are deleted. A 3-boss/V-groove kinematic couple constrains all 6 DOF repeatably, so accuracy comes from moulded geometry plus software, not manual setting.

costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: Rig/station amortisation + cycle-time €1.5–3/vehicle (screws/shims €0.6 + station €1–2) × 500k plus capex avoidance

Mitigation: CMM SPC on boss/groove, GD&T stack analysis to ±0.1°, validate auto-alignment convergence distance and store calibration proof in ECU for homologation.

title: Camera lens barrel: glass stack to hybrid glass-polymer with active-alignment cure
description: Element-count and precision-machining reduction outweigh AA cell amortisation at volume. Baseline front ADAS camera: 5-6 element all-glass barrel (S-BSL7/S-LAH53 spheres) threaded into a 6061-T6 aluminium holder, mechanically shimmed and locked with anaerobic adhesive (Loctite 648 class). Proposal: hybrid stack - 2 outer glass elements (Corning Gorilla or S-BSL7 for scratch/UV) plus 3 injection-moulded cyclo-olefin polymer aspheres (Zeonex E48R COP, dn/dT ~-8x10^-5/K) in a 30% glass-filled Ultem 1010 (PEI) barrel, aligned by 6-axis active-alignment robot and UV-cured with DELO Photobond 4497 acrylate in ~4 s at 200 mW/cm2. COP aspheres replace two glass spheres each while holding MTF50 >0.35 at Nyquist across -40/+105C, athermalised against PEI CTE (~20 ppm/K). AA relaxes barrel thread from ±5 um to ±30 um class.

costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~€3.0/module optics saving (2 glass elements @ €0.9 + threading/shim labour €1.2) × 800k units ≈ €2.4M mid-point; AA cell amortised over family

Mitigate with glass front element as environmental barrier and closed-loop AA data SPC. Long-term UV yellowing of adhesive addressed by DELO grade rated for optical bond lines.

title: Ultrasonic sensor: piezo disc + metal cup replaced by MEMS pMUT membrane
description: Eliminates precious mechanical tuning labour and lead-based ceramic supply risk. Baseline park-assist ultrasonic sensor: a PZT-5A lead-zirconate-titanate piezoceramic disc (~10-16 mm) bonded into a deep-drawn AlMg3/EN AW-5754 aluminium diaphragm cup, mechanically tuned to 48-58 kHz and decoupled with a moulded LSR silicone ring. Proposal: replace the discrete PZT-on-metal resonator with a silicon MEMS pMUT using a 1.0-1.5 um Sc-doped AlN (Al0.7Sc0.3N, higher e31,f) active layer over a batch-etched SOI membrane, in a 3x3 mm LGA. Frequency set lithographically (no per-unit tuning), enabling multi-frequency coded/chirp excitation for near-field ringdown and rain rejection. Removes PZT (lead/RoHS liability), the aluminium deep-draw, and the epoxy bond-and-tune step; ~10x smaller aperture for flush bumper integration.

title: Radar PCB-to-housing thermal path: gap-pad deleted via die-cast coined boss
description: Removes recurring consumable pad cost and its handling/inspection labour. Baseline 77 GHz corner/front radar dissipates ~4-6 W from the MMIC through a die-cut silicone gap-filler pad (3 W/mK, 1.0 mm) onto an AlSi10Mg HPDC housing. The pad is a consumable with placement labour, thickness stack, and pump-out risk. Proposal: replace the pad with a locally CNC-coined boss under the MMIC thermal-via array, running a thin (0.15 mm) dispensed gel (Dow Dowsil TC-3040, 3.4 W/mK) metered as a robot dot. Coining the AlSi10Mg boss to ±0.05 mm flatness (Ra <1.6 um) after casting closes the air gap physically, dropping bond-line thickness ~6x, cutting thermal resistance and lowering MMIC junction temperature or enabling a thinner housing section. Deletes the die-cut pad SKU and manual place step.

title: Radar radome: separately painted cover replaced by co-moulded frequency-matched skin
description: Removes paint+PVD conversion, the dominant cost of decorative radomes. Baseline emblem/front radar radome: a moulded PC or PC/ASA cover with a sprayed decorative topcoat and a non-continuous metal-look PVD layer that must be discontinuous to pass 77 GHz. This drives a paint/PVD line, masking, and dielectric tuning to keep the wall an integer number of half-wavelengths (n*lambda/2, ~1.9 mm per layer in PC, epsilon_r ~2.9, tan delta <0.006). Proposal: two-shot co-mould a gloss-black self-coloured PC substrate (e.g. Makrolon/Lexan, wall tuned to n*lambda/2) with a transparent PMMA gloss skin carrying an in-mould-decoration (IMD) film for appearance without PVD. Eliminates paint booth and PVD; the IMD film is dielectrically transparent, so tuning depends only on the controlled two-shot wall stack - more repeatable than sprayed paint.

ideaData.materialGrade: Self-coloured PC (Makrolon/Lexan, epsilon_r ~2.9) substrate; PMMA gloss skin with IMD film; no PVD metal

title: Camera-cleaning: dedicated pump deleted via shared washer circuit with check-valve manifold
description: Motor/actuator deletion is the highest-value lever in cleaning subassemblies. Baseline surround/rear ADAS camera cleaning uses a dedicated electric fluid pump, reservoir tap, and hose to each nozzle. Proposal: at subassembly level, replace the dedicated camera pumps with a single higher-flow dual-outlet washer pump feeding a moulded PA6-GF30 distribution manifold containing cracking-pressure poppet check valves (e.g. 0.35 bar for windscreen, 1.2 bar for camera jets). Because the camera jets require higher pressure than windscreen wash, a two-speed pump plus pressure-graded check valves routes flow to cameras only above a threshold, so one pump serves both duties without a solenoid per outlet. Deletes per-camera pump motors and connectors; manifold consolidates the plumbing into one clip-in module reducing hose joints and leak paths.

title: Camera FAKRA coax deleted via GMSL/FPD-Link over shielded twisted pair
description: Coax connector+cable is a persistent BOM cost; STP cuts both. Baseline ADAS camera links use a FAKRA/mini-FAKRA coaxial connector and 50 ohm coax carrying serialised video (GMSL2/FPD-Link III) plus PoC. FAKRA coax is costly per metre, needs precise crimp/terminate, and the connector is a cost driver. Proposal: migrate to shielded twisted pair (STP) with an ASA-ML or next-gen SerDes PHY qualified for STP at the required rate, using a compact H-MTD/MATEnet-class automotive connector and 100 ohm STP cable, retaining PoDL power. STP with IDC/press-fit termination costs materially less than coax crimp and shrinks the connector footprint, allowing a smaller camera gland. At the module level the SerDes equalisation/FFE budget covers STP channel insertion loss for typical <15 m harness runs, so RF coax is not required.

ideaData.title: Camera FAKRA coax deleted via GMSL/FPD-Link over shielded twisted pair
ideaData.technicalDescription: Baseline ADAS camera links use a FAKRA/mini-FAKRA coaxial connector and 50 ohm coax carrying serialised video (GMSL2/FPD-Link III) plus PoC. FAKRA coax is costly per metre, needs precise crimp/terminate, and the connector is a cost driver. Proposal: migrate to shielded twisted pair (STP) with an ASA-ML or next-gen SerDes PHY qualified for STP at the required rate, using a compact H-MTD/MATEnet-class automotive connector and 100 ohm STP cable, retaining PoDL power. STP with IDC/press-fit termination costs materially less than coax crimp and shrinks the connector footprint, allowing a smaller camera gland. At the module level the SerDes equalisation/FFE budget covers STP channel insertion loss for typical <15 m harness runs, so RF coax is not required.
ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Deletes coax crimp/terminate station and FAKRA connector SKU at the camera subassembly; adds STP IDC termination (faster, lower skill). Smaller connector gland simplifies housing seal. Harness cost moves to twisted-pair supply. Requires SerDes PHY change on the camera PCB.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Coax connector+cable is a persistent BOM cost; STP cuts both.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~€0.8/link (FAKRA €1.4 + coax delta − STP conn/cable) × 2.4M links ≈ €1.9M mid-point

ideaData.riskNotes: Channel EMC (radiated emissions/immunity per CISPR 25) and insertion loss over temperature must be validated for STP at the video rate; run full link-margin sweep and bit-error-rate soak. Legacy ECU compatibility gates rollout — align to platform SerDes roadmap. Bend-radius/abrasion durability of STP verified.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Automotive SerDes over STP (ASA Motion Link; next-gen FPD-Link on STP) is an established emerging standard; no named OEM vehicle programme claimed.

title: Radar housing/PCB join: laser weld replacing screws-plus-gasket seal
description: Fastener + gasket deletion plus fewer leak paths cuts both BOM and warranty. Baseline radar module seals a moulded PBT/PA cover to the housing with a compressed silicone/EPDM gasket and 4-6 self-tapping screws, needing screw bosses, torque monitoring, and a gasket SKU with placement labour. Proposal: for a same-family thermoplastic pair (both PBT-GF30 or PA6-GF30, laser-transparent cover to carbon-black-absorbing base), use quasi-simultaneous laser transmission welding at ~980-1064 nm to form a hermetic seam in ~2-4 s, deleting screws, bosses, and gasket. The welded joint gives IP67/IP6K9K with no compression-set concern over life and removes the boss-to-gasket-to-cover tolerance stack. Where an emblem radome interface exists, a moulded-in weld rib defines the seal geometry. Design rule: laser-transparent cover, ~0.2-0.5% carbon-black or Clearweld absorber in the base.

title: Wet-on-wet 3-coat paint replacing separate primer bake oven
timeToImplement: 24-36 months (new build or major paint shop refit)
description: Eliminates a full oven's gas and maintenance plus one process deck of labour Baseline three-wet booth applies e-coat, then primer surfacer, a full flash-off and dedicated primer bake at ~160C/~20 min, then base and clearcoat with a second bake. Change to an integrated process (BASF Integrated Process / PPG B1:B2 compact route) that deletes the primer-surfacer oven: waterborne primer, basecoat and clearcoat are applied wet-on-wet with intermediate dehydration flashes at ~80C and a single ~140-160C cure. The B1 primer (waterborne polyurethane dispersion) co-cures and inter-diffuses with the basecoat so the crosslink network forms in one thermal event. Deletes one ~40 m gas-fired oven (~2.5 MW NG burner load), conveyor length and a cooling zone. Stone-chip and humidity resistance retained via a B1 layer ~15 um film build.

ideaData.riskNotes: Colour match on metallic/effect pigments and clearcoat DOI must revalidate; wet-on-wet demands tighter booth humidity/temperature control (±1°C, ±3% RH). ideaData.timeToImplement: 24-36 months (new build or major paint shop refit)
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Integrated/compact paint processes (BASF Integrated Process, PPG Compact Process) are established practice, widely deployed across European car plants; no specific programme named.

title: Self-piercing rivets replaced by flow-drill screws in mixed-material BIW
description: Deletes SPR robots, die wear and dual-side fixturing on accessible joints Baseline aluminium-to-steel BIW joins use self-piercing rivets: each joint consumes a boron-steel rivet (~4-6 cents), a C-frame at ~50-80 kN, and a wearing die. Change high-access single-sided joints to flow-drill screwing (EJOT FDS/Arnold Flowform) where the M5-M6 screw generates its own bushing by friction heat, then forms threads and clamps, needing one-sided access only. FDS needs no bottom die or back-side C-frame throat, reaching closed hydroformed rails SPR cannot, deleting SPR guns and dies. Where SPR is retained, standardise one rivet family (e.g. C-class 5.3 mm, boron steel ~480 HV) to cut die-change and SKUs. Combine with crash-durable epoxy bonding for stiffness; typical stacks EN AW-6014-T4 to HC340/DP600.

ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Converts ~15-25% of SPR joints to FDS, deleting several C-frame SPR robots (each ~€180k) and their die-wear consumables. Single-sided access shortens fixture design and reduces robot count/floor. Adds spindle-drive FDS heads; net station count falls where SPR previously needed twin-side access.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Deletes SPR robots, die wear and dual-side fixturing on accessible joints
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~40 deleted SPR joints/car × €0.05 rivet + die wear €0.02 = €0.07/car ×150k = €1.05M consumables, plus 3 deleted SPR robots amortised (~€1.2M/yr) and reduced fixture capex

Mitigation: restrict FDS to stack-ups ≥2.5mm total, apply Al-flake coated screws + adhesive to break galvanic path; retain SPR on safety-critical crash load paths.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Flow-drill screwing in mixed-material bodies is established practice (EJOT FDS on aluminium-intensive premium bodies); no specific programme attributed.
ideaData.materialGrade: EJOT FDS M5-M6 flow-form screws; boron-steel SPR (C-class 5.3 mm, ~480 HV); EN AW-6014-T4 and DP600/HC340 stacks

title: Skillet-conveyor final assembly replacing overhead + floor plate mix
description: Lower conveyor energy, fewer transfer stations, reduced ergonomic downtime and rework Baseline final assembly moves bodies on a mix of overhead power-and-free carriers and floor slat conveyors, fixing operator height with poor ergonomics and needing transfer decks between systems. Change to a friction-driven skillet (skid pallet) conveyor where each skillet carries the body on a height-adjustable lift table, letting operators set working height per station and walk with the car. Skillets are driven by rows of friction rollers under a flat steel deck, so drive is distributed and low-power versus a heavy central chain; a failed drive isolates to one skillet rather than stopping the line. Adjustable height cuts static muscular load, reducing ergonomic downtime and enabling tool-arm deletion. Deletes overhead-to-floor transfer stations and their pit civil works.

ideaData.benchmarkReference: Skillet/skid friction conveyors in final assembly are established practice across high-volume car plants (Duerr/Eisenmann skillet systems); no specific programme named.

title: AGV kit-to-line replacing line-side rack storage for high-complexity zones
description: Cuts walk-and-search waste, line-side inventory and mis-build; frees floor Baseline trim/final line stores every option variant line-side in flow racks, so an operator with ~40 SKUs walks and searches (waste) and the plant carries days of line-side inventory. title: Overspray-free electrostatic applicators cutting paint waste and booth air
description: Eliminates two-tone masking consumables/labour and cuts paint + booth air use Baseline exterior colour is applied by rotary bell atomisers (ESTA, ~55-65k rpm) at ~70-85% transfer efficiency; the 15-30% overspray loads booth air, driving 0.3-0.5 m/s downdraft, water-wash/venturi scrubbing and sludge disposal. Change two-tone/roof/contrast zones to overspray-free application heads (Dürr EcoPaintJet class) laying a collimated curtain from a ~50-µm-orifice nozzle plate emitting parallel filaments, giving ~99% transfer and ~1 mm sharp edges with no masking film. This deletes masking labour/consumables and slashes overspray the booth must capture; where full-body bells remain, the freed budget allows lower air-change rates and smaller scrubber duty. Compatible with M-class waterborne basecoat (e.g. BASF iGloss/CathoGuard-family systems).

title: Returnable folding steel racks replacing single-trip export wood crates
description: Eliminates single-trip crate spend and cuts transit-damage warranty Baseline inbound/CKD and inter-plant shipments of painted/plastic exterior parts use single-trip ISPM-15 heat-treated wood crates with EPS/PU foam dunnage: consumed once, generating disposal cost and part-damage claims. Change to collapsible galvanised steel returnable racks (S235JR / hot-dip Z275 galvanised frame, RAL powder-coated) with part-specific thermoformed HDPE dunnage (3-5 mm sheet) on a closed-loop pool. A returnable folds to ~20-25% height empty, so backhaul cube cost is a fraction of outbound; each rack replaces dozens of wood-crate trips over a ~7-year life. Nested Class-A surfaces cut transit scratch/warranty. Pool sizing = (trip time × daily demand ÷ trips-per-rack-year) plus safety buffer; UHF Gen2 RFID tags manage loop and dwell.

title: In-line laser texturing replacing masking for e-coat contact-point protection
description: Removes manual masking labour and consumables and the rework it causes Baseline body shop leaves defined grounding/contact and weld-nut faces that must stay paint-free; these are protected in paint with hand-applied plugs, caps and tape, then de-masked — labour/consumable-heavy with rework when masks shift. Change to interfaces that delete masking: serrated/laser-textured contact bosses and thread-forming or paint-piercing grounding fasteners (e.g. EJOT/Arnold-type paint-cutting serrated ground bolts, M6-M8, property class 8.8/10.9 to ISO 898-1) that cut through the coating film at torque-up. The serration teeth locally penetrate the ~20-25 µm e-coat/topcoat to bare metal under clamp load (~15-25 Nm), so a painted surface grounds reliably to <5 mΩ, removing the bare-metal requirement and the mask. Combine with relocating masked features off Class-A show faces.

ideaData.materialGrade: Paint-piercing serrated ground bolts M6-M8, class 8.8/10.9 (ISO 898-1), zinc-flake coated

title: 3-wet high-solids compact process deleting primer booth and oven
description: Eliminates one bake oven's gas and one booth's air-conditioning energy plus one material layer. Baseline is a 4-layer process: cathodic e-coat, solvent-borne primer-surfacer (spray + full 160°C/25-min bake), waterborne basecoat (2 booths), 2K clearcoat, each with flash zones. Replace with a compact/3-wet architecture: e-coat, then functional primer-basecoat applied wet-on-wet-on-wet with no intermediate cure using high-solids waterborne materials with matched rheology and surface-tension gradients so layers do not intermix during an 80°C intermediate flash, then a single 140°C combined cure. Replacing the primer's stone-chip and UV-barrier function with a 12-15 µm functional basecoat engineered for a matched E-modulus gradient removes one full bake without losing chip resistance per SAE J400 gravelometer (target rating ≥7). Cuts ~1 oven, ~1 booth line and associated CO2/energy.

title: Framing station reconfigured to geo-set + respot for platform flexibility
description: Amortises one framing line over multiple models, avoiding a dedicated gate per variant. Baseline BIW framing uses dedicated hard-tooled geo gates per model, each with ~40-60 clamps referencing the underbody-to-bodyside marriage; a model change requires full gate swap and tooling re-buy. Replace fixed gates with a servo-driven, NC-programmable geo-set framer using common base fixtures plus model-specific lightweight net blocks on quick-change zero-point pallets (e.g. ISO 50 taper or Erowa/AMF zero-point, <0.1 mm repeatable datum), executing ~8-12 critical dimensional-set geo spots at station, with the remaining ~300 respot welds distributed to downstream robot respot cells. Dimensional integrity is set by the few geo-defining welds while the zero-point system guarantees repeatable datums, so tooling commonality does not degrade body BIP capability (Cpk >1.33 on key monitoring points).

ideaData.benchmarkReference: Established practice: flexible/global framing (Comau OpenGate, KUKA framing systems) widely deployed circa 2010s; mechanism proven, not naming a specific vehicle programme.

description: Removes heated phosphating, sludge handling and heavy-metal effluent treatment. ideaData.materialGrade: Zr-based thin-film conversion, ~50-100 nm (~20-40 mg/m² Zr), ambient temperature

costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~6 operators × 2 shifts × €55k fully loaded = €660k/shift-set; ~€1.3M labour + rework/warranty reduction; net after cell capex/depreciation

ideaData.riskNotes: Safety-critical fastener risk: mis-torque on subframe bolts is a field-safety issue — validate closed-loop torque-angle capability (Cmk >1.67), redundant angle monitoring, and 100% traceability. ideaData.benchmarkReference: Established practice: automated marriage/decking with vision guidance and multi-spindle runners at high-volume final-assembly plants; mechanism proven, not naming a specific programme.
ideaData.materialGrade: M12-M14 class 10.9 marriage bolts; DC transducerised multi-spindle nutrunners

title: Sequenced JIS door-off line balancing with cross-dock supplier hub
description: Cuts line-side inventory, door-damage rework, and trim cycle time simultaneously. Baseline final assembly runs doors-on through trim, causing damage-rework and requiring wide line-side racks holding all door-trim variants (speaker, switch, mirror, glass permutations), driving high inventory and picking error. Replace with a door-off strategy: doors removed after paint, routed to an offline door-build line, re-fitted at end of trim, combined with a just-in-sequence (JIS) supplier cross-dock hub feeding door hardware in build sequence via broadcast (EDI 866/sequence pull). Removing doors widens the operator access aperture at every trim station (faster cycle, less damage), and JIS sequencing collapses line-side door-variant inventory from N racks to a single flow-rack of the next few sequenced sets, moving buffer stock and sub-assembly labour to a lower-cost supplier hub.

ideaData.riskNotes: JIS sequence-break risk halts the line — needs robust broadcast, supplier discipline, and a small resequencing buffer. ideaData.benchmarkReference: Established practice: door-off assembly and JIS supplier hubs are standard across major OEM final assembly; mechanism proven, not naming a specific programme.

description: Cuts buffer inventory, search labour, and paint changeover material via live location and resequencing. ideaData.technicalDescription: Baseline body-shop and paint WIP tracking relies on fixed barcode/RFID read points at cell entries plus manual line-side counts, leaving 'blind' buffer zones (skid stores, paint select banks, repair loops) where a body's status/location is inferred, driving over-buffering and manual search for priority units. Real-time location removes the safety-stock buffer covering tracking uncertainty and eliminates operator search time and mis-sequencing, while enabling dynamic paint-block resequencing to cut colour changeovers and solvent purge.
ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Adds UWB anchors, tags and MES integration; no line hardware change. Reduces buffer skid count needed between body-paint-trim, freeing floor. Cuts manual counting/search labour. Enables paint colour-block optimisation reducing purge/changeover material.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Cuts buffer inventory, search labour, and paint changeover material via live location and resequencing.
costSavingPotential.percentage: 10-20% buffer WIP reduction; 3-5% paint changeover material
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: WIP carrying release + search-labour + paint purge savings; ~€8-15/vehicle × 200,000 net of RTLS capex/opex

ideaData.riskNotes: Multipath/metal-reflection can degrade UWB accuracy in dense steel body shops — requires anchor-density survey and calibration. Data-integrity risk if tags detach; use rugged skid-mounted tags. Change-management: MES must become the single source of truth versus legacy counts.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Established practice: UWB/RTLS (IEEE 802.15.4z) asset tracking deployed in automotive plants for WIP/tool tracking; mechanism proven, not naming a specific programme.

description: Cuts weld-cell electrical energy, electrode-cap consumables and gun/transformer count while improving stiffness. ideaData.title: Structural adhesive + fewer spot welds cutting weld-cell energy
ideaData.technicalDescription: Baseline BIW joins bodyside/roof/underbody with ~4,000-5,000 resistance spot welds, each drawing a high current pulse and needing ~120-150 weld guns/transformers, heavy secondary cabling, water-cooling and electrode-cap dressing consumables. Replace ~600-1,000 welds on continuous flange joints with crash-durable 1K heat-cured epoxy structural adhesive (e.g. Dow Betamate / Henkel Terokal class, ~4-5 mm bead, robot-applied), retaining a reduced spot pattern only for fixturing/hem and peel-critical points. Continuous adhesive distributes load over the whole flange, raising torsional stiffness and fatigue life more per gram than discrete welds, so weld count drops while body stiffness rises; the epoxy co-cures in the existing 160-180°C e-coat bake, adding no oven and cutting weld-cell energy and cap consumables.
ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Removes weld guns/transformers and their cooling and cap-dressing consumables for the substituted joints; adds adhesive-dispense robots and pumps. Net energy drops (adhesive cures free in e-coat bake). Fewer electrode caps consumed. Slight cycle change; improved NVH/stiffness as side benefit.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Cuts weld-cell electrical energy, electrode-cap consumables and gun/transformer count while improving stiffness.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: Reduced welds × (energy + cap-dressing consumable + gun maintenance) minus adhesive material; ~€10-20/vehicle net × 200,000

ideaData.riskNotes: Adhesive requires clean/oiled-surface compatibility, bead-continuity monitoring (vision/flow-meter), and crash validation — bond must survive full crash and 15-yr durability. Retain enough spot welds to fixture during cure and for peel-critical zones. Repairability in field must be addressed.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Established practice: crash-durable structural bonding with reduced spot-weld count is standard in modern BIW; mechanism proven, not naming a specific programme.
ideaData.materialGrade: 1K crash-durable epoxy structural adhesive (Betamate/Terokal class), ~4-5 mm bead, e-coat co-cure

title: Coarse two-block axial magnet split replacing six-block segmentation
description: Fewer cuts, less coating area, fewer glue lines and placements. Baseline IPM rotor uses N42UH NdFeB magnets segmented into 6 axial blocks per pole to suppress eddy-current loss (P_eddy ∝ length²), driving grinding, edge-passivation and epoxy-glue-line count up. Proposal: exploit that at 800V PWM with ~12 kHz carrier and a laminated 0.20mm rotor stack, axial eddy loss scales with block length squared; dropping from N42UH to N45SH (lower Hc-cost grade) and re-optimising to 2 axial blocks of 15mm each (vs 6×5mm) holds magnet temperature under 150°C while cutting magnet piece-count 66%. Fewer cut faces means less coating area (Ni-Cu-Ni or epoxy) and fewer 0.05mm glue lines, raising fill factor and torque density ~2%, permitting a slight mass reduction. Wire-EDM/slicing cuts per magnet fall from 5 to 1.

costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~€52 magnet content/rotor × ~10% avg processing+grade saving × 200k, plus ~€1/rotor placement labour

ideaData.riskNotes: Longer blocks raise localised eddy heating and demag risk at peak-torque/high-speed corner; mitigate with thermal FE plus back-EMF demag test at 160°C and rotor open-circuit spin to redline. Validate with locked-rotor thermal soak and 300h life dyno.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Axial magnet segmentation vs eddy loss is established traction-motor practice; block-count optimisation is standard, no specific programme claimed.

title: Hollow gun-drilled shaft replaces solid forged rotor shaft
description: Lower steel mass, integrated oil path, lighter rotating assembly. Baseline rotor shaft is solid 42CrMo4+QT (1.7225, quenched-and-tempered to ~900–1100 MPa UTS, spline induction-hardened to 55–58 HRC), turned then hard-turned, carrying ~4000 Nm through the spline with mass at a radius that adds no torsional stiffness (τ ∝ r near surface). Proposal: gun-drill a Ø18–22 mm concentric bore through the Ø34 mm shaft (bore-to-OD ~0.55–0.65), or friction-weld a two-piece design from EN 10305-1 E355+SR cold-drawn seamless tube (min yield ~450 MPa) with forged spline ends. Since J ∝ r⁴, removing the low-stress core cuts ~30% mass with <8% torsional-stiffness loss. Bore doubles as the oil-transfer passage, deleting a feed tube. Wall sized so first bending mode stays >1.3× max operating speed; bore ID to IT9, straightness <0.05 mm.

ideaData.materialGrade: 42CrMo4+QT (1.7225) solid, or EN 10305-1 E355+SR cold-drawn seamless tube for the two-piece welded route

title: Injection-overmoulded polymer end plates replacing aluminium castings
description: Cheaper feedstock, near-zero machining, integrated features. Baseline rotor end plates are die-cast AlSi9Cu3 or machined 6061-T6, serving as lamination-stack retainers, balance-material carriers and magnet-cavity closers. They are stressed mainly in the axial clamp direction, not torsionally. Proposal: replace with injection-moulded 50% glass-fibre-reinforced PA66-GF50 (or PPA-GF for >150°C zones) end plates that snap/heat-stake to the stack and integrate balancing bosses and cavity seals in one shot. PA66-GF50 gives ~180 MPa tensile and a CTE closer to the epoxy/magnet than aluminium, reducing thermal-clamp scatter. At the modest hoop loads of an internally-mounted plate (magnets retained by the steel bridges, not the plate), polymer is adequate; centrifugal load on the plate itself is low because it sits at small radius. Deletes machining of the cast plate entirely.

title: Self-bonded lamination stack deletes end-plate rivets and welds
description: Deletes fastening station, lowers iron loss, enables thinner gauge. Baseline rotor core is a stack of 0.35mm NO20 (M270-35A) laminations held by through-rivets or laser-weld beads plus a clamp plate, creating short-circuit paths across laminations that raise eddy loss and demanding a rivet/weld station. Proposal: use backlack (self-bonding) laminations — 0.20–0.35mm electrical steel pre-coated with a thermosetting epoxy on both faces (e.g. Bondlack-type coating), stacked and cured under press at ~180°C/pressure to form a monolithic glued core. Bond shear >6 MPa holds the stack against magnet-insertion and centrifugal loads while the continuous insulation between sheets suppresses inter-lamination eddy currents, cutting rotor iron loss and eliminating the rivet holes that concentrate stress at pole bridges. Thinner 0.20mm gauge becomes viable because bonding replaces mechanical clinch tab

ideaData.benchmarkReference: Backlack self-bonding rotor/stator cores are established high-volume practice; no specific programme named.

title: Ferrite-flux-barrier hybrid magnets cut NdFeB volume per pole
description: Displaces expensive rare-earth with cheap ferrite in low-flux zones. Baseline double-V IPM pole is filled entirely with N42UH sintered NdFeB. Field-weakening and low-load operation don't need full remanence everywhere in the cavity. Proposal: hybridise each pole — retain N42UH in the high-working-point inner V and fill the outer, lower-flux-density cavity segment with low-cost Sr-ferrite (Y30H-2) blocks. The ferrite contributes reluctance-torque-supporting flux barriers and modest airgap flux where NdFeB would be near-saturating the bridge anyway, so ~20–25% of the rare-earth volume is displaced by ferrite costing ~1/15 per kg of energy product. Careful magnetic-circuit design keeps the ferrite operating point above its knee (higher irreversible-demag risk at low temp for ferrite) by shielding it behind steel bridges. Net torque held within 2% at rated point.

ideaData.technicalDescription: Baseline double-V IPM pole is filled entirely with N42UH sintered NdFeB. Field-weakening and low-load operation don't need full remanence everywhere in the cavity. Proposal: hybridise each pole — retain N42UH in the high-working-point inner V and fill the outer, lower-flux-density cavity segment with low-cost Sr-ferrite (Y30H-2) blocks. The ferrite contributes reluctance-torque-supporting flux barriers and modest airgap flux where NdFeB would be near-saturating the bridge anyway, so ~20–25% of the rare-earth volume is displaced by ferrite costing ~1/15 per kg of energy product. Careful magnetic-circuit design keeps the ferrite operating point above its knee (higher irreversible-demag risk at low temp for ferrite) by shielding it behind steel bridges. Net torque held within 2% at rated point.
ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Adds a second magnet SKU and a second placement nest but both are net-shape pressed magnets. Ferrite is dimensionally cheaper and needs no Ni coating. Slightly more complex cavity geometry in the lamination die.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Displaces expensive rare-earth with cheap ferrite in low-flux zones.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~€52 magnet content × ~20% displaced × ~90% cost delta × 200k

ideaData.riskNotes: Ferrite has a positive-temperature-coefficient demag knee — risk of low-temperature irreversible demag under field-weakening current; validate cold (-40°C) demag with peak d-axis current, and back-EMF pre/post. Two-material supply adds complexity.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Ferrite/NdFeB hybrid and ferrite-assist IPM rotors are established research-to-production practice; no specific programme named.

title: In-cavity magnetise-after-assembly deletes handling of live magnets
description: Kills live-magnet handling scrap and slow placement; safer logistics. Baseline uses pre-magnetised N42UH blocks, which attract steel and each other during insertion, demanding non-magnetic tooling, force-controlled pushers, high scrap from chipped magnets, and slow robotic placement into the laminated cavities. Proposal: insert unmagnetised NdFeB blocks (green/thermally-demagnetised state — inert, easy to gang-load), then magnetise the fully-assembled rotor in a single pulse using a dedicated multi-pole fixture coil delivering the ~2–3 T saturating field per pole. Because unmagnetised blocks don't self-attract, insertion can be done in bulk with simple tooling and near-zero chipping scrap, and glue-line control improves. Full magnetisation post-assembly also guarantees optimal alignment of each pole to the steel geometry.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Kills live-magnet handling scrap and slow placement; safer logistics.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: chip/scrap ~2% of €52 magnet + ~€2 handling/placement labour × 200k, net of magnetiser amortisation

ideaData.riskNotes: Achieving full saturation of thick inner-V blocks through steel bridges is the risk — under-magnetisation lowers torque; validate flux with per-rotor open-circuit back-EMF gate. Fixture coil heating limits takt. Confirm no partial demag of already-set poles.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Magnetise-after-assembly is established for smaller PM rotors and emerging for traction; no specific programme named.

title: As-machined precision core deletes rotor grinding and cuts balance rework
description: Removes a grinding station and shrinks balance rework and scrap. Baseline bonds/stacks the rotor, grinds the OD and finish-machines the shaft interface, then two-plane balances with drilled correction — grinding exists to hit ~0.03 mm airgap concentricity and balance follows grind/clamp scatter. Proposal: control concentricity at source via high-precision progressive die-set stamping of M270-35A (0.35 mm) laminations with notch-index self-align features, plus a keyless self-centring hub — a tapered polygon P3G (DIN 32711) or hydraulic keyless bush — that seats the stack to <0.02 mm TIR, deleting the OD grind and moving balance to add-mass clips only. The concentric interface removes the dominant unbalance source, raising first-pass balance yield to a residual target <5 g·mm/kg and shortening two-plane balance takt.

ideaData.riskNotes: Stamping-die wear drifts concentricity — needs SPC on TIR and die-refresh schedule; conical interface torque-transfer and axial-retention must be fatigue-validated to 10⁷ cycles and against thermal-loosening. Whirl/NVH test to confirm balance holds at redline.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Grind-elimination via precision self-centring rotor interfaces (polygon/keyless conical hubs) is established practice; no specific programme named.
ideaData.materialGrade: M270-35A non-oriented electrical steel (0.35 mm) laminations; DIN 32711 P3G polygon or hydraulic keyless hub interface

title: Interference-fit shaft-to-core deletes keyway and adhesive bond
description: Removes adhesive consumable, cure energy, and a broach operation from every rotor. Baseline joins the M270-35A (0.35 mm) lamination stack to a splined/keyed 42CrMo4+QT shaft via a machined keyway plus anaerobic structural adhesive (e.g. Loctite 648-class, cure ~30 min at 80°C) to resist slip at 250 Nm peak, needing a dispense station, cure oven and torque-slip validation. Proposal: plain cylindrical shrink-fit with shaft OD to h6 and stack bore to H7 giving 40–60 µm diametral interference; induction-heat the stack to ~200°C and drop onto the ambient shaft. Contact pressure ~35–50 MPa yields friction torque (µ≈0.15) exceeding 250 Nm at >1.6 SF, so no key or adhesive is needed. Deletes keyway broaching, the adhesive cell and the cure oven; surface Ra ≤0.8 µm to secure the friction coefficient.

ideaData.technicalDescription: Baseline joins the M270-35A (0.35 mm) lamination stack to a splined/keyed 42CrMo4+QT shaft via a machined keyway plus anaerobic structural adhesive (e.g. Loctite 648-class, cure ~30 min at 80°C) to resist slip at 250 Nm peak, needing a dispense station, cure oven and torque-slip validation. ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Deletes adhesive dispense, cure oven, and shaft keyway broach station. Adds one induction-heat/press cell (~8 s cycle). Removes 30-min cure bottleneck, freeing WIP buffer. Eliminates adhesive consumable and its scrap. Net plant capex reduced by removing oven and broach; press cell payback under one year at volume.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Removes adhesive consumable, cure energy, and a broach operation from every rotor.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: €3.20 adhesive+cure/unit + €1.80 keyway broach/unit + amortised oven removal ≈ €5–7.5/unit × 200k

ideaData.riskNotes: Risk is loss of grip from thermal expansion at hot-soak (150°C rotor) reducing interference, and fretting at the bore under torque reversal. Mitigate by sizing minimum interference for worst-case hot condition, specifying bore surface finish Ra<0.8, and running torque-to-slip plus thermal-cycle validation (500 cycles -40/+150°C) with axial push-off audit.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Cylindrical shrink-fit (interference) rotor-core-to-shaft joints are established practice in EV traction motors; no specific programme named.
ideaData.materialGrade: M270-35A stack (H7 bore) on 42CrMo4+QT shaft (h6 OD); 40–60 µm diametral interference

title: Non-oriented steel scrap loop: nested blanking of rotor from stator skeleton
description: Converts stator centre scrap into free rotor blanks, cutting silicon-steel buy. Baseline blanks rotor laminations and stator laminations from separate coils of M270-35A, with rotor discs punched from fresh strip and the stator centre-web scrapped, giving stack material utilisation around 42–48% because the rotor OD is far smaller than the stator ID. Proposal nests the rotor lamination inside the stator bore aperture on a single progressive die and coil so the rotor disc is the punched-out slug of the stator, sharing one blanking pass. The physics/economics: the rotor OD (~130 mm) fits inside the stator ID (~150 mm) with a punch bridge, so what was scrap web becomes the rotor blank, lifting utilisation to ~68–72%. Requires matched OD/ID sizing between the two machines and a die redesign with a controlled shear-burr direction so both parts stack burr-consistent.

ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Redesigns the progressive blanking die to co-punch rotor and stator; one coil feed instead of two. Removes a separate rotor blanking line. Reduces electrical-steel purchase tonnage ~25%. Adds die complexity and slug-separation handling; net tooling amortisation favourable above 150k units.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Converts stator centre scrap into free rotor blanks, cutting silicon-steel buy.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~1.8 kg rotor steel × €2.6/kg saved-as-scrap-avoided × recovery fraction × 200k, plus scrap-credit delta

ideaData.riskNotes: Risk is burr direction and edge-work-hardening on the rotor OD (the cut edge) raising core loss locally, plus loss of design freedom to change rotor/stator sizes independently. Mitigate with edge deburr/anneal check, epstein-strip core-loss audit on the cut edge, and locking OD/ID geometry at design freeze.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Nested rotor-in-stator blanking is established die-design practice in high-volume motor lamination shops.

title: Laser-cut magnet slots eliminate separate flux-barrier bridges
description: Magnet-grade downgrade from recovered flux plus die simplification. Baseline IPM rotor stamps rectangular magnet pockets with mechanical iron bridges sized for burst-speed retention; those bridges leak ~4–6% short-circuit flux, forcing higher-remanence N42UH magnet to compensate. Proposal: single-mode fibre laser (~0.1 mm kerf) cuts optimised curved flux barriers with thin (0.3 mm) saturating bridges plus micro-slits impossible to stamp reliably, on the assembled bonded M270-35A (0.35 mm) stack rather than per-lamination. Bridges run at magnetic saturation so leakage flux drops, recovering enough air-gap flux to downgrade the magnet from N42UH to N38UH (lower Nd/Dy content, ~30 MGOe). Cutting the bonded stack avoids per-lamination burr accumulation at the bridge; heat-affected zone kept <0.1 mm to limit core-loss rise at the cut edge.

ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Replaces the magnet-pocket stamping stations in the progressive die with a post-stack laser-cut cell (~one pocket-set per second/pole). Adds laser capex but simplifies the blanking die. Enables thinner bridges than tool-steel punches survive, reducing scrap from bridge cracking.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Magnet-grade downgrade from recovered flux plus die simplification.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~0.9 kg NdFeB × ~€9/kg grade delta (UH→lower-Dy) × 200k, net of laser cell amortisation

ideaData.riskNotes: Risk: laser heat-affected zone at the bridge raising local core loss and reducing burst-speed strength; magnet-grade downgrade must hold demag margin at 150°C. Mitigate with HAZ metallurgical audit, overspeed burst test to 1.2× max, and back-EMF/demag validation confirming N38UH margin before release.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Laser-cutting of rotor flux barriers on bonded lamination stacks is an emerging but demonstrated practice; no specific programme named.
ideaData.materialGrade: M270-35A (0.35 mm) bonded stack; magnet downgraded from N42UH to N38UH sintered NdFeB

title: Balance-by-material-removal in end plate replaces added trim weights
description: Eliminates trim-weight parts and the detachment warranty exposure. Baseline two-plane balancing corrects residual unbalance by riveting or adhesive-bonding steel trim clips onto rotor end plates, adding a weight-handling station, consumables and a re-verify spin, with clip retention a warranty risk at 16,000 rpm. Proposal: balance by subtractive milling — a servo end mill removes material from sacrificial bosses cast into the EN-GJS-500-7 (GGG50) ductile-iron end plate, or drills blind holes in the shaft collar, at the measured heavy angle. Correction U = m·r is achieved by removing mass rather than adding it, so nothing can detach. The measure-mill-remeasure loop runs on one machine with closed-loop correction to <5 g·mm/kg residual; boss volume sized to cover the full expected unbalance range without breaching wall minima.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Eliminates trim-weight parts and the detachment warranty exposure.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: €2.50 clip+consumable/unit + reduced cycle labour + warranty-claim avoidance × 200k

ideaData.riskNotes: Risk: over-removal scrapping a part, and boss thinning below burst-strength or fatigue limit. Mitigate by pre-adding balancing-boss mass allowance in the casting, capping max removal depth in machine logic, and FE-verifying boss residual section for burst and thermal fatigue.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Material-removal balancing (drill/mill correction) is established practice on rotating machinery including turbocharger and e-motor rotors; no specific programme named.
ideaData.materialGrade: EN-GJS-500-7 (EN-JS1050 / GGG50) ductile-iron end plate with cast sacrificial correction bosses

title: Bonded magnet-array preform replaces individual segment insertion
description: Moves insertion labour and scrap off the constrained main line. Baseline inserts 6–8 sintered NdFeB (N42UH) segments per pole individually into rotor slots with per-segment adhesive dispense and cure — labour- and cycle-intensive and prone to chipping/misplacing live-magnetised bricks. Proposal: pre-assemble each pole's segment stack into one adhesive-bonded preform brick off-line on a low-cost fixture (segments kept ≤5 mm axial to break rotor-surface eddy paths for loss control), bonded with a high-Tg epoxy (Tg>150°C), then insert one preform per pole on the main line. Segmentation for eddy-loss is retained but high-precision insertion/dispense cycles on the constrained main line drop from ~48 to ~8 per rotor. Preforms are gauged and rejected off-line, keeping magnet chip scrap off the expensive line; brick outer profile held to ±0.05 mm for slot fit.

ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Adds an off-line preform bonding/curing fixture (cheap, parallelisable) and removes 40+ per-segment dispense/place cycles from the main insertion cell, cutting main-line cycle time ~30%. Reduces main-line magnet-handling scrap. Preform gauging catches defects before shaft assembly.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Moves insertion labour and scrap off the constrained main line.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: main-line cycle reduction €4–6/unit + scrap-off-line-recovery of live magnets × 200k

ideaData.riskNotes: Risk: preform bond-line thickness variation shifting flux and preform handling demagnetising exposure. Mitigate by insert-then-magnetise where feasible, controlling preform adhesive gap to ±0.05 mm, and cog/back-EMF audit on assembled rotor versus segment-by-segment baseline.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Pre-bonded magnet blocks/preforms feeding a single insertion step are established practice in high-volume PM rotor lines; no specific programme named.
ideaData.materialGrade: Sintered NdFeB N42UH segments (≤5 mm axial), high-Tg (>150°C) epoxy bonded preform

title: Powder-metal sintered shaft flange replaces machined-from-bar collar
description: Replaces high-scrap flange turning with near-net PM pressing. Baseline rotor shaft is turned from 42CrMo4 bar with an integral drive flange and end-plate seating collar machined out of oversized stock, generating heavy turning swirl chip (buy-to-fly near 2.5:1 at the flange) and long lathe cycle. Proposal makes the shaft a hybrid: a plain rolled/drawn 42CrMo4 tube-or-bar core joined to a net-shape powder-metal (FLN2-4405, sinter-hardened to ~30 HRC, ~7.0 g/cc) flange collar by press-fit plus laser weld, so the flange geometry (bolt bosses, resolver target, end-plate register) comes net from the PM tool with zero flange machining. The economics: PM converts flange features to a pressed-and-sintered net shape at ~90% material utilisation versus ~40% for turned flange, and the bar core stays cheap. Torque path validated through the weld collar.

costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: flange machining €3–4/unit + 42CrMo4 chip-loss €2/unit saved, net PM+weld add × 200k

ideaData.riskNotes: Risk: PM flange fatigue/porosity at bolt bosses and weld-collar torque capacity under reversing load. Mitigate with sinter-hardened dense grade, densification of boss surfaces, weld penetration audit, and full torsional fatigue plus overspeed validation before release.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Net-shape PM flanges and hybrid PM-to-steel welds are established powertrain practice; no programme named.

title: Filament-wound glass-fibre sleeve replaces machined Inconel band
description: Replaces costly machined superalloy band with wound composite and cuts eddy loss. Baseline surface-magnet high-speed rotors retain magnets with a machined Inconel 718 or 1.4404 (316L) shrink band — costly to turn, adds eddy-current loss in the conductive band and needs precision shrink-fit. ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Removes Inconel band turning and shrink-fit press; adds a filament-winding + cure cell (parallelisable heads). Eliminates conductive-band eddy loss allowing tighter air gap. Winding tension is process-controlled, reducing band-fit scrap; cure oven added.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Replaces costly machined superalloy band with wound composite and cuts eddy loss.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: Inconel band+machining ~€14/unit vs glass sleeve ~€5/unit, delta × 200k

ideaData.riskNotes: Risk: glass sleeve creep and matrix thermal limit at 150°C rotor temperature versus Inconel margin, and hoop-stress fatigue over life. Mitigate with high-Tg epoxy, S-glass where stress demands, spin-to-burst validation at 1.2× overspeed, and hot-soak creep testing before release.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Glass/epoxy retaining sleeves are established practice for high-speed PM rotors operating below the carbon-fibre stress band; no specific programme named.
ideaData.materialGrade: E-glass/epoxy (or S-2 glass/epoxy) filament-wound sleeve, ~55–60% fibre volume; replaces Inconel 718 or 1.4404 (316L) band

title: Direct lead-frame overmould replaces DBC substrate in power module
description: Removes the highest-cost passive material (AMB ceramic) and one bonding interface. Baseline SiC MOSFET module bonds bare die onto Si3N4 AMB substrate (0.32 mm ceramic, 0.3 mm Cu both sides), then sinters DBC to a Cu baseplate — two sinter/solder interfaces plus costly AMB ceramic. Proposal: mount die directly onto a stamped C194 or C7025 copper lead-frame (0.5–0.8 mm) with pressure-sintered silver die-attach (~230°C, ~10 MPa), then epoxy transfer-mould with a high-Tg alumina-filled EMC (Tg>200°C, CTE ~9 ppm/K, filler ~85 wt%). A thin (0.15 mm) filled dielectric layer isolates to the pin-fin cold plate, deleting the AMB ceramic entirely. AMB Si3N4 is the single most costly substrate material (~35%); the lead-frame carries current and heat while filled EMC handles isolation, and matched CTE limits die-shear fatigue over −40/+175°C cycling.

ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Deletes AMB substrate procurement and DBC-to-baseplate sinter station. Adds a transfer-mould press and lead-frame stamping die (~€400k). Net -1 sinter cycle, cycle time down ~40s/module. Scrap shifts from ceramic cracking to mould flash, easier to control.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Removes the highest-cost passive material (AMB ceramic) and one bonding interface.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: AMB substrate ~€14/module × 0.35 saving fraction + €6/module sinter-step deletion × 300,000 = ~€8/module × 300k

ideaData.riskNotes: Partial-discharge inception voltage of filled EMC must exceed 800V system stress with margin; validate per IEC 61287 PD<10pC at 1.5×Vdc. Power-cycling PCsec risk at die corners — mitigate with stress-relief EMC layer and rounded lead-frame die pads. Requires HAST and 1000-cycle TC qualification.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Transfer-moulded lead-frame power modules are established practice (Infineon HybridPACK Drive uses moulded construction, mid-2010s onward); direct-lead-frame isolation replacing AMB is an emerging extension, no specific programme named.
ideaData.materialGrade: C194 or C7025 Cu lead-frame (0.5–0.8 mm); sintered-Ag die-attach; alumina-filled high-Tg (>200°C) epoxy mould compound

title: Sinter-clad busbar-to-capacitor joint deletes screw terminals
description: Eliminates fasteners and torque control while enabling copper down-gauging. Baseline laminated busbar connects to the film DC-link capacitor via M6 threaded studs and screwed ring terminals — 6–8 fasteners, torque control and micro-fretting risk at the Cu/Al interface. Proposal: terminate the capacitor's sprayed Zn/Al schoopage tabs onto C11000 ETP-copper busbar pads pre-coated with pressureless nano-silver paste, then low-temperature sinter (250°C, ~3 MPa) the tab-to-busbar in one press stroke. The sintered joint gives high interface thermal conductivity and eliminates the contact-resistance drift that forces oversizing. Bolted joints degrade via creep and fretting at 105°C, raising ESR and self-heating; a metallurgical sinter joint has near-zero contact resistance and no relaxation, allowing ~10% busbar cross-section reduction at equal temperature rise. ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Deletes 6–8 studs, nuts, and torque-verify station. Adds one heated sinter-press fixture (~€180k). Cycle time neutral (single stroke vs multi-screw). Removes torque-audit rework loop and eliminates loose-terminal warranty returns.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Eliminates fasteners and torque control while enabling copper down-gauging.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: €5.50 fastener+labour + €3 Cu reduction per unit × ~0.6 realisation × 300,000

ideaData.riskNotes: Zn schoopage wettability with Ag paste is marginal — may need a thin flash Ni or Cu on the tab. Thermo-mechanical shear on the rigid joint during vibration must be validated to ISO 16750-3; add a compliant busbar geometry near the joint. Repairability lost — capacitor now non-serviceable.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Silver-sinter joining of busbars is established power-electronics practice; direct sintering to film-capacitor schoopage tabs is an emerging extension, no named programme.
ideaData.materialGrade: C11000 ETP copper busbar; pressureless nano-silver sinter paste; Zn/Al sprayed schoopage cap tabs

title: Insert-moulded PPS busbar replaces stamped-and-laminated Cu stack
description: Consolidates 3 parts + adhesive into one moulding. Baseline laminated busbar is two stamped C11000 copper layers separated by a die-cut PET/PEN dielectric film then hot-laminated — three parts, an adhesive film and a press. Proposal: stamp the C11000 conductors and insert-mould them in 40% glass-filled PPS (e.g. Fortron-class, CTI>250 V, RTI 220°C, UL94 V-0) so the polymer is both dielectric spacer and mechanical carrier in one shot. Overmoulding encapsulates conductor edges, raising creepage without added spacers, and the tool holds conductor spacing to ±0.1 mm for consistent parasitic inductance. The moulded dielectric replaces the film+adhesive stack; PPS's low dielectric loss and 220°C RTI let conductors sit closer, cutting loop inductance ~15% to reduce switching overshoot and DC-link cap stress. Wall between conductors sized to the working voltage for CTI-based creepage.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Consolidates 3 parts + adhesive into one moulding.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: €13 laminated assy → €10 moulded (film+adhesive+labour deleted) × 300,000 × realisation 0.9

ideaData.riskNotes: PPS-to-copper adhesion and thermal-cycle delamination is the key risk — specify adhesion promoter or mechanical keying (stamped windows). Validate partial discharge and dielectric withstand at 2×Vdc+1000V per IEC 60664; confirm no moisture-uptake creep-current path at 85/85.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Insert-moulded busbars in glass-filled PPS are established practice for EV power distribution and terminal blocks; DC-link inverter application is common but no single programme named.
ideaData.materialGrade: C11000 ETP copper conductors; 40% glass-filled PPS (CTI>250 V, RTI 220°C, UL94 V-0)

title: PCB-embedded die power stage replaces module + separate gate driver
description: Collapses three subassemblies and their interconnect into one board. Baseline architecture stacks a discrete power module, a laminated busbar, and a separate gate-driver PCB connected by press-fit pins — three subassemblies and their interconnect. Proposal: embed bare SiC MOSFET die directly inside the multilayer PCB (die placed in a routed cavity, laser-drilled Cu-plated microvias forming top-side contacts), co-locating the gate driver, gate resistors, and current-sense shunt on the same board. Physics: embedding removes wire bonds (the primary power-cycling failure site) and shrinks the gate loop to <5nH, cutting switching loss and letting the DC-link cap and heatsink both downsize. Heat is extracted through thermal vias into a rear cold plate via a thin filled TIM. The interconnect between driver and gate becomes a copper trace, deleting press-fit pins and the separate driver board.

ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Deletes module packaging line, gate-driver board, and press-fit station. Moves value into PCB fab (embedding is a specialist PCB process — outsourced). Adds die-attach-in-cavity and via-plating steps at the board house. Radically fewer in-house stations.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Collapses three subassemblies and their interconnect into one board.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: Module pkg + driver board + interconnect ~€120/inverter, 25% net after PCB cost uplift × 300,000

ideaData.riskNotes: Thermal management through PCB is the hard limit — restricts to <~30kW/phase or needs double-sided cooling; validate junction temp headroom. Embedded-die reliability (via cracking, delamination) needs AEC-Q104 system qualification. Supply base for automotive embedded-die PCB is thin — dual-source risk.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: PCB die-embedding (e.g. AT&S/Schweizer p2Pack-class technology) is established in industrial and emerging automotive power stages; no specific vehicle programme named.

title: Aluminium AA1350 busbar with Cu-clad terminals replaces solid copper
description: Substitutes majority copper mass with lower-cost aluminium at equal ampacity. Baseline DC-link and phase busbars are solid C11000 ETP copper (100% IACS, ~1.6 mm stock). Proposal: switch the conductor body to AA1350-H14 aluminium (99.5% Al, 61% IACS, ~0.028 µΩ·m) sized ~1.6× thicker (~2.6 mm) for equal ampacity, retaining copper only at joint interfaces via cold-roll-bonded Cu/Al bimetal tabs (~15% Cu-clad thickness, C11000 face) so all bolted/laser-welded connections remain Cu-to-Cu, avoiding galvanic and Al2O3-oxide contact issues. Physics: Al is ~65% lighter and ~1/3 the cost per unit conductance of Cu; the clad tab confines Cu to where fretting/galvanic corrosion and joint stability matter, while the bulk conductor exploits cheap Al. The larger Al cross-section is accommodated because inverter busbars are volume- not mass-constrained.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Substitutes majority copper mass with lower-cost aluminium at equal ampacity.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: Cu busbar ~€16 material → Al+clad ~€11, €5 saving × realisation 0.8 × 300,000

ideaData.riskNotes: Galvanic corrosion at any exposed Al/Cu boundary — must fully encapsulate and keep salt-spray path off the bimetal seam; validate to ISO 16750-4. Al creep at bolted joints (already mitigated by keeping joints on the Cu clad). Higher thermal expansion — check busbar-to-module stud stress over TC.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Copper-clad-aluminium (CCA) busbars are established practice in EV battery and PDU busbar packs; extension to inverter DC-link is a proven mechanism, no specific programme named.
ideaData.materialGrade: AA1350-H14 aluminium busbar body; C11000 ETP copper cold-roll-bonded (CuAl bimetal) terminal tabs; replaces solid C11000

title: Shared cooling interface: cap and driver on the module cold plate
description: Eliminates two separate thermal-interface systems and their hardware. Baseline gives the DC-link capacitor its own AA6063-T5 heat-sink boss and the gate driver a separate thermal pad to housing, while the SiC power module has its dedicated cold plate — three independent thermal interfaces. Proposal: mount the film capacitor baseplate and the driver board's power-loss components onto extended lands of a single HPDC AlSi10Mg (or machined 6061-T6) cold plate with routed coolant, using a screen-printed alumina/silicone gap-filler (~3 W/m·K, 0.3–0.5 mm) at each land. Physics: the capacitor's dominant loss is ohmic in schoopage/leads (~few W), within the plate's thermal budget once SiC losses drop; consolidating the sink deletes two conduction paths plus fasteners/pads and stabilises capacitor core temperature to extend film life (Arrhenius: ~10°C cooler roughly doubles life).

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Eliminates two separate thermal-interface systems and their hardware.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: Cap sink boss €5 + driver pad €2 + fasteners/labour €2 = €9 × realisation 0.9 × 300,000

ideaData.riskNotes: Coolant-fault case: if module drives cold plate hot, cap now sees that heat — validate worst-case coolant-loss derating so cap core stays <105°C. Gap-filler pump-out under vibration/TC; use cure-in-place material and validate to ISO 16750. Ground-loop/EMC of shared conductive plate to be checked.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Consolidated single-cold-plate thermal architecture is established practice in integrated 3-in-1 inverters; co-cooling of cap+driver is a proven design move, no programme named.
ideaData.materialGrade: HPDC AlSi10Mg or machined 6061-T6 cold plate; ~3 W/m·K screen-printed silicone/alumina gap filler

title: Metallised-PP film step-change downsizes DC-link capacitor 20%
description: Higher energy density shrinks film, can, and mounting. Baseline DC-link uses standard 3.0 µm metallised biaxially-oriented polypropylene (BOPP) film sized conservatively for ripple current and hot-spot at 105°C. Proposal: adopt high-crystallinity high-temperature BOPP at reduced 2.5 µm thickness with graded heavy-edge segmented Zn/Al metallisation (self-healing, higher segment count, ~2–4 Ω/sq active field, thick edge schoop). Physics: thinner film raises volumetric capacitance density (C ∝ 1/d) so the same µF fits ~20% less winding volume/mass; segmentation contains fault energy so the working field can rise from ~200 to ~230 V/µm without life penalty, and the heavy-edge schoop lowers ESR/self-heating to hold the smaller can within limits. Enables a smaller can, less PP, less Zn/Al, and a shorter busbar.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Higher energy density shrinks film, can, and mounting.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: Cap BOM ~€100, 18% average saving × realisation 0.85 × 300,000

ideaData.riskNotes: Thinner film lowers dielectric-withstand margin — validate corona/PD at 1.5×Vdc and full life at 105°C per IEC 61071. Heavy-edge schoopage adhesion and ripple-current hot-spot mapping needed. Confirm humidity-robustness (flat-metallisation corrosion) at 85/85.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Segmented heavy-edge thin BOPP is established state-of-the-art in automotive DC-link caps (product families from TDK/EPCOS, Vishay, Kemet); a proven material lever, no vehicle programme named.
ideaData.materialGrade: 2.5 µm high-temperature high-crystallinity BOPP film; segmented heavy-edge Zn/Al metallisation (replaces 3.0 µm plain-metallised BOPP)

title: Double-sided cooled power module deletes second cold plate
description: SiC die is the dominant module cost; a 25% die-area cut is the single largest lever on the power stage. Baseline is a single-sided pin-fin SiC module (die on AlN/Al2O3 DBC over a pin-fin baseplate) where the die top is cooled only by mold compound — one-way heat flow forces a large baseplate and derated die count. Net die-attach stations +1, wire-bond -1. Coolant manifold becomes double-sided, minor jig capex. Cycle time roughly flat; scrap risk from post co-planarity.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: SiC die is the dominant module cost; a 25% die-area cut is the single largest lever on the power stage.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~€180 die content/inverter × 0.25 reduction × 200,000, offset by ~€8/unit added assembly = net ~€37/unit × 200k

CTE mismatch between AMB and Cu posts under -40/150°C power cycling requires AQG324 2000-cycle validation. Mitigate with matched-CTE spacer and thicker sinter bondline.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Double-sided cooled traction modules are established practice (e.g. Denso/Toyota double-sided IGBT module lineage from ~2008 Camry Hybrid, extended to SiC on later BEVs); exact programme for this SiC spec not confirmed.
ideaData.materialGrade: Si3N4 AMB substrates, Cu spacer posts, Ag sinter (double-sided); 4.6×4.6 mm SiC MOSFET die (replaces single-sided AlN/Al2O3 DBC pin-fin module)

title: Ceramic-substrate DC-link snubber replaces bulk film headroom
description: Film dielectric and copper-Zn end-spray are the film cap's cost drivers; volume reduction directly cuts both. Baseline sizes the metallised-PP DC-link cap partly to absorb HF ringing and turn-off overvoltage from parasitic loop inductance (~15–20 nH), forcing extra µF and voltage derating. Proposal: add a low-ESL ceramic snubber array — multiple 100 nF 1000 V C0G/NP0 (or X7R for energy) MLCCs, ideally reverse-geometry/low-inductance terminations — mounted directly across each half-bridge DC terminal on the module, cutting effective loop inductance to <5 nH. Snubber must be validated for resonance with bulk cap (avoid new LC ring) via double-pulse test across temperature. Ripple re-rating needs thermal soak on downsized film.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Local ceramic snubbing of half-bridges is established power-electronics practice; specific inverter programme not named.
ideaData.materialGrade: 100 nF 1000 V C0G/NP0 and X7R MLCC snubber array (low-inductance/reverse-geometry terminations); metallised-PP bulk film retained

title: Fan-out wafer-level packaged gate driver co-located on module
description: Removes a whole PCB subassembly, its test, and a connector warranty risk from the gate loop. Baseline gate driver is a discrete FR-4 PCB with isolated gate-driver ICs, DC-DC isolation, and a ribbon/flex link to the module gate pads — the link adds gate-loop inductance and a connector. Proposal: use a fan-out wafer-level package (eWLB/RDL, Cu redistribution ~2–5 µm) integrating driver die, digital isolator, and passives, bonded directly onto the module's signal substrate (AMB/DBC) over the gate pads. Removes the driver PCB, board-to-module connector, and shortens the gate loop below 10 nH, allowing a smaller external gate resistor and faster, lower-loss switching. Physics: shorter, tighter gate loop reduces ringing and Miller-induced turn-on cross-talk, improving switching robustness while eliminating a rigid-flex assembly and its connector reliability failure mode.

Isolation creepage/clearance on RDL must meet reinforced-isolation (VDE 0884-11); requires partial-discharge testing. Thermal proximity to power stage raises driver junction temp — validate 150°C-capable driver die.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: FOWLP is mature in RF/PMIC (established since ~2010s); co-located gate drive on module substrate is an emerging but real practice in traction power stages, no programme named.
ideaData.materialGrade: eWLB/RDL fan-out wafer-level package (Cu RDL) mounted on AMB/DBC signal substrate (replaces FR-4 driver PCB with flex link)

title: Coolant-agnostic module reuses ICE plant WCAC braze line
description: Amortised high-volume braze line beats dedicated CNC on both piece price and capex. Baseline direct-cooled inverter cold plates are CNC-machined or roll-bonded aluminium with pin-fins, run on a dedicated line. Proposal: fabricate the module cooling interface as a controlled-atmosphere-brazed (CAB) folded-fin core in AA3003-clad AA4045, i.e. the exact stack-up and NOCOLOK flux line used for ICE water-cooled charge-air coolers and radiators. Louvered/offset-strip fins in the coolant channel deliver higher heat-transfer coefficient per unit pressure drop than pin-fins for the same footprint, and CAB tooling and furnaces are already amortised at high volume in incumbent thermal-systems plants. Physics: offset-strip fins periodically restart the thermal boundary layer, raising Nusselt number ~30% versus straight pin-fins at equal pumping power, allowing thinner die or lower coolant flow.

Flux residue must be cleaned to avoid coolant contamination and galvanic issues with the WEG coolant. Validate fin-core burst pressure to 3x system pressure and 150k-cycle thermal fatigue.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: CAB brazing of louvered/offset-fin cores is decades-established in automotive HVAC/radiator manufacturing; applying to inverter cold plate is the transfer.

title: Press-fit PCB pins replace soldered module-to-driver joints
description: Removes a solder process and its dominant signal-joint warranty failure mode. Baseline connects module signal pins to the gate-driver PCB by wave/selective soldering (SAC305), requiring flux, a solder cell, and a solder-joint fatigue regime under thermal cycling. Proposal: switch to compliant press-fit (eye-of-the-needle) pins pressed into plated-through holes (Cu barrel with Ni/Au or Sn finish, ~0.05–0.10 mm interference) on the driver PCB — a solderless gas-tight cold-weld interconnect. Deletes the selective-solder cell and flux-cleaning, and gives superior thermal-cycle fatigue life because the compliant zone absorbs CTE strain rather than a rigid solder fillet. Physics: the pin's elastic deformation maintains gas-tight metal-to-metal contact under -40/125°C cycling, eliminating solder-fatigue crack initiation that dominates soldered signal-pin warranty returns.

ideaData.riskNotes: PTH plating thickness and hole tolerance must be controlled (±25µm) or insertion force/gas-tightness drifts — SPC on plating and 100% press-force monitoring required. Repeated re-insertion degrades the joint; limit to single insert or spec re-work pins. Validate per IEC 60352-5 gas-tight and current-cycling.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Press-fit is established automotive practice for ECU and power-electronics interconnect (widely used since the 2010s); specific inverter programme not named.
ideaData.materialGrade: Compliant eye-of-the-needle press-fit pins (CuSn/CuNiSi bronze, Sn or Ni/Au finish) into Cu plated-through holes; replaces SAC305 selective solder

title: Shunt-in-busbar current sensing deletes discrete phase sensors
description: Replaces three calibrated sensor modules with weld segments and one IC per phase. Baseline measures phase current with three discrete Hall/fluxgate sensor modules clamped around each output busbar — parts, brackets, calibration, and stray-field error. Proposal: integrate a low-TCR manganin (Cu86/Mn12/Ni2, ~±15 ppm/°C, ~0.43 µΩ·m) shunt segment, typically 50–200 µΩ, laser-welded (or friction-welded) inline into each phase busbar, sensed by an isolated delta-sigma modulator on the driver PCB. The busbar becomes the sensing element, deleting three sensor modules and brackets. Physics: manganin's near-zero TCR keeps the mV/A transfer stable across the inverter thermal range, while inline placement removes air-gap and external-field sensitivity that forces Hall calibration; isolation moves to the low-cost modulator already required for gate isolation.
