ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Deletes three sensor sub-modules, brackets, and their fixture/calibration station; adds a manganin-to-copper laser-weld joint (2 welds per phase) into the busbar stamping line and a modulator SMT placement. Net BOM lines down; busbar becomes a slightly higher-value part.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Replaces three calibrated sensor modules with weld segments and one IC per phase.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: 3 × ~€6 Hall modules + brackets + calib ~€22/unit → ~€8/unit shunt+modulator, ~€14 net × 200,000

ideaData.riskNotes: Manganin-Cu dissimilar-metal weld must be validated for fatigue and IR drop stability; Seebeck thermo-EMF at the junction can offset µV-level reading — mitigate with symmetric Kelvin sense taps. Self-heating of shunt must be modelled to keep <5°C rise at peak phase current. Functional-safety ASIL-rated modulator required.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Inline manganin shunts with isolated sigma-delta sensing are established practice in industrial and automotive inverters; specific programme not named.
ideaData.materialGrade: Manganin (Cu86/Mn12/Ni2) shunt segment, ~50–200 µΩ, laser-welded into Cu phase busbar; isolated delta-sigma modulator sensing

title: Cure-in-place foam gasket replaces moulded EMC/coolant seal
description: Removes two seal SKUs, kitting logistics, and misload scrap; relaxes a housing machining tolerance. Baseline seals the housing lid and coolant-manifold interface with pre-formed moulded silicone gaskets plus a separate conductive EMC gasket, each a bought part needing inventory, placement, and precise groove machining. Proposal: robot-dispense a formed-in-place foam gasket (FIPFG) — a two-component polyurethane or silicone foam bead (~50% closed-cell, ~25% compression set, Shore 00) — directly onto the flange, and for the EMC path a dispensed Ag- or Ni/graphite-filled silicone conductive elastomer bead (<0.1 Ω·cm volume resistivity) on the shielded seam. The foam fills flange tolerance variation, relaxing flange flatness spec and eliminating two SKUs. Physics: closed-cell foam's low compression set and high compressibility accommodate ±0.4 mm flange gap variation a solid moulded gasket c

Allows relaxing housing-flange flatness tolerance, reducing CNC pass on the housing. In-line, cycle-matched dispensing avoids gasket-placement misload defects.

Conductive bead must meet shielding-effectiveness (>40dB) after 1000h humidity — validate resistance stability of filled elastomer. IP67 leak-down test retained 100%.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: FIPFG gasketing is established practice for automotive ECU/housing sealing (widely used); dispensed conductive EMC bead is likewise established, no programme named.
ideaData.materialGrade: Two-component PUR or silicone FIPFG foam (closed-cell, low compression set); Ag- or Ni/graphite-filled silicone conductive EMC bead (replaces moulded silicone + discrete EMC gasket)

title: Structural adhesive cell-to-tray bonding deletes carrier frames
description: Removes carrier aluminium and one join operation while adding structural stiffness that offsets tray gauge. Baseline CTP packs seat cells into stamped EN AW-5754-H22 cell-carrier trays with mechanical retention plus FIPG, then bolt the carrier to the pack floor — two joining ops and ~2.8 kg/pack of Al carrier. Proposal bonds prismatic LFP cells directly to an HPDC AlSi10MnMg (Aural/Silafont-type, ~T7) tray floor using a two-component crash-durable epoxy (tensile shear ~25 MPa, T-peel >6 N/mm, Tg >90°C, e.g. Sika/Henkel structural EV grades) dispensed as a 2.0–3.0 mm bead at ~35 g/cell. The bondline carries shear from lateral crash and inertial loads, letting the cell wall act as a stressed member so the carrier frame is deleted. Physics: bonded cell shear stiffness raises pack lateral bending frequency ~15%, replacing the carrier's structural role, while bead compliance absorbs ±0.4 mm c

Removes ~12 fasteners/pack. Scrap risk shifts to dispense quality, controlled by inline bead-height vision. Net one station deleted, tray tooling amortised over HPDC.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Removes carrier aluminium and one join operation while adding structural stiffness that offsets tray gauge.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~€55/pack carrier+fastener+labour saved less €8/pack adhesive = ~€47 net × 120k = €5.6M; +€2–5M from tray downgauge

ideaData.riskNotes: Bonded cells are non-serviceable — end-of-life recycling and warranty cell swap require thermal/mechanical debonding validated for reversibility. Crash shear durability after 1000h 85°C/85%RH humidity ageing and thermal cycling −40/+85°C must be shown. Mitigate with debond-on-demand expandable epoxy and traceable cure logging.

ideaData.benchmarkReference: Structural cell-bonding in CTP is established practice (e.g. Tesla structural pack, ~2021, and CATL/BYD cell-to-pack architectures); no specific programme claimed for this exact bead spec.

title: Cast-in cooling channel tray floor deletes separate cold plate
description: Eliminates an entire aluminium subassembly and its leak-test/join operations. Baseline stacks a discrete stamped/roll-bond cold plate above an HPDC ADC12 tray, joined with TIM (~0.5 K·cm²/W) and a sealed coolant interface — two Al layers plus a leak-critical joint. Proposal casts a single tray in AlSi9Cu3 (EN AC-46000, T5) with cast-in cooling channels directly under the cell field, so the floor IS the cold plate. Lost-core variant uses a water-soluble Na/K-sulphate salt core (bending strength >8 MPa) forming 6–8 mm serpentine channels at 3 mm cast wall; tube-insert variant over-casts pre-bent EN AW-3003-O tube (Ø8×1 mm). Physics: single conductive path (cell base → 3 mm cast wall → coolant) removes one TIM interface and the cold-plate bondline, improving base cooling ~20% at equal pump duty while collapsing two parts into one.

Adds core-setting or tube-loading pre-op at the HPDC cell and a single pressure-decay leak test on the tray. Cell time +8–12 s for core placement; net one major subassembly deleted.

costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~€70–95/pack (plate material + bond + leak-test + logistics) × 120k, net of +€6/pack casting complexity

Salt-core residue must be fully flushed to avoid corrosion. Tube-insert variant risks tube collapse — validate with pre-form annealing and internal support pressure during casting.
dfmaPrinciples: Reduce interfaces in the thermal path
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Cast-in/integrated-channel cooling in die-cast enclosures is established practice in cell-to-pack architectures (early 2020s); no specific OEM programme claimed for this spec.
ideaData.materialGrade: HPDC AlSi9Cu3 (EN AC-46000) tray, T5; EN AW-3003-O tube insert Ø8×1 mm; water-soluble sulphate salt core

title: Composite SMC pack lid replaces stamped-aluminium lid
description: Lower tooling and part cost for a non-load-critical closure with net-shape features. Baseline lid is a stamped EN AW-5182-O panel (~1.2 mm, ~5.5 kg) with bonded stiffener beads, a peripheral sealing flange, and a separate EMI treatment. Proposal moulds the lid from vinyl-ester glass SMC (~30 wt% E-glass, density ~1.9 g/cm³, flex modulus ~11 GPa, class A optional) with integrally moulded ribs, bosses, and a moulded-in seal groove, plus a co-moulded Ni/Cu-coated conductive nonwoven veil (surface resistivity <0.1 Ω/sq) or sprayed Zn shield for EMI. Physics: rib geometry sets bending stiffness independent of gauge, so a 2.5 mm ribbed SMC panel matches lid stiffness at comparable mass while removing stamping dies, trimming, and flange-bead welding. Moulded bosses net-form fastener/breather interfaces, cutting secondary machining.

ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Replaces multi-die stamp line + weld/bond stiffener station with one compression-mould press (cycle ~90–120 s) and deflash. Adds EMI veil placement. Tooling capex is one SMC tool vs. a die set — lower for the programme volume. Deletes lid weld fixtures.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Lower tooling and part cost for a non-load-critical closure with net-shape features.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~€35–50/lid saved (die amortisation + weld labour + shielding) × 120k

ideaData.riskNotes: SMC must pass pack fire-containment (thermal-runaway flame/particle) and crush-load requirements — vinyl-ester alone may need intumescent filler; validate to GB 38031 / ECE R100 venting and no-flame-penetration criteria. EMI attenuation of conductive veil must meet CISPR 25; verify against aluminium baseline. Mitigate flammability with ATH/intumescent loading.
dfmaPrinciples: Consolidate stiffeners and seal into one moulding
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Composite battery lids/covers for non-structural closures are established practice; no specific programme claimed.
ideaData.materialGrade: Vinyl-ester glass SMC ~30 wt% E-glass; Ni/Cu-coated nonwoven EMI veil or sprayed Zn shield

title: Shared thermal-runaway vent duct commonised across pack sizes
description: Collapses several bespoke vent assemblies into one extruded+capped design across a pack family. Baseline each pack length has a bespoke sheet-metal or moulded gas-venting/exhaust duct routing runaway effluent to a dedicated burst membrane, with size-specific tooling per platform. Proposal defines a single modular extruded EN AW-6060-T6 vent-duct profile (constant cross-section sized for worst-case mass-flow of the largest pack) cut to length per variant, with a common injection-moulded PA6-GF30 end-cap carrying the laser-scored burst membrane and flame arrestor mesh. Physics: runaway vent flow is cross-section-limited, not length-limited, so one profile sized for peak flow serves all lengths; cut-to-length replaces per-variant stamping tools. The common end-cap standardises the pressure-relief threshold and flame-arrest path across the family.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Collapses several bespoke vent assemblies into one extruded+capped design across a pack family.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: €1.5–2.5M tooling avoidance amortised + ~€12/pack part-cost delta × 120k

ideaData.riskNotes: Common duct must satisfy worst-case runaway gas velocity/temperature without back-pressure that impedes venting on the smallest pack (over-sized cross-section is conservative). Burst-membrane threshold and flame-arrest efficacy must be re-validated per GB 38031 propagation and no-external-flame tests for each variant. Mitigate with propagation-tank testing per length.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Family commonisation of vent hardware is established VA/VE practice; no specific programme claimed.
ideaData.materialGrade: EN AW-6060-T6 extrusion, PA6-GF30 end-cap

title: Pack tray doubles as vehicle floor cross-member load path
description: Removes duplicated lateral crash structure across BIW and pack. Baseline the BEV floor has a body cross-member set AND a separately stiffened pack tray with its own internal cross-beams — duplicated lateral crash structure. Proposal deletes the body floor cross-members in the pack footprint and upgrades the pack tray internal beams to extruded EN AW-6082-T6 multi-cavity crossbeams (wall 2.0–2.5 mm) FSW-welded to the tray frame, sized to carry the full IIHS/ECE side-pole intrusion load. Physics: two parallel lateral load paths are redundant; consolidating into the tray beams (which sit lower and closer to the sill load introduction) improves crash efficiency per kg and lets the body-in-white delete stampings and spot-weld flanges. The pack becomes a structural floor element.

ideaData.manufacturingImpact: In BIW: deletes 2–4 cross-member stampings and ~40 spot welds per body. In pack: upgrades extrusion section and adds FSW passes. Net shifts content from BIW line to pack line; overall stamping tools and weld robots reduced. Requires joint crash co-development.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Removes duplicated lateral crash structure across BIW and pack.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~€45–70/vehicle (BIW stampings + welds) + tooling avoidance, net of +€15/pack extrusion upgrade, × 120k

ideaData.riskNotes: Cross-domain crash responsibility: side-pole intrusion, sill load transfer, and post-crash pack integrity (no cell breach) must be co-validated by CAE + physical crash. Serviceability of a structural pack and repair strategy after minor impact must be defined. Mitigate with sacrificial sill deformation zones and defined repair boundaries.
dfmaPrinciples: Combine body and pack structural functions
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Cell-to-body / structural-pack floor integration is established (e.g. BYD CTB, Tesla structural pack) — this idea targets cross-member deletion specifically, distinct from lid-as-floor.
ideaData.materialGrade: EN AW-6082-T6 multi-cavity extrusion (FSW)

title: Integrated moulded frunk/tray underbody skidplate consolidation
description: Consolidates shield, spacers, and isolation hardware into one moulded panel. Baseline carries a separate steel (DC01) or Al (EN AW-5754) ballistic/skid shield bolted below the tray via ~20 fasteners plus spacers, protecting against road-debris per GB 38031 bottom-ball-drop. Proposal integrates the impact function into a single glass/basalt-reinforced polyurethane panel (LFI or RTM, ~40 wt% fibre, areal ~4 kg/m²) co-fastened at the tray seal flange, replacing both the discrete metal shield and its standoff hardware. Physics: fibre-reinforced PU absorbs point-impact energy by local delamination/matrix crushing rather than plastic denting, giving equal debris-penetration resistance at lower mass and removing galvanic-isolation washers needed between a steel shield and Al tray. One panel replaces shield + spacers + isolation stack.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Consolidates shield, spacers, and isolation hardware into one moulded panel.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~€25–40/pack (shield + fasteners + isolation + labour) net of +€10/pack moulded panel, × 120k

Long-term UV and gravel erosion of the polymer face needs a hard gelcoat or sacrificial layer. Validate to bottom-impact per GB 38031 and OEM off-road load cases; mitigate with basalt hybrid layer at impact zones.

ideaData.materialGrade: Glass- or basalt-reinforced polyurethane (LFI/RTM, ~40 wt% fibre, ~4 kg/m²)

title: Snap-fit cell-tab pre-alignment frame cuts busbar weld scrap
description: Reduces busbar weld scrap/rework and consolidates the isolation carrier while raising throughput. Baseline in CTP assembly locates cell tabs only by tray tolerance stack before laser busbar welding, so tab-to-busbar gap varies ±0.6 mm, forcing conservative parameters, higher spatter, and ~1.5% weld reject/rework. Proposal adds a thin injection-moulded PA66-GF35 (UL94 V-0, CTI >600 V) tab-alignment comb that snaps over the cell field and net-locates each tab to ±0.15 mm before welding, then remains as the busbar isolation carrier. Physics: laser lap/fillet weld quality is dominated by joint gap (>0.2 mm collapses fusion, causes blow-through); tightening the gap lets the process run faster at lower power margin, cutting spatter-driven scrap and enabling remote galvo welding at higher speed. The frame doubles as busbar holder and creepage barrier, deleting a separate isolation part.

costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: 1.5%→0.4% weld reject on ~€1,200 WIP + 20% weld throughput gain + isolation-part deletion (~€6/pack) × 120k

title: Anodised tray floor as busbar dielectric deletes laminate isolator
description: Removes a purchased laminate part and a manual assembly step with associated scrap. Baseline CTP packs isolate the HV busbar array from an EN AW-3003 or 6xxx tray floor with a discrete FR-rated PET/PEN laminate (~0.3 mm) plus adhesive, hand-laid across the tray. Proposal: hard-anodise (Type III, MIL-A-8625) the busbar-contact zones of a 6082-T6 tray floor to a 40–60 µm Al2O3 dielectric (breakdown ~15–25 kV, >800 V/mil), then route flat rolled-Cu (C11000) or EN AW-1350 busbars directly onto the anodised surface with a thin epoxy overcoat for creepage. The anodic oxide is integral, abrasion-resistant, and thermally couples the busbar to the tray for passive spreading. Local masking confines the layer to functional zones, avoiding full-tank cost. Physics: the grown oxide replaces an assembled part and its air-gap tolerance stack, deleting a manual lay-up station and its rework scrap.

title: Cell-integrated pouch tab foil laser-welded straight to tray busbar
description: Halves interconnect joint count and deletes an entire busbar part. Baseline pouch packs weld cell tabs to a module busbar, then bolt/weld module busbars to a pack distribution plate — two joint generations. Proposal (assembly level): with cells fixtured directly in the tray (CTP), laser-weld the Al (EN AW-1050A cathode) and nickel-plated Cu (C11000) pouch tabs in a single pass to a stamped hybrid pack busbar frame pre-located to the tray, deleting the intermediate module busbar. Use remote galvo welding with clamping combs holding the ~0.2 mm tab stack, gap <0.1 mm to limit porosity. Physics: each eliminated joint removes ~30–50 µΩ contact resistance and a fatigue initiation site; single-generation joining halves weld count and removes the module busbar as a part.

Vibration durability (ISO 16750) of direct tab-to-frame joints without module compliance must be validated; add local strain relief loop in tab.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Remote laser tab welding and CTP joint-generation reduction are established practice; not attributed to a specific named programme.
ideaData.materialGrade: EN AW-1050A (Al tab), nickel-plated C11000 (Cu tab), stamped Al/Cu hybrid busbar frame

title: Reusable expandable-bladder cell clamp replaces foam-in-place stack pressure
description: Converts per-pack consumable foam into one-time tooling plus a cheap spring part. Baseline prismatic CTP packs maintain cell stack preload against swelling with foam-in-place PU compression pads or fixed elastomer buffers between cells — consumable material added to every pack and cured in-line. Proposal: integrate two full-length reusable inflatable stainless/silicone bladders along the stack ends that are pressurised to a controlled ~1.0-1.5 bar during pack close, then vented, with the residual set carried by simple sprung endplates and a thin EPDM spacer only at cell faces. The bladder is tooling, not BOM. Physics: swelling force (up to ~0.3 MPa over life) is reacted by the sprung endplate travel curve rather than by compressing a per-pack foam block, so the expensive per-unit compliant material is largely removed and replaced with a designed spring rate.

costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~€15–26/pack foam + cure labour/energy saved, less ~€2/pack spring endplate amortised × 100k

Validate cell face pressure map at BOL/EOL, and confirm no localized over-pressure causing separator damage. Bladder maintenance/leak-down interval to be qualified.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Reusable inflatable clamping fixtures are established assembly practice; sprung-endplate swelling management is standard cell-mechanics engineering.

title: Aerogel-mica hybrid runaway barrier replaces full-coverage mica plates
description: Applies the most expensive barrier only where the plume actually travels. Baseline interposes continuous muscovite/phlogopite mica sheets (1.0–1.5 mm) between every cell and under the lid for runaway-propagation resistance — expensive material applied everywhere. Proposal (pack level): zone the protection using a thin (2–3 mm) silica-aerogel-reinforced mica hybrid mat (~0.018–0.022 W/m·K, rated to ~1000 °C) only in the direct vent-plume path and cell-to-cell interfaces, while non-plume structural gaps use lower-cost intumescent-coated E-glass mat. Aerogel's low conductivity lets a 2–3 mm layer match thicker mica's propagation delay precisely where the flame front travels. Physics: propagation is dominated by radiant/convective plume energy along defined channels; matching insulation R-value to the actual thermal load path removes over-specification of the whole cavity.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Applies the most expensive barrier only where the plume actually travels.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~€22–30 mica saved less ~€6 aerogel/intumescent added = ~€16–27/pack × 150k

ideaData.riskNotes: Must prove single-cell-to-pack no-propagation per GB 38031 / UN GTR 20 with the zoned scheme, not just full coverage — burden of proof is high. Validate with instrumented thermal-runaway trigger tests (nail/heater) mapping actual plume path; conservative margin on aerogel thickness. Aerogel dusting/handling controls needed.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Silica aerogel and mica runaway barriers are established EV materials; zoning to plume path is an engineering optimisation, no named programme cited.
ideaData.materialGrade: Silica-aerogel-reinforced mica mat (~0.018–0.022 W/m·K); intumescent-coated E-glass mat; muscovite/phlogopite mica

title: Pack lid as EMC shield deletes separate copper-mesh screen
description: Reuses the structural lid metal as the shield instead of adding a screen. Baseline packs with SMC/composite or plastic lids add a discrete copper/aluminium EMC shielding layer (foil, mesh, or conductive coating) plus grounding tabs to contain HV switching noise and meet CISPR 25/ECE R10. Proposal: specify the lid as a die-cast or stamped EN AW-5754 / GJS aluminium lid whose inherent conductivity forms the Faraday enclosure, using stitched conductive-gasket flange sealing (EN AW alloy + form-in-place conductive EPDM) so the metal lid itself is the shield — deleting the separate screen and its grounding hardware. Physics: an aluminium wall >0.5 mm gives >60 dB shielding effectiveness above 1 MHz; the limiting factor is seam/aperture leakage, solved by continuous conductive gasket rather than an added internal mesh.

costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~€10–18/pack (shield material + grounding + step) less ~€2 gasket delta × 100k

Conductive gasket must survive salt-spray galvanic corrosion at Al-steel interfaces — use compatible plating and drainage. Requires early EMC co-design.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Metal enclosures as intrinsic EMC shields with conductive gaskets are established EMC practice across power electronics housings.

title: Injected 2K structural foam bonds and seals lid in one shot
description: Collapses seal, bond and fastening into one dispensed bead. Baseline lid sealing uses a cured RTV/PU bead plus ~80–120 M6 fasteners into rivnuts around the flange, with a separate structural adhesive if the lid is load-bearing — three functions, three materials, one long torque cycle. Proposal: robotically apply a single 2K polyurethane structural-foam bead (~40–50 MPa lap shear, expansion factor ~2–3× to fill flange tolerance) to the flange; it seals (IP67), bonds, and stiffens simultaneously, cutting fasteners to ~12 service/handling bolts. Physics: expanding 2K PU tolerates 0.5–2 mm flange gap variation without pre-machining, and its shear strength lets the bonded flange carry lid shear so most mechanical fasteners become redundant; adhesive shear over the full perimeter beats point-loaded bolts for stiffness.

costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~€16–28/pack (fasteners €0.15×~90 + insertion labour + separate sealant) less ~€4 PU × 130k

Validate IP67, thermal-cycle bond durability, and crash/rollover lid retention (FMVSS 305) via structural test. Cure time must fit takt; heat-accelerate if needed.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: 2K PU structural bonding-and-sealing of enclosures is established BIW/battery-closure practice; not attributed to a named programme.
ideaData.materialGrade: 2K polyurethane structural foam, ~40–50 MPa lap shear, IP67 seal

title: Flat-flex wiring harness laminated into tray deletes round-wire BMS loom
description: Replaces hundreds of crimped sense wires with a single printed circuit placement. Baseline CTP voltage/temperature sense wiring uses a round-wire BMS harness with hundreds of crimped terminals routed and clipped across the pack, plus separate module control boards. Proposal (assembly level): replace the sense loom with a single die-cut FPC/FFC (rolled-Cu ~35–70 µm on ~50 µm polyimide, with NTC sense pads) laminated to a carrier and dropped onto the busbar frame in one placement, contacted by laser-weld or pierce terminals at each sense point. Physics: the FPC carries many parallel low-current sense lines at a fraction of the mass and eliminates hundreds of crimps (each a failure/labour point); planar routing removes clipping and abrasion tape. One placement replaces manual loom lay-in.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Replaces hundreds of crimped sense wires with a single printed circuit placement.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~€30–48/pack (harness build + crimps + clipping labour) less ~€8 FPC × 130k

ideaData.riskNotes: FPC contact reliability under vibration and thermal cycling must be validated (contact resistance drift, ISO 16750); polyimide flame rating and dielectric spacing to HV busbars per creepage rules. Repair strategy: FPC damage means larger replacement — mitigate with zoned FPC segments and connectorised joints.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: FPC/CCS busbar-and-sense assemblies are established practice in modern cell-to-pack designs (early 2020s); stated as technology, no specific programme named.
ideaData.materialGrade: Rolled-Cu ~35–70 µm on ~50 µm polyimide FPC (cell-contact system)

title: Steel spring-strap compression replacing bolted endplate tie-rods
description: Removes fasteners, torque station, and endplate mass simultaneously Baseline module uses two HPDC AlSi10Mg endplates joined by 4× M6 grade-8.8 steel tie-rods torqued to ~10 Nm holding ~4–6 kN preload against cell swelling. Replace the tie-rod/endplate corners with a single wrap-around spring strap of 1.4310 (301) austenitic stainless, 0.5–0.8 mm, cold-worked/hardened to ~1300 MPa, stamped and roll-formed into a closed loop around the cell stack, delivering constant force via its own spring rate. The long free length flattens the force-deflection curve so end-of-life swelling (~2–3% graphite-cell growth) raises preload only ~15% versus ~200% for rigid tie-rods — eliminating endplate over-design. Removes 8 threaded fasteners, 2 machined boss faces per module, and the torque-verification station.

Endplates thin from ~8 mm to ~4 mm cast wall, cutting HPDC shot weight and cycle. Net one station removed per module line; modest tooling capex for progressive die.

costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~€0.90/module fastener+labour + €0.30/module Al mass saved × 10 modules × 200k packs = ~€2.4M; upper bound adds endplate cycle-time savings

ideaData.riskNotes: Risk: strap relaxation and creep over 15-yr life shifting preload out of the 4-8 kN cell spec, plus corrosion of spring steel in condensing pack humidity. Mitigate with zinc-nickel or cataphoretic coating, stress-relief temper, and force-decay validation via 1000-cycle mechanical swell fixture + 85/85 damp-heat per module DV plan.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Spring-strap/banding compression is established practice in cylindrical and prismatic modules; the constant-force spring mechanism is not tied to a single named programme.
ideaData.materialGrade: 1.4310 (AISI 301) spring stainless, 0.5–0.8 mm, ~1300 MPa; HPDC AlSi10Mg endplates (baseline)

title: Structural-foam potting replaces mechanical cell retention frame
description: Collapses multiple moulded parts and manual assembly into one dispense Baseline prismatic module carries cells in an injection-moulded PA6-GF30 cell-holder frame plus PP top/bottom trays, adding ~250-400 g of non-functional plastic and a multi-part assembly. Replace the frame with a dispensed 2K rigid polyurethane structural foam (isocyanate/polyol, free-rise density 300-500 kg/m3, e.g. Sika SikaForce or Henkel Loctite PUR FIP systems) injected into inter-cell and perimeter gaps after cells are jigged, bonding cells into a self-supporting monolith with lap-shear >2 MPa (ISO 4587) and compressive strength >4 MPa. Foam gel time 60-120 s at 40-60 C tool temperature. It provides retention, damping (first bending mode >200 Hz), and inter-cell runaway insulation (thermal conductivity <0.08 W/mK). Eliminates frame tooling and manual cell insertion.

costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~€1.50-2.25/module part+labour saved net of foam cost × 10 modules × 200k = €3.0-4.5M

Mitigate with adhesion-promoter cell-can pretreatment, designed venting channels moulded into foam, and lap-shear ageing tests across -40 to +85°C thermal shock.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Foam-in-place cell fixation with dispensed 2K PUR is established practice in high-volume EV module assembly; specific mechanism proven, no named programme claimed.
ideaData.materialGrade: 2K rigid PUR structural foam, 300-500 kg/m3 free-rise density (e.g. SikaForce / Loctite PUR FIP); replaces PA6-GF30 frame

title: Embossed-channel cooling plate integrated as module base
description: Combines cold plate and module base into one commodity-formed part Baseline module sits on a separate extruded AlSi (EN AW-6060/6063) cooling plate with a discrete gap-filler pad, plus its own AlMg3 (EN AW-5754) sheet base — two aluminium parts plus interface. Replace both with a single roll-bond plate (two EN AW-3003 or 1050A sheets, 1.5-2.0 mm each) whose inflated channels double as the module structural base. Roll-bond prints a graphite anti-bond pattern between sheets, hot-rolls at ~480-520 C to metallurgical bond, then inflates channels to 2-3 mm at 100-150 bar. This yields near-arbitrary serpentine geometry at a fraction of extrusion+CNC cost, with weld-land walls as thin as 1.5 mm. The plate carries cell load directly, deleting the separate module base and one aluminium part per module.

ideaData.benchmarkReference: Roll-bond aluminium cold plates are established practice for EV battery thermal management; mechanism proven, no named programme claimed.
ideaData.materialGrade: EN AW-3003 (optionally 1050A) roll-bond two-sheet, 1.5-2.0 mm per skin; replaces EN AW-6060/6063 extrusion + EN AW-5754 base

title: Aluminium busbar with laser-cleaned copper transition inlay
description: Substitutes low-cost aluminium for the majority of interconnect copper Baseline interconnect busbars are solid C11000 ETP copper (8.9 g/cm3, ~EUR 8-9/kg) laser-welded to aluminium cell terminals via an inserted bimetal transition — copper mass drives cost. Replace the bulk body with EN AW-1050A (99.5% Al, O/H14 temper) sized for equal conductance: Al cross-section ~1.6x copper for equal IR drop, but ~1/3 the mass and ~1/8 the EUR/kg. Retain copper only as a small friction-stir-lap-welded or ultrasonic-clad C11000 inlay at sense-taps and copper-terminal cells. Pulsed fibre-laser or IR pre-clean of Al ablates the Al2O3 layer immediately before welding so nugget resistance stays <30 uOhm. Net copper content per module drops ~70%.

Bimetal insert count reduced; ultrasonic clad cell for the few Cu joints. Slight busbar height increase must fit existing envelope.

costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~€1.80-2.70/module copper displaced (0.25 kg Cu × €7 saved net Al) × 10 modules × 200k = €3.6-5.4M

ideaData.riskNotes: Risk: Al busbar creep and galvanic corrosion at Cu-Al interface, plus higher thermal expansion loosening joints. Mitigate with conformal coating over joints, joint-resistance 100% end-of-line testing, and thermal-cycle + current-cycle validation to confirm <10% IR rise at 1000 cycles.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Aluminium busbars with copper bimetal transitions and laser oxide pre-clean for Al weldability are established practice; mechanism proven, no named programme claimed.
ideaData.materialGrade: EN AW-1050A (H14) busbar body; C11000 ETP copper transition inlay only at sense-taps

title: Screen-printed TIM replacing gap-filler dispense under module
description: Cuts TIM mass and dispense scrap while improving thermal path Baseline thermal interface is a 1-3 mm dispensed 2K silicone gap filler (~3 W/mK, e.g. Dow TC-series) applied by meter-mix, consuming 150-250 g/module of a EUR 18-28/kg material with purge waste and thick bondlines to absorb tolerance stack. Replace with a stencil/screen-printed thin (0.3-0.6 mm) filled-silicone or alumina/BN-loaded TIM (>3 W/mK) applied to a flatness-controlled (<=0.15 mm) roll-bond EN AW-3003 base, enabled by tightening cell-to-plate gap tolerance. Halving bondline at equal conductivity roughly halves thermal resistance and material mass; screen printing wastes near-zero material versus dispense purge. For residual tolerance, add a phase-change film (paraffin/graphite matrix, reflow ~50 C) to fill micro-gaps.

Mitigate with 100% base-plate flatness gauging, PCM retention geometry, and thermal-imaging validation of cell ΔT under fast-charge load plus 1000-cycle pump-out test.

ideaData.materialGrade: Screen-printable filled-silicone or alumina/BN TIM >3 W/mK, 0.3-0.6 mm; PCM film (paraffin/expanded-graphite) reflow ~50 C

title: Frameless stacked-module using shared pack-wall compression
description: Eliminates duplicated module walls by reusing pack structure Baseline each module is a self-contained box (endplates + side walls + base + lid) then bolted into the pack — walls duplicate structure the pack tray already provides. Convert to a frameless 'brick': cells + spring-strap + top interconnect plate only, compressed laterally by the pack tray's own cross-members and side rails at install. Pack cross-beams (already present for side-impact, typically EN AW-6082-T6 extrusion or hot-stamped 22MnB5) become the module endplates; a die-cut PP or PET-GF inter-brick divider (0.3-0.5 mm) provides creepage (>=6 mm) and runaway isolation. This deletes the four module side/end walls and base, moving retention load into structure that must exist anyway, cutting module structural parts from ~8 to ~2.

costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~€2.00-3.00/module wall+base parts deleted × 10 modules × 200k = €4.0-6.0M

Mitigate with a returnable shipping cradle, brick-level shunt banding for handling only, and a full tolerance-stack + crush-test on the pack-integrated compression path.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Cell-to-pack frameless brick architecture is established industry direction in high-volume BEV packs (e.g. cell-to-pack designs from ~2020 onward); this shared-wall compression is a design mechanism, no specific programme claimed.
ideaData.materialGrade: PP or PET-GF inter-brick divider 0.3-0.5 mm; reaction structure is existing EN AW-6082-T6 / 22MnB5 pack cross-beams (no new module frame material)

title: Cell-connecting system on FR-1 paper phenolic vs FR-4
description: Right-sizes sensing substrate away from over-specified FR-4 Baseline voltage/temperature sensing uses a flex-PCB or FR-4 glass-epoxy cell-connection board carrying sense traces and fuse links — FR-4 is over-specified for low-current sensing and its glass weave drives cost and CO2-laser routing. Where the CCS carries only sense signals (busbars handle power separately), substitute FR-1 phenolic paper laminate (Tg ~110 C) or a punched flexible flat cable (FFC) with tin-plated copper conductors (35-70 um) laminated in 100 um PET. FR-1 is die-punched not routed (no glass abrasion, faster, cheaper) at ~40% lower cost/dm2 than FR-4; FFC eliminates the rigid board entirely for pure sensing. Fusible links move to discrete stamped Sn-plated C11000 elements laser-welded at each tap.

Removes ENIG/immersion finish steps if OSP-compatible. Lower incoming-material cost and faster board processing.

costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~€0.80-1.30/module board cost delta × 10 modules × 200k = €1.6-2.6M

ideaData.materialGrade: FR-1 phenolic paper laminate or PET-laminated FFC with tin-plated C11000 conductors (35-70 um); stamped Sn-plated C11000 fuse links

title: Wave-spring stack preload replacing foam compression pad
description: Removes a viscoelastic component whose over-specification drives cost and warranty pressure-loss risk. Baseline NMC prismatic modules use a compressed PU foam pad (3-5 mm, 40-60 kPa working stress) between endplate and cell stack to hold 300-500 kPa across the cell's 0.6-1.2% swelling range and calendar growth. Foam force decays ~30% over life (compression set per ISO 1856) and its non-linear stiffness makes end-of-life pressure uncertain. Replace with 2-3 stacked oil-tempered SiCr wave springs (DIN EN 10270-2, grade VDSiCr) captured in a machined pocket in a GJS-450-10 nodular-iron or HPDC AlSi10Mn(Fe) endplate. Near-constant spring rate over ~2 mm working travel holds stack pressure within +/-15% for life, with the spring flat sized to the design band — a deterministic, testable force replacing a viscoelastic foam whose relaxation must be over-specified.

Springs are catalogue-drawn, no module-specific tooling. Cycle time neutral; scrap from foam mis-place eliminated. Slight endplate machining for spring pocket.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Removes a viscoelastic component whose over-specification drives cost and warranty pressure-loss risk.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: Foam pad + adhesive ~€2.10/module vs wave-spring set ~€0.70; €1.40 × 200k = €280k material, plus 2 deleted stations amortised + warranty avoidance ~€1.0M.

ideaData.benchmarkReference: Wave-spring preload is established practice in bearing and clutch assemblies; applied to cell-stack compression as a foam substitute, mechanism proven, no named programme claimed.
ideaData.materialGrade: Oil-tempered SiCr wave spring, DIN EN 10270-2 VDSiCr; endplate GJS-450-10 or HPDC AlSi10Mn(Fe)

title: Fixtured cold-plate co-cure of TIM eliminating gap-fill dispense
description: Replaces high-volume dispensed filler with a thin controlled film, cutting the most expensive thermal consumable. Baseline modules bond to the pack cold plate via a dispensed 2K thermally conductive gap filler (2-3.5 W/mK, 2-4 mm bondline) applied wet at pack assembly; bondline varies with module flatness stack (+/-0.8 mm), forcing extra volume — often the most expensive pack consumable at EUR 4-9/module. Instead pre-apply a phase-change TIM film (paraffin/expanded-graphite matrix, ~3 W/mK, 0.25-0.5 mm) to the module base at the module line, protected by release liner, and reflow at first thermal cycle. The thin controlled bondline cuts material volume ~70% and removes the pack-line dispense robot. PCM wets only >45 C so handling is dry and clean; module base flatness is controlled at subassembly by machining or coining to +/-0.15 mm so the thin film suffices.

Reduces rework (no cure-in-place voids). Modest capex for laminator vs 6-figure dispense robot saved.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Replaces high-volume dispensed filler with a thin controlled film, cutting the most expensive thermal consumable.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: Gap filler €6.50/module vs PCM film €2.10 = €4.40 × 200k = €880k material; dispense robot + mixer waste + cure oven avoidance ~€1.2M/yr.

ideaData.benchmarkReference: Phase-change TIM films are established in power-electronics and CPU cooling; applied at module-base subassembly here, proven mechanism, no named programme claimed.
ideaData.materialGrade: Phase-change TIM film, paraffin/expanded-graphite matrix, ~3 W/mK, 0.25-0.5 mm; module base coined/machined to +/-0.15 mm flatness

title: Ultrasonic-welded aluminium interconnect on cylindrical cell array
description: Removes nickel plating, separate fuse and laser consumables while cutting interconnect resistance. Baseline 21700 cylindrical modules interconnect cells with Al wire bonds (300-400 um) or a nickel-plated steel busbar laser-welded to each terminal — nickel and laser both costly, and steel busbar I2R loss is high (resistivity ~7x Cu). Proposal: single-stroke ultrasonic metal welding of a stamped EN AW-1050A (99.5% Al, 0.3-0.5 mm) busbar directly to the cell can/terminal via a fusible tab that also serves as the fuse element. Ultrasonic welding at ~20 kHz forms solid-state Al-Al bonds below cell-damaging temperature (<80 C at can), avoiding the laser HAZ and spatter, and works on the oxide-bearing Al can without pre-clean because the scrubbing disrupts oxide. The 1050A tab cross-section is tuned (neck ~0.5-1.0 mm2) to open as a fuse at defined overcurrent, deleting a separate fuse component

Deletes nickel plating on busbar and separate cell-fuse. Adds sonotrode wear maintenance. Lower reject rate — weld quality monitored in-process by power/collapse signature.

costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: Ni busbar+fuse €5.80/module vs 1050A ultrasonic-welded fused tab €3.10 = €2.70 × 200k = €540k; laser cell + plating line avoidance ~€2.0M/yr.

ideaData.benchmarkReference: Ultrasonic wire/ribbon bonding and Al busbar ultrasonic welding are established practice in cylindrical-cell module assembly; mechanism proven, no named programme claimed.
ideaData.materialGrade: EN AW-1050A (99.5% Al), 0.3-0.5 mm stamped busbar with fusible neck ~0.5-1.0 mm2

title: Thin-wall roll-formed steel module wrap replacing extruded Al frame
description: Trades expensive Al extrusion for high-strength thin steel with cheaper continuous forming. Baseline prismatic module frame is a machined or extruded EN AW-6063-T6 four-wall shell (~2.5 mm wall) reacting stack compression and providing intrusion protection — extrusion die, cut-to-length, endplate-interface machining. Proposal: replace the two long side walls with a roll-formed DP600 dual-phase steel wrap (0.8-1.0 mm, ~600 MPa UTS, 340-420 MPa yield) closed by a single resistance seam weld, retaining only cast AlSi10Mn endplates for tie-rod/compression reaction. DP600 at 0.9 mm matches the tensile hoop capacity of 2.5 mm 6063-T6 for swelling reaction at ~40% of wall thickness and lower cost/kg. Roll-forming is continuous, near-zero-scrap with cheap tooling versus the per-profile extrusion die and the aluminium price premium. Apply Zn or Zn-Ni coating for galvanic isolation from the Al end

DP600 at 0.9 mm matches the tensile hoop capacity of 2.5 mm 6063-T6 for swelling reaction at ~40% of wall thickness and lower cost/kg. Adds cathodic e-coat/zinc for corrosion. Net capex modest; unit cost falls sharply at volume. Weight up slightly but offset at pack level.

costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: 6063-T6 side walls €14/module vs DP600 roll-form €7.50 = €6.50 × 200k = €1.3M material; extrusion die + CNC avoidance vs roll-form amortisation ~€1.2M/yr.

ideaData.riskNotes: Galvanic corrosion at steel-Al endplate interface — isolate with e-coat + sealant; validate salt-spray per ISO 9227. Confirm DP600 wall meets side-crush and cell-swelling reaction with FEA + physical crush. Dimensional spring-back in roll-form controlled by over-bend calibration.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Roll-formed DP600 structures are established practice in body-in-white (rockers, bumper beams); applied to module side walls here, proven mechanism, no named programme claimed.
ideaData.materialGrade: DP600 dual-phase steel wrap, 0.8-1.0 mm, Zn/Zn-Ni coated; endplates HPDC AlSi10Mn; replaces EN AW-6063-T6 extrusion

title: Adhesive cell stacking eliminating rigid intercell spacers
description: Removes a per-cell moulded part and its place operation, collapsing part count. Baseline prismatic stacks alternate cells with injection-moulded PP or PC-ABS intercell frames (0.5-1.0 mm) providing isolation, swell take-up and alignment — a per-cell part with its own tool and place op. Proposal: bond cells directly with a 0.4-0.8 mm bead of 2K dielectric-filled polyurethane structural adhesive (e.g. Sika SikaPower / Henkel Loctite EA cell-bonding grades, dielectric strength ~1000 V/mm, shear ~8-12 MPa, elongation >100% to absorb ~1% swell), robot-applied in a dot-matrix and cured in-line. The adhesive delivers isolation, compliant gap and stack cohesion so the stack becomes self-supporting, cutting endplate/tie-rod loads. Cell face already carries PET shrink-wrap; adhesive adds compliance and deletes the moulded spacer.

ideaData.materialGrade: 2K PUR structural adhesive (Sika/Henkel cell-bonding grade); PET shrink-wrap cell wrap

title: Mica-composite compression endplate replacing cast metal
description: Merges structural endplate and fire barrier into one moulded part while cutting mass. Baseline endplates are HPDC AlSi10Mn or GJS-450-10 ductile iron (~4-6 mm) reacting stack compression (~15-25 kN tie-rod load) while resisting runaway propagation; aluminium's ~600°C melt limits its barrier value. Proposal: a compression-moulded phenolic-bonded muscovite-mica/E-glass composite endplate (rigid mica board ~3-5 mm, >600-900°C service, high through-plane compressive strength) with moulded-in tie-rod bosses. It carries the compressive reaction in bearing and provides an intrinsic runaway barrier aluminium cannot, deleting a separate mica insulation sheet (e.g. Elmelin/Cogebi rigid mica). Net: structure + fire barrier in one moulded part, saving mass and cost.

costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: Al endplates + mica sheet €11/module vs composite endplates €6.50 = €4.50 × 200k = €900k; casting die + place-op avoidance ~€1.0M/yr.

Confirm dielectric and UN R100 thermal-propagation performance. Moisture uptake of mica composite controlled by resin selection.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Rigid mica composites are established EV thermal-barrier material; compression-moulded structural mica parts are an established composite technique, no specific programme named.
ideaData.materialGrade: Phenolic-bonded muscovite (rigid) mica-board + E-glass, ~3-5 mm (Elmelin/Cogebi class)

title: Snap-fit flex-busbar CSC dropped as single interconnect layer
description: Collapses busbar + CSC + fixture into one self-locating drop-in assembly, cutting labour and SKUs. Baseline sense-and-interconnect uses a rigid stamped busbar set plus a separate FPC/FR-4 cell-supervision (CSC) carrier, aligned, fastened, then laser/wire-welded — multiple parts, place-and-fasten ops and alignment tooling. Proposal: a single integrated CCS carrier laminating sense traces (35µm rolled Cu on 50-75µm polyimide) and 0.3-0.5 mm stamped C11000 (H02) copper busbar segments to a PET/PI film, with pre-formed compliant snap features self-locating over cell terminals — one drop, snap-retained, then all welds in one laser pass through pre-registered windows. Self-location removes the alignment fixture and collapses CSC+busbar into one SKU. Al/Cu terminal welds are now spatially registered, raising first-pass yield.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Collapses busbar + CSC + fixture into one self-locating drop-in assembly, cutting labour and SKUs.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: Separate busbar+CSC+fasteners €9.50 vs integrated flex-busbar €6.80 = €2.70 × 200k = €540k; alignment fixture + place-op + rework avoidance ~€1.5M/yr.

ideaData.riskNotes: Flex-to-terminal weld through-window registration must hold across thermal expansion — validate weld pull strength and CTE mismatch fatigue. Snap-feature retention force under vibration validated per ISO 12405. Repairability defined for single-cell replacement.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Integrated flex-busbar cell-connecting systems (CCS assemblies) are established production practice; snap-fit self-location is proven, no specific programme named.
ideaData.materialGrade: C11000 H02 copper busbar 0.3-0.5 mm; 35µm rolled Cu on 50-75µm polyimide FPC; PET/PI carrier

title: LiFePO4 aqueous CMC/SBR cathode binder replaces PVDF/NMP
description: Eliminates NMP consumable and recovery energy; PVDF is a fluoropolymer far costlier than CMC/SBR per kg of binder solids. Baseline LFP cathode uses PVDF (Solef 5130/HSV900) in NMP, requiring solvent-recovery condensers and an N2-inerted oven. Proposal: migrate LFP cathodes to a water-based binder — CMC (DS 0.7-0.9, ~1-2 wt%) as rheology modifier plus SBR latex to ~1.5-2.0 wt% total, already standard on graphite anodes. LFP tolerates aqueous processing far better than Ni-rich NMC; a phosphoric-acid pH buffer (target slurry pH ~7.5-9) plus carbon-coated LFP particles suppress Al collector corrosion in the wet window. This deletes the NMP recovery loop and lets anode/cathode share one water-based mixing/coating line. Peel strength held >15 N/m via the SBR fibrillar network; drying duty falls as NMP recovery load is removed.

Coating cycle time neutral. Removes solvent-handling capex (~€3-5M/line) and NMP make-up consumable. Aluminium foil corrosion control adds an inline pH-buffer dosing station.

ideaData.riskNotes: Risk: residual moisture in LFP electrode causes HF generation and first-cycle gassing; mitigate with -40°C dew-point vacuum bake before winding and Karl-Fischer moisture spec <300 ppm. Al foil pitting during wet window mitigated by phosphate passivation and slurry pot-life limit of 8h. Requires full cell abuse and calendar-life re-validation.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Aqueous CMC/SBR LFP cathode binder is established practice among Chinese LFP cell makers; PVDF/NMP elimination is a documented industry direction, no programme named.
ideaData.materialGrade: CMC (DS 0.7-0.9); SBR latex binder; carbon-coated LiFePO4; 15µm Al (1235/1085) collector

title: Ultrasonic-to-laser tab weld swap on Al/Cu foil stacks
description: Eliminates consumable ultrasonic tooling and reduces cold-weld field returns. Baseline multi-layer tab joint (30-60 layers of 12µm Cu anode / 15µm Al cathode foil to tab) is ultrasonically welded, needing a sonotrode/anvil per format, wearing knurled tooling and marking foil. Proposal: green (515 nm) or blue (450 nm) wobble laser for the Cu stack and single-mode IR fibre laser for Al. Green/blue is absorbed ~40-60% by copper vs ~5% for 1064 nm, killing reflectivity-driven spatter and enabling a stable keyhole into thin stacks. Circular wobble (0.3-0.6 mm amplitude) distributes heat, fuses all layers into a controlled nugget and cuts resistance scatter vs cold-weld. No consumable tooling; one optics head does Cu and Al by recipe. Enables inline back-reflection and OCT seam monitoring to catch cold joints ultrasonic can hide.

ideaData.riskNotes: Risk: over-penetration burns through 12µm foil edge; mitigate with power ramp and wobble tuned to layer count, plus OCT depth control. Copper spatter onto separator risks internal short; enclose and use crossjet. Requires weld pull-strength and milliohm resistance PPAP and HALT.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Green/blue-wavelength laser copper welding for battery tabs is established production practice (green-laser systems from suppliers such as Trumpf and Laserline); no OEM programme named.
ideaData.materialGrade: 12µm C10xx Cu anode foil; 15µm 1235/1085 Al cathode foil; Ni-plated Cu / Al tabs

title: Single-side-coated thick electrode pairs delete one foil pass
description: Cuts copper foil, separator and tab count per kWh — attacks the costliest inactive materials. Baseline stacked prismatic cells use double-side-coated electrodes at ~70µm/side on 15µm Al and 8-12µm Cu. Proposal for energy-optimised (not power) cells: raise loading to ~100-110µm/side thick electrodes, cutting layers for a given capacity by ~25-30% — fewer foil passes, separators and tab welds. Physics: at low C-rate (urban/LFP duty) the tortuosity penalty is acceptable and inactive fraction (foil+separator+tab) falls, lifting cell energy density and cutting €/kWh of the costliest inactive item, Cu foil. Pair with laser-structured electrode channels (ns/fs pulsed laser drilling vertical pores at ~5% area) to restore Li+ diffusion and recover rate. Net: same capacity with materially less copper and separator per Wh.

Coater must handle higher wet-film without mud-cracking; may need slower drying or multi-zone oven. Net foil and separator consumption per kWh drops.

costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~25% reduction in Cu foil+separator inactive cost (~€6-8/kWh baseline) × 20M kWh

ideaData.riskNotes: Risk: thick electrode delamination and Li-plating at fast charge; restrict to LFP/energy cells and cap charge C-rate, validate with three-electrode plating detection. Mud-cracking on drying mitigated by binder tuning and IR/NIR staged drying. Laser structuring throughput must match line.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Thick electrodes with laser structuring are established R&D-to-pilot practice (KIT/Fraunhofer 3D-electrode work); mechanism proven, no production programme named.
ideaData.materialGrade: ~100-110µm/side NMC or LFP coating; 15µm Al (1235); 8-12µm C10xx Cu; laser-structured pore array

title: Foil edge overhang tolerance widening via z-fold stacking
description: Higher stacking throughput and yield offset small anode area penalty. Baseline notched-electrode stacking demands ±0.3 mm anode-over-cathode overhang to prevent edge Li plating, driving precision notching lasers and vision alignment that gate line speed. Proposal: adopt continuous z-fold (zig-zag) stacking where a single ~12-16µm ceramic-coated PE separator web is folded between alternating electrode sheets, and oversize the anode footprint so tolerance opens to ±0.6 mm without breaching the plating margin. Continuous separator eliminates per-layer handling and its registration error; wider allowable overhang lets vision run faster with fewer rejects. Physics: plating margin is one-sided (anode must exceed cathode); generous anode overhang converts a two-sided precision problem into a robust one-sided one, trading a few % anode area for throughput/yield.

Vision alignment throughput rises as tolerance opens; stacking scrap falls. Slight anode active-area increase offsets partially. Fewer separator cut edges reduce particulate short risk.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Higher stacking throughput and yield offset small anode area penalty.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: stacking yield +1-2pt and throughput gain ~€0.20/cell × ~25M cells/yr

ideaData.riskNotes: Risk: extra anode overhang adds inactive graphite cost and marginally lowers volumetric density; quantify vs yield gain. Z-fold separator wrinkle can cause thickness variation; mitigate with tension control and inline thickness scan. Re-validate edge Li-plating with n-on-p ratio confirmation.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Continuous z-fold stacking is established practice on pouch/prismatic lines (stacking-equipment suppliers); mechanism proven, no OEM programme named.
ideaData.materialGrade: ~12-16µm ceramic (Al2O3)-coated PE separator web; standard graphite anode / NMC-LFP cathode

title: Carbon-nanotube conductive additive downgauges cathode and foil
description: Frees inactive volume for active material, cutting foil/separator per kWh and enabling Si-anode retention. Baseline NMC/LFP cathode uses 2-4 wt% carbon black (Super-P / acetylene black) for the electron percolation network. Proposal: replace most with single-wall CNT dispersion at 0.1-0.4 wt% (~0.4-1.0 wt% as supplied paste in NMP or water). SWCNTs (aspect ratio >1000, diameter ~1.6 nm) form a 1D percolating network at ~10x lower loading than spherical black. Freeing 2-3 wt% for active material raises capacity per coated area — fewer layers, hence less Cu/Al foil and separator per kWh. On Si-bearing anodes the SWCNT network also buffers Si expansion, maintaining contact through cycling and improving retention. Monetises at foil level: every point of inactive-material cut removes the costliest current-collector mass per Wh.

Higher active fraction reduces layers per cell → fewer tab welds and less foil/separator throughput. Mixing viscosity must be managed.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Frees inactive volume for active material, cutting foil/separator per kWh and enabling Si-anode retention.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~2-3 wt% active-fraction gain reducing foil/separator/layer count ~€3-6/kWh × 20M kWh net of SWCNT cost

ideaData.riskNotes: Risk: poor SWCNT dispersion creates agglomerate hot-spots and rate loss; mitigate with qualified pre-dispersion supply and inline rheology QC. SWCNT cost per kg is high but net-positive at low loading; validate calendar life and DCR. EHS handling of nanotubes per REACH.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: SWCNT conductive additives below 0.4 wt% are established production practice (OCSiAl Tuball dispersions in the cell industry); no OEM programme named.
ideaData.materialGrade: SWCNT dispersion 0.1-0.4 wt% (OCSiAl Tuball class); residual acetylene/Super-P carbon black

title: Reduced-cobalt NMC to LNMO high-voltage spinel for entry cells
description: Removes cobalt entirely and shifts to low-cost manganese-rich chemistry. Baseline mid-nickel cathode (NMC622, ~12% Co of transition metal) carries cobalt cost and supply risk. Proposal for entry/urban cells: cobalt-free high-voltage spinel LiNi0.5Mn1.5O4 (LNMO) operating at ~4.7 V vs Li, giving ~650 Wh/kg cathode-level energy from cheap Ni+Mn with no cobalt and no layered-oxide sintering-atmosphere control; the 3D spinel gives strong rate and thermal stability. Cost physics: deleting cobalt removes the most price-volatile input, and Mn is far cheaper than Ni or Co. Enablers: high-voltage-stable electrolyte (fluorinated carbonate / LiPF6 with additives such as LiBOB or a sulfone co-solvent) plus a thin Al2O3 or LiPON cathode surface coat (few-nm ALD) to suppress oxidation and Mn dissolution at 4.7 V.

Requires high-voltage electrolyte dosing spec change and cathode surface-coating step. Cell hardware unchanged.

costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: Co+Ni reduction ~€8-12/kWh cathode delta × 15M kWh, net of high-voltage electrolyte premium

ideaData.riskNotes: Risk: 4.7V accelerates electrolyte oxidation and Mn dissolution poisoning the anode SEI; mitigate with fluorinated electrolyte, cathode coating, and voltage-window management in BMS. Full calendar/cycle and safety re-validation required. Limit to duty cycles matching energy target.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: LNMO high-voltage spinel is in established late-stage development across the cell industry; mechanism proven, no production OEM programme named.
ideaData.materialGrade: LiNi0.5Mn1.5O4 (LNMO) spinel; fluorinated-carbonate/LiPF6 electrolyte + LiBOB; ALD Al2O3/LiPON coat

title: Prelithiation reservoir additive offsets first-cycle loss
description: Recovers irreversible first-cycle Li, allowing cathode downsizing — the largest BOM lever. Baseline graphite (and especially Si-blend) anodes lose 8-30% of cathode-supplied Li irreversibly to first-cycle SEI, forcing an oversized, expensive cathode. Proposal: add a sacrificial Li reservoir at the cathode via a Li-rich additive — Li2NiO2 or Li5FeO4 (LFO) at 2-6 wt% — or dry-coat the anode with stabilised lithium metal powder (SLMP, e.g. FMC/Livent grade, ~5-20µm particles). On first charge these release extra Li+ consumed by SEI, so the working cathode need not be oversized. Cost physics: cathode active material is the largest BOM line, so every point of first-cycle loss recovered shrinks cathode loading. Especially valuable for Si-C anodes where first-cycle loss is largest, unlocking their capacity without a cathode penalty.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Recovers irreversible first-cycle Li, allowing cathode downsizing — the largest BOM lever.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: 5-10% first-cycle-loss recovery enabling cathode load cut ~€5-9/kWh × 15M kWh net of additive cost

ideaData.riskNotes: Risk: residual decomposition products (e.g. O2/N2 gas from LFO) cause first-cycle gassing; manage with degassing step and additive selection. SLMP is highly reactive — dry-room and inert atmosphere required. Validate long-term calendar life and safety; confirm no impedance rise.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Cathode prelithiation additives and SLMP are established development/early-production practice in the cell industry; mechanism proven, no OEM programme named.
ideaData.materialGrade: Li2NiO2 or Li5FeO4 (LFO) additive 2-6 wt%; stabilised lithium metal powder (SLMP, Livent grade)

title: Aluminum anode current collector via alloy interlayer
description: Replaces the second-most-expensive passive material in the cell for suitable chemistries Baseline anode collector: 8 µm rolled-annealed C11000 ETP copper foil (~$9-11/kg), ~7-9% of cell mass and a top-3 material cost, chosen because Cu resists lithiation below 0.3 V vs Li. Proposal: substitute 12-15 µm EN AW-1050A (Al99.5, H18) or EN AW-1085 foil bearing a 200-400 nm magnetron-sputtered TiN (or Ti/TiN bilayer) barrier plus a ~1-2 µm carbon-conductive primer (carbon black in PVDF or acrylic), restricted to LTO (Li4Ti5O12, 1.55 V plateau) or high-floor buffered designs staying above ~0.35 V so Al does not alloy with Li. TiN blocks residual Li diffusion; the primer restores contact resistance to Cu-comparable <5 mΩ·cm². Al foil is ~1/3 cost/kg and ~1/3 density (2.70 vs 8.96 g/cm³).

TiN blocks residual Li diffusion; the primer restores contact resistance to Cu-comparable <5 mΩ·cm². Al foil is ~1/3 cost/kg and ~1/3 density (2.70 vs 8.96 g/cm³).

Slitting and calendering retained; Al is softer, so calender gap and tension control retuned to avoid necking. No change to stacking stations.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Replaces the second-most-expensive passive material in the cell for suitable chemistries
costSavingPotential.percentage: 6-9% of cell material cost on LTO/high-floor cells
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: Cu foil ~$0.95/cell delta vs Al foil+coating ~$0.35/cell = ~$0.60/cell × ~40M applicable cells (LTO share)

ideaData.riskNotes: Al alloys with Li below ~0.35 V causing pulverization — restrict to LTO/high-floor chemistries only, never standard graphite full cells. Validate barrier integrity by float-potential and 1000-cycle testing; abuse-test for local plating at edges. Corrosion at Al/electrolyte at low potential must be screened with LiFSI-compatible salts.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: TiN/Al barrier-foil current collectors are established practice in LTO chemistries and the academic literature; not tied to a named production programme.
ideaData.materialGrade: EN AW-1050A / EN AW-1085 Al foil, H18 temper, 12-15 µm; 200-400 nm sputtered TiN or Ti/TiN barrier; carbon-conductive primer; vs baseline C11000 ETP Cu 8 µm

title: Dry-room dewpoint relaxation via LiFSI-stable moisture-getter electrode additive
description: Attacks fixed plant utility cost rarely challenged by cell BOM teams Baseline electrodes are handled at -40 to -60°C dewpoint (≈32-11 ppm H2O), 20-35% of finishing-area energy and a large HVAC capex driver, because residual H2O hydrolyses LiPF6 to HF, attacking the cathode and cutting calendar life. Proposal: blend 0.3-0.8 wt% calcined nano-CaO plus molecular-sieve 3A (3Å pore) getter into the cathode binder slurry (PVDF/NMP or aqueous CMC/SBR) to scavenge trace water in-situ, and shift to a partially LiFSI-based salt (e.g. 0.6M LiFSI + 0.4M LiPF6) whose S-F bond does not liberate HF on hydrolysis. This relaxes the dry room to ~-35°C dewpoint (≈22 ppm) without HF penalty; getter binds H2O faster than LiPF6 hydrolysis kinetics, breaking the tight-dewpoint dependency.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Attacks fixed plant utility cost rarely challenged by cell BOM teams
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: Dry-room energy ~€12-18M/yr per 10 GWh; 30% reduction net of additive cost (~€0.02/cell)

ideaData.riskNotes: Getter must be fully calcined and dosed precisely; excess CaO consumes active Li and raises impedance. Validate gassing, HF titration, and 45°C calendar-life vs baseline. Confirm no getter agglomeration causing coating defects. LiFSI Al-corrosion at high voltage needs corrosion inhibitor screening.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: In-situ HF scavengers and LiFSI-based electrolytes are established cell-engineering practice; the specific dry-room relaxation link is not tied to a named programme.
ideaData.materialGrade: Calcined nano-CaO + molecular sieve 3A (0.3-0.8 wt%) in cathode slurry; LiFSI-blended electrolyte (LiFSI/LiPF6); PVDF/NMP or aqueous CMC/SBR binder

title: Notch-free continuous electrode via laser tab cutting eliminates die
description: Removes hard tooling and unlocks multi-format line flexibility Baseline prismatic/pouch electrodes are die-notched to form the uncoated tab, needing hard progressive notching dies per format that wear (edge burr >5 µm pierces the separator and drives internal-short rejects) and lock format flexibility. Proposal: replace mechanical notching with single-mode fiber-laser cutting (~500 W, 1070 nm, remote galvo scanner) of tab geometry directly on the coated foil web at line speed, with intermittent uncoated-patch coating upstream so the laser cuts only 8-15 µm foil, not active material. Optimized pulse parameters and inert assist gas (N2/Ar) yield <2 µm recast/burr and no mechanical burr, removing the dominant internal-short mode; format changeover becomes a software file, enabling one line across cell sizes.

Fume/debris control critical to avoid metallic particle contamination causing shorts. Speed-matching laser to coater web speed needs closed-loop control.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Laser electrode notching/cutting is established practice on advanced high-volume cell lines; the burr/short mechanism is widely documented, no named programme claimed.

title: Nonwoven cellulose separator replaces trilayer PP/PE/PP
description: Swaps a supply-constrained specialty film for a commodity feedstock Baseline separator is a 16-20 µm dry-process trilayer PP/PE/PP (Celgard-type) at ~$1.2-2.0/m², supply-constrained, valued for thermal shutdown (PE melts ~130°C closing pores). Proposal: substitute a 20-25 µm wet-laid nanocellulose / regenerated-cellulose (lyocell) nonwoven with a 2-3 µm boehmite/Al2O3 ceramic coat (PVDF or acrylic binder) for stable-format LFP or sodium-ion cells. Cellulose has higher intrinsic thermal stability (no melt/shrink below ~200°C) and near-zero MD shrinkage, and its higher porosity (>60% vs ~40%) and wettability lower ionic resistance. It sacrifices polyolefin shutdown, so it suits inherently safer LFP/Na-ion. Wood-pulp feedstock is far cheaper than specialty polyolefin.

title: Cathode single-pass double-side simultaneous slot-die coating
description: Halves drying passes and floor area, the largest capex/energy sink in cell making Baseline NMC/LFP cathode is coated one side, dried in a ~40-80 m oven, then rewound and coated on the reverse in a second pass through the same oven — two oven passes, two solvent-recovery cycles, and a rewind that risks first-side scratching. Proposal: dual opposed slot-die heads coating both foil faces simultaneously on a vertically-oriented, floating-web (air-flotation) dryer, so the foil is dried once with no contact. Physics: air-flotation support eliminates back-roll contact that forces sequential coating; simultaneous deposition halves solvent-drying throughput time per unit and cuts NMP recovery energy roughly in half. Coating-weight symmetry (both sides dried identically) tightens loading tolerance to ±1.5% improving capacity binning yield.

Air-flotation drying must avoid skinning that traps solvent. Requires requalification of electrode adhesion and porosity vs sequential baseline.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Simultaneous double-side / air-flotation drying is established coating technology (used in film/battery pilot lines); no named OEM cell programme claimed.

title: Micro-perforated cathode foil for double-side ion transport
description: Raises active-mass fraction, cutting inactive materials per kWh Baseline cathode collector is 12-15 µm continuous EN AW-1085 aluminum foil; ions must travel laterally within each coating layer to the separator, capping usable coating thickness (~70-90 µm/side) before rate capability collapses. Proposal: use a laser- or roll-micro-perforated Al foil (10-20 µm holes, ~3-5% open area) so electrolyte and Li-ions can transport through the foil, letting the two coating layers act as a shared ion reservoir. Physics: through-foil ion paths shorten effective diffusion length, permitting thicker single-side-equivalent loadings (up to ~120 µm) at the same C-rate, which raises the active-to-inactive ratio — fewer foil/separator layers per kWh. This directly attacks the inactive-mass fraction driving $/kWh.

Open area reduces foil cross-section — check current-carrying and mechanical tension limits during winding. Thicker electrodes risk lithium plating at fast charge; restrict to standard-charge trims and validate rate maps.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Perforated current collectors for thick electrodes are established R&D/pilot practice; no named production programme claimed.

title: Formation fast-track via targeted-voltage partial SEI protocol
description: Attacks the highest-capex, lowest-visibility step in cell finishing Baseline formation runs 1-3 full slow charge/discharge cycles over 12-30 h to build graphite SEI — the most capital- and floor-intensive step (formation+aging ~15-25% of cell cost, driven by rows of costly cyclers). Proposal: adopt a targeted stepped-current protocol building SEI only across the critical 0.2-0.8 V vs Li window at optimized C-rate (~C/5 in-band, higher out-of-band) with a controlled 40-45°C temperature ramp, plus an FEC/VC film-forming additive package (2-4 wt%, e.g. 2% FEC + 1% VC). SEI-forming reactions concentrate in a narrow potential band; dwelling there at elevated temperature with a fast-nucleating additive completes SEI in a fraction of a full cycle, cutting formation time ~40-60% and freeing cycler capacity — the real cost lever.

ideaData.riskNotes: Aggressive formation risks incomplete/unstable SEI → gassing and calendar-life loss. Validate with 45°C storage, gas-chromatography of gassing, and 1000-cycle life vs baseline before release. FEC can worsen high-temp gassing on some cathodes — screen per chemistry. Requires robust in-line OCV/impedance quality gate.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Additive-assisted accelerated formation is established cell-engineering practice and an active industry focus; no named OEM programme claimed.
ideaData.materialGrade: FEC/VC electrolyte additive package (~2 wt% FEC + ~1 wt% VC, 2-4 wt% total); no structural material lever

title: Two-phase pumped CO2 loop replaces subcooled single-phase glycol cold plate
description: Deletes chiller HX, shrinks pump, thins plate, cuts coolant fill. Baseline: 50/50 water-glycol single-phase cold plate carrying ~6 kW at 8-10 L/min via a 150W pump, with 4-6°C cell-to-cell spread from sensible heat rise (cp ~3.4 kJ/kgK) along the flow path. Proposal: a pumped two-phase R744 (CO2) loop where refrigerant enters as saturated liquid at ~5°C/40 bar and boils near-isothermally, exploiting latent heat (~230 kJ/kg). The isothermal boiling front cuts cell-to-cell spread below 2°C at half the mass flow, permitting narrower stamped microchannels (2.0 mm vs 4.5 mm hydraulic diameter) in AA3003-O aluminium and deleting the intermediate chiller heat exchanger. Pump power falls ~60% (small gerotor circulator). Plate wall thinned to 0.8 mm since 40 bar in small channels is within hoop-stress limits for 3003.

ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Deletes brazed chiller station and glycol fill/degas stations. Cold plate becomes narrower-channel stamped-and-FSW pair; adds pressure-rated braze validation and He leak-test station at 60bar. Circulator replaces 150W pump. Net plant capex neutral: one heat-exchanger cell removed, one leak-test cell added.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Deletes chiller HX, shrinks pump, thins plate, cuts coolant fill.
costSavingPotential.percentage: 15-22% of the pack thermal subassembly BOM
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~€60 chiller HX delete + €18 pump downgrade + €12 plate metal + €8 coolant/fill = ~€98 × ~0.55 realisation × 120,000 ≈ €6.5M

Two-phase flow maldistribution risk across parallel channels mitigated by inlet orifice restrictors sizing each channel to critical quality <0.3. Refrigerant charge safety per R744 handling.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Pumped two-phase CO2 cooling is established practice in aerospace and datacentre thermal management; not naming a specific vehicle programme.
ideaData.materialGrade: AA3003-O aluminium stamped microchannel plate, 0.8 mm wall, 2.0 mm hydraulic diameter; R744 (CO2) refrigerant; vs 50/50 water-glycol baseline

title: Foam-metal-core cold plate replaces machined pin-fin channels
description: Eliminates channel-forming tooling and downstream spreaders. Baseline: stamped/CNC serpentine cold plate relying on wall conduction and channel-wall convection, with cell-to-plate ΔT limited by low glycol-side heat-transfer coefficient (~2000 W/m2K) at laminar Re. Proposal: braze an open-cell aluminium foam core (AA6101, 10-40 PPI, ~90% porosity) between two AA3003 skins to form the flow passage. Foam multiplies wetted area 20-40x and forces tortuous mixing, raising volumetric heat-transfer coefficient to 8,000-15,000 W/m2K, allowing a 30% thinner footprint or lower flow for equal ΔT — enough for hotter NMC fast-charge cells without an added vapor chamber or PCM buffer. Foam is inserted as a cut blank and controlled-atmosphere (CAB, NOCOLOK flux) brazed in the same furnace pass as the skins — no channel machining or serpentine stamping die.

Foam is inserted as a cut blank and controlled-atmosphere (CAB, NOCOLOK flux) brazed in the same furnace pass as the skins — no channel machining or serpentine stamping die.
ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Deletes serpentine stamping die and CNC channel milling; adds foam blanking and placement station ahead of CAB braze. Braze fixture must compress foam to skins for wetting. Cycle time neutral; scrap lower (no thin-wall channel splits). Tooling capex drops (no progressive channel die).

costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~€22 tooling/machining delete + €14 spreader/PCM avoidance = ~€36 net (foam adds ~€9) × 0.6 × 120,000 ≈ €3.6M

ideaData.riskNotes: Higher pressure drop through foam raises pump duty — mitigate with graded PPI (coarse at inlet). Braze wetting into foam ligaments needs flux control to avoid blocked cells; validate with flow-CT scan sampling. Long-term glycol erosion of thin ligaments requires inhibitor spec and 3000hr flow-loop durability.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Open-cell metal-foam heat exchangers are established practice in power electronics and HVAC; mechanism proven, no specific vehicle programme cited.
ideaData.materialGrade: AA6101 open-cell Al foam core (10-40 PPI, ~90% porosity); AA3003 skins; CAB/NOCOLOK braze

title: Dielectric single-phase immersion with tray-integrated jet plate deletes cold plate
description: Deletes cold plate and TIM entirely; improves uniformity cutting warranty. Baseline: cells bonded to a discrete stamped-brazed cold plate via cure-in-place TIM, the plate bolted separately into the tray. Proposal: submerge cell bottoms in a shallow bath of single-phase dielectric coolant (hydrofluoroether, e.g. 3M Novec-class, or synthetic ester ~1.9 kJ/kgK, dielectric strength >30 kV/mm) and pump it through a low-profile jet-impingement distribution plate stamped directly into the AlSi10MnMg HPDC tray floor. This deletes both the discrete cold plate and all TIM — the fluid is the thermal interface, contacting the full can surface (10-20x a bottom-only plate footprint) with directed jets at hot zones for near-uniform temperature. The ~0.3 K·cm2/W TIM bondline resistance is eliminated since there is no solid interface.

ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Deletes discrete cold-plate subassembly line and TIM dispense/cure station. Tray HPDC gains cast jet-distribution rib pattern (revised die). Adds dielectric fill, seal-integrity and fluid-level stations. Seal complexity rises; net station count roughly neutral but shifts capex from plate line to tray die + fill.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Deletes cold plate and TIM entirely; improves uniformity cutting warranty.
costSavingPotential.percentage: 18-25% of thermal subassembly, offset by fluid cost
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: (~€70 plate + €22 TIM) delete − €35 fluid/fill add = ~€57 net × 0.6 × 120,000 ≈ €4.1M

ideaData.riskNotes: Dielectric fluid cost and mass are significant; mitigate with shallow partial-immersion (cans only, not full pack) to cap fill volume. Fluid ageing/acidity and material compatibility with can coatings, vents and adhesives needs 3000hr compatibility matrix. Fire-safety and venting-under-fluid behaviour must be validated to pack abuse standards.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Single-phase immersion battery cooling is an established emerging practice; distinct from cell-to-cell immersion by using tray-integrated jet distribution. No specific programme cited.
ideaData.materialGrade: Hydrofluoroether (3M Novec-class) or synthetic ester dielectric coolant; AlSi10MnMg HPDC tray with integrated stamped jet-impingement plate

title: Reversible refrigerant heat-pump plate deletes PTC heater subassembly
description: Deletes entire PTC heater subassembly and its HV harness/contactor. Baseline: pack thermal subassembly carries a separate HV PTC or resistive glycol heater (~5-7 kW) for cold-start/preconditioning, with its own contactors, harness and mount. Proposal: make the pack cold plate a reversible refrigerant evaporator/condenser tied into the vehicle heat pump; in heating mode the plate condenses refrigerant against the cells, delivering compressor + ambient-harvested heat (COP ~2-3) instead of resistive watts (COP 1). One stamped AA3003 plate rated for R1234yf (or R134a) serves both duties via a 4-way reversing valve in the shared valve block, deleting the entire PTC subassembly — element, sheath, contactor, mount, harness. Pack-warming energy drops 50-65%; the plate absorbs added condenser-side pressure (~25 bar) with a 1.0 mm AA3003 wall.

costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~€90 PTC+contactor+harness delete − €18 plate upgrade − €14 valve = ~€58 net × 0.85 × 120,000 ≈ €5.9M

ideaData.benchmarkReference: Refrigerant heat-pump battery heating is established in modern BEV thermal architectures; mechanism proven, no specific programme named.
ideaData.materialGrade: AA3003 stamped plate, 1.0 mm wall, rated for R1234yf/R134a; 4-way reversing valve; deletes PTC heater

title: Phase-change TIM replaces cure-in-place gap filler bondline
description: Removes metering/mixing waste and cure energy; lower material usage. Baseline: cure-in-place liquid gap filler (two-part silicone, ~3 W/mK, ~€25-35/kg, dispensed 200-600 g/pack) fills the cell-to-plate gap, needing two-component metering, static mixer, cure oven/dwell and difficult rework. Proposal: replace with a screen-printed or pre-form phase-change TIM (paraffin/olefin matrix filled with hexagonal boron-nitride plus graphite, ~4-6 W/mK) that is solid at assembly (clean, no dispense mess) and melts at ~45-50°C to wet the interface and collapse to a <100 µm bondline at first thermal cycle. This deletes the two-part metering pump, static-mixer waste and cure dwell while lowering thermal resistance versus 3 W/mK silicone because the molten PCTIM conforms to microroughness at a thinner bondline. Reworkable on reheat, cutting scrap of mis-stacked modules.

ideaData.technicalDescription: Baseline: cure-in-place liquid gap filler (two-part silicone, ~3 W/mK, ~€25-35/kg, dispensed 200-600 g/pack) fills the cell-to-plate gap, needing two-component metering, static mixer, cure oven/dwell and difficult rework. Proposal: replace with a screen-printed or pre-form phase-change TIM (paraffin/olefin matrix filled with hexagonal boron-nitride plus graphite, ~4-6 W/mK) that is solid at assembly (clean, no dispense mess) and melts at ~45-50°C to wet the interface and collapse to a <100 µm bondline at first thermal cycle. This deletes the two-part metering pump, static-mixer waste and cure dwell while lowering thermal resistance versus 3 W/mK silicone because the molten PCTIM conforms to microroughness at a thinner bondline.
