ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Deletes 2K metering pump, mixer-tip consumables and cure oven dwell. Adds screen-print or pre-form pick-place station (faster tact). Scrap of purge/mixer waste (typ. 8-12%) eliminated. Lower cure energy. Net capex reduction on the TIM line.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Removes metering/mixing waste and cure energy; lower material usage.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~€10 dispense-waste + €6 cure energy + €5 material reduction = ~€21 × 0.6 × 120,000 ≈ €1.5M (upper case with rework recovery ~€4M)

ideaData.riskNotes: PCTIM pump-out and dry-out over 15yr/thousands of thermal cycles is the key risk; mitigate with cross-linked/gelled matrix and confirm via 2000-cycle thermal shock plus thermal-resistance drift limit. Ensure melt point below worst-case first-fill temp to guarantee wet-out. Flammability rating of matrix to pack standard.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Phase-change TIMs are established practice in CPU/power-module thermal management; distinct from graphite sheet and cure-in-place filler. No programme named.
ideaData.materialGrade: Phase-change TIM: paraffin/olefin matrix with hexagonal boron-nitride + graphite fill, ~4-6 W/mK, melt point ~45-50°C; vs 3 W/mK cure-in-place silicone

title: Serpentine cooling ribbon replaces cold plate in cylindrical-cell pack
description: Replaces large brazed plate with cheaper extruded ribbon; better cell uniformity. Baseline for 4680/21700 cylindrical packs: a full bottom cold plate contacts only the cell-can end face, giving high axial ΔT and a large brazed plate. Proposal: replace the plate with a thin serpentine multi-port ribbon extruded from EN AW-3003-H14 aluminium (~2.0 mm wall, 8–10 microports of 1.2 mm bore, 0.4 mm web) weaving vertically between cell rows to contact the cylindrical side wall — the low-resistance radial path. Side-wall cooling cuts core-to-surface ΔT versus end cooling and deletes the bottom plate. The ribbon is a single extrusion cut to length and CNC-bent to R6, replacing the stamped-brazed plate. TIM becomes a thermally-conductive silicone potting bead (2–3 W/m·K) dispensed along the contact line rather than a full-area gap pad.

ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Deletes bottom cold-plate stamp/braze line. Adds ribbon extrusion cut-and-bend and inter-row insertion during cell stacking. Requires potting bead dispense along ribbon. Header brazing of ribbon ends replaces full-plate braze — smaller furnace load.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Replaces large brazed plate with cheaper extruded ribbon; better cell uniformity.
costSavingPotential.percentage: 14-20% of cold-plate cost for cylindrical packs
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~€55 plate delete − €22 ribbon+potting = ~€33 net × 0.6 × 100,000 ≈ €2.0M (upper with warranty gain)

ideaData.riskNotes: Ribbon-to-cell contact pressure and gap tolerance during stacking is the main risk; mitigate with compliant potting and stack-compression fixture. Leak paths at many bend radii — validate burst and cycle on bent extrusion. Cell side-wall electrical isolation from Al ribbon must be guaranteed (anodise + potting).
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Inter-cell serpentine ribbon cooling is established practice for cylindrical-cell packs (widely used across 18650/21700 architectures); mechanism only, no specific programme named.
ideaData.materialGrade: EN AW-3003-H14 extruded aluminium microport tube; 2–3 W/m·K silicone potting adhesive

title: Plastic-composite manifold replaces aluminium coolant distribution header
description: Replaces machined/brazed Al with net-shape molded polymer, fewer seals. Baseline: the pack coolant inlet/outlet manifold splitting flow to parallel cold-plate zones is a machined or brazed aluminium block with O-ring ports. Proposal: injection-mould the manifold from 35% glass-filled PPA — PA9T or PA6T grade (e.g. Kuraray Genestar or Solvay Amodel AS-1133), HDT >280 °C at 1.8 MPa, hydrolysis-stabilised for 50/50 glycol/water at 65–70 °C and 2–3 bar — as one part with integrated barbs, mounting bosses and a snap-in NTC pocket. Polymer at 1.5 g/cc vs 2.7 for aluminium cuts manifold mass ~55% and removes machining, brazing and galvanic-inhibitor concerns. Wall 3.0 mm with 2 mm molded ribs and 1.5° draft handles the low pressure at 3× safety factor; ports IR/vibration-welded to the plate inlet instead of O-ring stack-ups.

ideaData.riskNotes: Long-term glycol hydrolysis resistance of GF-PPA and creep at ports under thermal cycling are the key risks; mitigate with PA9T grade validated to 3000hr in 65°C glycol and metal-insert or overmolded threaded bosses at bolt joints. title: Aluminium-clad steel cold plate replaces monolithic 3003 Al plate
description: Substitutes ~55% of Al mass with 3x cheaper steel and deletes a structural bracket subframe Baseline cold plate is a two-piece EN AW-3003-H14 stamped tray + 3003 lid, CAB-brazed with AA4045 cladding, 1.5 mm wall, ~2.8 kg for an 80 kWh plate. Replace the structural half with roll-clad tri-layer strip: a 0.6 mm DC01 low-carbon steel core with 0.15 mm AA3003 clad on each face (AA4045 braze-clad on the wetted side). The steel core carries pack crush and hold-down load, letting the aluminium channel wall drop to 0.7 mm. Steel at ~0.9 €/kg vs 2.9 €/kg for 3003 sheet lowers cost, and the Al cladding preserves brazeability to the Al lid and TIM wetting. Cell ΔT is governed by the 0.7 mm Al skin and unchanged; the steel sits outside the thermal path in the load-bearing flange only. Galvanic couple managed by the continuous Al cladding isolating steel from glycol.

ideaData.benchmarkReference: Roll-clad Al/steel strip is established practice in brazed HVAC heat-exchanger tube stock; structural cold-plate use is emerging, no named programme.
ideaData.materialGrade: Roll-clad DC01 steel core (0.6 mm) / AA3003 clad (0.15 mm/face), AA4045 braze skin; EN AW-3003-H14 lid

title: Thermosiphon loop replaces pumped glycol for low-C-rate cruise
description: Downsizes pump and reduces HV parasitic energy, freeing DC-DC and range margin Baseline runs a single-phase 50/50 glycol loop with an electric pump circulating through the cold plate whenever cells exceed setpoint, drawing 40–90 W parasitic. Add a passive two-phase thermosiphon branch charged with R1233zd(E) (or dielectric Novec 649 / FK-5-1-12) into the cold-plate galleries, with the condenser mounted above the plate against the pack lid for gravity return. During cruise/park rejection (<0.5C), latent evaporation (~180–270 kJ/kg) moves heat at zero pump work with tiny mass flow; the pump and chiller engage only above a C-rate threshold. The pump downsizes one frame size and duty-cycles off ~60% of a WLTP cycle, cutting HV load and allowing a smaller HV DC-DC allocation. Gallery internal volume sized to a 25–40% liquid fill fraction.

costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: Pump downsize ~€6/pack + parasitic energy allowing 2% smaller cell allocation valued ~€5/pack effective = ~€11 × 100k

Orientation dependence on grade (park on hills) needs worst-case modelling. Dielectric fill adds cost partly offsetting pump saving; refrigerant GWP/regulatory review required.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Loop thermosiphons are established practice in telecom and power-electronics cooling; battery-pack application is developmental, no named OEM programme.
ideaData.materialGrade: R1233zd(E) or Novec 649 (FK-5-1-12) working fluid; EN AW-3003 cold-plate galleries

title: Sensor-diode-in-busbar deletes discrete NTC harness per module
description: Eliminates discrete thermistors, pots, connectors and a harness leg Baseline temperature sensing uses 8–12 discrete 10 kΩ NTC thermistors per pack potted into the cold plate/module with a dedicated LV harness, connectors and routing. Replace with the intrinsic temperature dependence of the cell-monitoring interconnect: sense the TCR of the nickel-plated Cu-ETP (C11000) busbar — or a printed Cu/PTC trace on the FPC/ICB already present for voltage sensing — calibrated so existing BMS ADC channels report both voltage and local temperature. Cu resistivity rises ~0.39%/°C (monotonic), so a 4-wire Kelvin read across a defined busbar segment yields ±1.5 °C after two-point cal. Requires a stable low-current reference (~1 mA) and segment geometry held to ±2% to bound error. Deletes NTCs, their pots, connectors and a dedicated harness leg from the thermal subassembly.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Eliminates discrete thermistors, pots, connectors and a harness leg
costSavingPotential.percentage: 8-12% of sensing/harness portion of thermal subassembly
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~9 NTC channels × (sensor €0.4+pot+connector+harness ~€0.7) ≈ €10/pack, keep 2 refs, net ~€8 × 150k

ideaData.riskNotes: TCR read accuracy degrades with busbar joint aging and self-heating under load — needs compensation model validated over life and current range. Functional-safety (ASIL) reclassification of temperature channel required; keep 1-2 reference NTCs for plausibility cross-check to satisfy ISO 26262. Calibration drift validation over 8-year life.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Copper-trace RTD sensing is established practice in power electronics; busbar-integrated cell-temperature sensing is emerging, no named programme.
ideaData.materialGrade: Cu-ETP (C11000) Ni-plated busbar; alternatively printed Cu RTD trace on polyimide FPC

title: Waterless PCM-only conditioning for LFP city-fleet packs
description: Removes the entire active liquid loop from a bounded-duty variant Baseline LFP pack carries a full glycol cold plate + chiller branch sized for peak fast-charge, even though city/fleet duty rarely exceeds 1C and LFP tolerates wider temperature. Replace the active plate with a passive graphite-matrix expanded-graphite/paraffin composite PCM slab (melt point tuned ~35-40 °C, ~200 kJ/kg latent, ~15 W/m·K in-plane via 8-12% graphite loading) bonded cell-to-slab, sized to absorb a full DC charge/discharge thermal pulse and re-solidify during park via a small finned Al skin to ambient. Deletes the cold plate, chiller, pump, valves and glycol from the thermal subassembly for the low-DCFC-frequency use case, exploiting LFP's flat OCV and thermal robustness.

costSavingPotential.percentage: 35-50% of thermal subassembly cost on that variant
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: Delete cold plate €55 + pump/valve/chiller/coolant ~€60, add PCM ~€25 = ~€90 net × 40k

PCM leakage/pyrolysis at abuse temps and cyclic latent-capacity fade over 3000 cycles require validation; graphite loading vs conductivity vs latent-mass trade must be modelled.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Expanded-graphite/paraffin PCM battery buffering is established research practice; passive-only LFP packs are emerging in fleet vehicles, no named OEM programme confirmed.

title: Blow-moulded PA6-GF condenser plenum replaces stamped Al ducting
description: Consolidates stamped/brazed plenum parts into one moulding, cutting mass and joints Baseline pack-integrated heat-pump/condenser branch uses stamped and welded EN AW-3003 sheet plenums and Al brackets to route the condenser air/coolant crossover, adding braze joints and mass. Replace the non-pressure-bearing air/coolant plenum shells (not the wetted micro-channel core) with suction blow-moulded PA6-GF30, hydrolysis-stabilised grade (e.g. BASF Ultramid A3WG6 HRX or equivalent), incorporating snap-in condenser retention, sensor bosses and hose ports as moulded features. GF30 PA6 gives ~9 GPa flex modulus, 120 °C continuous rating and cuts mass ~45% while consolidating 4–6 stamped/brazed parts into one moulding, wall 2.5–3.0 mm. Wetted refrigerant path stays EN AW-3003 aluminium; only the structural/air-guiding plenum converts to polymer.

costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: Part consolidation ~€8 + mass/braze delete ~€5 = ~€13/pack × 90k, less tool amortisation

ideaData.riskNotes: PA6-GF hydrolysis and glycol/refrigerant-vapour compatibility at 120 °C over life needs grade validation (consider PA66-GF or PPA if margin short). Thermal expansion mismatch at Al-condenser-to-plastic interface requires floating mounts. Creep at retention snaps under vibration validated by PSD durability.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Blow-moulded PA6-GF air/fluid ducts are established practice in charge-air and HVAC modules; condenser-plenum use in packs is emerging, no named programme.
ideaData.materialGrade: PA6-GF30 hydrolysis-stabilised (heat-stabilised) blow-mould grade; wetted core EN AW-3003

title: Insert-moulded FPC-plus-microchannel hybrid cold plate carrier
description: Merges cold plate, interconnect board and TIM frame into one carrier Baseline stacks three subassemblies onto cells: brazed Al cold plate, the FPC/ICB interconnect with busbars, and separate TIM. Integrate the polyimide FPC voltage/temperature sensing and low-current Cu busbar tabs directly onto a roll-bonded EN AW-3003 cold-plate face by insert-moulding a PA6-GF or PPS dielectric isolation layer, forming one carrier that is coolant channel + interconnect + TIM-locating frame. A 0.2 mm dielectric overmould (CTI >600, tracked to IEC 60664) provides creepage/clearance for 2.5 kV isolation between busbar and coolant channel while keeping the cell-to-coolant path <1.5 mm Al. Deletes the separate ICB substrate, its standoffs, fasteners and one assembly index. Overmould selected for 3003 adhesion and CTE compatibility to survive thermal cycling.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Merges cold plate, interconnect board and TIM frame into one carrier
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ICB substrate+standoffs+fasteners ~€14 + index/handling ~€4 = ~€18/pack × 110k, less tool

ideaData.riskNotes: Dielectric integrity between HV busbar and grounded coolant plate is safety-critical — needs 2.5 kV hipot after thermal cycling and coolant-leak fault-tree analysis (single-fault isolation). FPC-to-Al CTE delamination over cycling validated. Rework/serviceability of an integrated part reduces — must be scrap-if-fail justified by yield.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Insert-moulded FPC busbar carriers are established practice; integration onto the cold-plate face is emerging, no named programme.
ideaData.materialGrade: Roll-bonded EN AW-3003 plate; PA6-GF or PPS-GF dielectric overmould; polyimide FPC

title: Bottom-only cold plate with anisotropic graphite cell base spreader
description: Shrinks cold-plate area and deletes side plates using in-plane graphite spreading Baseline prismatic packs cool through a bottom cold plate but rely on thick ceramic-filled gap pads (3–5 W/m·K) to bridge the poor through-plane path, and some designs add side/top plates for hotspots. Replace the premium isotropic gap pad with a 0.5 mm pyrolytic graphite sheet (PGS, ~700–1500 W/m·K in-plane) or compressed natural graphite (~150–400 W/m·K in-plane) laminated to the cell base, moving heat laterally to the single bottom-plate footprint. This lets the bottom plate shrink channel density and deletes any secondary side plate, since the graphite equalises the base isotherm and cuts peak cell ΔT. Through-plane, a thin filled epoxy/silicone adhesive (~3 W/m·K, <0.2 mm) completes the joint. Attacks cost by deleting metal plate area and downgrading the gap-filler grade to a low-cost 1.5 W/m·K bead.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Shrinks cold-plate area and deletes side plates using in-plane graphite spreading
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: Side plate delete ~€10 + bottom plate area/channel reduction ~€6 - graphite add ~€2 = ~€14 × 100k

ideaData.benchmarkReference: PGS/graphite heat spreaders are established practice in consumer electronics and some EV modules; base-spreader plate-reduction is emerging, no named programme.
ideaData.materialGrade: Pyrolytic graphite sheet (PGS) or compressed natural graphite, 0.5 mm; ~3 W/m·K filled adhesive bond line

title: Injection-moulded PA66-GF35 thermal frontend replaces Al valve-hose stack
description: Removes hose/clamp BOM lines and manual routing labour while cutting leak-warranty exposure Baseline unified thermal module carries 6–9 discrete coolant valves, an Al chiller manifold, and ~14 EPDM hose segments joined by spring clamps on steel brackets. Replace the mounting/routing architecture with a single PA66-GF35 (35% short glass, 1.65 g/cm³, e.g. BASF Ultramid A3WG7 or DuPont Zytel) injection-moulded thermal frontend: coolant galleries cored into two shells joined by hot-plate/IR welding to a burst rating >4 bar, integrating pump seats, expansion tank and O-ring valve ports. Wall 3.0–3.5 mm with 1.5° draft; galleries 12–16 mm bore. Consolidating routing deletes ~10 hose-to-nipple interfaces, each a leak/warranty node and €0.6–1.1 clamped-joint labour cost. GF35 gives HDT ~245 °C at 1.8 MPa, ample for 90 °C glycol; grade specified hydrolysis-stabilised for long-term glycol contact.

Two multi-cavity tools (~€380k) needed. Cycle ~55s vs multi-minute manual hose routing. Scrap shifts to weld-flash controllable <1%.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Removes hose/clamp BOM lines and manual routing labour while cutting leak-warranty exposure
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~€21/unit saved (10 joints × €1.1 labour + €7 hose/clamp BOM + €3 bracket) × 200k = €4.2M; upper from warranty avoidance

ideaData.benchmarkReference: Polymer coolant-distribution modules are established practice among Tier-1 thermal suppliers (moulded PA-GF coolant manifolds); no specific programme named.
ideaData.materialGrade: PA66-GF35 (35% short glass), hydrolysis-stabilised, 1.65 g/cm³

title: Bistable-latching solenoid valves cut thermal-module parasitic power
description: Cuts parasitic 12V draw of the valve island, translating to range/pack credit Baseline unified thermal module uses 4–6 continuously-energised proportional or on/off solenoid coolant valves each drawing 6–9 W held-open, plus a multiway rotary valve with a geared BLDC actuator. Replace steady-state valves with permanent-magnet bistable latching solenoids using an N42SH detent magnet (150 °C-rated NdFeB, high intrinsic coercivity for underhood temps) that consume power only during the ~30 ms state transition and hold position magnetically at 0 W. For loop-isolation valves that dwell for hours (heat-pump mode select, degas isolation), held-coil I²R is pure parasitic loss. Eliminating ~30 W continuous across the valve set at highway cruise recovers usable pack energy; latching also removes coil self-heating that derates EPDM seal life. Driver needs an H-bridge for bipolar reset pulses.

Valve unit cost rises ~€1.2 each for magnet/latch mechanism; net vehicle-level saving is energy/range, enabling small pack downsize or cooling-of-coil deletion. Driver software adds pulse-drive H-bridge logic.

costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~30W avg saved × range value; expressed as ~€10–14/unit pack-energy credit × 200k

ideaData.benchmarkReference: Bistable latching solenoids are established practice in fluidic/hydraulic control; EV coolant-valve application stated as mechanism, no programme named.
ideaData.materialGrade: N42SH NdFeB latching-detent magnet (150 °C rated); EPDM seals

title: Overmoulded busbar-and-signal thermal module deletes discrete wiring harness
description: Removes internal harness BOM and crimp/route labour, and internal splice failure modes Baseline wires each pump, valve actuator and coolant temp/pressure sensor with individual leads to a bulk connector, adding ~2.5 m harness, 8-12 crimped terminals, tape and clips per module. Replace with a stamped-grid leadframe (CuSn0.15 / C19400 copper alloy, 0.8 mm strip, tin-plated 2-3 µm at contact zones) overmoulded in PA66-GF35 (heat-stabilised, 1.6 mm nominal wall) into the carrier top shell, presenting header pins at each actuator seat and one sealed IP67 blade connector to the vehicle. Physics: consolidating point-to-point wires into a planar stamped grid removes per-terminal crimp labour and connector interfaces (each a corrosion/warranty node); stamped conductors sized ~2.5 mm width carry pump inrush (12-15 A) with lower IR drop and a defined conduction thermal path.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Removes internal harness BOM and crimp/route labour, and internal splice failure modes
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~€11/unit (harness €5 + 10 crimps × €0.3 + route/tape €3) × 200k = €2.2M mid

ideaData.riskNotes: Leadframe-to-plastic adhesion and sealing at pin exits need PV under thermal cycling -40/+120°C and salt-fog; risk of micro-cracking at overmould pin roots. Mitigate with stress-relief geometry, pre-heated inserts, and potted connector interface. Validate current-carrying/derating for pump stall.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Overmoulded stamped-leadframe electrical carriers are established practice in automotive mechatronic modules (transmission control units, junction boxes); no programme named.
ideaData.materialGrade: Leadframe C19400 (CuFeP) 0.8 mm, Sn plating 2-3 µm; overmould PA66-GF35 heat-stabilised

title: Single 4-port coaxial heat exchanger consolidates chiller and LCC into module
description: Consolidates two exchangers, brackets and interconnects into one core Baseline hosts two separate brazed-plate exchangers — a refrigerant chiller (R1234yf/glycol) and a low-temp coolant-coolant LCC (battery/EDU) — each with 4 ports, 2 brackets, 6 hose stubs. Replace with a single tri-fluid CAB-brazed stack of AA3003 core plates clad both sides with AA4045 (10-12% clad ratio), three interleaved circuits (refrigerant, battery-glycol, EDU-glycol) separated by internal partition plates, brazed at ~600°C under nitrogen with non-corrosive Nocolok flux, mounted to the carrier boss. Physics: sharing the brazed wall between all three circuits eliminates one exchanger's end-plates, ports and interconnect hoses; counterflow interleaving raises UA per brazed area, dropping total plate count ~20% for equal duty. Refrigerant channels use a 1.2 mm gap for boiling ΔT; stack proof 45 bar refrigerant side

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Consolidates two exchangers, brackets and interconnects into one core
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~€15/unit (one exchanger core €9 + 2 brackets €2 + 6 hoses €4) × 200k = €3.0M mid

ideaData.riskNotes: Cross-circuit internal leak (refrigerant into glycol) is a critical failure — requires 100% dual-medium leak test and burst margin >4× MOP on refrigerant side. Braze-joint integrity between three media validated by pressure-cycle and vibration. Thermal cross-talk modelling to avoid unwanted battery/EDU coupling.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Multi-circuit brazed-plate exchangers are established practice in stationary HVAC and automotive chillers; automotive tri-fluid integration stated as mechanism, no programme named.
ideaData.materialGrade: AA3003 core / AA4045 clad plates; AA3003 end-plates; Nocolok (KAlF4) flux CAB braze

title: Thermosiphon passive loop deletes secondary pump in low-load module branch
description: Eliminates an entire pump-and-driver branch where duty is low Baseline runs an active EC pump on the cabin-heater/degas circulation branch that mostly operates at low flow to keep sensors wetted and avoid air pockets. Replace this branch's pump with a gravity/density-driven thermosiphon loop: route a rising hot leg from the heat source and a falling cold return to a header ~150 mm higher, sized 16 mm bore (EPDM 50/50 glycol hose or moulded PA612-GF30 channel) to hold laminar buoyant flow >0.3 L/min. Physics: temperature-induced density difference (Δρ ≈ 20 kg/m³ across 40°C in 50/50 ethylene-glycol) generates a self-circulating head sufficient for low-duty branches, deleting one pump, its driver channel, harness and mount for that branch. Loop routed with continuous upward slope >2° to avoid vapour trap.

ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Deletes one pump, one driver output, one connector and mount from module build (~3 fewer assembly operations). Requires geometric routing discipline in carrier design — no new tooling beyond gallery re-layout. Removes a rotating-part warranty item.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Eliminates an entire pump-and-driver branch where duty is low
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~€10/unit (pump €6 + driver channel €2 + harness/mount €2) × 200k = €2.0M mid

ideaData.riskNotes: Thermosiphon only works within a defined orientation/tilt window and above threshold ΔT; risk of stagnation at cold-start or on steep grades. Mitigate by reserving thermosiphon for non-safety-critical low-duty branches only and CFD-validating vent/deaeration. Confirm no reverse-flow into main loop via check orifice.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Thermosiphon/natural-convection cooling is established practice in distribution transformers and some engine recirculation; EV module branch application stated as mechanism, no programme named.

title: Snap-fit vibration-welded carrier replaces bolted thermal-module chassis
description: Removes fastener hardware and torque labour, cuts mass and machining Baseline bolts pumps, valve block, exchangers and reservoir onto a die-cast AlSi10Mg (or steel-bracket) chassis using ~18-24 M6 fasteners with steel threaded inserts and torque-monitored stations. Replace the metal chassis with a PA66-GF40 (heat-stabilised, ~2.5 mm rib wall) injection-moulded carrier capturing components via integrated snap-fit ribs and vibration-welded pockets (linear weld, 240 Hz, ~1.6 mm collapse), fasteners retained only at the 4 vehicle-interface M8 mounts. Physics: moulded datum features locate components to ±0.3 mm without machining, and snap/weld retention withstands road-load PSD (per ISO 16750-3) via designed bead stiffness; deleting ~18 fasteners removes hardware BOM and torque-station labour while cutting mass ~1.8 kg vs cast AlSi10Mg.

ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Replaces ~18 torque-controlled bolting operations with snap-insert and one vibration-weld cell. One injection tool (~€260k) replaces cast chassis tool. Cycle drops; eliminates thread-insert install and torque-verification error-proofing. Component locating accuracy from tool, reducing shim/adjust.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Removes fastener hardware and torque labour, cuts mass and machining
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~€13/unit (18 fasteners+inserts €4 + 18 torque ops × €0.35 €6.3 + chassis material delta €3) × 200k = €2.6M mid

ideaData.riskNotes: Retention under 20g shock and long-term creep at 90°C for snap features needs PV; risk of component fretting/loosening. Mitigate with metal-reinforced snap zones at heavy components (pump), vibration-weld for load-bearing joints, and NVH resonance check. Confirm serviceability strategy (module is now non-serviceable).
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Snap-fit and vibration-welded polymer component carriers are established practice in air-intake modules and cooling-fan shrouds; thermal-module application stated as mechanism, no programme named.
ideaData.materialGrade: Carrier PA66-GF40 heat-stabilised; delete AlSi10Mg die-cast; M8 vehicle mounts

title: 6-port rotary disc valve replaces four solenoids in module
description: One actuated valve replaces four solenoids plus their drivers and wiring Baseline implements loop routing (series/parallel battery-EDU, chiller bypass, heater path) with 4 discrete 3/2 solenoid valves plus cast interconnect passages — 4 actuators, 4 connectors, ~8 O-ring ports. Replace with a single 6-port ceramic-disc rotary selector: a lapped 96% Al2O3 alumina stator/rotor pair (sealing faces lapped to Ra <0.1 µm, flatness <1 µm) driven by one geared BLDC stepper indexing 6 discrete flow states, body in PPS-GF40 with EPDM static seals. Physics: ceramic-on-ceramic lapped faces give near-zero cross-port leak at 3 bar with low actuation torque (<0.4 Nm), so one actuator does four valves' work; consolidating routing into a single disc deletes three actuators, three drivers, their harness/connectors and shrinks the cast passage network.

Ceramic disc lapping is the cost driver but amortised across states. Simplifies carrier casting/moulding (fewer valve bosses). One position-calibration step at EOL.

costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: ~€18/unit (3 solenoids × €4 + 3 driver channels × €1.5 + 3 connectors/harness × €1) × 200k = €3.6M mid

Mitigate with inline filter screen, dead-band flush states, and Hall-based closed-loop position feedback. Validate transition sequencing avoids momentary all-closed deadhead pressure spike.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Multi-port rotary coolant valves are established practice in current EV thermal systems (multiway rotary coolant actuators); ceramic-disc 6-state consolidation stated as mechanism, no programme named.
ideaData.materialGrade: Rotor/stator 96% Al2O3 alumina lapped Ra <0.1 µm; body PPS-GF40; EPDM seals

title: Plastic-encapsulated coolant distribution backbone replaces machined Al manifold plate
description: Removes the entire machining route and swarf/coolant overhead for a low-cost moulded part. Baseline central coolant distribution is a CNC-machined EN AW-6060-T6 aluminium block with 6-8 drilled cross-bores, O-ring ports and plugged blind-hole intersections carrying battery, EDU and cabin branches. Replace with a two-shell PA612-GF30 (hydrolysis-resistant) injection-moulded backbone, hot-plate or infrared welded along a planar flange, with hose stubs and mounting bosses moulded in one shot. Cored channels of 12-20 mm hydraulic diameter delete all drilling, deburring and >10 blind-bore plugs. PA612-GF30 tolerates 50/50 glycol at 125°C continuous with <0.3% swell; welded flange burst >12 bar at 3 bar working. Physics: cored channels give smooth radii vs sharp drilled intersections, cutting local pressure-drop 15-25% so pump duty falls. Mass drops ~2.1 kg Al to ~0.75 kg polymer.

ideaData.benchmarkReference: Polymer welded coolant distribution modules are established practice in EV thermal frontends; mechanism proven, no specific programme named.
ideaData.materialGrade: PA612-GF30 hydrolysis-resistant (replaces EN AW-6060-T6); hot-plate/IR welded
ideaData.regulatoryContext: Coolant compatibility per SAE J1455; no homologation impact

title: Electrically-actuated 3-way proportional valve replaces mixing valve plus bypass loop
description: Consolidates thermostat + solenoid + fittings into one controllable device and cuts fan/pump energy. Baseline regulates radiator vs bypass split with a wax-thermostat mixing valve plus a separate solenoid bypass and its hoses/tees. Replace with a single brushless-DC rotary proportional 3-way valve: PPS-GF40 body, PPA-GF (or Al2O3-coated) seat, EPDM/PTFE-lined ball, giving continuously variable radiator/bypass blend under CAN control. Deletes the wax element, discrete bypass solenoid, two tees and ~0.4 m hose. Physics: proportional blending removes on/off hunting of the wax element, holding coolant setpoint within ±1.5°C so the loop runs nearer optimum viscosity and radiator fan/pump run at lower average duty. One 12 V actuator, 0.6 Nm, <1 W hold via detented worm gear. Consolidates 3 flow-control functions into one valve stack.

ideaData.riskNotes: Loss of fail-safe wax behaviour: on actuator failure coolant could route wrong path. Mitigate with spring-return default-to-radiator position and diagnostic on position sensor. Validate ball-seat wear over 250k cycles and cold-crank torque at -40°C.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Proportional/rotary electric coolant valves are established EV thermal practice; mechanism proven, no specific programme named.
ideaData.materialGrade: Body PPS-GF40; seat PPA-GF; ball EPDM/PTFE-lined
ideaData.regulatoryContext: Functional-safety ASIL-B position feedback; no homologation impact

title: Delete standalone reservoir via integrated degas volume in distribution shell
description: Removes an entire moulded bottle, its bracket and interconnect hoses by reusing the module shell. Baseline carries a separate blow-moulded HDPE expansion/degas bottle with its own bracket, cap, level sensor and two connecting hoses. Eliminate the discrete bottle by moulding a baffled degas chamber into the top shell of the PA612-GF30 distribution backbone, with an internal swirl-separator rib and moulded-in filler neck (with pressure cap rated ~1.4 bar). Physics: the swirl baffle uses centrifugal separation of entrained air at the highest loop point, so gas collects above the coolant line and vents to a small vertical expansion volume; integrating it deletes the two connecting hoses that were the main air-ingress and leak sites. Level sensing moves to a single moulded capacitive-pad boss. Consolidates reservoir + bracket + 2 hoses into the existing shell.

costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: Bottle €7 + bracket €3 + hoses/clamps €5 + assy labour €2 = €17 vs €4 core-cost adder; delta €13 × 200,000

ideaData.riskNotes: Degas efficiency and thermal expansion headroom must be re-proven when integrated. Risk of insufficient air separation causing pump cavitation. Mitigate with CFD-sized swirl rib, expansion volume ≥7% of loop, and 200 h air-purge/degassing bench test plus cold-fill cycling.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Integrated degas/expansion volumes in coolant distribution modules are established practice; mechanism proven, no specific programme named.
ideaData.materialGrade: PA612-GF30 shell (integrated degas); deletes blow-moulded HDPE bottle
ideaData.regulatoryContext: Pressure-cap relief per OEM spec; no homologation impact

title: Loop topology change from parallel to series cabin-pack heating cuts one pump
description: Removes a full pump and coupler by exploiting cascade heat use in a serial loop. Baseline dual-loop architecture runs a dedicated PTC-fed cabin heater loop and a separate battery-warming loop, each with its own EC pump plus a coupling heat exchanger. Re-architect to a single serial glycol loop where the heat-pump waterside condenser plate warms coolant flowing through the battery plate first, then the cabin heater core, controlled by the existing rotary blend valve. Physics: battery warm-up needs ~35-40°C and cabin needs higher supply, so sequencing battery-then-cabin lets residual enthalpy do useful work; one correctly-sized EC pump (25 W, 20 L/min at 0.6 bar) replaces two 15 W pumps. Deletes the second pump, its controller channel, two hoses and the intermediate coupler. Architecture/topology move, so no material grade lever.

ideaData.benchmarkReference: Serialised single-pump heat-pump coolant loops are established EV practice; mechanism proven, no specific programme named.
ideaData.regulatoryContext: Cabin warm-up per OEM comfort spec; no homologation impact

title: Aluminium heat-exchanger cores brazed into module frame delete four flanges
description: Metallurgical joining replaces bolted flanges and an interconnect hose, cutting parts and leak warranty. Baseline bolts a separate chiller and a coolant-coolant LCC exchanger onto a carrier, each with 4 O-ring flanges and gaskets. Replace with two brazed plate cores — AA3003 core clad with AA4045 (10-12% clad ratio) — whose end-tanks are brazed directly to a shared AA3003 header plate in one CAB furnace cycle (~600°C, nitrogen atmosphere, Nocolok non-corrosive flux), so the two cores plus interconnect become a single brazed monoblock. Physics: brazing forms metallurgical joints replacing 8 elastomer-sealed flanges, removing the dominant leak and permeation paths and the bolted-flange mass; the shared header eliminates the external hose between chiller and LCC. A single furnace pass forms all joints simultaneously, and the monoblock bolts to the module at just two M8 points.

ideaData.riskNotes: Braze-joint integrity and refrigerant-side cleanliness are critical; a furnace defect scraps the whole monoblock (higher unit-scrap value). Mitigate with SPC on braze clad thickness, 100% He leak test, and fillet radiography sampling. Validate refrigerant compatibility of flux residues.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: CAB-brazed multi-core aluminium thermal modules are established supplier practice; mechanism proven, no specific programme named.
ideaData.materialGrade: AA3003 core / AA4045 clad plates and AA3003 header; Nocolok flux CAB braze
ideaData.regulatoryContext: Refrigerant tightness per SAE J2727; no homologation impact

title: Push-in blind-mate manifold interface deletes robotic hose routing at vehicle line
description: Collapses per-hose assembly and leak checks into one docking operation and enables off-line test. Baseline connects module to vehicle-side battery, EDU and HVAC coolant lines via ~8 individually clamped or quick-connect hoses fitted one-by-one on the trim line. Replace with a single planar blind-mate coolant interface plate: all module ports terminate on one PA66-GF35 face (heat-stabilised, 35% short-glass, ~130 MPa tensile) carrying floating, radially-sealed coupling bores using peroxide-cured EPDM O-rings (70 Shore A, dual-lip, coolant-rated to 50/50 glycol at 120 C). Mates to a matching plate in one linear push with two conical guide pins (H8/f7 lead-in) and one over-centre cam latch. Floating seals accommodate +/-1.5 mm radial float; one stroke seals all 8 circuits, converting 8 sequential manual joins into one docking motion and enabling module pre-fill/pre-test off-line. ideaData.title: Push-in blind-mate manifold interface deletes robotic hose routing at vehicle line
ideaData.technicalDescription: Baseline connects module to vehicle-side battery, EDU and HVAC coolant lines via ~8 individually clamped or quick-connect hoses fitted one-by-one on the trim line. Replace with a single planar blind-mate coolant interface plate: all module ports terminate on one PA66-GF35 face (heat-stabilised, 35% short-glass, ~130 MPa tensile) carrying floating, radially-sealed coupling bores using peroxide-cured EPDM O-rings (70 Shore A, dual-lip, coolant-rated to 50/50 glycol at 120 C). Mates to a matching plate in one linear push with two conical guide pins (H8/f7 lead-in) and one over-centre cam latch. Floating seals accommodate +/-1.5 mm radial float; one stroke seals all 8 circuits, converting 8 sequential manual joins into one docking motion and enabling module pre-fill/pre-test off-line. Deletes per-hose clamps and leak checks at final assembly.
ideaData.manufacturingImpact: Converts 8 sequential hose-join+clamp ops at final line into 1 dock stroke, cutting station takt sharply and enabling off-line module fill/test. Adds interface-plate mould and vehicle-side counter-plate. Net final-line ops -7; enables parallel sub-assembly flow.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Collapses per-hose assembly and leak checks into one docking operation and enables off-line test.
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: 8 joins × ~18 s + 8 clamps + leak recheck ≈ €14 labour vs €5 dock; delta €9 × 200,000 plus flow-time gain

ideaData.riskNotes: Blind-mate multi-seal risks partial engagement and micro-leaks under vibration. Mitigate with latch-confirm sensor, colour/keying to prevent cross-connect, and 3-axis vibration + thermal-shock validation of the sealed pack. Verify seal set life at 150k cycles equivalent.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Blind-mate multi-port fluid interfaces are established practice in data-centre liquid cooling and aerospace; the floating radial-seal coupling mechanism is proven engineering practice, but I am not confident naming a specific automotive production programme.
ideaData.materialGrade: Plate: PA66-GF35 (heat-stabilised, e.g. Ultramid A3WG7); seals: peroxide-cured EPDM 70 Shore A dual-lip O-rings; guide pins hardened steel, H8/f7 fit
ideaData.regulatoryContext: Coolant leak class per OEM spec; no homologation impact

title: Common thermal-module platform scaled by valve-count across three vehicle tiers
description: Amortises one tool and one validation across three programmes and slashes part-number count. Baseline uses three distinct thermal modules (base BEV, long-range, performance) with unique housings, pump ratings and valve maps, each carrying its own tooling and validation. Replace with one PA612-GF30 module carrier (30% glass, low moisture uptake for dimensional stability vs PA66) and channel backbone shared across all three tiers; differentiation is solely by populating a common valve/pump interface pattern: base tier fits a 4-port rotary multi-way valve and ~20 W BLDC pump, top tier a 6-port valve and ~30 W pump into an identical M6 bolt grid and O-ring port pattern. Housing and channel cross-sections are dimensioned for worst-case top-tier flow (~15 L/min), so lower tiers under-populate. One injection tool amortises across ~3x volume; one validation dossier covers the platform by bracket

ideaData.title: Common thermal-module platform scaled by valve-count across three vehicle tiers
ideaData.technicalDescription: Baseline uses three distinct thermal modules (base BEV, long-range, performance) with unique housings, pump ratings and valve maps, each carrying its own tooling and validation. Replace with one PA612-GF30 module carrier (30% glass, low moisture uptake for dimensional stability vs PA66) and channel backbone shared across all three tiers; differentiation is solely by populating a common valve/pump interface pattern: base tier fits a 4-port rotary multi-way valve and ~20 W BLDC pump, top tier a 6-port valve and ~30 W pump into an identical M6 bolt grid and O-ring port pattern. Housing and channel cross-sections are dimensioned for worst-case top-tier flow (~15 L/min), so lower tiers under-populate. One injection tool amortises across ~3x volume; one validation dossier covers the platform by bracketing the flow/thermal extremes.
ideaData.manufacturingImpact: One mould and one assembly fixture family serve 3 variants; changeover is component population, not retooling. Cuts distinct part numbers ~60%, reduces tool sets from 3 to 1, and shrinks spares/logistics complexity. EOL test program bracketed to 2 extremes.

costSavingPotential.qualitative: Amortises one tool and one validation across three programmes and slashes part-number count.
costSavingPotential.percentage: 20-30% of module tooling and PPAP cost
costSavingPotential.calculationBasis: 2 avoided tool sets ~€0.8M + validation reuse ~€1.2M + ~€10/unit complexity delta × 300,000

ideaData.riskNotes: Over-dimensioned base-tier module carries slight excess mass/cost; and platform-wide defect would affect all tiers. Mitigate with worst-case-flow CFD sizing, DFMEA on shared carrier, and bracketed validation (test min and max configs) accepted by OEM engineering release.
ideaData.benchmarkReference: Common thermal-module platforms differentiated by valve/pump population, and integrated multi-way coolant valves, are established OEM practice; the scale-by-population mechanism is proven engineering practice without a specific programme I can confidently name.
ideaData.materialGrade: Module carrier: PA612-GF30 (low-moisture-absorption glass-filled polyamide); common ports sealed with EPDM O-rings; M6 bolt-grid interface
ideaData.regulatoryContext: Bracketed validation acceptance; no homologation impact
